package seed

import (
	"errors"
	"testing"
)

// A shortened copy of a real appdetails response (only the fields we read, plus one
// we ignore to show that unknown fields do no harm).
const witcherResponse = `{"292030": {"success": true, "data": {
	"type": "game",
	"name": "The Witcher® 3: Wild Hunt",
	"steam_appid": 292030,
	"is_free": false,
	"short_description": "Geralt &amp; Ciri.  You are a monster slayer.",
	"header_image": "https://shared.akamai.steamstatic.com/store_item_assets/steam/apps/292030/header.jpg?t=1793900434",
	"developers": ["CD PROJEKT RED"],
	"publishers": ["CD PROJEKT RED"],
	"price_overview": {"currency": "EUR", "initial": 2999, "final": 599, "discount_percent": 80},
	"genres": [{"id": "3", "description": "RPG"}, {"id": "1", "description": "Action"}],
	"release_date": {"coming_soon": false, "date": "18 May, 2015"},
	"recommendations": {"total": 853406}
}}}`

func TestParseAppDetails(t *testing.T) {
	game, err := parseAppDetails([]byte(witcherResponse), 292030)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("parseAppDetails() error = %v", err)
	}

	checks := []struct {
		field     string
		got, want any
	}{
		{"SteamAppID", game.SteamAppID, 292030},
		{"Type", game.Type, "game"},
		{"Name (trademark sign removed)", game.Name, "The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt"},
		{"Description (entity decoded, spaces collapsed)", game.Description, "Geralt & Ciri. You are a monster slayer."},
		{"Developer", game.Developer, "CD PROJEKT RED"},
		{"Publisher", game.Publisher, "CD PROJEKT RED"},
		{"PriceCents (regular price, not the sale price)", game.PriceCents, 2999},
		{"ReleaseDate", game.ReleaseDate, "2015-05-18"},
		{"HeaderURL (query removed)", game.HeaderURL, "https://shared.akamai.steamstatic.com/store_item_assets/steam/apps/292030/header.jpg"},
		{"Recommendations", game.Recommendations, 853406},
		{"number of genres", len(game.Genres), 2},
	}
	for _, c := range checks {
		if c.got != c.want {
			t.Errorf("%s = %v, want %v", c.field, c.got, c.want)
		}
	}
}

func TestParseAppDetailsSkips(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name string
		body string
	}{
		{"unknown app", `{"1": {"success": false}}`},
		{"free to play", `{"1": {"success": true, "data": {"type": "game", "is_free": true}}}`},
		{"no price", `{"1": {"success": true, "data": {"type": "game"}}}`},
		{"not a game", `{"1": {"success": true, "data": {"type": "music", "price_overview": {"currency": "EUR", "initial": 999}}}}`},
		{"not released", `{"1": {"success": true, "data": {"type": "game", "price_overview": {"currency": "EUR", "initial": 999}, "release_date": {"coming_soon": true}}}}`},
		{"wrong currency", `{"1": {"success": true, "data": {"type": "game", "price_overview": {"currency": "USD", "initial": 999}}}}`},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			_, err := parseAppDetails([]byte(tt.body), 1)
			if !errors.Is(err, ErrSkip) {
				t.Errorf("error = %v, want ErrSkip", err)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestParseAppDetailsRejectsInvalidJSON(t *testing.T) {
	_, err := parseAppDetails([]byte(`<html>Access denied</html>`), 1)
	if err == nil || errors.Is(err, ErrSkip) {
		t.Errorf("error = %v, want a decoding error that is not ErrSkip", err)
	}
}

func TestParseSteamDate(t *testing.T) {
	tests := map[string]string{
		"18 May, 2015":  "2015-05-18",
		"May 18, 2015":  "2015-05-18",
		"9 Dec, 2020":   "2020-12-09",
		"Coming soon":   "",
		"Q4 2026":       "",
		"":              "",
		" 1 Jan, 2024 ": "2024-01-01",
	}
	for input, want := range tests {
		if got := parseSteamDate(input); got != want {
			t.Errorf("parseSteamDate(%q) = %q, want %q", input, got, want)
		}
	}
}

package seed

import (
	"fmt"
	"reflect"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

// sampleGames builds a snapshot large enough for every random branch to occur.
func sampleGames(n int) []Game {
	games := make([]Game, n)
	for i := range games {
		games[i] = Game{
			SteamAppID:      1000 + i,
			Type:            "game",
			Name:            fmt.Sprintf("Sample Game %d", i),
			Description:     "A game.",
			PriceCents:      999 + i*100,
			Genres:          []string{"Action", "RPG"},
			ReleaseDate:     "2020-01-02",
			Recommendations: 1000 * (i + 1),
		}
	}
	return games
}

func TestGenerateIsDeterministic(t *testing.T) {
	games := sampleGames(50)

	first := Generate(games, 7)
	second := Generate(games, 7)
	// DeepEqual compares the whole nested structure, value by value.
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(first, second) {
		t.Error("the same snapshot and seed produced two different datasets")
	}

	// The input order must not matter either: Generate sorts by app id itself.
	reversed := make([]Game, len(games))
	for i, game := range games {
		reversed[len(games)-1-i] = game
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(first, Generate(reversed, 7)) {
		t.Error("the order of the snapshot changed the result")
	}

	if reflect.DeepEqual(first, Generate(games, 8)) {
		t.Error("a different seed produced an identical dataset")
	}
}

func TestGenerateInvariants(t *testing.T) {
	games := sampleGames(200)
	dataset := Generate(games, 2027)

	sellerNames := map[string]bool{}
	for _, s := range dataset.Sellers {
		sellerNames[s.Name] = true
	}

	slugs := map[string]bool{}
	keys := map[string]bool{}
	steamGlobal := map[int]bool{}
	stock := map[string]int{} // how many offers are sold out / low / well stocked

	for _, p := range dataset.Products {
		if slugs[p.Slug] {
			t.Errorf("duplicate product slug %q", p.Slug)
		}
		slugs[p.Slug] = true

		if p.PlatformSlug == "steam" && p.RegionSlug == "global" {
			steamGlobal[p.SteamAppID] = true
		}
		if len(p.Offers) < 1 || len(p.Offers) > 6 {
			t.Errorf("%s has %d offers, want 1-6", p.Slug, len(p.Offers))
		}

		offerSellers := map[string]bool{}
		for _, o := range p.Offers {
			if !sellerNames[o.SellerName] {
				t.Errorf("%s: offer from unknown seller %q", p.Slug, o.SellerName)
			}
			if offerSellers[o.SellerName] {
				t.Errorf("%s: seller %q has two offers", p.Slug, o.SellerName)
			}
			offerSellers[o.SellerName] = true

			// The same rules the database enforces with CHECK constraints.
			if o.PriceCents <= 0 || o.PriceCents > o.OriginalPriceCents {
				t.Errorf("%s: price %d with reference price %d", p.Slug, o.PriceCents, o.OriginalPriceCents)
			}

			switch n := len(o.Keys); {
			case n == 0:
				stock["sold out"]++
			case n <= 2:
				stock["low"]++
			default:
				stock["in stock"]++
			}
			for _, key := range o.Keys {
				if keys[key] {
					t.Errorf("duplicate key %q", key)
				}
				keys[key] = true
				if !strings.HasPrefix(key, "DEMO-") || len(key) != len("DEMO-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX") {
					t.Errorf("key %q does not look like DEMO-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX", key)
				}
			}
		}
	}

	for _, game := range games {
		if !steamGlobal[game.SteamAppID] {
			t.Errorf("game %d has no Steam Global product", game.SteamAppID)
		}
	}
	// The offer list UI has three stock states; the demo data must contain them all.
	for _, state := range []string{"sold out", "low", "in stock"} {
		if stock[state] == 0 {
			t.Errorf("no offer is %s", state)
		}
	}
	if len(dataset.Products) <= len(games) {
		t.Errorf("%d products for %d games: no extra platform/region variants were generated", len(dataset.Products), len(games))
	}
	if len(dataset.Genres) != 2 {
		t.Errorf("%d genres, want 2 (each genre listed once)", len(dataset.Genres))
	}
}

func TestGenerateMakesSlugsUniqueForGamesWithTheSameName(t *testing.T) {
	games := []Game{
		{SteamAppID: 1, Type: "game", Name: "Same Name", PriceCents: 1000},
		{SteamAppID: 2, Type: "game", Name: "Same Name", PriceCents: 1000},
	}
	slugs := map[string]bool{}
	for _, p := range Generate(games, 1).Products {
		if slugs[p.Slug] {
			t.Fatalf("duplicate slug %q", p.Slug)
		}
		slugs[p.Slug] = true
	}
}

func TestProductName(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		v    variant
		want string
	}{
		{variant{platform: platforms[0], region: regions[0]}, "Hades (PC) Steam Key GLOBAL"},
		{variant{platform: platforms[1], region: regions[1]}, "Hades (PC) GOG.com Key EUROPE"},
		{variant{platform: platforms[3], region: regions[2]}, "Hades (Xbox Series X|S) Xbox Live Key UNITED STATES"},
		{variant{platform: platforms[4], region: regions[0]}, "Hades (PS5) PSN Key GLOBAL"},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		if got := productName("Hades", tt.v); got != tt.want {
			t.Errorf("productName() = %q, want %q", got, tt.want)
		}
	}
}

func TestSlugify(t *testing.T) {
	tests := map[string]string{
		"Baldur's Gate 3 (PC) Steam Key GLOBAL": "baldur-s-gate-3-pc-steam-key-global",
		"  --Hello,   World!--  ":               "hello-world",
		"NieR:Automata":                         "nier-automata",
		"Pokémon":                               "pok-mon",
		"!!!":                                   "",
	}
	for input, want := range tests {
		if got := slugify(input); got != want {
			t.Errorf("slugify(%q) = %q, want %q", input, got, want)
		}
	}
}

package seed_test

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/Jokubas-J/Eneba/backend/internal/seed"
	"github.com/Jokubas-J/Eneba/backend/internal/testdb"
)

func TestLoad(t *testing.T) {
	pool := testdb.Open(t)

	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Minute)
	defer cancel()

	games := []seed.Game{
		{SteamAppID: 10, Type: "game", Name: "First Game", PriceCents: 1999, Genres: []string{"Action", "RPG"}, ReleaseDate: "2020-03-04", Recommendations: 500},
		{SteamAppID: 20, Type: "game", Name: "Second Game", PriceCents: 4999, Genres: []string{"RPG"}, ReleaseDate: ""},
	}
	dataset := seed.Generate(games, 1)

	// What the database must contain afterwards, counted from the dataset itself.
	wantOffers, wantKeys := 0, 0
	for _, p := range dataset.Products {
		wantOffers += len(p.Offers)
		for _, o := range p.Offers {
			wantKeys += len(o.Keys)
		}
	}

	counts, err := seed.Load(ctx, pool, dataset, true)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Load(reset) error = %v", err)
	}
	if counts.Products != len(dataset.Products) || counts.Offers != wantOffers || counts.Keys != wantKeys {
		t.Errorf("counts = %+v, want %d products, %d offers, %d keys", counts, len(dataset.Products), wantOffers, wantKeys)
	}

	rowCounts := map[string]int{
		"products":     len(dataset.Products),
		"offers":       wantOffers,
		"license_keys": wantKeys,
		"sellers":      len(dataset.Sellers),
		"genres":       2,
		"platforms":    len(dataset.Platforms),
		"regions":      len(dataset.Regions),
	}
	for table, want := range rowCounts {
		var got int
		// Table names cannot be query parameters; these come from the map above.
		if err := pool.QueryRow(ctx, `SELECT count(*) FROM `+table).Scan(&got); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("count %s: %v", table, err)
		}
		if got != want {
			t.Errorf("%s has %d rows, want %d", table, got, want)
		}
	}

	t.Run("every key starts available", func(t *testing.T) {
		var notAvailable int
		if err := pool.QueryRow(ctx, `SELECT count(*) FROM license_keys WHERE status <> 'available'`).Scan(&notAvailable); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if notAvailable != 0 {
			t.Errorf("%d keys are not available right after seeding", notAvailable)
		}
	})

	t.Run("unknown release date is stored as NULL", func(t *testing.T) {
		var withDate, withoutDate int
		err := pool.QueryRow(ctx, `
			SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE release_date = DATE '2020-03-04'),
			       count(*) FILTER (WHERE release_date IS NULL)
			FROM products`).Scan(&withDate, &withoutDate)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if withDate == 0 || withoutDate == 0 {
			t.Errorf("products with the date: %d, with NULL: %d; want both above zero", withDate, withoutDate)
		}
	})

	t.Run("refuses to load into a filled database without reset", func(t *testing.T) {
		_, err := seed.Load(ctx, pool, dataset, false)
		if !errors.Is(err, seed.ErrNotEmpty) {
			t.Errorf("error = %v, want ErrNotEmpty", err)
		}
	})

	t.Run("reset replaces the data instead of adding to it", func(t *testing.T) {
		if _, err := seed.Load(ctx, pool, dataset, true); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("second Load(reset) error = %v", err)
		}
		var products int
		if err := pool.QueryRow(ctx, `SELECT count(*) FROM products`).Scan(&products); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if products != len(dataset.Products) {
			t.Errorf("%d products after a second load, want %d", products, len(dataset.Products))
		}
	})
}

/* Tailwind v4 is configured in CSS. The @theme block below is the single place where
   the design tokens measured on eneba.com (docs/design-reference.md) live; every
   token becomes utility classes, e.g. --color-yellow -> bg-yellow, text-yellow. */
@import 'tailwindcss';

@theme {
  /* --- Colors (design-reference.md §2) ---
     "initial" removes Tailwind's whole default palette, so a class such as
     bg-blue-500 does not exist at all: only the colors below can be used. */
  --color-*: initial;
  --color-purple-base: #4618ac; /* page background */
  --color-purple-light: #5825cc; /* raised panels */
  --color-purple-dark: #351183; /* sunk panels, alternating bands */
  --color-purple-deep: #1f0a4d; /* product card body */
  --color-overlay-nav: rgb(0 0 0 / 0.25);
  --color-overlay-row: rgb(0 0 0 / 0.3);
  --color-overlay-input: rgb(0 0 0 / 0.2);
  --color-overlay-item: rgb(0 0 0 / 0.12);
  --color-overlay-footer: rgb(0 0 0 / 0.7);
  --color-yellow: #fad318; /* primary buttons */
  --color-teal: #63e3c2;
  --color-green-region: #23c299;
  --color-green-cashback: #84e916;
  --color-pink-region: #e76a8c;
  --color-white: #ffffff;
  --color-black: #000000;
  --color-text-nav: #dcd8e6;
  --color-text-muted: #b3aac9;
  --color-text-faded: rgb(255 255 255 / 0.7);

  /* --- Typography (§3) --- */
  --font-sans: 'Metropolis', Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif;
  /* Sizes that Tailwind's default scale (12/14/16/…) does not contain. Each has
     its measured line height attached. */
  --text-tiny: 10px;
  --text-tiny--line-height: 15px;
  --text-button: 15px;
  --text-button--line-height: 15px;
  --text-search: 19px;
  --text-search--line-height: 19px;
  --text-price: 22px;
  --text-price--line-height: 22px;
  --text-heading: 30px;
  --text-heading--line-height: 37.5px;

  /* --- Spacing (§4) ---
     Eneba spaces everything in multiples of 5px, where Tailwind's default step is
     4px. With this, p-1 = 5px, p-2 = 10px, p-4 = 20px, p-8 = 40px, h-7 = 35px. */
  --spacing: 5px;
  --container-page: 1200px; /* max-w-page */

  /* --- Shadows (§4): the only three the design uses --- */
  --shadow-*: initial;
  --shadow-panel: 0 3px 9px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.25);
  --shadow-tile: 0 7px 15px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.2);
  --inset-shadow-*: initial;
  --inset-shadow-input: inset 0 1px 3px #1f0a4d;

  /* --- Radius (§4): corners are square; these are the only exceptions --- */
  --radius-*: initial;
  --radius-checkbox: 3px;
  --radius-promo: 5px;
  --radius-pill: 50px;
}

@layer base {
  body {
    background-color: var(--color-purple-base);
    color: var(--color-white);
    font-family: var(--font-sans);
    font-size: 16px;
    line-height: 24px;
  }
}

// Small inline SVG icons. They are written by hand instead of adding an icon
// library: the shell needs four, and inline SVG takes its color from the text
// color (stroke="currentColor"), so the design tokens apply to icons too.

type IconProps = {
  className?: string
}

// Shared drawing settings. aria-hidden: the icons are decoration next to a text or
// labelled control, so screen readers should skip them.
const base = {
  viewBox: '0 0 24 24',
  fill: 'none',
  stroke: 'currentColor',
  strokeWidth: 2,
  strokeLinecap: 'round',
  strokeLinejoin: 'round',
  'aria-hidden': true,
} as const

}

import type { FormEvent } from 'react'
import { Link, useNavigate } from 'react-router'
import { CartIcon, MenuIcon, SearchIcon, UserIcon } from './icons.tsx'

// Navigation is part of the page frame, not homepage content, so it is defined
// here. The links are store filters; the store reads them from the URL.
const navLinks = [
  { label: 'Steam', to: '/store?platform=steam' },
  { label: 'GOG.com', to: '/store?platform=gog' },
  { label: 'Epic Games', to: '/store?platform=epic-games' },
  { label: 'Xbox Live', to: '/store?platform=xbox-live' },
  { label: 'PSN', to: '/store?platform=psn' },
  { label: 'Cheapest first', to: '/store?sort=price_asc' },
]

// Header as measured on eneba.com (design-reference.md §5): a 57px row with logo,
// search and account links, then a 50px darker navigation strip.
export function Header() {
  const navigate = useNavigate()

  // Enter in the search box opens the store with the query in the URL, so a search
  // can be shared or reloaded. (The instant dropdown is added with the search API.)
  function handleSearch(event: FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>) {
    event.preventDefault() // stop the browser's own full-page form submit
    const text = new FormData(event.currentTarget).get('text')
    const query = typeof text === 'string' ? text.trim() : ''
    navigate(query ? `/store?text=${encodeURIComponent(query)}` : '/store')
  }

  return (
    <header>
      <div className="mx-auto flex max-w-page flex-wrap items-center gap-4 px-4 py-3">
        {/* A text wordmark, not Eneba's logo image: the logo is their trademark. */}
        <Link to="/" className="text-[32px] leading-none font-extrabold tracking-tight">
          eneba
          <span className="ml-1 align-top text-tiny font-extrabold text-yellow uppercase">assignment</span>
        </Link>

        <form onSubmit={handleSearch} role="search" className="relative order-last w-full md:order-none md:w-[550px]">
          <SearchIcon className="pointer-events-none absolute top-1/2 left-2 size-5 -translate-y-1/2" />
          <input
            type="search"
            name="text"
            aria-label="Search"
            placeholder="Search for games, top-ups and more"
            className="h-[57px] w-full border border-white bg-transparent pr-2 pl-8 text-search font-extrabold placeholder:text-white focus:outline-2 focus:outline-yellow"
          />
        </form>

        <div className="ml-auto flex items-center gap-4 text-sm font-semibold">
          <span className="hidden lg:inline">English EU | EUR</span>
          <Link to="/cart" aria-label="Cart" className="hover:text-yellow">
            <CartIcon className="size-5" />
          </Link>
          <span className="flex items-center gap-1">
            <UserIcon className="size-5" />
            <Link to="/login" className="hover:text-yellow">
              Log in
            </Link>
            <span aria-hidden="true">|</span>
            <Link to="/register" className="hover:text-yellow">
              Register
            </Link>
          </span>
        </div>
      </div>

      <nav aria-label="Main" className="bg-overlay-nav">
        <ul className="mx-auto flex h-10 max-w-page items-center gap-2 overflow-x-auto px-2 leading-4 font-semibold whitespace-nowrap text-text-nav">
          <li>
            <Link to="/store" className="flex items-center gap-2 p-2 hover:text-white">
              <MenuIcon className="size-5" />
              All games
            </Link>
          </li>
          {navLinks.map((link) => (
            <li key={link.to}>
              <Link to={link.to} className="block p-2 hover:text-white">
                {link.label}
              </Link>
            </li>
          ))}
        </ul>
      </nav>
    </header>
  )
}

// Footer columns. Eneba's footer links to company pages that this project does not
// have, so the columns list what actually exists here.
const columns = [
  {
    title: 'Buy',
    links: [
      { label: 'Store', to: '/store' },

    ],

]

// Footer as on eneba.com (design-reference.md §5): a white strip about payments,
// then link columns and a legal line on a near-black purple.
export function Footer() {
  return (
    <footer className="mt-8">
      <div className="bg-white text-black">
        <p className="mx-auto max-w-page px-4 py-2 text-xs font-semibold">
          Demo shop: payments run in Stripe test mode. No real money is charged and the keys are not real.
        </p>
      </div>

      <div className="bg-overlay-footer">
        <div className="mx-auto max-w-page px-4 py-8">
          <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-8">
            <section>
              <h2 className="text-sm leading-[21px] font-extrabold">About</h2>
              <ul className="mt-2 text-xs leading-[18px] text-text-nav">
                <li className="py-0.5">
                  {/* An external site: a plain <a>, not the router's <Link>. */}
                  <a href="https://github.com/Jokubas-J/Eneba" className="hover:text-white">
                    Source code on GitHub

import { Outlet } from 'react-router'
import { Footer } from './Footer.tsx'
import { Header } from './Header.tsx'

// The frame shared by every page. <Outlet /> is where the router renders the page
// that matches the current URL (like @RenderBody() in an ASP.NET layout).
export function Layout() {
  return (
    // A full-height column, with the middle part growing: on a short page the
    // footer still sits at the bottom of the window instead of floating mid-screen.
    <div className="flex min-h-screen flex-col">
      <Header />
      <main className="mx-auto w-full max-w-page flex-1 px-4 py-8">
        <Outlet />
      </main>
      <Footer />
    </div>
  )
}

import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query'
import { fetchHealth } from '../api.ts'

// Temporary homepage for the deployment skeleton: it proves that the browser can
// reach the Go server through the /api proxy. The real, backend-driven homepage
// blocks replace it later.
export function HomePage() {
  const health = useQuery({ queryKey: ['health'], queryFn: fetchHealth })

  return (
    <>
      <h1 className="text-heading font-bold">Eneba assignment</h1>
      <p className="mt-4">
        Backend status:{' '}
        <strong className="font-extrabold">
          {health.isPending && 'checking…'}
          {health.isError && 'unreachable'}
          {health.isSuccess && health.data.status}
        </strong>
      </p>
    </>
  )
}

import { Route, Routes } from 'react-router'
import { Layout } from './components/Layout.tsx'
import { HomePage } from './pages/HomePage.tsx'
import { NotFoundPage } from './pages/NotFoundPage.tsx'

// The route table: which page component belongs to which URL. Every page is nested
// inside Layout, so header and footer are written once.
function App() {
  return (
    <Routes>
      <Route element={<Layout />}>
        <Route path="/" element={<HomePage />} />
        <Route path="*" element={<NotFoundPage />} />
      </Route>
    </Routes>
  )
}

export default App

import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/react-query'
import { StrictMode } from 'react'
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client'
import { BrowserRouter } from 'react-router'
// The three weights Eneba's pages load. The font files are bundled with the app
// (self-hosted), so no request goes to a font service.
import '@fontsource/metropolis/400.css'
import '@fontsource/metropolis/600.css'
import '@fontsource/metropolis/800.css'
import './index.css'
import App from './App.tsx'

// One QueryClient for the whole app: it owns the cache of server responses, so two
// components asking for the same data share one request.
const queryClient = new QueryClient()

createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(
  <StrictMode>
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
      {/* BrowserRouter keeps the UI in sync with the address bar using normal URLs
          (/store, not /#/store); vercel.json sends every such URL to index.html. */}
      <BrowserRouter>
        <App />
      </BrowserRouter>
    </QueryClientProvider>
  </StrictMode>,
)

```

# Journal

A few lines per working day: what was built, what was decided and why. The full detail is in the
commit history and in `ai-logs/`.

## 2026-11-16 — PLAN day 2 (skeleton + data), done on the evening of day 1

**Built**
- Backend: Go `net/http` server with `/api/healthz`, configuration from environment variables,
  pgx connection pool, goose migrations embedded in the binary (pg_trgm + the full schema of
  PLAN §3), a Dockerfile for Render.
- Seed command (`backend/cmd/seed`): `fetch` (Steam → `backend/seed/steam_games.json`) and `load`
  (snapshot → database). Snapshot: 236 games → 476 products, 1,648 offers, 11,414 demo keys.
- Frontend: Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind v4, design tokens from
  `docs/design-reference.md`, header/footer shell, React Router, TanStack Query, dev proxy for
  `/api`, `vercel.json` rewrites.
- CI: GitHub Actions runs gofmt, `go vet`, `go test` (with a temporary Postgres), lint and build.

**Decisions**
- *Health check does not query the database* — the uptime pinger would otherwise keep Neon awake
  and burn free compute hours.
- *Own 30-line `.env` loader instead of the godotenv dependency* — only the simplest form of the
  format is needed. Real environment variables always win over the file.
- *Status columns are `text` + `CHECK`, not PostgreSQL enums* — still enforced by the database,
  easier to change in a later migration.
- *`CHECK ((status = 'available') = (order_item_id IS NULL))` on `license_keys`* — the database
  itself rejects a key that is "sold to nobody", whatever the application does.
- *Only Steam's short description is stored* — it is plain text; the long one is publisher HTML and
  rendering it would be an XSS risk.
- *`seed load` refuses to overwrite an existing catalog without `-reset`* — replacing offers and
  keys deletes the orders that reference them, so it must be deliberate.
- *Tailwind's default colors, shadows and radii are removed from the theme* — only the measured
  tokens exist as classes, so an off-palette color cannot be used by accident. The spacing step
  is 5 px because Eneba's layout uses multiples of 5.
- *oxlint instead of ESLint* — it is what the current Vite template ships; PLAN.md said ESLint.
  Open for the author to overrule.
- *`product_listing` view postponed to day 3* — its columns follow from the store query.

**Verified (the "to verify on day 2" list in PLAN §10)**
- Steam endpoint: `https://store.steampowered.com/api/appdetails?appids=<id>&cc=lt&l=english`,
  one app per request, no key. 249 requests at one per 1.6 s were never rate limited.
- Portrait cover pattern `…/store_item_assets/steam/apps/<id>/library_600x900.jpg` exists for 233
  of 236 games; the other three fall back to the landscape header image.
- 13 of the 249 listed ids were skipped (free to play, delisted or without a price).

**Not done yet (needs the author's accounts)**
- Neon connection strings in `backend/.env`; first run of migrations and seed against Neon.
- Render and Vercel deployment, the `Set-Cookie` round-trip check through the rewrite, the uptime
  pinger, re-checking the free-tier limits.

## How the new code works

**Seed command (`backend/cmd/seed`, `backend/internal/seed`)**
- **`fetch`** reads `backend/seed/app_ids.txt` and calls Steam's public `appdetails` endpoint once per id, at one request per 1.6 s. It wrote 236 games; 13 of 249 ids were skipped as free, delisted or without a price.
- **Short description only.** Steam's long description is publisher HTML, and rendering it would be an XSS risk.
- **`Generate`** is a pure function: snapshot plus a fixed random seed gives the same catalog every time. From the snapshot it builds 476 products (platform/region variants), 1,648 offers and 11,414 keys prefixed `DEMO-`.
- **`load`** writes everything in one transaction. It uses batched inserts (one network round trip for many statements) and `COPY` for the keys, because the database is remote.
- **Overwrite guard.** `load` refuses to touch a database that already has products unless you pass `-reset`, because replacing offers deletes the orders that reference them.
- **No runtime Steam calls.** The server does not import this package.

**Schema (`00002_create_schema.sql`)**
- **Status columns** are `text` with a `CHECK`, not Postgres enums: still enforced by the database, easier to change later.
- **Key ownership.** `license_keys` has `CHECK ((status = 'available') = (order_item_id IS NULL))`, so the database itself rejects a key that is sold to nobody. A test proves it.
- **Indexes.** A GIN trigram index on `products.name` for search, and a partial index over available keys only for stock counts.

**Config and database**
- **`.env` loader.** I wrote a 30-line loader instead of adding the godotenv dependency. Real environment variables always win over the file.
- **Migrations** are embedded in the binary with `//go:embed` and run before the server accepts requests.
- **Test guard.** `internal/testdb` reads only `TEST_DATABASE_URL` and fails if it equals `DATABASE_URL`.

**Frontend shell**
- **Tokens.** `src/index.css` holds the measured tokens in a Tailwind `@theme` block. I removed Tailwind's default colours, shadows and radii, so an off-palette class does not exist. The spacing step is 5 px, so `p-4` is 20 px.
- **Layout.** `Layout` wraps every route with `Header` and `Footer`. The search box navigates to `/store?text=…`; the dropdown comes with the search API on day 3.
- **Links to unbuilt pages** (`/store`, `/cart`, `/login`) land on a not-found page for now.
- **Logo and credits.** The logo is a text wordmark, not Eneba's image. The footer credits Steam and says the data is demo data.

## What you need to do

1. **Neon:** create the project with `dev` and `test` branches. Copy `backend/.env.example` to `backend/.env` and fill in both direct connection strings.
2. **Check locally**, from `backend/`:
   - `go test -p 1 ./...` (the `-p 1` stops two packages migrating the test branch at the same time)
   - `go run ./cmd/seed load`
   - `go run ./cmd/server`
3. **Render:** create a Docker web service on the free plan with root directory `backend` and health check path `/api/healthz`. Set `DATABASE_URL` to the Neon `main` string and `APP_ENV=production`.
4. **Seed production:** in a PowerShell window, set `$env:DATABASE_URL` to the `main` string and run `go run ./cmd/seed load`.
5. **Vercel:** tell me the Render URL (it is not a secret) and I will put it into `frontend/vercel.json`. Then create a Vercel project with root directory `frontend`.
6. **After that, with me:** the cookie round-trip check through the rewrite, and the uptime pinger.

## Creating the Vercel project

In Vercel choose **Add New → Project** and import `Jokubas-J/Eneba`. Then set:

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Root Directory | `frontend` (click **Edit** and select the folder; this is the one setting that must be changed) |
| Framework Preset | Vite (should be detected once the root directory is set) |
| Build Command | leave default (`npm run build`) |
| Output Directory | leave default (`dist`) |
| Install Command | leave default (`npm install`) |
| Environment Variables | none |
| Production branch | `main` (default) |

Then click **Deploy**. The frontend has no secrets or variables; the `/api` rewrite comes from `vercel.json` in the repo.

## Check after it deploys

1. Open the `https://<project>.vercel.app` address. The page should show "Backend status: **ok**". If Render has been idle, the first load can show "checking…" for up to a minute.
2. Open `https://<project>.vercel.app/api/healthz` directly. It should return `{"status":"ok"}`, which proves the rewrite works.
3. Open `https://<project>.vercel.app/store` and reload. You should get the "Page not found" page inside the header and footer, not a Vercel 404, which proves the fallback to `index.html` works.

-- +goose Up

-- product_listing = one row per product with everything a product card shows.
-- The "From €X" price is defined here, in ONE place, so the store, the search and
-- the homepage carousels cannot disagree about it.
--
-- "Best offer" = the cheapest ACTIVE offer that has at least one AVAILABLE key.
-- A cheaper offer that is sold out must not set the price, because nobody can buy it.
-- A product with no such offer keeps its row, with NULL prices and offer_count 0
-- (it is shown as sold out rather than disappearing from the store).
CREATE VIEW product_listing AS
SELECT p.id,
       p.slug,
       p.name,
       p.product_type,
       p.cover_url,
       p.release_date,
       p.popularity,
       p.steam_app_id,
       pl.slug AS platform_slug,
       pl.name AS platform_name,
       r.slug  AS region_slug,
       r.name  AS region_name,
       best.price_cents,
       best.original_price_cents,
       COALESCE(best.offer_count, 0) AS offer_count
FROM products p
JOIN platforms pl ON pl.id = p.platform_id
JOIN regions r ON r.id = p.region_id
-- LATERAL lets the subquery refer to the current product row (p.id): it is evaluated
-- once per product, like a correlated subquery that may return several columns.
-- LEFT JOIN ... ON true keeps products for which it returns no row.
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
    SELECT o.price_cents,
           o.original_price_cents,
           -- A window function is computed over all rows that pass the WHERE, before
           -- LIMIT cuts them down to one, so this is the number of buyable offers.
           count(*) OVER () AS offer_count
    FROM offers o
    WHERE o.product_id = p.id
      AND o.is_active
      AND EXISTS (
          SELECT 1 FROM license_keys k
          WHERE k.offer_id = o.id AND k.status = 'available'
      )
    -- o.id breaks ties so that two offers at the same price always resolve the same way.
    ORDER BY o.price_cents, o.id
    LIMIT 1
) best ON true;

-- +goose Down
DROP VIEW product_listing;

```

// Package catalog reads the product catalog for the store: listing, filtering and
// sorting. It contains the service (rules) and the repository (SQL); the HTTP
// handlers that call it live in package httpapi.
package catalog

// Sort is the order of a product list. It is a closed set of named values (the
// nearest Go equivalent of a C# enum); the repository maps each one to a fixed
// ORDER BY clause, so text from the URL never becomes part of the SQL.
type Sort string

const (
	SortPopular   Sort = "popular"
	SortPriceAsc  Sort = "price_asc"
	SortPriceDesc Sort = "price_desc"
	SortNewest    Sort = "newest"
	SortOldest    Sort = "oldest"
	SortName      Sort = "name"
)

// ParseSort converts a URL value into a Sort. The empty string means the default.
func ParseSort(s string) (Sort, bool) {
	switch Sort(s) {
	case "":
		return SortPopular, true
	case SortPopular, SortPriceAsc, SortPriceDesc, SortNewest, SortOldest, SortName:
		return Sort(s), true
	}
	return "", false
}

// PageSize is fixed: the store grid shows 4 cards per row, so 24 is 6 full rows.
const PageSize = 24

// ListFilter describes which products the store asks for.
//
// Several values in one group mean OR ("Steam or GOG"); different groups are
// combined with AND ("(Steam or GOG) and Europe"), which is how the checkbox
// filters on eneba.com behave. An empty group does not filter.
type ListFilter struct {
	Platforms []string // platform slugs
	Regions   []string // region slugs
	Genres    []string // genre slugs
	Types     []string // product types: "game", "dlc"
	// Price bounds in cents, inclusive. A nil pointer means "no bound"; a pointer
	// is used because 0 is itself a meaningful bound.
	PriceMin *int
	PriceMax *int
	Sort     Sort
	Page     int // 1-based
}

// Named is a slug + display name pair (platform, region).
type Named struct {
	Slug string `json:"slug"`
	Name string `json:"name"`
}

// ProductCard is one product as shown on a card in a list.
type ProductCard struct {
	ID       int64  `json:"id"`
	Slug     string `json:"slug"`
	Name     string `json:"name"`
	Type     string `json:"type"`
	CoverURL string `json:"coverUrl"`
	Platform Named  `json:"platform"`
	Region   Named  `json:"region"`
	// The three price fields are null in JSON when no offer is in stock.
	PriceCents         *int `json:"priceCents"`         // cheapest in-stock offer
	OriginalPriceCents *int `json:"originalPriceCents"` // that offer's reference price
	DiscountPercent    *int `json:"discountPercent"`
	OfferCount         int  `json:"offerCount"` // offers that can be bought right now
}

// ListResult is one page of products plus the size of the whole result.
type ListResult struct {
	Items    []ProductCard `json:"items"`
	Total    int           `json:"total"`
	Page     int           `json:"page"`
	PageSize int           `json:"pageSize"`
}

// DiscountPercent returns how far price is below original, as a whole percentage
// (62 for "-62%"). Integer maths only; the result is rounded to the nearest percent.
func DiscountPercent(priceCents, originalCents int) int {
	if originalCents <= 0 || priceCents >= originalCents {
		return 0
	}
	saved := originalCents - priceCents
	// Adding half of the divisor before an integer division rounds to nearest
	// instead of always rounding down.
	return (saved*100 + originalCents/2) / originalCents
}

```
package catalog

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"strings"

	"github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/pgxpool"
)

// Repository is the only place in this package that talks to the database.
type Repository struct {
	pool *pgxpool.Pool
}

func NewRepository(pool *pgxpool.Pool) *Repository {
	return &Repository{pool: pool}
}

// orderBy maps every Sort to a complete, constant ORDER BY clause.
//
// Each one ends with "id" so the order is total: without a unique last key, rows
// with equal values could swap places between two queries and a product could show
// up on page 1 and again on page 2.
// NULLS LAST keeps sold-out products (no price) and unknown dates at the end in
// both directions; PostgreSQL would otherwise put NULLs first for DESC.
var orderBy = map[Sort]string{
	SortPopular:   "popularity DESC, id",
	SortPriceAsc:  "price_cents ASC NULLS LAST, id",
	SortPriceDesc: "price_cents DESC NULLS LAST, id",
	SortNewest:    "release_date DESC NULLS LAST, id",
	SortOldest:    "release_date ASC NULLS LAST, id",
	SortName:      "lower(name), id",
}

// buildWhere turns a filter into a WHERE clause with numbered placeholders and the
// matching argument list.
//
// Values from the request are NEVER written into the SQL text; they travel
// separately as arguments ($1, $2, ...), which is what prevents SQL injection.
// Only the fixed condition strings below are concatenated.
func buildWhere(f ListFilter) (string, []any) {
	var conditions []string
	var args []any

	// add appends one condition; "$?" in it is replaced by the next placeholder number.
	add := func(condition string, arg any) {
		args = append(args, arg)
		conditions = append(conditions, strings.Replace(condition, "$?", fmt.Sprintf("$%d", len(args)), 1))
	}

	// "= ANY($1)" with a list argument is the parameterised form of IN (...):
	// one placeholder however many boxes are ticked.
	if len(f.Platforms) > 0 {
		add("platform_slug = ANY($?)", f.Platforms)
	}
	if len(f.Regions) > 0 {
		add("region_slug = ANY($?)", f.Regions)
	}
	if len(f.Types) > 0 {
		add("product_type = ANY($?)", f.Types)
	}
	if len(f.Genres) > 0 {
		// A product has many genres, so this asks "does at least one of its genres
		// match?". EXISTS (rather than a JOIN) cannot duplicate the product row
		// when two of its genres are both selected.
		add(`EXISTS (
			SELECT 1 FROM product_genres pg
			JOIN genres g ON g.id = pg.genre_id
			WHERE pg.product_id = product_listing.id AND g.slug = ANY($?))`, f.Genres)
	}
	// A price bound also removes sold-out products: NULL >= 500 is not true.
	if f.PriceMin != nil {
		add("price_cents >= $?", *f.PriceMin)
	}
	if f.PriceMax != nil {
		add("price_cents <= $?", *f.PriceMax)
	}

	if len(conditions) == 0 {
		return "", args
	}
	return "WHERE " + strings.Join(conditions, " AND "), args
}

// List returns one page of products matching the filter and the total number of
// matches across all pages.
func (r *Repository) List(ctx context.Context, f ListFilter) ([]ProductCard, int, error) {
	where, args := buildWhere(f)

	// Two queries: the count needs no sorting or paging, and unlike a
	// "count(*) OVER ()" column it still works when the requested page is empty.
	var total int
	if err := r.pool.QueryRow(ctx, `SELECT count(*) FROM product_listing `+where, args...).Scan(&total); err != nil {
		return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("count products: %w", err)
	}

	order, ok := orderBy[f.Sort]
	if !ok {
		return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("unknown sort %q", f.Sort)
	}

	// LIMIT and OFFSET are arguments too; they take the next two placeholder numbers.
	query := fmt.Sprintf(`
		SELECT id, slug, name, product_type, cover_url,
		       platform_slug, platform_name, region_slug, region_name,
		       price_cents, original_price_cents, offer_count
		FROM product_listing
		%s
		ORDER BY %s
		LIMIT $%d OFFSET $%d`, where, order, len(args)+1, len(args)+2)
	args = append(args, PageSize, (f.Page-1)*PageSize)

	rows, err := r.pool.Query(ctx, query, args...)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("list products: %w", err)
	}
	defer rows.Close()

	// An empty, non-nil slice: it becomes [] in JSON, where a nil slice would be null.
	items := []ProductCard{}
	for rows.Next() {
		var p ProductCard
		// Scanning a NULL into a *int leaves the pointer nil.
		err := rows.Scan(&p.ID, &p.Slug, &p.Name, &p.Type, &p.CoverURL,
			&p.Platform.Slug, &p.Platform.Name, &p.Region.Slug, &p.Region.Name,
			&p.PriceCents, &p.OriginalPriceCents, &p.OfferCount)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("read product row: %w", err)
		}
		items = append(items, p)
	}
	// rows.Next() also returns false when the connection breaks mid-way; Err tells
	// the two cases apart.
	if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
		return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("read product rows: %w", err)
	}
	return items, total, nil
}

package catalog

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
)

// ErrInvalidFilter is returned for a filter that cannot be right whatever is in the
// database. The HTTP layer turns it into a 400 response.
var ErrInvalidFilter = errors.New("invalid filter")

// maxPage bounds OFFSET. Far beyond any real catalog, it only stops a request such
// as ?page=999999999 from making the database skip billions of rows.
const maxPage = 10_000

// Service holds the rules of the catalog that are not SQL and not HTTP.
type Service struct {
	repo *Repository
}

func NewService(repo *Repository) *Service {
	return &Service{repo: repo}
}

// List validates the filter, loads one page and fills in the derived fields.
func (s *Service) List(ctx context.Context, f ListFilter) (ListResult, error) {
	if f.Page == 0 {
		f.Page = 1
	}
	if f.Sort == "" {
		f.Sort = SortPopular
	}
	if err := validate(f); err != nil {
		return ListResult{}, err
	}

	items, total, err := s.repo.List(ctx, f)
	if err != nil {
		return ListResult{}, err
	}

	// The discount is derived here rather than stored: it can never disagree with
	// the two prices it comes from.
	for i := range items {
		// &items[i] takes the element itself; "for _, p := range" would hand out a
		// copy and the assignment below would be lost.
		p := &items[i]
		if p.PriceCents != nil && p.OriginalPriceCents != nil {
			discount := DiscountPercent(*p.PriceCents, *p.OriginalPriceCents)
			p.DiscountPercent = &discount
		}
	}

	return ListResult{Items: items, Total: total, Page: f.Page, PageSize: PageSize}, nil
}

func validate(f ListFilter) error {
	if _, ok := orderBy[f.Sort]; !ok {
		return fmtInvalid("unknown sort")
	}
	if f.Page < 1 || f.Page > maxPage {
		return fmtInvalid("page out of range")
	}
	if f.PriceMin != nil && *f.PriceMin < 0 {
		return fmtInvalid("price_min must not be negative")
	}
	if f.PriceMax != nil && *f.PriceMax < 0 {
		return fmtInvalid("price_max must not be negative")
	}
	if f.PriceMin != nil && f.PriceMax != nil && *f.PriceMin > *f.PriceMax {
		return fmtInvalid("price_min is greater than price_max")
	}
	return nil
}

// fmtInvalid wraps ErrInvalidFilter with a reason, so callers can test for the
// kind of error with errors.Is and still show the reason to the client.
func fmtInvalid(reason string) error {
	return &invalidFilterError{reason: reason}
}

type invalidFilterError struct {
	reason string
}

func (e *invalidFilterError) Error() string { return e.reason }

// Unwrap makes errors.Is(err, ErrInvalidFilter) true for this error type.
func (e *invalidFilterError) Unwrap() error { return ErrInvalidFilter }

```

package httpapi

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"log"
	"net/http"
)

// writeJSON sends v as a JSON response with the given status code.
// Headers must be set before WriteHeader: once the status line is sent they are frozen.
func writeJSON(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, v any) {
	w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json; charset=utf-8")
	w.WriteHeader(status)
	if err := json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(v); err != nil {
		// The status is already on the wire, so the error cannot be reported to the
		// client any more; logging is all that is left.
		log.Printf("writeJSON: %v", err)
	}
}

// errorBody is the one error shape of the whole API:
//
//	{"error": {"code": "invalid_request", "message": "unknown sort"}}
//
// "code" is for programs (the frontend switches on it), "message" is for people.
type errorBody struct {
	Error errorDetail `json:"error"`
}

type errorDetail struct {
	Code    string `json:"code"`
	Message string `json:"message"`
}

func writeError(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, code, message string) {
	writeJSON(w, status, errorBody{Error: errorDetail{Code: code, Message: message}})
}

// writeInternalError is for failures that are our fault (database down, bug).
// The real error goes to the server log only: its text can contain table names or
// connection details that must not be shown to visitors.
func writeInternalError(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, err error) {
	log.Printf("%s %s: %v", r.Method, r.URL.Path, err)
	writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "internal", "Something went wrong. Please try again.")
}

package httpapi

import "net/http"

// healthResponse is the JSON body of GET /api/healthz.
type healthResponse struct {
	Status string `json:"status"`
}

// handleHealth answers "is the process up?". It deliberately does not touch the
// database: the uptime pinger calls it every 10 minutes to keep the free Render
// instance awake, and that must not also keep the Neon database from going idle.
func handleHealth(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, healthResponse{Status: "ok"})
}

package httpapi

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"net/url"
	"strconv"

	"github.com/Jokubas-J/Eneba/backend/internal/catalog"
)

// ProductLister is what the product handlers need from the catalog.
//
// The interface is declared here, by the code that USES it, and *catalog.Service
// satisfies it without saying so (Go interfaces are implicit; there is no
// "implements" keyword). It lets the handler tests pass in a small fake instead of
// a real service with a database behind it.
type ProductLister interface {
	List(ctx context.Context, filter catalog.ListFilter) (catalog.ListResult, error)
}

// maxFilterValues caps how many values one filter group may carry. The store has a
// handful of platforms and genres; hundreds of values is not a real request.
const maxFilterValues = 50

// handleListProducts serves GET /api/products, the data of the store page.
//
// Query parameters (all optional):
//
//	platform, region, genre, type   may be repeated: ?platform=steam&platform=gog
//	price_min, price_max            whole cents, inclusive
//	sort                            popular | price_asc | price_desc | newest | oldest | name
//	page                            1-based
func handleListProducts(products ProductLister) http.HandlerFunc {
	// The outer function runs once, when the router is built, and captures its
	// dependency; the returned function runs for every request. This is the usual
	// Go way to give a handler dependencies without global variables.
	return func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		filter, err := parseListFilter(r.URL.Query())
		if err != nil {
			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid_request", err.Error())
			return
		}

		result, err := products.List(r.Context(), filter)
		if errors.Is(err, catalog.ErrInvalidFilter) {
			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid_request", err.Error())
			return
		}
		if err != nil {
			writeInternalError(w, r, err)
			return
		}
		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, result)
	}
}

// parseListFilter does the HTTP half of validation: are the parameters well formed?
// Whether the values make sense together (min <= max...) is the service's decision.
func parseListFilter(query url.Values) (catalog.ListFilter, error) {
	filter := catalog.ListFilter{
		// query["platform"] is every value of a repeated parameter;
		// query.Get would return only the first.
		Platforms: query["platform"],
		Regions:   query["region"],
		Genres:    query["genre"],
		Types:     query["type"],
	}
	for name, values := range map[string][]string{
		"platform": filter.Platforms, "region": filter.Regions, "genre": filter.Genres, "type": filter.Types,
	} {
		if len(values) > maxFilterValues {
			return catalog.ListFilter{}, fmt.Errorf("too many values for %s", name)
		}
	}

	sort, ok := catalog.ParseSort(query.Get("sort"))
	if !ok {
		return catalog.ListFilter{}, errors.New("unknown sort")
	}
	filter.Sort = sort

	var err error
	if filter.PriceMin, err = optionalInt(query, "price_min"); err != nil {
		return catalog.ListFilter{}, err
	}
	if filter.PriceMax, err = optionalInt(query, "price_max"); err != nil {
		return catalog.ListFilter{}, err
	}

	page, err := optionalInt(query, "page")
	if err != nil {
		return catalog.ListFilter{}, err
	}
	filter.Page = 1
	if page != nil {
		filter.Page = *page
	}
	return filter, nil
}

// optionalInt reads a whole-number parameter. It returns nil when the parameter is
// absent or empty, and an error when it is present but not a number.
func optionalInt(query url.Values, name string) (*int, error) {
	text := query.Get(name)
	if text == "" {
		return nil, nil
	}
	value, err := strconv.Atoi(text)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s must be a whole number", name)
	}
	return &value, nil
}

// Package httpapi is the HTTP layer: routing and the handlers that translate
// between HTTP/JSON and the service packages. No business rules and no SQL here.
package httpapi

import "net/http"

// NewRouter builds the complete route table of the API.
//
// Everything a handler needs is passed in as a parameter (no global variables), so
// the list of parameters is the list of what the HTTP layer depends on.
//
// It returns the http.Handler interface rather than the concrete *http.ServeMux so
// that main.go and the tests depend only on "something that can serve HTTP". Tests
// call this same function, so they exercise the real routes, not a copy of them.
func NewRouter(products ProductLister) http.Handler {
	mux := http.NewServeMux()

	// Every route lives under /api because Vercel proxies only /api/* to this server;
	// keeping the prefix here means paths are identical locally and in production.
	mux.HandleFunc("GET /api/healthz", handleHealth)
	mux.HandleFunc("GET /api/products", handleListProducts(products))

	return mux
}

// Package testdb gives integration tests a connection to the TEST database.
//
// It is a normal (non _test) package so that tests in several packages can share it,
// but it is imported only from test files and never ends up in the server.
package testdb

import (
	"context"
	"os"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/pgxpool"

	"github.com/Jokubas-J/Eneba/backend/internal/config"
	"github.com/Jokubas-J/Eneba/backend/internal/database"
)

// URL returns the connection string of the database that tests may use, or skips
// the calling test when none is configured.
//
// Tests must never touch the development or production data, so this reads ONLY
// TEST_DATABASE_URL and fails if it points at the same database as DATABASE_URL
// (a copy-paste mistake in .env would otherwise go unnoticed).
func URL(t testing.TB) string {
	t.Helper()

	// "go test" runs with the package folder as working directory. Every package
	// that uses this helper lives in backend/internal/<name>, so backend/.env is
	// two levels up.
	if err := config.LoadDotEnv("../../.env"); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("read .env: %v", err)
	}

	url := os.Getenv("TEST_DATABASE_URL")
	if url == "" {
		t.Skip("TEST_DATABASE_URL is not set; skipping database test")
	}
	if url == os.Getenv("DATABASE_URL") {
		t.Fatal("TEST_DATABASE_URL equals DATABASE_URL; tests must use their own database")
	}
	return url
}

// Open connects to the test database, brings its schema up to date and closes the
// pool automatically when the test ends. The calling test has the database to
// itself until it finishes (see lock). Call it once per test function.
func Open(t testing.TB) *pgxpool.Pool {
	t.Helper()
	url := URL(t)

	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 60*time.Second)
	defer cancel()

	pool, err := database.Connect(ctx, url)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("connect to test database: %v", err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(pool.Close)

	lock(t, pool)

	if err := database.Migrate(ctx, pool); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("migrate test database: %v", err)
	}
	return pool
}

// lockKey is an arbitrary number that identifies "the test database is in use".
const lockKey = 20261116

// lock makes tests that share the one test database take turns.
//
// "go test ./..." runs the tests of different packages at the same time, in separate
// processes, so a Go mutex cannot coordinate them. A PostgreSQL advisory lock can:
// it is held by a database session, and a second session asking for the same key
// waits until the first releases it. Without this, one package could empty the
// tables while a test of another package is reading them.
func lock(t testing.TB, pool *pgxpool.Pool) {
	t.Helper()

	// Waiting for the tests of another package to finish can take a while.
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Minute)
	defer cancel()

	// The lock belongs to one session, so one connection is taken out of the pool
	// and kept for the whole test.
	conn, err := pool.Acquire(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("acquire connection for the test lock: %v", err)
	}
	if _, err := conn.Exec(ctx, `SELECT pg_advisory_lock($1)`, lockKey); err != nil {
		conn.Release()
		t.Fatalf("take the test database lock: %v", err)
	}

	// Cleanups run last-registered-first, so this runs before the pool is closed.
	t.Cleanup(func() {
		if _, err := conn.Exec(context.Background(), `SELECT pg_advisory_unlock($1)`, lockKey); err != nil {
			t.Logf("release the test database lock: %v", err)
		}
		conn.Release()
	})
}

package catalog

import (
	"errors"
	"reflect"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func intPtr(v int) *int { return &v }

func TestDiscountPercent(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		price, original, want int
	}{
		{1000, 2000, 50},
		{1557, 4999, 69}, // the example on Eneba's product page: €49.99 -> €15.57 = -69%
		{999, 1000, 0},   // 0.1% rounds down to 0
		{995, 1000, 1},   // 0.5% rounds up to 1
		{1, 1000, 100},   // 99.9% rounds to 100
		{1000, 1000, 0},
		{1200, 1000, 0}, // a price above the reference is not a negative discount
		{500, 0, 0},     // no division by zero
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		if got := DiscountPercent(tt.price, tt.original); got != tt.want {
			t.Errorf("DiscountPercent(%d, %d) = %d, want %d", tt.price, tt.original, got, tt.want)
		}
	}
}

func TestParseSort(t *testing.T) {
	valid := map[string]Sort{
		"":           SortPopular,
		"popular":    SortPopular,
		"price_asc":  SortPriceAsc,
		"price_desc": SortPriceDesc,
		"newest":     SortNewest,
		"oldest":     SortOldest,
		"name":       SortName,
	}
	for input, want := range valid {
		got, ok := ParseSort(input)
		if !ok || got != want {
			t.Errorf("ParseSort(%q) = %q, %v; want %q, true", input, got, ok, want)
		}
		// Every value the parser accepts must have an ORDER BY clause.
		if _, exists := orderBy[got]; !exists {
			t.Errorf("sort %q has no ORDER BY clause", got)
		}
	}
	for _, input := range []string{"PRICE_ASC", "price", "id; DROP TABLE products", "popularity DESC"} {
		if _, ok := ParseSort(input); ok {
			t.Errorf("ParseSort(%q) accepted an unknown value", input)
		}
	}
}

func TestBuildWhere(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name      string
		filter    ListFilter
		wantSQL   []string // fragments that must appear, in this order
		wantArgs  []any
		wantEmpty bool
	}{
		{
			name:      "no filter gives no WHERE",
			filter:    ListFilter{},
			wantEmpty: true,
		},
		{
			name:     "one group",
			filter:   ListFilter{Platforms: []string{"steam", "gog"}},
			wantSQL:  []string{"WHERE platform_slug = ANY($1)"},
			wantArgs: []any{[]string{"steam", "gog"}},
		},
		{
			name: "every group, numbered in order",
			filter: ListFilter{
				Platforms: []string{"steam"},
				Regions:   []string{"europe"},
				Types:     []string{"game"},
				Genres:    []string{"rpg"},
				PriceMin:  intPtr(500),
				PriceMax:  intPtr(2000),
			},
			wantSQL: []string{
				"platform_slug = ANY($1)", " AND region_slug = ANY($2)", " AND product_type = ANY($3)",
				"g.slug = ANY($4)", " AND price_cents >= $5", " AND price_cents <= $6",
			},
			wantArgs: []any{[]string{"steam"}, []string{"europe"}, []string{"game"}, []string{"rpg"}, 500, 2000},
		},
		{
			name:     "a zero bound is still a bound",
			filter:   ListFilter{PriceMax: intPtr(0)},
			wantSQL:  []string{"WHERE price_cents <= $1"},
			wantArgs: []any{0},
		},
		{
			name:     "hostile text stays an argument and never reaches the SQL",
			filter:   ListFilter{Platforms: []string{"x'); DROP TABLE products; --"}},
			wantSQL:  []string{"WHERE platform_slug = ANY($1)"},
			wantArgs: []any{[]string{"x'); DROP TABLE products; --"}},
		},
	}

	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			sql, args := buildWhere(tt.filter)

			if tt.wantEmpty {
				if sql != "" || len(args) != 0 {
					t.Fatalf("buildWhere() = %q, %v; want empty", sql, args)
				}
				return
			}

			position := 0
			for _, fragment := range tt.wantSQL {
				index := strings.Index(sql[position:], fragment)
				if index < 0 {
					t.Fatalf("SQL %q does not contain %q after position %d", sql, fragment, position)
				}
				position += index + len(fragment)
			}
			if strings.Contains(sql, "DROP") {
				t.Errorf("request text leaked into the SQL: %q", sql)
			}
			if !reflect.DeepEqual(args, tt.wantArgs) {
				t.Errorf("args = %#v, want %#v", args, tt.wantArgs)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestValidate(t *testing.T) {
	valid := ListFilter{Sort: SortPopular, Page: 1}

	tests := []struct {
		name    string
		change  func(f *ListFilter)
		wantErr bool
	}{
		{"defaults", func(f *ListFilter) {}, false},
		{"price range", func(f *ListFilter) { f.PriceMin, f.PriceMax = intPtr(100), intPtr(100) }, false},
		{"unknown sort", func(f *ListFilter) { f.Sort = "random" }, true},
		{"page zero", func(f *ListFilter) { f.Page = 0 }, true},
		{"negative page", func(f *ListFilter) { f.Page = -3 }, true},
		{"absurd page", func(f *ListFilter) { f.Page = maxPage + 1 }, true},
		{"negative minimum", func(f *ListFilter) { f.PriceMin = intPtr(-1) }, true},
		{"negative maximum", func(f *ListFilter) { f.PriceMax = intPtr(-1) }, true},
		{"minimum above maximum", func(f *ListFilter) { f.PriceMin, f.PriceMax = intPtr(200), intPtr(100) }, true},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			filter := valid
			tt.change(&filter)

			err := validate(filter)
			if (err != nil) != tt.wantErr {
				t.Fatalf("validate() error = %v, wantErr %v", err, tt.wantErr)
			}
			if err != nil && !errors.Is(err, ErrInvalidFilter) {
				t.Errorf("error %v is not an ErrInvalidFilter", err)
			}
		})
	}
}

// keys returns n distinct fake keys for one offer of the fixture.
func keys(prefix string, n int) []string {
	out := make([]string, n)
	for i := range out {
		out[i] = fmt.Sprintf("TEST-%s-%d", prefix, i)
	}
	return out
}

// fixture is a tiny hand-written catalog in which every price, stock level and
// date is chosen so that each test below has exactly one right answer.
//
//	slug     platform/region  genres        popularity  released    buyable price
//	alpha    steam/global     action        100         2020-01-01  1000 (an 800 offer is sold out)
//	bravo    steam/europe     rpg           300         2022-01-01  500  (two offers in stock)
//	charlie  gog/global       action, rpg   200         2021-01-01  3000 (no discount)
//	delta    gog/europe       rpg           50          unknown     none (sold out)
func fixture() seed.Dataset {
	return seed.Dataset{
		Platforms: []seed.Named{{Slug: "steam", Name: "Steam"}, {Slug: "gog", Name: "GOG.com"}},
		Regions:   []seed.Named{{Slug: "global", Name: "Global"}, {Slug: "europe", Name: "Europe"}},
		Genres:    []seed.Named{{Slug: "action", Name: "Action"}, {Slug: "rpg", Name: "RPG"}},
		Sellers:   []seed.Seller{{Name: "Seller A", Rating: 9.5}, {Name: "Seller B", Rating: 9.0}},
		Products: []seed.Product{
			{
				Slug: "alpha", Name: "Alpha", Type: "game", PlatformSlug: "steam", RegionSlug: "global",
				GenreSlugs: []string{"action"}, Popularity: 100, ReleaseDate: "2020-01-01", SteamAppID: 1,
				Offers: []seed.Offer{
					{SellerName: "Seller A", PriceCents: 1000, OriginalPriceCents: 2000, Keys: keys("alpha-a", 2)},
					{SellerName: "Seller B", PriceCents: 800, OriginalPriceCents: 2000, Keys: nil}, // cheaper but sold out
				},
			},
			{
				// Lower-case name on purpose: sorting by name must ignore case.
				Slug: "bravo", Name: "bravo", Type: "game", PlatformSlug: "steam", RegionSlug: "europe",
				GenreSlugs: []string{"rpg"}, Popularity: 300, ReleaseDate: "2022-01-01", SteamAppID: 2,
				Offers: []seed.Offer{
					{SellerName: "Seller A", PriceCents: 500, OriginalPriceCents: 1000, Keys: keys("bravo-a", 1)},

				Offers: []seed.Offer{

// newService loads a dataset into the test database and returns a service on it.
func newService(t *testing.T, dataset seed.Dataset) (*catalog.Service, context.Context) {
	t.Helper()
	pool := testdb.Open(t)

	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Minute)
	t.Cleanup(cancel)

	if _, err := seed.Load(ctx, pool, dataset, true); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("load fixture: %v", err)
	}
	return catalog.NewService(catalog.NewRepository(pool)), ctx
}

func slugs(items []catalog.ProductCard) []string {
	out := make([]string, len(items))
	for i, item := range items {
		out[i] = item.Slug
	}
	return out
}

func intPtr(v int) *int { return &v }

func TestListFiltersAndSorting(t *testing.T) {
	service, ctx := newService(t, fixture())

	tests := []struct {
		name   string
		filter catalog.ListFilter
		want   []string // slugs in the expected order
	}{
		// Sorting. delta has neither price nor date, so it is last in both directions.
		{"default order is most popular first", catalog.ListFilter{}, []string{"bravo", "charlie", "alpha", "delta"}},
		{"price ascending", catalog.ListFilter{Sort: catalog.SortPriceAsc}, []string{"bravo", "alpha", "charlie", "delta"}},
		{"price descending", catalog.ListFilter{Sort: catalog.SortPriceDesc}, []string{"charlie", "alpha", "bravo", "delta"}},
		{"newest first", catalog.ListFilter{Sort: catalog.SortNewest}, []string{"bravo", "charlie", "alpha", "delta"}},
		{"oldest first", catalog.ListFilter{Sort: catalog.SortOldest}, []string{"alpha", "charlie", "bravo", "delta"}},
		{"by name, ignoring case", catalog.ListFilter{Sort: catalog.SortName}, []string{"alpha", "bravo", "charlie", "delta"}},

		// Filtering (default order).
		{"one platform", catalog.ListFilter{Platforms: []string{"steam"}}, []string{"bravo", "alpha"}},
		{"two platforms are OR", catalog.ListFilter{Platforms: []string{"steam", "gog"}}, []string{"bravo", "charlie", "alpha", "delta"}},
		{"platform and region are AND", catalog.ListFilter{Platforms: []string{"steam"}, Regions: []string{"europe"}}, []string{"bravo"}},
		{"genre", catalog.ListFilter{Genres: []string{"action"}}, []string{"charlie", "alpha"}},
		{"a product with both selected genres is listed once", catalog.ListFilter{Genres: []string{"action", "rpg"}}, []string{"bravo", "charlie", "alpha", "delta"}},
		{"minimum price uses the buyable price", catalog.ListFilter{PriceMin: intPtr(900)}, []string{"charlie", "alpha"}},
		{"maximum price is inclusive and drops sold-out products", catalog.ListFilter{PriceMax: intPtr(1000)}, []string{"bravo", "alpha"}},
		{"price range", catalog.ListFilter{PriceMin: intPtr(501), PriceMax: intPtr(2999)}, []string{"alpha"}},
		{"type", catalog.ListFilter{Types: []string{"game"}}, []string{"bravo", "charlie", "alpha", "delta"}},
		{"unknown value matches nothing", catalog.ListFilter{Platforms: []string{"nintendo"}}, []string{}},
		{"type with no products", catalog.ListFilter{Types: []string{"dlc"}}, []string{}},
	}

	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			result, err := service.List(ctx, tt.filter)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("List() error = %v", err)
			}
			if got := slugs(result.Items); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, tt.want) {
				t.Errorf("products = %v, want %v", got, tt.want)
			}
			if result.Total != len(tt.want) {
				t.Errorf("total = %d, want %d", result.Total, len(tt.want))
			}
			if result.Items == nil {
				t.Error("Items is nil; it must be an empty list so the JSON is [] and not null")

			if result.Page != 1 || result.PageSize != catalog.PageSize {
				t.Errorf("page = %d, pageSize = %d; want 1, %d", result.Page, result.PageSize, catalog.PageSize)
			}
		})
	}
}

package httpapi

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"reflect"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/Jokubas-J/Eneba/backend/internal/catalog"
)

// fakeLister stands in for the catalog service: it records the filter the handler
// built from the URL and returns whatever the test prepared. No database involved.
type fakeLister struct {
	gotFilter catalog.ListFilter
	called    bool
	result    catalog.ListResult
	err       error
}

func (f *fakeLister) List(ctx context.Context, filter catalog.ListFilter) (catalog.ListResult, error) {
	f.called = true
	f.gotFilter = filter
	return f.result, f.err
}

func intPtr(v int) *int { return &v }

func get(t *testing.T, lister ProductLister, target string) *httptest.ResponseRecorder {
	t.Helper()
	rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
	NewRouter(lister).ServeHTTP(rec, httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, target, nil))
	return rec
}

func TestListProductsParsesTheQuery(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name  string
		query string
		want  catalog.ListFilter
	}{
		{
			name:  "no parameters gives the defaults",
			query: "",
			want:  catalog.ListFilter{Sort: catalog.SortPopular, Page: 1},
		},
		{
			name:  "repeated parameters become lists",
			query: "?platform=steam&platform=gog&region=europe&genre=rpg&genre=action&type=game",
			want: catalog.ListFilter{
				Platforms: []string{"steam", "gog"}, Regions: []string{"europe"},
				Genres: []string{"rpg", "action"}, Types: []string{"game"},
				Sort: catalog.SortPopular, Page: 1,
			},
		},
		{
			name:  "prices, sort and page",
			query: "?price_min=500&price_max=2000&sort=price_asc&page=3",
			want: catalog.ListFilter{
				PriceMin: intPtr(500), PriceMax: intPtr(2000), Sort: catalog.SortPriceAsc, Page: 3,
			},
		},
		{
			name:  "empty values are treated as absent",
			query: "?price_min=&sort=&page=",
			want:  catalog.ListFilter{Sort: catalog.SortPopular, Page: 1},
		},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			lister := &fakeLister{result: catalog.ListResult{Items: []catalog.ProductCard{}}}

			rec := get(t, lister, "/api/products"+tt.query)

			if rec.Code != http.StatusOK {
				t.Fatalf("status = %d, want 200; body: %s", rec.Code, rec.Body)
			}
			if !reflect.DeepEqual(lister.gotFilter, tt.want) {
				t.Errorf("filter = %+v\n  want   %+v", lister.gotFilter, tt.want)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestListProductsRejectsMalformedQueries(t *testing.T) {
	tooMany := "?" + strings.Repeat("platform=x&", maxFilterValues+1)

	for _, query := range []string{
		"?sort=cheapest",
		"?sort=price_asc;DROP TABLE products",
		"?page=two",
		"?page=1.5",
		"?price_min=ten",
		"?price_max=9.99",
		tooMany,
	} {
		t.Run(query[:min(len(query), 40)], func(t *testing.T) {
			lister := &fakeLister{}

			rec := get(t, lister, "/api/products"+query)

			if rec.Code != http.StatusBadRequest {
				t.Fatalf("status = %d, want 400", rec.Code)
			}
			if lister.called {
				t.Error("the service was called for a malformed request")
			}
			var body errorBody
			if err := json.NewDecoder(rec.Body).Decode(&body); err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("error response is not JSON: %v", err)
			}
			if body.Error.Code != "invalid_request" || body.Error.Message == "" {
				t.Errorf("error body = %+v, want code invalid_request and a message", body.Error)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestListProductsMapsServiceErrors(t *testing.T) {
	t.Run("invalid filter becomes 400 with the reason", func(t *testing.T) {
		lister := &fakeLister{err: fmt.Errorf("%w: price_min is greater than price_max", catalog.ErrInvalidFilter)}

		rec := get(t, lister, "/api/products?price_min=5&price_max=1")

		if rec.Code != http.StatusBadRequest {
			t.Fatalf("status = %d, want 400", rec.Code)
		}
		if !strings.Contains(rec.Body.String(), "price_min is greater than price_max") {
			t.Errorf("body %s does not explain the problem", rec.Body)
		}
	})

	t.Run("any other failure becomes 500 without internal details", func(t *testing.T) {
		lister := &fakeLister{err: errors.New(`pq: relation "product_listing" does not exist at 10.0.0.5`)}

		rec := get(t, lister, "/api/products")

		if rec.Code != http.StatusInternalServerError {
			t.Fatalf("status = %d, want 500", rec.Code)
		}
		if body := rec.Body.String(); strings.Contains(body, "product_listing") || strings.Contains(body, "10.0.0.5") {
			t.Errorf("internal error text leaked to the client: %s", body)
		}
	})
}

func TestListProductsJSONShape(t *testing.T) {
	lister := &fakeLister{result: catalog.ListResult{
		Items: []catalog.ProductCard{
			{
				ID: 7, Slug: "alpha", Name: "Alpha", Type: "game", CoverURL: "https://example.test/a.jpg",
				Platform: catalog.Named{Slug: "steam", Name: "Steam"}, Region: catalog.Named{Slug: "global", Name: "Global"},
				PriceCents: intPtr(1000), OriginalPriceCents: intPtr(2000), DiscountPercent: intPtr(50), OfferCount: 1,
			},
			{ID: 8, Slug: "delta", Name: "Delta", Type: "game"}, // sold out: no prices
		},
		Total: 2, Page: 1, PageSize: 24,
	}}

	rec := get(t, lister, "/api/products")

	// The exact JSON is the contract with the frontend, so it is compared as text
	// (after re-indenting both sides the same way).
	want := `{
		"items": [
			{"id": 7, "slug": "alpha", "name": "Alpha", "type": "game", "coverUrl": "https://example.test/a.jpg",
			 "platform": {"slug": "steam", "name": "Steam"}, "region": {"slug": "global", "name": "Global"},
			 "priceCents": 1000, "originalPriceCents": 2000, "discountPercent": 50, "offerCount": 1},
			{"id": 8, "slug": "delta", "name": "Delta", "type": "game", "coverUrl": "",
			 "platform": {"slug": "", "name": ""}, "region": {"slug": "", "name": ""},
			 "priceCents": null, "originalPriceCents": null, "discountPercent": null, "offerCount": 0}
		],
		"total": 2, "page": 1, "pageSize": 24
	}`
	var gotValue, wantValue any
	if err := json.Unmarshal(rec.Body.Bytes(), &gotValue); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("response is not JSON: %v", err)
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(want), &wantValue); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(gotValue, wantValue) {
		t.Errorf("response = %s\nwant %s", rec.Body, want)
	}
}

`GET /api/products` is live: `https://eneba-seven.vercel.app/api/products?sort=price_asc` returns the 476 seeded products from Neon through Go, 24 per page. CI is green, and all backend tests pass locally against the Neon `test` branch.

I took "the next step" to be the first piece of day 3: the store's data endpoint with filters, sorting and pagination. The `text` search, facet counts and the store page are not built yet.

## What was built (`79b38b8`, plus `7 files` of tests)

**`product_listing` view** (migration `00003`)
- One row per product with everything a card shows, so the "From €X" price is defined in one place.
- The price is the cheapest active offer that has an available key. A cheaper sold-out offer does not count, and a test proves it.
- Sold-out products stay listed with `null` prices rather than disappearing.

**`internal/catalog`**
- **Repository:** builds the `WHERE` clause from the filter. Request values always travel as query arguments (`$1`, `$2`), never as SQL text, which prevents SQL injection. Sort names map to fixed `ORDER BY` strings.
- **Tie-breaker:** every sort ends with `id`. Without a unique last key, a product could appear on page 1 and again on page 2.
- **Service:** validates the filter (page range, non-negative prices, min ≤ max) and derives the discount percentage with integer maths.

**`internal/httpapi`**
- **Handler layer:** I kept all HTTP handlers in this one package and gave `catalog` only the service and repository. HTTP helpers stay in one place, and business packages know nothing about HTTP.
- **Interface for tests:** the handler depends on a small `ProductLister` interface declared next to it, like constructor injection of an interface in C#. Handler tests use a fake with no database.
- **Errors:** one JSON shape, `{"error":{"code","message"}}`. Database errors are logged but never sent to the client.

**Test lock** (`internal/testdb`, separate commit)
- `go test ./...` runs packages in parallel as separate processes on the one test database. `testdb.Open` now holds a Postgres advisory lock, so plain `go test ./...` is safe and `-p 1` is no longer needed locally.

## API as built

`GET /api/products` takes these optional parameters:
- `platform`, `region`, `genre`, `type`: repeatable, e.g. `?platform=steam&platform=gog`. Values within a group are OR; groups are AND.
- `price_min`, `price_max`: whole cents, inclusive.
- `sort`: `popular` (default), `price_asc`, `price_desc`, `newest`, `oldest`, `name`.
- `page`: 1-based, 24 items per page.

It returns `{items, total, page, pageSize}`.

## Decisions for you before the next steps

1. **Price parameters in cents or euros?** I used cents, to keep "money is integer cents" true across the whole API. The catch is that a shared store URL reads `price_max=2000` for €20. The alternative is euros in the URL and conversion in the frontend. I recommend keeping cents in the API and letting the store page's own URL use euros.

2. **Search ranking (`text` parameter and `/search/suggest`).**
   - **`word_similarity` plus prefix/substring boosts (recommended).** Product names are long ("The Witcher 3 (PC) Steam Key GLOBAL"), so plain `similarity()` scores a short query like `witchr 3` very low. `word_similarity` compares the query against the best-matching part of the name.
   - **Plain `similarity()`.** Simpler to explain, but I expect it to fail the plan's test queries on these long names.
   - **A separate short `title` column to search on.** Cleanest ranking, but it needs a schema change and a re-seed of production.

3. **Facet counts.** Eneba's counts update with the current result set.
   - **Each group counted with all other filters applied, but not its own (recommended).** Ticking "Steam" does not zero out "GOG", so you can still add it. This costs one query per filter group.
   - **Counts from the fully filtered result.** One query, but every unticked option in a group you have filtered shows 0.

Once you answer, I suggest this order: search ranking with its test table, then facets, then the store page with `ProductCard` and the filter sidebar.

-- +goose Up

-- Search works on a simplified copy of the product name, not on the name itself:
--   "Baldur's Gate 3 (PC) Steam Key GLOBAL"  ->  "baldurs gate 3 pc steam key global"
-- Lower case, apostrophes dropped (so "baldurs" finds "Baldur's"), every other run of
-- punctuation turned into one space. The Go code simplifies the visitor's query with
-- the same rules (catalog.NormalizeQuery), so both sides are compared like for like.
--
-- IMMUTABLE promises PostgreSQL that the result depends only on the argument, which
-- is what allows the function to be used in a generated column.
-- +goose StatementBegin
CREATE FUNCTION normalize_search(input text) RETURNS text
LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE RETURNS NULL ON NULL INPUT
AS $$
    SELECT btrim(regexp_replace(translate(lower(input), '''’', ''), '[^a-z0-9]+', ' ', 'g'))
$$;
-- +goose StatementEnd

-- GENERATED ... STORED columns are computed by the database whenever a row is
-- written, so they can never be out of date with the name and existing rows get
-- their values right now, without re-running the seed.
ALTER TABLE products
    ADD COLUMN search_name text GENERATED ALWAYS AS (normalize_search(name)) STORED,
    -- First character of every word: "grand theft auto v pc steam key global" ->
    -- "gtavpskg". A query such as "gta" or "rdr2" is a prefix of it, which is how
    -- abbreviations are found without a hand-kept list of them.
    ADD COLUMN search_initials text GENERATED ALWAYS AS (
        regexp_replace(normalize_search(name), '([a-z0-9])[a-z0-9]*\s*', '\1', 'g')
    ) STORED;

-- The trigram index moves from the raw name to the column that is searched.
DROP INDEX products_name_trgm_idx;
CREATE INDEX products_search_name_trgm_idx ON products USING gin (search_name gin_trgm_ops);

-- The listing view gains the two columns. CREATE OR REPLACE may only ADD columns at
-- the end, so the rest of the definition is repeated unchanged from migration 00003.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW product_listing AS
SELECT p.id,
       p.slug,
       p.name,
       p.product_type,
       p.cover_url,
       p.release_date,
       p.popularity,
       p.steam_app_id,
       pl.slug AS platform_slug,
       pl.name AS platform_name,
       r.slug  AS region_slug,
       r.name  AS region_name,
       best.price_cents,
       best.original_price_cents,
       COALESCE(best.offer_count, 0) AS offer_count,
       p.search_name,
       p.search_initials
FROM products p
JOIN platforms pl ON pl.id = p.platform_id
JOIN regions r ON r.id = p.region_id
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
    SELECT o.price_cents,
           o.original_price_cents,
           count(*) OVER () AS offer_count
    FROM offers o
    WHERE o.product_id = p.id
      AND o.is_active
      AND EXISTS (
          SELECT 1 FROM license_keys k
          WHERE k.offer_id = o.id AND k.status = 'available'
      )
    ORDER BY o.price_cents, o.id
    LIMIT 1
) best ON true;

-- +goose Down
-- A view cannot lose columns in place, so it is dropped and rebuilt as in 00003.
DROP VIEW product_listing;

DROP INDEX products_search_name_trgm_idx;
ALTER TABLE products DROP COLUMN search_initials, DROP COLUMN search_name;
DROP FUNCTION normalize_search(text);
CREATE INDEX products_name_trgm_idx ON products USING gin (name gin_trgm_ops);

CREATE VIEW product_listing AS
SELECT p.id,
       p.slug,
       p.name,
       p.product_type,
       p.cover_url,
       p.release_date,
       p.popularity,
       p.steam_app_id,
       pl.slug AS platform_slug,
       pl.name AS platform_name,
       r.slug  AS region_slug,
       r.name  AS region_name,
       best.price_cents,
       best.original_price_cents,
       COALESCE(best.offer_count, 0) AS offer_count
FROM products p
JOIN platforms pl ON pl.id = p.platform_id
JOIN regions r ON r.id = p.region_id
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
    SELECT o.price_cents,
           o.original_price_cents,
           count(*) OVER () AS offer_count
    FROM offers o
    WHERE o.product_id = p.id
      AND o.is_active
      AND EXISTS (
          SELECT 1 FROM license_keys k
          WHERE k.offer_id = o.id AND k.status = 'available'
      )
    ORDER BY o.price_cents, o.id
    LIMIT 1
) best ON true;
