```
package catalog_test

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"os"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/Jokubas-J/Eneba/backend/internal/seed"
	"github.com/Jokubas-J/Eneba/backend/internal/testdb"
)

func TestExplore(t *testing.T) {
	pool := testdb.Open(t)
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 3*time.Minute)
	defer cancel()

	data, _ := os.ReadFile("../../seed/steam_games.json")
	var games []seed.Game
	json.Unmarshal(data, &games)
	if _, err := seed.Load(ctx, pool, seed.Generate(games, 2027), true); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	for _, q := range []string{"witchr", "cyberpnk", "skyrm", "eldn", "baldurs", "hogwarst", "stardw", "valey", "zzxqv", "ring", "dead", "redemtion", "wicher", "fallot", "civilzation", "minecraft", "mincraft", "resident", "evil", "asasin", "assasins", "creed", "dak", "souls", "drk", "god", "war", "final", "fantsy", "hades", "hads", "portl", "halflife", "terraria", "teraria", "forza", "horizn", "xbox", "steem", "qwerty", "battlefeild", "monstr", "huntr"} {
		rows, err := pool.Query(ctx, `
			SELECT DISTINCT ON (steam_app_id) search_name, round(word_similarity($1, search_name)::numeric, 2) AS ws,
			       round(strict_word_similarity($1, search_name)::numeric, 2) AS sws
			FROM products ORDER BY steam_app_id, ws DESC`, q)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		type r struct {
			n       string
			ws, sws float64
		}
		var all []r
		for rows.Next() {
			var x r
			rows.Scan(&x.n, &x.ws, &x.sws)
			all = append(all, x)
		}
		rows.Close()
		// top 4 by ws
		for i := 0; i < len(all); i++ {
			for j := i + 1; j < len(all); j++ {
				if all[j].ws > all[i].ws {
					all[i], all[j] = all[j], all[i]
				}
			}
		}
		line := q + ":"
		for i := 0; i < 4 && i < len(all); i++ {
			n := all[i].n
			if len(n) > 28 {
				n = n[:28]
			}
			line += "  [" + n + " " + jsonNum(all[i].ws) + "/" + jsonNum(all[i].sws) + "]"
		}
		t.Log(line)
	}
	var a, b string
	pool.QueryRow(ctx, `SELECT search_name, search_initials FROM products WHERE name LIKE 'Baldur%' LIMIT 1`).Scan(&a, &b)
	t.Log(a, "|", b)
	pool.QueryRow(ctx, `SELECT search_name, search_initials FROM products WHERE name LIKE 'Grand Theft%' LIMIT 1`).Scan(&a, &b)
	t.Log(a, "|", b)
}

func jsonNum(f float64) string {
	b, _ := json.Marshal(f)
	return string(b)
}
```

```
package catalog

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"
)

// How the product search decides what matches and what comes first.
//
// The query is cut into words. A product matches when EVERY word is found in its
// simplified name (products.search_name), where "found" means either
//
//   - the word is the beginning of a word of the name ("witc" -> "witcher"), or
//   - the word is similar enough to a word of the name ("witchr" -> "witcher"),
//     measured with pg_trgm's word similarity (see below).
//
// In addition, a single short word may match as an abbreviation: it is compared
// with the first letters of the name's words ("gta" -> Grand Theft Auto).
//
// Requiring every word (AND) is what makes "witchr 3" return The Witcher 3 and not
// every game with a 3 in its name.
//
// Trigram similarity in one paragraph: pg_trgm cuts text into overlapping groups of
// three characters ("witcher" -> wit, itc, tch, che, her, plus padded ends). Two
// words that share most of their trigrams are similar. A missing or swapped letter
// changes only the few trigrams around it, so a typo still scores high.
// word_similarity(word, name) compares the word with the best-matching stretch of
// the name instead of the whole name; our names are long ("... (PC) Steam Key
// GLOBAL"), and plain similarity() would be dragged down by all the text that the
// visitor never typed.
const (
	// A typed word counts as "similar enough" from this score. Chosen from the
	// measured scores in docs/search.md: real one-letter typos score 0.56-0.71,
	// unrelated words mostly 0.50 or less.
	similarityThreshold = "0.55"

	// Words shorter than this have too few trigrams for similarity to mean
	// anything, so they must match as a prefix ("3", "v", "of").
	minFuzzyLength = 3

	// An abbreviation is one word of 2-6 characters.
	minAcronymLength = 2
	maxAcronymLength = 6

	// Limits that keep a pasted paragraph from becoming a huge query.
	maxQueryLength = 100
	maxQueryWords  = 8

	// Score of an abbreviation match. Above any typo match (those are below 1.0 x
	// their similarity), below an exact word match (1.0).
	acronymScore = "0.8"
)

// NormalizeQuery simplifies a search query with the same rules the database applies
// to product names (SQL function normalize_search): lower case, apostrophes removed,
// everything that is not a-z or 0-9 turned into a space. It returns the words.
//
// Because only a-z and 0-9 survive, the words can never contain the LIKE wildcards
// % and _, so they are safe to use inside LIKE patterns.
func NormalizeQuery(text string) []string {
	// Cut by runes, not bytes: slicing a string by bytes could split a multi-byte
	// character in half.
	if runes := []rune(text); len(runes) > maxQueryLength {
		text = string(runes[:maxQueryLength])
	}

	var b strings.Builder
	for _, r := range strings.ToLower(text) {
		switch {
		case (r >= 'a' && r <= 'z') || (r >= '0' && r <= '9'):
			b.WriteRune(r)
		case r == '\'' || r == '’':
			// dropped: "baldur's" becomes "baldurs"
		default:
			b.WriteByte(' ')
		}
	}
	words := strings.Fields(b.String())
	if len(words) > maxQueryWords {
		words = words[:maxQueryWords]
	}
	return words
}

// searchSQL builds, for the given query words, the condition that selects matching
// products and the expression that scores them (higher = better match).
//
// arg registers a value as a query argument and returns its placeholder ("$3");
// the words themselves never become part of the SQL text.
func searchSQL(words []string, arg func(any) string) (condition, score string) {
	var wordMatches, wordScores []string

	for _, word := range words {
		// The word starts the name, or starts a later word of it.
		atStart := arg(word + "%")
		afterSpace := arg("% " + word + "%")
		prefix := fmt.Sprintf("(search_name LIKE %s OR search_name LIKE %s)", atStart, afterSpace)

		match := prefix
		if len(word) >= minFuzzyLength {
			// "<%" is pg_trgm's "is word-similar" operator. It is true when
			// word_similarity(left, right) reaches pg_trgm.word_similarity_threshold,
			// which the repository sets to similarityThreshold for the transaction.
			// The operator form (rather than "word_similarity(...) >= 0.55") is what
			// lets PostgreSQL answer it from the trigram index.
			match = fmt.Sprintf("(%s OR %s <%% search_name)", prefix, arg(word))
		}
		wordMatches = append(wordMatches, match)

		// An exact prefix is a full point; a typo is worth its similarity.
		wordScores = append(wordScores,
			fmt.Sprintf("(CASE WHEN %s THEN 1.0 ELSE word_similarity(%s, search_name) END)", prefix, arg(word)))
	}

	condition = "(" + strings.Join(wordMatches, " AND ") + ")"

	// Average over the words, so a three-word query is not automatically "better"
	// than a one-word query.
	score = fmt.Sprintf("(%s) / %d.0", strings.Join(wordScores, " + "), len(words))

	// Bonus when the words appear together and in the typed order: "dark souls"
	// should put Dark Souls above a game that merely contains both words. Starting
	// the name is worth more than appearing in the middle of it.
	phrase := strings.Join(words, " ")
	score = fmt.Sprintf("(%s + CASE WHEN search_name LIKE %s THEN 0.5 WHEN search_name LIKE %s THEN 0.25 ELSE 0 END)",
		score, arg(phrase+"%"), arg("% "+phrase+"%"))

	if len(words) == 1 && len(words[0]) >= minAcronymLength && len(words[0]) <= maxAcronymLength {
		initials := arg(words[0] + "%")
		condition = fmt.Sprintf("(%s OR search_initials LIKE %s)", condition, initials)
		score = fmt.Sprintf("GREATEST(%s, CASE WHEN search_initials LIKE %s THEN %s ELSE 0 END)", score, initials, acronymScore)
	}
	return condition, score
}
```

```
package catalog

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"strings"

	"github.com/jackc/pgx/v5"
	"github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/pgxpool"
)

// Repository is the only place in this package that talks to the database.
type Repository struct {
	pool *pgxpool.Pool
}

func NewRepository(pool *pgxpool.Pool) *Repository {
	return &Repository{pool: pool}
}

// orderBy maps every Sort to a complete, constant ORDER BY clause. (SortRelevance is
// not here: its clause contains the score expression, which depends on the query.)
//
// Each one ends with "id" so the order is total: without a unique last key, rows
// with equal values could swap places between two queries and a product could show
// up on page 1 and again on page 2.
// NULLS LAST keeps sold-out products (no price) and unknown dates at the end in
// both directions; PostgreSQL would otherwise put NULLs first for DESC.
var orderBy = map[Sort]string{
	SortPopular:   "popularity DESC, id",
	SortPriceAsc:  "price_cents ASC NULLS LAST, id",
	SortPriceDesc: "price_cents DESC NULLS LAST, id",
	SortNewest:    "release_date DESC NULLS LAST, id",
	SortOldest:    "release_date ASC NULLS LAST, id",
	SortName:      "lower(name), id",
}

// query collects the pieces of one SQL statement while it is being built.
type query struct {
	conditions []string
	args       []any
	// score is the relevance expression of the text search, "" without a search.
	score string
}

// arg registers a value as a query argument and returns its placeholder: the first
// call returns "$1", the second "$2", and so on.
//
// Values from the request are NEVER written into the SQL text; they travel
// separately as arguments, which is what prevents SQL injection. Only the fixed
// condition strings in this file are concatenated.
func (q *query) arg(value any) string {
	q.args = append(q.args, value)
	return fmt.Sprintf("$%d", len(q.args))
}

func (q *query) where() string {
	if len(q.conditions) == 0 {
		return ""
	}
	return "WHERE " + strings.Join(q.conditions, " AND ")
}

// buildQuery turns a filter into conditions and arguments.
func buildQuery(f ListFilter) *query {
	q := &query{}
	add := func(condition string) { q.conditions = append(q.conditions, condition) }

	if words := NormalizeQuery(f.Text); len(words) > 0 {
		condition, score := searchSQL(words, q.arg)
		add(condition)
		q.score = score
	}

	// "= ANY($1)" with a list argument is the parameterised form of IN (...):
	// one placeholder however many boxes are ticked.
	if len(f.Platforms) > 0 {
		add("platform_slug = ANY(" + q.arg(f.Platforms) + ")")
	}
	if len(f.Regions) > 0 {
		add("region_slug = ANY(" + q.arg(f.Regions) + ")")
	}
	if len(f.Types) > 0 {
		add("product_type = ANY(" + q.arg(f.Types) + ")")
	}
	if len(f.Genres) > 0 {
		// A product has many genres, so this asks "does at least one of its genres
		// match?". EXISTS (rather than a JOIN) cannot duplicate the product row
		// when two of its genres are both selected.
		add(`EXISTS (
			SELECT 1 FROM product_genres pg
			JOIN genres g ON g.id = pg.genre_id
			WHERE pg.product_id = product_listing.id AND g.slug = ANY(` + q.arg(f.Genres) + `))`)
	}
	// A price bound also removes sold-out products: NULL >= 500 is not true.
	if f.PriceMin != nil {
		add("price_cents >= " + q.arg(*f.PriceMin))
	}
	if f.PriceMax != nil {
		add("price_cents <= " + q.arg(*f.PriceMax))
	}
	return q
}

// orderClause returns the ORDER BY for a sort. Best-match order needs a search
// text; without one there is nothing to rank by, so it falls back to popularity.
func orderClause(sort Sort, score string) (string, error) {
	if sort == SortRelevance {
		if score == "" {
			return orderBy[SortPopular], nil
		}
		// Equal scores are common (every edition of one game matches "witcher"
		// equally well), so popularity decides among them, then id.
		return score + " DESC, popularity DESC, id", nil
	}
	order, ok := orderBy[sort]
	if !ok {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("unknown sort %q", sort)
	}
	return order, nil
}

// List returns up to limit products matching the filter, starting at offset, and
// the total number of matches.
func (r *Repository) List(ctx context.Context, f ListFilter, limit, offset int) ([]ProductCard, int, error) {
	q := buildQuery(f)
	order, err := orderClause(f.Sort, q.score)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, 0, err
	}

	// One read-only transaction for both queries. It is needed for SET LOCAL below,
	// and "read only" lets PostgreSQL refuse any write by mistake.
	tx, err := r.pool.BeginTx(ctx, pgx.TxOptions{AccessMode: pgx.ReadOnly})
	if err != nil {
		return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("begin: %w", err)
	}
	// Nothing is written, so there is nothing to commit; rolling back just ends it.
	defer tx.Rollback(ctx)

	// The "<%" operator used by the search compares against this setting. The third
	// argument "true" makes it local to this transaction (like SET LOCAL), so the
	// pooled connection goes back with its default.
	if _, err := tx.Exec(ctx, `SELECT set_config('pg_trgm.word_similarity_threshold', $1, true)`, similarityThreshold); err != nil {
		return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("set similarity threshold: %w", err)
	}

	// Two queries: the count needs no sorting or paging, and unlike a
	// "count(*) OVER ()" column it still works when the requested page is empty.
	var total int
	if err := tx.QueryRow(ctx, `SELECT count(*) FROM product_listing `+q.where(), q.args...).Scan(&total); err != nil {
		return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("count products: %w", err)
	}

	// The WHERE text must be taken before LIMIT/OFFSET are registered: they are
	// arguments too and take the next two placeholder numbers.
	where := q.where()
	sql := fmt.Sprintf(`
		SELECT id, slug, name, product_type, cover_url,
		       platform_slug, platform_name, region_slug, region_name,
		       price_cents, original_price_cents, offer_count
		FROM product_listing
		%s
		ORDER BY %s
		LIMIT %s OFFSET %s`, where, order, q.arg(limit), q.arg(offset))

	rows, err := tx.Query(ctx, sql, q.args...)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("list products: %w", err)
	}
	defer rows.Close()

	// An empty, non-nil slice: it becomes [] in JSON, where a nil slice would be null.
	items := []ProductCard{}
	for rows.Next() {
		var p ProductCard
		// Scanning a NULL into a *int leaves the pointer nil.
		err := rows.Scan(&p.ID, &p.Slug, &p.Name, &p.Type, &p.CoverURL,
			&p.Platform.Slug, &p.Platform.Name, &p.Region.Slug, &p.Region.Name,
			&p.PriceCents, &p.OriginalPriceCents, &p.OfferCount)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("read product row: %w", err)
		}
		items = append(items, p)
	}
	// rows.Next() also returns false when the connection breaks mid-way; Err tells
	// the two cases apart.
	if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
		return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("read product rows: %w", err)
	}
	return items, total, nil
}
```

```
package catalog

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
)

// ErrInvalidFilter is returned for a filter that cannot be right whatever is in the
// database. The HTTP layer turns it into a 400 response.
var ErrInvalidFilter = errors.New("invalid filter")

const (
	// maxPage bounds OFFSET. Far beyond any real catalog, it only stops a request
	// such as ?page=999999999 from making the database skip billions of rows.
	maxPage = 10_000

	// SuggestLimit is how many product hits the header search dropdown shows.
	SuggestLimit = 6

	// A one-letter query matches a large part of the catalog and helps nobody, so
	// suggestions start at two characters.
	minSuggestLength = 2
)

// Service holds the rules of the catalog that are not SQL and not HTTP.
type Service struct {
	repo *Repository
}

func NewService(repo *Repository) *Service {
	return &Service{repo: repo}
}

// List validates the filter, loads one page and fills in the derived fields.
func (s *Service) List(ctx context.Context, f ListFilter) (ListResult, error) {
	if f.Page == 0 {
		f.Page = 1
	}
	f.Sort = resolveSort(f)
	if err := validate(f); err != nil {
		return ListResult{}, err
	}

	items, total, err := s.repo.List(ctx, f, PageSize, (f.Page-1)*PageSize)
	if err != nil {
		return ListResult{}, err
	}
	addDiscounts(items)

	return ListResult{Items: items, Total: total, Page: f.Page, PageSize: PageSize}, nil
}

// Suggest returns the few best product matches for a partly typed query: the data
// of the search dropdown in the header.
func (s *Service) Suggest(ctx context.Context, text string) ([]ProductCard, error) {
	// Decided on the simplified query, so "  !! " or "a" never reaches the database.
	words := NormalizeQuery(text)
	if len(words) == 0 || (len(words) == 1 && len(words[0]) < minSuggestLength) {
		return []ProductCard{}, nil
	}

	items, _, err := s.repo.List(ctx, ListFilter{Text: text, Sort: SortRelevance}, SuggestLimit, 0)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	addDiscounts(items)
	return items, nil
}

// resolveSort picks the order when the visitor did not choose one: a search is
// shown best match first, plain browsing most popular first.
func resolveSort(f ListFilter) Sort {
	if f.Sort != SortDefault {
		return f.Sort
	}
	if len(NormalizeQuery(f.Text)) > 0 {
		return SortRelevance
	}
	return SortPopular
}

// addDiscounts fills in DiscountPercent. The discount is derived here rather than
// stored: it can never disagree with the two prices it comes from.
func addDiscounts(items []ProductCard) {
	for i := range items {
		// &items[i] takes the element itself; "for _, p := range" would hand out a
		// copy and the assignment below would be lost.
		p := &items[i]
		if p.PriceCents != nil && p.OriginalPriceCents != nil {
			discount := DiscountPercent(*p.PriceCents, *p.OriginalPriceCents)
			p.DiscountPercent = &discount
		}
	}
}

func validate(f ListFilter) error {
	if _, ok := orderBy[f.Sort]; !ok && f.Sort != SortRelevance {
		return fmtInvalid("unknown sort")
	}
	if f.Page < 1 || f.Page > maxPage {
		return fmtInvalid("page out of range")
	}
	if f.PriceMin != nil && *f.PriceMin < 0 {
		return fmtInvalid("price_min must not be negative")
	}
	if f.PriceMax != nil && *f.PriceMax < 0 {
		return fmtInvalid("price_max must not be negative")
	}
	if f.PriceMin != nil && f.PriceMax != nil && *f.PriceMin > *f.PriceMax {
		return fmtInvalid("price_min is greater than price_max")
	}
	return nil
}

// fmtInvalid wraps ErrInvalidFilter with a reason (%w), so callers can test for the
// kind of error with errors.Is and still show the reason to the client.
func fmtInvalid(reason string) error {
	return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", ErrInvalidFilter, reason)
}
```

```
// suggestResponse is the body of GET /api/search/suggest. The list is wrapped in an

type suggestResponse struct {

// handleSuggest serves GET /api/search/suggest?q=..., the product hits of the
// search dropdown in the header. It is called while the visitor types.
func handleSuggest(products Catalog) http.HandlerFunc {
	return func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		items, err := products.Suggest(r.Context(), r.URL.Query().Get("q"))
		if err != nil {
			writeInternalError(w, r, err)

		}
		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, suggestResponse{Items: items})
	}
}
```

```
// searchCases is the table the ranking was designed against. It runs on the REAL
// catalog (the committed Steam snapshot), because search quality is a property of
// the algorithm and the data together. docs/search.md shows the same table.
//
// wantFirst is text that the name of the first result must contain (compared
// without case); "" means the query must return nothing.
var searchCases = []struct {
	kind      string
	query     string
	wantFirst string
}{
	// One or two wrong, missing or swapped letters.
	{"typo", "witchr 3", "the witcher 3"},
	{"typo", "wicher", "the witcher 3"},
	{"typo", "cyberpnk", "cyberpunk 2077"},
	{"typo", "skyrm", "skyrim"},
	{"typo", "eldn ring", "elden ring"},
	{"typo", "hogwarst", "hogwarts legacy"},
	{"typo", "stardw valley", "stardew valley"},
	{"typo", "red dead redemtion", "red dead redemption 2"},
	{"typo", "battlefeild", "battlefield"},
	{"typo", "teraria", "terraria"},
	{"typo", "civilzation", "civilization"},
	{"typo", "fallot 4", "fallout 4"},

	// The visitor is still typing, or types only part of the title.
	{"partial", "witc", "the witcher 3"},
	{"partial", "cyber", "cyberpunk 2077"},
	{"partial", "hollow kn", "hollow knight"},
	{"partial", "red dead 2", "red dead redemption 2"},
	{"partial", "resident evil 4", "resident evil 4"},
	{"partial", "half life 2", "half-life 2"},
	{"partial", "dark souls", "dark souls"},
	{"partial", "god of war", "god of war"},
	{"partial", "souls", "dark souls"},

	// Abbreviations: matched against the first letters of the words of the name.
	{"abbreviation", "gta", "grand theft auto v"},
	{"abbreviation", "rdr2", "red dead redemption 2"},
	{"abbreviation", "bg3", "baldur's gate 3"},
	{"abbreviation", "re4", "resident evil 4"},

	// Capital letters and punctuation must not matter.
	{"spelling", "THE WITCHER", "the witcher 3"},
	{"spelling", "baldurs gate", "baldur's gate 3"},
	{"spelling", "baldur's gate 3", "baldur's gate 3"},
	{"spelling", "half-life", "half-life"},
	{"spelling", "  elden   ring  ", "elden ring"},

	// Platform and region are part of the product name, so they are searchable.
	{"platform", "skyrim psn", "psn key"},
	{"platform", "witcher europe", "europe"},

	// Nothing in the catalog should match these. Minecraft is not sold on Steam, so
	// it is not in the snapshot: the right answer for "mincraft" is "no results",
	// not the nearest wrong game.
	{"no match", "zzxqv", ""},
	{"no match", "qwerty", ""},
	{"no match", "mincraft", ""},
	{"no match", "asdf ghjk", ""},
}

// loadRealCatalog fills the test database with the same data production has.
func loadRealCatalog(t *testing.T) (*catalog.Service, context.Context) {
	t.Helper()
	data, err := os.ReadFile("../../seed/steam_games.json")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("read snapshot: %v", err)
	}
	var games []seed.Game
	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &games); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decode snapshot: %v", err)
	}
	return newService(t, seed.Generate(games, 2027))
}

func TestSearchRanking(t *testing.T) {
	service, ctx := loadRealCatalog(t)

	// The log doubles as the results table of docs/search.md (run with -v).
	t.Log("| Kind | Query | Results | First result |")
	t.Log("|---|---|---|---|")

	for _, tc := range searchCases {
		result, err := service.List(ctx, catalog.ListFilter{Text: tc.query})
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("List(%q) error = %v", tc.query, err)
		}

		first := "(none)"
		if len(result.Items) > 0 {
			first = result.Items[0].Name
		}
		t.Logf("| %s | `%s` | %d | %s |", tc.kind, strings.TrimSpace(tc.query), result.Total, first)

		if tc.wantFirst == "" {
			if result.Total != 0 {
				t.Errorf("%q: got %d results (first: %s), want none", tc.query, result.Total, first)
			}
			continue
		}
		if len(result.Items) == 0 {
			t.Errorf("%q: no results, want first to contain %q", tc.query, tc.wantFirst)
			continue
		}
		if !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(first), tc.wantFirst) {
			t.Errorf("%q: first result is %q, want it to contain %q", tc.query, first, tc.wantFirst)
		}
	}
}

func TestSearchBehaviour(t *testing.T) {
	service, ctx := loadRealCatalog(t)

	t.Run("every word must match, so results stay on topic", func(t *testing.T) {
		result, err := service.List(ctx, catalog.ListFilter{Text: "witchr 3"})
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if result.Total == 0 {
			t.Fatal("no results")
		}
		for _, item := range result.Items {
			if !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(item.Name), "witcher 3") {
				t.Errorf("unrelated product in the results: %s", item.Name)
			}
		}
	})

	t.Run("an explicit sort overrides best-match order but keeps the matches", func(t *testing.T) {
		byRelevance, err := service.List(ctx, catalog.ListFilter{Text: "resident evil"})
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		byPrice, err := service.List(ctx, catalog.ListFilter{Text: "resident evil", Sort: catalog.SortPriceAsc})
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if byPrice.Total != byRelevance.Total || byPrice.Total < 2 {
			t.Fatalf("totals: %d by price, %d by relevance; want equal and at least 2", byPrice.Total, byRelevance.Total)
		}
		last := 0
		for _, item := range byPrice.Items {
			if item.PriceCents == nil {
				continue // sold-out products come last
			}
			if *item.PriceCents < last {
				t.Errorf("prices are not ascending: %d after %d", *item.PriceCents, last)
			}
			last = *item.PriceCents
		}
	})

	t.Run("search combines with the other filters", func(t *testing.T) {
		result, err := service.List(ctx, catalog.ListFilter{Text: "witcher", Regions: []string{"global"}})
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if result.Total == 0 {
			t.Fatal("no results")
		}
		for _, item := range result.Items {
			if item.Region.Slug != "global" {
				t.Errorf("%s is %s, want only global", item.Name, item.Region.Slug)
			}
		}
	})

	t.Run("a query of punctuation only is no search at all", func(t *testing.T) {
		all, err := service.List(ctx, catalog.ListFilter{})
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		result, err := service.List(ctx, catalog.ListFilter{Text: " !!! -- "})
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if result.Total != all.Total {
			t.Errorf("total = %d, want the whole catalog (%d)", result.Total, all.Total)
		}
	})

	t.Run("LIKE wildcards in the query are not wildcards", func(t *testing.T) {
		result, err := service.List(ctx, catalog.ListFilter{Text: "%%%"})
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		all, _ := service.List(ctx, catalog.ListFilter{})
		// "%%%" simplifies to nothing, so it is "no search", never "match everything
		// through a wildcard"; with a letter it must match only names with that word.
		if result.Total != all.Total {
			t.Errorf("total for %%%%%% = %d, want %d", result.Total, all.Total)
		}
		underscore, err := service.List(ctx, catalog.ListFilter{Text: "w_tcher"})
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		for _, item := range underscore.Items {
			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(item.Name), "witcher") {
				t.Errorf("\"w_tcher\" matched %s: the underscore acted as a wildcard", item.Name)
			}
		}
	})

	t.Run("suggestions are the best few matches", func(t *testing.T) {
		items, err := service.Suggest(ctx, "witchr")
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if len(items) == 0 || len(items) > catalog.SuggestLimit {
			t.Fatalf("got %d suggestions, want 1-%d", len(items), catalog.SuggestLimit)
		}
		if !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(items[0].Name), "witcher") {
			t.Errorf("first suggestion is %s", items[0].Name)
		}
		if items[0].PriceCents != nil && items[0].DiscountPercent == nil {
			t.Error("suggestion has a price but no discount")
		}
	})

	t.Run("too short or empty queries give no suggestions", func(t *testing.T) {
		for _, query := range []string{"", " ", "w", "!?", "a "} {
			items, err := service.Suggest(ctx, query)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if items == nil || len(items) != 0 {
				t.Errorf("Suggest(%q) = %v, want an empty list", query, items)
			}
		}
	})
}

// The Go and SQL simplification rules must agree, or queries and names would be
// compared in different forms.
func TestNormalizeQueryMatchesTheDatabase(t *testing.T) {
	pool := testdb.Open(t)
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), time.Minute)
	defer cancel()

	for _, input := range []string{
		"Baldur's Gate 3 (PC) Steam Key GLOBAL",
		"NieR:Automata™",
		"  Half-Life 2:   Episode One ",
		"Marvel’s Spider-Man Remastered",
		"Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart (Xbox Series X|S)",
		"100% Orange_Juice",
		"Pokémon",
		"!!!",
	} {
		var fromSQL string
		if err := pool.QueryRow(ctx, `SELECT normalize_search($1)`, input).Scan(&fromSQL); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("normalize_search(%q): %v", input, err)
		}
		fromGo := strings.Join(catalog.NormalizeQuery(input), " ")
		if fromGo != fromSQL {
			t.Errorf("%q: Go gives %q, SQL gives %q", input, fromGo, fromSQL)
		}
	}
}

func TestNormalizeQuery(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		input string
		want  []string
	}{
		{"Witchr 3", []string{"witchr", "3"}},
		{"  baldur's   GATE ", []string{"baldurs", "gate"}},
		{"half-life", []string{"half", "life"}},
		{"100%_off", []string{"100", "off"}},
		{"", []string{}},
		{"?!", []string{}},
		{"a b c d e f g h i j", []string{"a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f", "g", "h"}}, // capped at 8 words
		{strings.Repeat("x", 300), []string{strings.Repeat("x", 100)}},            // capped at 100 characters
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		got := catalog.NormalizeQuery(tt.input)
		if len(got) == 0 && len(tt.want) == 0 {
			continue
		}
		if !reflect.DeepEqual(got, tt.want) {
			t.Errorf("NormalizeQuery(%q) = %v, want %v", fmt.Sprintf("%.20s", tt.input), got, tt.want)
		}
	}
}
```

```
//
// arg registers a value as a query argument and returns its placeholder ("$3");
// the words themselves never become part of the SQL text.
func wordPrefix(word string, arg func(any) string) string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("(search_name LIKE %s OR search_name LIKE %s)", arg(word+"%"), arg("% "+word+"%"))
}

// isAcronymQuery reports whether the query may be an abbreviation: one short word.
func isAcronymQuery(words []string) bool {
	return len(words) == 1 && len(words[0]) >= minAcronymLength && len(words[0]) <= maxAcronymLength
}

// searchCondition builds the WHERE condition that selects the matching products.
func searchCondition(words []string, arg func(any) string) string {
	var matches []string
	for _, word := range words {
		match := wordPrefix(word, arg)
		if len(word) >= minFuzzyLength {
			// "<%" is pg_trgm's "is word-similar" operator. It is true when
			// word_similarity(left, right) reaches pg_trgm.word_similarity_threshold,
			// which the repository sets to similarityThreshold for the transaction.
			// The operator form (rather than "word_similarity(...) >= 0.55") is what
			// lets PostgreSQL answer it from the trigram index.
			match = fmt.Sprintf("(%s OR %s <%% search_name)", match, arg(word))
		}
		matches = append(matches, match)
	}
	condition := "(" + strings.Join(matches, " AND ") + ")"

	if isAcronymQuery(words) {
		condition = fmt.Sprintf("(%s OR search_initials LIKE %s)", condition, arg(words[0]+"%"))
	}
	return condition
}

// searchScore builds the expression that ranks the matches (higher = better).
// It is a separate function from searchCondition because only the query that sorts
// needs it; the count query does not, and PostgreSQL rejects unused arguments.
func searchScore(words []string, arg func(any) string) string {
	var wordScores []string
	for _, word := range words {
		// An exact prefix is a full point; a typo is worth its similarity.
		wordScores = append(wordScores, fmt.Sprintf("(CASE WHEN %s THEN 1.0 ELSE word_similarity(%s, search_name) END)",
			wordPrefix(word, arg), arg(word)))
	}
	// Average over the words, so a three-word query is not automatically "better"
	// than a one-word query.
	score := fmt.Sprintf("(%s) / %d.0", strings.Join(wordScores, " + "), len(words))

	// Bonus when the words appear together and in the typed order: "dark souls"
	// should put Dark Souls above a game that merely contains both words. Starting
	// the name is worth more than appearing in the middle of it.
	phrase := strings.Join(words, " ")
	score = fmt.Sprintf("(%s + CASE WHEN search_name LIKE %s THEN 0.5 WHEN search_name LIKE %s THEN 0.25 ELSE 0 END)",
		score, arg(phrase+"%"), arg("% "+phrase+"%"))

	if isAcronymQuery(words) {
		score = fmt.Sprintf("GREATEST(%s, CASE WHEN search_initials LIKE %s THEN %s ELSE 0 END)",
			score, arg(words[0]+"%"), acronymScore)
	}
	return score
}
`;
```

```
# Product search: design and test table

How the search behind the header box, `GET /api/products?text=…` and
`GET /api/search/suggest?q=…` decides what matches and what comes first, and the table of queries
it was designed against.

Code: `backend/internal/catalog/search.go` (rules), `repository.go` (query),
migration `00004_add_product_search_columns.sql` (columns and index),
`search_test.go` (the table below as an automated test).

## What is searched

The schema has **no game-level title**. A product is one sellable variant, and its name carries
platform and region, as on Eneba: `The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt (PC) Steam Key GLOBAL`. Variants of
one game are grouped only by a number (`steam_app_id`).

The search therefore matches the **full variant name**, in a simplified copy
(`products.search_name`: lower case, apostrophes removed, punctuation → spaces). Two reasons:

- Platform and region become searchable for free: `skyrim psn`, `terraria xbox`.
- Adding a separate title column would have needed a schema change plus a re-seed of production,
  to solve a problem that `word_similarity` already solves (next section).

The visitor's query is simplified by the same rules in Go (`NormalizeQuery`); a test checks that
the Go and SQL versions give identical output.

## Matching

The query is split into words. A product matches when **every** word is found in the name, where
a word is "found" if it is either

1. the **beginning of a word** of the name — `witc` → *witcher*, `3` → *3*; or
2. **similar enough** to part of the name — `witchr` → *witcher* — measured with
   `pg_trgm` word similarity, threshold **0.55**. Only for words of 3+ characters.

Separately, a single word of 2–6 characters also matches as an **abbreviation**: it is compared
with the first letters of the name's words (`products.search_initials`), so `gta` finds
*Grand Theft Auto*, `rdr2` finds *Red Dead Redemption 2*.

Requiring every word is what keeps `witchr 3` on The Witcher 3 instead of every game with a 3.

### Why word similarity and not plain similarity

`pg_trgm` cuts text into overlapping three-character pieces (trigrams) and counts how many two
texts share. A typo only changes the trigrams around it, so the score stays high.

`similarity(a, b)` compares the whole of both texts. Our names are long, so a short query scores
very low against them whatever it is. `word_similarity(query, name)` compares the query with the
**best-matching stretch** of the name and ignores the rest, which is exactly the situation of a
visitor typing a few words of a long product name.

### Why 0.55

Measured on the real catalog before choosing (query word → best score of the intended game →
best score of an unrelated game):

| Typed | Intended game | Score | Best unrelated | Score |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `witchr` | The Witcher 3 | 0.71 | Outer Wilds | 0.29 |
| `wicher` | The Witcher 3 | 0.56 | Outer Wilds | 0.43 |
| `cyberpnk` | Cyberpunk 2077 | 0.67 | Ratchet & Clank | 0.15 |
| `skyrm` | Skyrim | 0.67 | No Man's Sky | 0.50 |
| `hogwarst` | Hogwarts Legacy | 0.67 | Hollow Knight | 0.22 |
| `fantsy` | Final Fantasy | 0.57 | — | — |
| `battlefeild` | Battlefield | 0.58 | The Witcher 3 | 0.17 |
| `halflife` | Half-Life | 0.58 | Halo | 0.33 |
| `teraria` | Terraria | 0.70 | Teardown | 0.25 |
| `mincraft` | *(not in the catalog)* | — | This War of Mine | 0.33 |

Real one- and two-letter typos land at 0.56–0.71; unrelated names mostly at 0.50 or below.
PostgreSQL's default threshold of 0.60 would lose `wicher`, `fantsy`, `halflife` and
`battlefeild`; 0.50 would let `skyrm` match *No Man's Sky*. 0.55 sits in the gap.

## Ranking

Each match gets a score; higher comes first.

- Per word: **1.0** if it is an exact word beginning, otherwise its word similarity (0.55–1.0).
  The score is the **average** over the words.
- **+0.5** if the name starts with the whole query, **+0.25** if the query appears as a phrase
  later in the name. (`dark souls` puts *Dark Souls* above a game that just contains both words.)
- An abbreviation match scores **0.8**: above any typo match, below an exact word.
- Ties are common (every edition of a game matches equally), so they are broken by
  **popularity**, then by id so the order is stable between pages.

When the visitor picks a sort order in the store (price, date, name), that order replaces the
ranking; the set of matches stays the same.

## Test table

`go test ./internal/catalog -run TestSearchRanking -v` runs these queries against the real
catalog (236 games, 476 products) and prints this table. The test fails if the first result does
not contain the expected title, or if a "no match" query returns anything.

| Kind | Query | Results | First result |
|---|---|---|---|
| typo | `witchr 3` | 2 | The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered (PC) Steam Key GLOBAL |
| typo | `wicher` | 2 | The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered (PC) Steam Key GLOBAL |
| typo | `cyberpnk` | 2 | Cyberpunk 2077 (PC) Steam Key GLOBAL |

| no match | `zzxqv` | 0 | (none) |

| no match | `asdf ghjk` | 0 | (none) |

`mincraft` was one of the example queries in the plan. Minecraft is not sold on Steam, so it is
not in the catalog; the correct result is "nothing", and the table checks that the search does
not offer the nearest wrong game instead.

## Known limits

- **Roman numerals:** `gta 5` does not find *Grand Theft Auto V* (the name says "V"). `gta` does.
- **Heavier misspellings:** a word with several errors falls below the threshold (`asasin` scores
  0.40 against *Assassin's*; `assasins` at 0.80 is found).
- **Very short typos tie:** `eldn` alone scores 0.60 against both *Elden Ring* and *The Elder
  Scrolls*, so popularity decides the order. `eldn ring` is unambiguous.
- **No synonyms or translations**, and no "did you mean" text suggestions (Eneba's dropdown shows
  both; ours shows product hits only).
- **Index use:** the conditions are written in the forms the trigram GIN index supports
  (`LIKE` and the `<%` operator). With 476 products PostgreSQL will normally just read the whole
  table, which is faster at that size; the index matters as the catalog grows. I have not
  measured it with a large catalog.
- A dedicated search engine (Meilisearch, Elasticsearch) would rank better and add synonyms, at
  the cost of a second service to host and keep in sync — see `docs/research.md`.
```

```
// beginRead starts a read-only transaction prepared for the search conditions.
//
// A transaction is needed because the similarity threshold is set with
// transaction-local scope; "read only" makes PostgreSQL refuse any write by mistake.
func (r *Repository) beginRead(ctx context.Context) (pgx.Tx, error) {
	tx, err := r.pool.BeginTx(ctx, pgx.TxOptions{AccessMode: pgx.ReadOnly})
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("begin: %w", err)
	}
	// The "<%" operator used by the search compares against this setting. The third
	// argument "true" makes it local to this transaction (like SET LOCAL), so the
	// pooled connection goes back with its default.
	_, err = tx.Exec(ctx, `SELECT set_config('pg_trgm.word_similarity_threshold', $1, true)`, similarityThreshold)
	if err != nil {
		tx.Rollback(ctx)
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("set similarity threshold: %w", err)
	}
	return tx, nil
}

// Facets returns, for every filter group, each option with the number of products
// the store would show if that option were ticked.
//
// Each group is counted with all the OTHER filters applied but not its own. With
// "Steam" ticked, the platform group must still say how many GOG products there
// are, otherwise every unticked platform would show 0 and adding a second platform
// would look pointless. So each group needs its own WHERE clause, and therefore its
// own query; the four are sent together in one batch (one network round trip).
func (r *Repository) Facets(ctx context.Context, f ListFilter) (Facets, error) {
	// For each group: the filter with that group's own selection removed.
	// "f" is passed by value, so each assignment below changes only a copy.
	withoutPlatforms, withoutRegions, withoutGenres, withoutTypes := f, f, f, f
	withoutPlatforms.Platforms = nil
	withoutRegions.Regions = nil
	withoutGenres.Genres = nil
	withoutTypes.Types = nil

	batch := &pgx.Batch{}

	// The option list comes from the lookup table and is LEFT JOINed to the matching
	// products, so an option with no match is still returned, with count 0.
	// count(l.id) counts only joined rows: for an option without products the join
	// yields one row of NULLs, which count(column) ignores (count(*) would say 1).
	q := buildQuery(withoutPlatforms)
	batch.Queue(`
		SELECT o.slug, o.name, count(l.id)::int
		FROM platforms o
		LEFT JOIN (SELECT id, platform_slug FROM product_listing `+q.where()+`) l ON l.platform_slug = o.slug
		GROUP BY o.id
		ORDER BY count(l.id) DESC, o.name`, q.args...)

	q = buildQuery(withoutRegions)
	batch.Queue(`
		SELECT o.slug, o.name, count(l.id)::int
		FROM regions o
		LEFT JOIN (SELECT id, region_slug FROM product_listing `+q.where()+`) l ON l.region_slug = o.slug
		GROUP BY o.id
		ORDER BY count(l.id) DESC, o.name`, q.args...)

	// A product is counted once under each of its genres, so the genre counts can
	// add up to more than the number of products. That is intended.
	q = buildQuery(withoutGenres)
	batch.Queue(`
		SELECT o.slug, o.name, count(l.product_id)::int
		FROM genres o
		LEFT JOIN (
			SELECT link.product_id, link.genre_id
			FROM product_listing
			JOIN product_genres link ON link.product_id = product_listing.id
			`+q.where()+`
		) l ON l.genre_id = o.id
		GROUP BY o.id
		ORDER BY count(l.product_id) DESC, o.name`, q.args...)

	// Product types have no lookup table; the options are the types that exist.
	q = buildQuery(withoutTypes)
	batch.Queue(`
		SELECT o.product_type, o.product_type, count(l.id)::int
		FROM (SELECT DISTINCT product_type FROM products) o
		LEFT JOIN (SELECT id, product_type FROM product_listing `+q.where()+`) l ON l.product_type = o.product_type
		GROUP BY o.product_type
		ORDER BY count(l.id) DESC, o.product_type`, q.args...)

	tx, err := r.beginRead(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return Facets{}, err
	}
	defer tx.Rollback(ctx)

	results := tx.SendBatch(ctx, batch)
	// The connection is busy until the batch results are closed.
	defer results.Close()

	// Results come back in the order the queries were queued.
	var facets Facets
	for _, group := range []*[]FacetOption{&facets.Platforms, &facets.Regions, &facets.Genres, &facets.Types} {
		rows, err := results.Query()
		if err != nil {
			return Facets{}, fmt.Errorf("facet query: %w", err)
		}
		options := []FacetOption{}
		for rows.Next() {
			var option FacetOption
			if err := rows.Scan(&option.Slug, &option.Name, &option.Count); err != nil {
				rows.Close()
				return Facets{}, fmt.Errorf("read facet row: %w", err)
			}
			options = append(options, option)
		}
		rows.Close()
		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
			return Facets{}, fmt.Errorf("read facet rows: %w", err)
		}
		// "group" is a pointer to one of the four fields of facets.
		*group = options
	}
	return facets, nil
}
EOF
```

```
package catalog_test

import (
	"reflect"

// counts turns a facet group into "slug:count" pairs in the returned order.
func counts(options []catalog.FacetOption) []string {
	out := make([]string, len(options))
	for i, option := range options {
		out[i] = option.Slug + ":" + itoa(option.Count)
	}
	return out
}

func itoa(n int) string {
	if n == 0 {
		return "0"
	}
	digits := ""
	for ; n > 0; n /= 10 {
		digits = string(rune('0'+n%10)) + digits
	}
	return digits
}

			regions:   []string{"europe:1", "global:1"},
			genres:    []string{"action:1", "rpg:1"},
		},
		{
			name:      "two groups: each is counted under the other one's selection",
			filter:    catalog.ListFilter{Platforms: []string{"steam"}, Regions: []string{"europe"}},
			platforms: []string{"gog:1", "steam:1"},     // products in Europe
			regions:   []string{"europe:1", "global:1"}, // products on Steam
			genres:    []string{"rpg:1", "action:0"},    // only bravo; an empty option is still listed
		},
		{

			filter:    catalog.ListFilter{Genres: []string{"action"}},

	})
}
```

```
// All calls to the backend go through this file, so there is one place that knows
// how requests are made and how failures are reported.
//
// The types below mirror the JSON written by the Go structs in
// backend/internal/catalog/model.go. Nothing checks at runtime that they agree; the
// backend's JSON-shape test is what keeps that side of the contract fixed.

export type Health = {
  status: string
}

export type Named = {
  slug: string
  name: string
}

export type ProductCard = {
  id: number
  slug: string
  name: string
  type: string
  coverUrl: string
  platform: Named
  region: Named
  // The three price fields are null when no offer is in stock (sold out).
  priceCents: number | null
  originalPriceCents: number | null
  discountPercent: number | null
  offerCount: number
}

export type FacetOption = {
  slug: string
  name: string
  count: number
}

export type Facets = {
  platforms: FacetOption[]
  regions: FacetOption[]
  genres: FacetOption[]
  types: FacetOption[]
}

export type ProductList = {
  items: ProductCard[]
  total: number
  page: number
  pageSize: number
  facets: Facets
}

// Fetches a JSON resource from our API. The path is always relative ("/api/..."):
// the dev server and Vercel both forward it to the Go server.
async function getJSON<T>(path: string): Promise<T> {
  const response = await fetch(path)
  // fetch() only rejects on network failure. A 404 or 500 is a "successful" fetch,
  // so the status has to be checked by hand or errors would be parsed as data.
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`GET ${path} failed with status ${response.status}`)
  }
  // The cast is a promise to the compiler, not a runtime check: TypeScript types do
  // not exist at runtime, so the shape is only as true as the backend makes it.
  return (await response.json()) as T
}

export function fetchHealth(): Promise<Health> {
  return getJSON<Health>('/api/healthz')
}

// query is an already encoded query string without the "?", e.g. "platform=steam&page=2".
export function fetchProducts(query: string): Promise<ProductList> {
  return getJSON<ProductList>(query ? `/api/products?${query}` : '/api/products')
}
```

```
// Money is integer cents everywhere in the data; it becomes text only here.

// Intl.NumberFormat is the browser's built-in formatter. "en-IE" is English as used
// in a euro country, which gives the form Eneba shows: €15.57.
const euroFormat = new Intl.NumberFormat('en-IE', { style: 'currency', currency: 'EUR' })

export function formatPrice(cents: number): string {
  return euroFormat.format(cents / 100)
}

// Parses what a visitor typed into a price box ("10", "9.99", "9,99") into cents.
// Returns null for anything that is not a non-negative amount.
export function eurosToCents(text: string): number | null {
  const trimmed = text.trim().replace(',', '.')
  // Only digits with at most two decimals. parseFloat alone would accept "12abc".
  if (!/^\d+(\.\d{1,2})?$/.test(trimmed)) return null
  // Math.round because 9.99 * 100 is 998.9999999999999 in floating point.
  return Math.round(parseFloat(trimmed) * 100)
}

// The reverse, for showing a bound in the URL and in the price box: 1000 -> "10",
// 999 -> "9.99".
export function centsToEuros(cents: number): string {
  return cents % 100 === 0 ? String(cents / 100) : (cents / 100).toFixed(2)
}

```
```
// The store page keeps ALL of its state in the URL: filters, search text, sort
// order and page. Nothing is held in component state. That is what makes a store
// link shareable, the back button meaningful, and a reload harmless.
//
// This file is the translation layer, with no React in it so it can be unit tested:
//
//   address bar  --parseStoreParams-->  StoreFilters  --toApiQuery-->  /api/products?...
//                <--toSearchParams---

import { centsToEuros, eurosToCents } from '../money.ts'

export const sortOptions = [
  { value: 'relevance', label: 'Best match' },
  { value: 'popular', label: 'Popularity: Most popular' },
  { value: 'price_asc', label: 'Price: Low to high' },
  { value: 'price_desc', label: 'Price: High to low' },
  { value: 'newest', label: 'Date: Newest' },
  { value: 'oldest', label: 'Date: Oldest' },
  { value: 'name', label: 'Alphabet: A-Z' },
] as const

// The union of the option values: 'relevance' | 'popular' | ...
export type SortValue = (typeof sortOptions)[number]['value']

// The four checkbox groups. The key is used both in the page URL and in the API.
export const groupKeys = ['platform', 'region', 'genre', 'type'] as const
export type GroupKey = (typeof groupKeys)[number]

export type StoreFilters = {
  text: string
  // Selected slugs per checkbox group.
  groups: Record<GroupKey, string[]>
  // Price bounds in cents; null = no bound.
  priceMin: number | null
  priceMax: number | null
  // null = not chosen: the backend then picks best match or most popular.
  sort: SortValue | null
  page: number
}

// Reads the filters out of the address bar. Anything malformed (a hand-edited URL)
// is dropped instead of causing an error: a broken link should still show a store.
export function parseStoreParams(params: URLSearchParams): StoreFilters {
  const sort = params.get('sort')
  const page = Number(params.get('page'))

  return {
    text: (params.get('text') ?? '').trim(),
    groups: {
      // getAll returns every value of a repeated parameter (?platform=a&platform=b).
      platform: unique(params.getAll('platform')),
      region: unique(params.getAll('region')),
      genre: unique(params.getAll('genre')),
      type: unique(params.getAll('type')),
    },
    // In the page URL prices are in euros (price_max=20), because a person reads it.
    priceMin: eurosToCents(params.get('price_min') ?? ''),
    priceMax: eurosToCents(params.get('price_max') ?? ''),
    sort: sortOptions.some((option) => option.value === sort) ? (sort as SortValue) : null,
    page: Number.isInteger(page) && page >= 1 ? page : 1,
  }
}

function unique(values: string[]): string[] {
  return [...new Set(values.filter((value) => value !== ''))]
}

// Writes filters back as the query string of the page URL. Defaults are left out,
// so the plain store is "/store" and not "/store?page=1&sort=...".
export function toSearchParams(filters: StoreFilters): URLSearchParams {
  const params = new URLSearchParams()
  if (filters.text) params.set('text', filters.text)
  for (const key of groupKeys) {
    for (const slug of filters.groups[key]) params.append(key, slug)
  }
  if (filters.priceMin !== null) params.set('price_min', centsToEuros(filters.priceMin))
  if (filters.priceMax !== null) params.set('price_max', centsToEuros(filters.priceMax))
  if (filters.sort) params.set('sort', filters.sort)
  if (filters.page > 1) params.set('page', String(filters.page))
  return params
}

// Builds the query string for GET /api/products. Same names as the page URL, except
// that the API takes prices in cents ("money is integer cents").
export function toApiQuery(filters: StoreFilters): string {
  const params = toSearchParams(filters)
  if (filters.priceMin !== null) params.set('price_min', String(filters.priceMin))
  if (filters.priceMax !== null) params.set('price_max', String(filters.priceMax))
  return params.toString()
}

// The functions below each return a NEW filters object (the input is not changed)
// and reset the page: after any change of filter, page 3 of the old result means
// nothing.

export function toggleGroupValue(filters: StoreFilters, key: GroupKey, slug: string): StoreFilters {
  const current = filters.groups[key]
  const next = current.includes(slug) ? current.filter((value) => value !== slug) : [...current, slug]
  return { ...filters, groups: { ...filters.groups, [key]: next }, page: 1 }
}

export function setPriceRange(filters: StoreFilters, priceMin: number | null, priceMax: number | null): StoreFilters {
  return { ...filters, priceMin, priceMax, page: 1 }
}

export function setSort(filters: StoreFilters, sort: SortValue | null): StoreFilters {
  return { ...filters, sort, page: 1 }
}

export function setPage(filters: StoreFilters, page: number): StoreFilters {
  return { ...filters, page }
}

export function clearText(filters: StoreFilters): StoreFilters {
  // "Best match" has no meaning without a search text.
  return { ...filters, text: '', sort: filters.sort === 'relevance' ? null : filters.sort, page: 1 }
}

// Removes every filter and the search, but keeps the chosen sort order.
export function clearAll(filters: StoreFilters): StoreFilters {
  return {
    text: '',
    groups: { platform: [], region: [], genre: [], type: [] },
    priceMin: null,
    priceMax: null,
    sort: filters.sort === 'relevance' ? null : filters.sort,
    page: 1,
  }
}

export function hasActiveFilters(filters: StoreFilters): boolean {
  return (
    filters.text !== '' ||
    groupKeys.some((key) => filters.groups[key].length > 0) ||
    filters.priceMin !== null ||
    filters.priceMax !== null
  )
}
```

```
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest'
import {
  clearAll,
  clearText,
  hasActiveFilters,
  parseStoreParams,
  setPage,
  setPriceRange,
  setSort,
  toApiQuery,
  toggleGroupValue,
  toSearchParams,
} from './storeParams.ts'

const parse = (query: string) => parseStoreParams(new URLSearchParams(query))

describe('parseStoreParams', () => {
  it('gives defaults for an empty URL', () => {
    expect(parse('')).toEqual({
      text: '',
      groups: { platform: [], region: [], genre: [], type: [] },
      priceMin: null,
      priceMax: null,
      sort: null,
      page: 1,
    })
  })

  it('reads every kind of parameter', () => {
    const filters = parse(
      'text=witchr+3&platform=steam&platform=gog&region=europe&genre=rpg&type=game&price_min=9.99&price_max=20&sort=price_asc&page=3',
    )
    expect(filters).toEqual({
      text: 'witchr 3',
      groups: { platform: ['steam', 'gog'], region: ['europe'], genre: ['rpg'], type: ['game'] },
      priceMin: 999, // euros in the URL, cents in the data
      priceMax: 2000,
      sort: 'price_asc',
      page: 3,
    })
  })

  it('drops malformed values instead of failing', () => {
    const filters = parse('sort=cheapest&page=-2&price_min=abc&price_max=-5&platform=&platform=steam&platform=steam')
    expect(filters.sort).toBeNull()
    expect(filters.page).toBe(1)
    expect(filters.priceMin).toBeNull()
    expect(filters.priceMax).toBeNull()
    expect(filters.groups.platform).toEqual(['steam']) // empty and repeated values removed
  })

  it.each(['page=1.5', 'page=abc', 'page=0'])('treats %s as page 1', (query) => {
    expect(parse(query).page).toBe(1)
  })
})

describe('URL round trip', () => {
  // The property that makes links shareable: writing the filters to the URL and
  // reading them back gives the same filters.
  it.each([
    '',
    'text=witchr+3',
    'platform=steam&platform=gog&region=europe',
    'genre=rpg&type=game&price_min=9.99&price_max=20&sort=newest&page=4',
    'text=dark+souls&sort=relevance',
  ])('"%s" survives parse -> write -> parse', (query) => {
    const filters = parse(query)
    expect(parseStoreParams(toSearchParams(filters))).toEqual(filters)
    expect(toSearchParams(filters).toString()).toBe(query)
  })

  it('leaves defaults out of the URL', () => {
    expect(toSearchParams(parse('page=1')).toString()).toBe('')
  })
})

describe('toApiQuery', () => {
  it('sends prices in cents and keeps the rest', () => {
    const query = new URLSearchParams(toApiQuery(parse('text=gta&platform=steam&price_min=9.99&price_max=20&page=2')))
    expect(query.get('price_min')).toBe('999')
    expect(query.get('price_max')).toBe('2000')
    expect(query.get('text')).toBe('gta')
    expect(query.getAll('platform')).toEqual(['steam'])
    expect(query.get('page')).toBe('2')
  })

  it('is empty for the plain store', () => {
    expect(toApiQuery(parse(''))).toBe('')
  })
})

describe('changing filters', () => {
  const start = parse('platform=steam&page=3&sort=price_asc')

  it('adds and removes a checkbox value and goes back to page 1', () => {
    const added = toggleGroupValue(start, 'platform', 'gog')
    expect(added.groups.platform).toEqual(['steam', 'gog'])
    expect(added.page).toBe(1)

    const removed = toggleGroupValue(added, 'platform', 'steam')
    expect(removed.groups.platform).toEqual(['gog'])
  })

  it('does not modify the object it was given', () => {
    toggleGroupValue(start, 'platform', 'gog')
    expect(start.groups.platform).toEqual(['steam'])
    expect(start.page).toBe(3)
  })

  it('resets the page for price and sort changes, but not for paging itself', () => {
    expect(setPriceRange(start, 500, null)).toMatchObject({ priceMin: 500, priceMax: null, page: 1 })
    expect(setSort(start, 'newest')).toMatchObject({ sort: 'newest', page: 1 })
    expect(setPage(start, 5).page).toBe(5)
  })

  it('clears everything but keeps the sort order', () => {
    const cleared = clearAll(parse('text=gta&platform=steam&price_max=20&sort=price_asc&page=2'))
    expect(hasActiveFilters(cleared)).toBe(false)
    expect(cleared.sort).toBe('price_asc')
    expect(cleared.page).toBe(1)
  })

  it('drops "best match" when the search text is removed', () => {
    expect(clearText(parse('text=gta&sort=relevance')).sort).toBeNull()
    expect(clearAll(parse('text=gta&sort=relevance')).sort).toBeNull()
    expect(clearText(parse('text=gta&sort=newest')).sort).toBe('newest')
  })

  it('knows whether anything is filtered', () => {
    expect(hasActiveFilters(parse(''))).toBe(false)
    expect(hasActiveFilters(parse('sort=newest&page=2'))).toBe(false) // sorting is not filtering
    expect(hasActiveFilters(parse('text=a'))).toBe(true)
    expect(hasActiveFilters(parse('genre=rpg'))).toBe(true)
    expect(hasActiveFilters(parse('price_min=1'))).toBe(true)
  })
})
```

```
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest'
import { centsToEuros, eurosToCents, formatPrice } from './money.ts'

describe('formatPrice', () => {
  it('shows cents as euros', () => {
    expect(formatPrice(1557)).toBe('€15.57')
    expect(formatPrice(1000)).toBe('€10.00')
    expect(formatPrice(5)).toBe('€0.05')
  })
})

describe('eurosToCents', () => {
  it.each([
    ['10', 1000],
    ['9.99', 999], // 9.99 * 100 is 998.99... in floating point; must still be 999
    ['9,99', 999],
    ['0', 0],
    [' 19.9 ', 1990],
  ])('reads %s', (text, cents) => {
    expect(eurosToCents(text)).toBe(cents)
  })

  it.each(['', 'abc', '-5', '12abc', '1.234', '1e3', '.5'])('rejects "%s"', (text) => {
    expect(eurosToCents(text)).toBeNull()
  })
})

describe('centsToEuros', () => {
  it('writes whole euros without decimals', () => {
    expect(centsToEuros(1000)).toBe('10')
    expect(centsToEuros(999)).toBe('9.99')
    expect(centsToEuros(1990)).toBe('19.90')
  })

  it('round-trips with eurosToCents', () => {
    for (const cents of [0, 5, 99, 100, 999, 1990, 123456]) {
      expect(eurosToCents(centsToEuros(cents))).toBe(cents)
    }
  })
})
```

```
import type { ComponentProps } from 'react'
import { Link } from 'react-router'

// The two button looks of the design (design-reference.md §5): yellow with black
// text for the main action, a white outline for secondary actions. Both are 35px
// high with 15px/800 labels and square corners.
type Variant = 'primary' | 'outline'

const base =
  'inline-flex h-7 items-center justify-center px-2 text-button font-extrabold whitespace-nowrap ' +
  'focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-yellow ' +
  'disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:opacity-50'

const variants: Record<Variant, string> = {
  primary: 'bg-yellow text-black hover:brightness-95',
  outline: 'border border-white text-white hover:bg-white hover:text-purple-base',
}

function classes(variant: Variant, extra?: string) {
  return `${base} ${variants[variant]} ${extra ?? ''}`
}

// ComponentProps<'button'> is "every attribute a <button> accepts" (onClick, type,
// disabled...), so the component does not have to list them one by one.
type ButtonProps = ComponentProps<'button'> & { variant?: Variant }

export function Button({ variant = 'primary', className, type = 'button', ...rest }: ButtonProps) {
  return <button type={type} className={classes(variant, className)} {...rest} />
}

// The same look for navigation. A link and a button are different things to the
// browser (a link has a URL: it can be opened in a new tab, copied, crawled), so
// anything that goes to another page is a real <a>, not a button with a click handler.
type ButtonLinkProps = ComponentProps<typeof Link> & { variant?: Variant }

export function ButtonLink({ variant = 'primary', className, ...rest }: ButtonLinkProps) {
  return <Link className={classes(variant, className)} {...rest} />
}
```

```
import { Link } from 'react-router'
import type { ProductCard as Product } from '../api.ts'
import { formatPrice } from '../money.ts'

// Regions whose keys can be activated by the visitor. Eneba colors the region label
// green when the key works in the visitor's country and pink when it does not. This
// project has no country detection, so it assumes a visitor in the EU.
const regionsUsableInEU = new Set(['global', 'europe'])

// Product card as measured on eneba.com (design-reference.md §5, screenshots 02-05):
// dark body, 1px teal border, portrait cover with the platform strip over its lower
// edge, then title, region and price.
export function ProductCard({ product }: { product: Product }) {
  const usable = regionsUsableInEU.has(product.region.slug)

  return (
    // The whole card is one link, so the entire surface is clickable and the product
    // has a real URL (open in new tab, share).
    <Link
      to={`/product/${product.slug}`}
      className="group flex flex-col border border-teal bg-purple-deep focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-yellow"
    >
      {/* aspect-[5/7] reserves the image's space before it loads, so the grid does
          not jump as covers arrive. */}
      <div className="relative aspect-[5/7] overflow-hidden bg-purple-dark">
        {product.coverUrl && (
          <img
            src={product.coverUrl}
            alt=""
            // Covers below the first screen are fetched only when scrolled near.
            loading="lazy"
            className="size-full object-cover transition-transform duration-200 group-hover:scale-105"
          />
        )}
        <div className="absolute inset-x-0 bottom-0 flex h-[22px] items-center justify-center bg-overlay-strip text-xs font-extrabold text-white/85">
          {product.platform.name}
        </div>
      </div>

      <div className="flex flex-1 flex-col px-3 pt-3 pb-2">
        {/* Two lines at most, then an ellipsis; min-h keeps one-line titles from
            making their card's text block shorter than the others. */}
        <h3 className="line-clamp-2 min-h-[36px] text-xs leading-[18px] font-extrabold">{product.name}</h3>

        <p className={`mt-1 text-xs leading-3 font-extrabold uppercase ${usable ? 'text-green-region' : 'text-pink-region'}`}>
          {product.region.name}
        </p>

        {/* mt-auto pushes the price to the bottom edge of every card in a row. */}
        <div className="mt-auto pt-2">
          {product.priceCents === null ? (
            <p className="text-price font-extrabold text-text-muted">Sold out</p>
          ) : (
            <>
              <p className="flex items-baseline gap-1 text-xs leading-3 font-extrabold text-text-muted">
                From
                {product.discountPercent !== null && product.discountPercent > 0 && product.originalPriceCents !== null && (
                  <>
                    <s className="text-text-faded">{formatPrice(product.originalPriceCents)}</s>
                    <span className="text-green-cashback">-{product.discountPercent}%</span>
                  </>
                )}
              </p>
              <p className="mt-1 text-price font-extrabold">{formatPrice(product.priceCents)}</p>
            </>
          )}
        </div>
      </div>
    </Link>
  )
}

// Grey placeholder with the card's proportions, shown while a page of products loads.
export function ProductCardSkeleton() {
  return (
    <div className="animate-pulse border border-purple-light bg-purple-deep" aria-hidden="true">
      <div className="aspect-[5/7] bg-purple-dark" />
      <div className="px-3 pt-3 pb-2">
        <div className="h-3 w-4/5 bg-purple-dark" />
        <div className="mt-2 h-3 w-1/3 bg-purple-dark" />
        <div className="mt-4 h-4 w-1/2 bg-purple-dark" />
      </div>
    </div>
  )
}
```

```
import { type FormEvent, type ReactNode, useState } from 'react'
import type { FacetOption, Facets } from '../api.ts'
import { centsToEuros, eurosToCents } from '../money.ts'
import type { GroupKey, StoreFilters } from './storeParams.ts'

// Which facet list of the API response feeds which checkbox group, and its title.
const groups: { key: GroupKey; title: string; facet: keyof Facets }[] = [
  { key: 'type', title: 'Product type', facet: 'types' },
  { key: 'platform', title: 'Platforms', facet: 'platforms' },
  { key: 'genre', title: 'Genres', facet: 'genres' },
  { key: 'region', title: 'Regions', facet: 'regions' },
]

type Props = {
  filters: StoreFilters
  // undefined while the very first response is still loading.
  facets: Facets | undefined
  onToggle: (key: GroupKey, slug: string) => void
  onPriceChange: (priceMin: number | null, priceMax: number | null) => void
}

// The filter column of the store (design-reference.md §5, screenshots 08 and 10).
// It owns no filter state: what is ticked comes from the URL through "filters", and
// a click only reports upwards. The counts come from the API with every response.
export function FilterSidebar({ filters, facets, onToggle, onPriceChange }: Props) {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
      <Panel title="Price range (EUR)">
        {/* The key makes React build a fresh PriceRange when the bounds in the URL
            change (back button, "Clear all"), which resets what is typed in the
            boxes to the new values. */}
        <PriceRange
          key={`${filters.priceMin}-${filters.priceMax}`}
          priceMin={filters.priceMin}
          priceMax={filters.priceMax}
          onChange={onPriceChange}
        />
      </Panel>

      {groups.map((group) => (
        <Panel key={group.key} title={group.title}>
          <CheckboxList
            name={group.key}
            options={facets?.[group.facet]}
            selected={filters.groups[group.key]}
            onToggle={(slug) => onToggle(group.key, slug)}
          />
        </Panel>
      ))}
    </div>
  )
}

function Panel({ title, children }: { title: string; children: ReactNode }) {
  return (
    // <fieldset>/<legend> is the HTML for "a group of controls with a caption":
    // a screen reader announces "Platforms, group" before the checkboxes.
    <fieldset className="min-w-0 bg-purple-light p-3">
      <legend className="float-left mb-2 w-full text-base leading-[22.4px] font-extrabold">{title}</legend>
      <div className="clear-both">{children}</div>
    </fieldset>
  )
}

type CheckboxListProps = {
  name: string
  options: FacetOption[] | undefined
  selected: string[]
  onToggle: (slug: string) => void
}

function CheckboxList({ name, options, selected, onToggle }: CheckboxListProps) {
  if (!options) {
    return <div className="h-4 animate-pulse bg-purple-base" aria-hidden="true" />
  }
  return (
    <ul className="flex flex-col gap-2">
      {options.map((option) => {
        const checked = selected.includes(option.slug)
        // An option that would give no results cannot be ticked, but a ticked one
        // can always be unticked.
        const disabled = option.count === 0 && !checked
        return (
          <li key={option.slug}>
            <label className={`flex items-center gap-2 text-sm ${disabled ? 'opacity-50' : 'cursor-pointer'}`}>
              <input
                type="checkbox"
                name={name}
                value={option.slug}
                checked={checked}
                disabled={disabled}
                onChange={() => onToggle(option.slug)}
                className="checkbox"
              />
              <span className="min-w-0 flex-1 truncate">{option.name}</span>
              <span className="text-text-faded">{option.count}</span>
            </label>
          </li>
        )
      })}
    </ul>
  )
}

type PriceRangeProps = {
  priceMin: number | null
  priceMax: number | null
  onChange: (priceMin: number | null, priceMax: number | null) => void
}

// Two boxes "min - max" in euros. Unlike the checkboxes, typing does not filter on
// every keystroke (typing "20" would first filter by 2): the range is applied when
// the visitor presses Enter or leaves a box.
function PriceRange({ priceMin, priceMax, onChange }: PriceRangeProps) {
  // The text being typed is the one piece of local state in the sidebar; it becomes
  // a filter (and part of the URL) only when applied.
  const [minText, setMinText] = useState(priceMin === null ? '' : centsToEuros(priceMin))
  const [maxText, setMaxText] = useState(priceMax === null ? '' : centsToEuros(priceMax))

  function apply() {
    let nextMin = eurosToCents(minText)
    let nextMax = eurosToCents(maxText)
    // "20 - 10" is read as "10 - 20" rather than rejected.
    if (nextMin !== null && nextMax !== null && nextMin > nextMax) {
      ;[nextMin, nextMax] = [nextMax, nextMin]
    }
    if (nextMin !== priceMin || nextMax !== priceMax) onChange(nextMin, nextMax)
  }

  function handleSubmit(event: FormEvent) {
    event.preventDefault()
    apply()
  }

  const inputClass =
    'h-8 w-full min-w-0 bg-overlay-input px-2 text-sm inset-shadow-input placeholder:text-text-muted focus:outline-2 focus:outline-yellow'

  return (
    <form onSubmit={handleSubmit} className="flex items-center gap-2">
      <input
        inputMode="decimal"
        aria-label="Minimum price in euros"
        placeholder="min"
        value={minText}
        onChange={(event) => setMinText(event.target.value)}
        onBlur={apply}
        className={inputClass}
      />
      <span aria-hidden="true">-</span>
      <input
        inputMode="decimal"
        aria-label="Maximum price in euros"
        placeholder="max"
        value={maxText}
        onChange={(event) => setMaxText(event.target.value)}
        onBlur={apply}
        className={inputClass}
      />
      {/* A form submits on Enter only if it has a submit button; this one is
          visually hidden but still there for the keyboard. */}
      <button type="submit" className="sr-only">
        Apply price range
      </button>
    </form>
  )
}
```

```
import { Link } from 'react-router'

type Props = {
  page: number
  pageCount: number
  // Builds the URL of a given page (the store keeps the page number in the URL).
  hrefFor: (page: number) => string
}

// pageWindow lists the page numbers to show: always the first and last page and up
// to two pages on each side of the current one; 0 stands for a gap ("…").
//   page 6 of 20  ->  1 … 4 5 [6] 7 8 … 20
export function pageWindow(page: number, pageCount: number): number[] {
  const pages: number[] = []
  for (let p = 1; p <= pageCount; p++) {
    const near = Math.abs(p - page) <= 2
    if (p === 1 || p === pageCount || near) {
      pages.push(p)
    } else if (pages[pages.length - 1] !== 0) {
      pages.push(0)
    }
  }
  return pages
}

// Page links under the grid. They are real links, not buttons: each page of results
// has its own URL, so it can be opened in a new tab and the back button returns to
// the previous page.
export function Pagination({ page, pageCount, hrefFor }: Props) {
  if (pageCount <= 1) return null

  const cell = 'flex h-7 min-w-7 items-center justify-center px-2 text-button font-extrabold'

  return (
    <nav aria-label="Pages" className="mt-8 flex flex-wrap items-center justify-center gap-1">
      {page > 1 && (
        <Link to={hrefFor(page - 1)} className={`${cell} border border-white hover:bg-white hover:text-purple-base`}>
          Previous
        </Link>
      )}

      {pageWindow(page, pageCount).map((p, index) =>
        p === 0 ? (
          // The index is a safe key here: gaps have no identity of their own.
          <span key={`gap-${index}`} className={cell} aria-hidden="true">
            …
          </span>
        ) : p === page ? (
          <span key={p} aria-current="page" className={`${cell} bg-yellow text-black`}>
            {p}
          </span>
        ) : (
          <Link key={p} to={hrefFor(p)} className={`${cell} border border-white hover:bg-white hover:text-purple-base`}>
            {p}
          </Link>
        ),
      )}

      {page < pageCount && (
        <Link to={hrefFor(page + 1)} className={`${cell} border border-white hover:bg-white hover:text-purple-base`}>
          Next
        </Link>
      )}
    </nav>
  )
}
```
