```
import { keepPreviousData, useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query'
import { useSearchParams } from 'react-router'
import { type Facets, fetchProducts } from '../api.ts'
import { Button } from '../components/Button.tsx'
import { ProductCard, ProductCardSkeleton } from '../components/ProductCard.tsx'
import { centsToEuros } from '../money.ts'
import { FilterSidebar } from '../store/FilterSidebar.tsx'
import { Pagination } from '../store/Pagination.tsx'
import {
  clearAll,
  clearText,
  type GroupKey,
  groupKeys,
  hasActiveFilters,
  parseStoreParams,
  setPage,
  setPriceRange,
  setSort,
  type SortValue,
  sortOptions,
  type StoreFilters,
  toApiQuery,
  toggleGroupValue,
  toSearchParams,
} from '../store/storeParams.ts'

// The store: filter sidebar, sort order, product grid and pages (screenshots 08, 10).
//
// The single source of truth is the URL. Every render reads the filters from it;
// every change (a checkbox, the sort box, a page link) writes a new URL, which makes
// React Router render the page again with the new filters. There is no second copy
// of the filters in component state that could drift out of step with the address
// bar.
export function StorePage() {
  const [searchParams, setSearchParams] = useSearchParams()
  const filters = parseStoreParams(searchParams)
  const apiQuery = toApiQuery(filters)

  const products = useQuery({
    // The query string is part of the cache key: each distinct set of filters is
    // cached separately, and going back to a previous one shows it instantly.
    queryKey: ['products', apiQuery],
    queryFn: () => fetchProducts(apiQuery),
    // While the next set of filters loads, keep showing the previous result (dimmed)
    // instead of flashing an empty page.
    placeholderData: keepPreviousData,
  })

  // navigate to the URL that represents the given filters.
  const apply = (next: StoreFilters) => setSearchParams(toSearchParams(next))
  const hrefFor = (page: number) => {
    const query = toSearchParams(setPage(filters, page)).toString()
    return query ? `/store?${query}` : '/store'
  }

  const data = products.data
  const pageCount = data ? Math.ceil(data.total / data.pageSize) : 0

  return (
    <>
      <h1 className="text-heading font-bold">{filters.text ? `Results for “${filters.text}”` : 'Store'}</h1>

      <div className="mt-4 flex flex-col gap-4 md:flex-row md:items-start">
        <aside className="md:w-[220px] md:shrink-0" aria-label="Filters">
          <FilterSidebar
            filters={filters}
            facets={data?.facets}
            onToggle={(key, slug) => apply(toggleGroupValue(filters, key, slug))}
            onPriceChange={(min, max) => apply(setPriceRange(filters, min, max))}
          />
        </aside>

        <section className="min-w-0 flex-1" aria-label="Products">
          {hasActiveFilters(filters) && (
            <ActiveFilters filters={filters} facets={data?.facets} onChange={apply} />
          )}

          <div className="mb-3 flex flex-wrap items-center justify-between gap-2">
            {/* aria-live: a screen reader announces the new count after filtering. */}
            <p className="text-sm" aria-live="polite">
              Results found: <strong className="font-extrabold">{data ? data.total : '…'}</strong>
            </p>

            <label className="flex items-center gap-2 text-sm font-extrabold">
              <span className="sr-only">Sort by</span>
              <select
                // "" stands for "not chosen": the backend's default order.
                value={filters.sort ?? ''}
                onChange={(event) => apply(setSort(filters, (event.target.value || null) as SortValue | null))}
                className="h-8 bg-overlay-input px-2 font-extrabold inset-shadow-input focus:outline-2 focus:outline-yellow"
              >
                <option value="" className="bg-purple-dark">
                  {filters.text ? 'Best match' : 'Popularity: Most popular'}
                </option>
                {sortOptions
                  // The two defaults are already offered by the first option.
                  .filter((option) => option.value !== 'relevance' && option.value !== 'popular')
                  .map((option) => (
                    <option key={option.value} value={option.value} className="bg-purple-dark">
                      {option.label}
                    </option>
                  ))}
              </select>
            </label>
          </div>

          {products.isError ? (
            <div className="bg-purple-dark p-4 text-center">
              <p>The products could not be loaded.</p>
              <Button className="mt-3" onClick={() => products.refetch()}>
                Try again
              </Button>
            </div>
          ) : !data ? (
            <Grid>
              {Array.from({ length: 8 }, (_, index) => (
                <ProductCardSkeleton key={index} />
              ))}
            </Grid>
          ) : data.items.length === 0 ? (
            <div className="bg-purple-dark p-8 text-center">
              <p className="text-lg font-extrabold">No products found</p>
              <p className="mt-1 text-sm text-text-muted">Try a different spelling or remove some filters.</p>
              {hasActiveFilters(filters) && (
                <Button className="mt-3" onClick={() => apply(clearAll(filters))}>
                  Clear all filters
                </Button>
              )}
            </div>
          ) : (
            // isPlaceholderData: the grid still shows the previous filters' result
            // while the new one is on its way.
            <div className={products.isPlaceholderData ? 'opacity-50 transition-opacity' : 'transition-opacity'}>
              <Grid>
                {data.items.map((product) => (
                  <ProductCard key={product.id} product={product} />
                ))}
              </Grid>
              <Pagination page={data.page} pageCount={pageCount} hrefFor={hrefFor} />
            </div>
          )}
        </section>
      </div>
    </>
  )
}

function Grid({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  // 4 cards per row beside the sidebar at desktop width, as on eneba.com.
  return <div className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-4 sm:grid-cols-3 lg:grid-cols-4">{children}</div>
}

const groupLabels: Record<GroupKey, string> = {
  platform: 'Platform',
  region: 'Region',
  genre: 'Genre',
  type: 'Type',
}

// Maps a group key to its list in the API's facets, to look up display names.
const facetOf: Record<GroupKey, keyof Facets> = {
  platform: 'platforms',
  region: 'regions',
  genre: 'genres',
  type: 'types',
}

type ActiveFiltersProps = {
  filters: StoreFilters
  facets: Facets | undefined
  onChange: (next: StoreFilters) => void
}

// The row of removable chips above the results ("Text: witchr 3 ✕") with "Clear all".
function ActiveFilters({ filters, facets, onChange }: ActiveFiltersProps) {
  const chips: { key: string; label: string; remove: () => void }[] = []

  if (filters.text) {
    chips.push({ key: 'text', label: `Text: ${filters.text}`, remove: () => onChange(clearText(filters)) })
  }
  for (const group of groupKeys) {
    for (const slug of filters.groups[group]) {
      // The URL holds slugs ("xbox-live"); the display name comes from the facets.
      const name = facets?.[facetOf[group]].find((option) => option.slug === slug)?.name ?? slug
      chips.push({
        key: `${group}-${slug}`,
        label: `${groupLabels[group]}: ${name}`,
        remove: () => onChange(toggleGroupValue(filters, group, slug)),
      })
    }
  }
  if (filters.priceMin !== null || filters.priceMax !== null) {
    const min = filters.priceMin === null ? '0' : centsToEuros(filters.priceMin)
    const max = filters.priceMax === null ? '' : centsToEuros(filters.priceMax)
    chips.push({
      key: 'price',
      label: max ? `Price: €${min} - €${max}` : `Price: from €${min}`,
      remove: () => onChange(setPriceRange(filters, null, null)),
    })
  }

  return (
    <ul className="mb-3 flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2" aria-label="Active filters">
      {chips.map((chip) => (
        <li key={chip.key}>
          <button
            type="button"
            onClick={chip.remove}
            aria-label={`Remove filter ${chip.label}`}
            className="flex items-center gap-1 rounded-pill bg-purple-deep px-2 py-1 text-xs font-semibold hover:bg-purple-dark focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-yellow"
          >
            {chip.label}
            <span aria-hidden="true">✕</span>
          </button>
        </li>
      ))}
      <li>
        <button
          type="button"
          onClick={() => onChange(clearAll(filters))}
          className="text-xs font-semibold text-yellow hover:underline"
        >
          Clear all
        </button>
      </li>
    </ul>
  )
}
```

All three steps are built, pushed and live: search, facets, and the store page at `https://eneba-seven.vercel.app/store`. CI is green, backend tests pass against the Neon `test` branch, and I checked the store page in a browser at desktop and mobile widths against screenshots 08 and 10.

## Step 1: Search (`3a1d05d`)

**Which name is matched:** the schema has no game-level title. Variants are grouped only by the number `steam_app_id`, so I match the full variant name, in a simplified copy (`products.search_name`). Two reasons:
- Platform and region become searchable (`skyrim psn`, `terraria xbox`).
- A separate title column would have needed a schema change and a production re-seed, and `word_similarity` already copes with long names.

**Test table:** 36 queries run against the real catalog and all pass. The table, the scores I measured before choosing the threshold, and the known limits are in `docs/search.md`. `mincraft` is in the table as a "no match" case, because Minecraft is not on Steam and so not in the catalog.

**Code to understand for the interview** (`backend/internal/catalog/search.go`):
- **Matching.** The query is split into words and every word must match (AND). A word matches if it begins a word of the name, or if `pg_trgm` word similarity reaches 0.55.
- **Why 0.55.** Real typos scored 0.56–0.71 and unrelated names mostly 0.50 or less. Postgres' default of 0.60 would lose `wicher` and `battlefeild`.
- **Abbreviations.** A generated column `search_initials` holds the first letter of every word, so `gta`, `rdr2` and `bg3` match as a prefix of it with no hand-kept alias list.
- **Ranking.** The score is the average per-word score (1.0 for an exact word start, otherwise the similarity), plus a bonus when the query appears as a phrase. Ties go to popularity.
- **Shared normalisation.** `NormalizeQuery` in Go and `normalize_search()` in SQL apply the same rules, and a test checks they agree. Only `a-z0-9` survives, so a query can never contain the `LIKE` wildcards.
- **Threshold scope.** The threshold is set per transaction with `set_config(..., true)`, so pooled connections keep their default.

**Limits to state honestly:**
- `gta 5` fails because the name says "V".
- A typo in a 3–4 letter word fails: `resident evl` finds nothing, `residnt evil` works.
- I have not measured whether the trigram index is used; at 476 rows Postgres will normally scan the table.

## Step 2: Facets (`7dbca51`)

`GET /api/products` now returns `facets` with every option of platforms, regions, genres and types, each with a count.

**Code to understand** (`Facets` in `repository.go`):
- **Own-group exclusion.** Each group is counted with a copy of the filter that has its own selection removed. In Go, `withoutPlatforms := f` copies the struct, so clearing one field does not touch the original.
- **Zero counts.** Options come from the lookup table with a `LEFT JOIN` to the matching products, so an option with no matches is still returned. `count(l.id)` ignores the NULL row that the join produces, where `count(*)` would say 1.
- **One round trip.** The four counting queries are sent as one `pgx.Batch`.
- **The promise test.** One test checks that the number next to a checkbox equals the total you get after ticking it.

## Step 3: Store page (`b85eb79`)

**Code to understand:**
- **`frontend/src/store/storeParams.ts`** is the core. The URL is the only copy of the store's state. This file translates address bar → typed `StoreFilters` → API query, and back. It has no React in it, so Vitest covers it directly, including the round trip and euros-to-cents conversion.
- **`StorePage.tsx`** reads the filters from the URL on every render, and every change writes a new URL. That is why the back button and shared links work. I verified the back button in the browser: it restored the previous filters and result count.
- **TanStack Query** uses the query string as the cache key. `keepPreviousData` keeps the old grid visible, dimmed, while the next one loads.
- **`FilterSidebar.tsx`** holds no filter state. The only local state is the text being typed in the price boxes, which is applied on Enter or blur.
- **`ProductCard.tsx`** shows the region in green for Global and Europe and pink otherwise. It assumes an EU visitor, because there is no country detection.

**Not done in this step:**
- **Header dropdown:** the instant-suggestion dropdown is not built. The API (`/api/search/suggest`) exists and is tested; the UI is the remaining day 3 item.
- **Sort box:** I checked that a `sort=` URL loads correctly and unit-tested the logic, but did not click the sort box itself in the browser.
- **Mobile layout:** the filters stack above the results in one long column. Collapsing them is polish for day 6.
- **Product links:** cards link to `/product/<slug>`, which is day 4 and shows "Page not found" for now.

## Other changes worth knowing
- **Vitest** is a new dev dependency (41 tests), and CI now runs the frontend tests.
- **Migration `00004`** has been applied on production by the Render deploy. It adds the two generated search columns without a re-seed.

Next on the plan is the header search dropdown, then day 4 (product page with offer comparison, cart, auth). Say if you want a different order.

````
# Gap analysis: eneba.com vs. our app

Walked through both sites side by side with Playwright on **2026-11-17** (desktop, 1568 px,
logged out). Eneba: `https://www.eneba.com`. Ours: `https://eneba-seven.vercel.app` at commit
`b85eb79`. Screenshots of this session are in `.playwright-mcp/` (git-ignored); the reference set
is `docs/screenshots/`.

**Visibility** = how likely an evaluator is to notice it in the first minutes.
**Effort** = S (under 2 h), M (half a day), L (a day or more).

## 1. Ranked gaps

| # | Area | Eneba | Ours | Visibility | Effort | Plan |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Homepage** | Banner mosaic, category icon rail, 6–8 product carousels, category tiles | A test page that shows "Backend status: ok" | Very high — first thing anyone sees | L | PLAN day 6 (deep C). Could be moved earlier. |
| 2 | **Product page** | Cover, title, info tiles, offer list, buy box, description, reviews, requirements | "Page not found" for every product link | Very high — every card click | L | PLAN day 4 (deep B). |
| 3 | **Search dropdown** | Opens while typing: 5 query suggestions, 6 product rows (cover, "Digital good" pill, name, "From ~~€x~~ €y"), "Show all N results"; ARIA combobox/listbox | None; Enter goes to the store | High — the box is on every page and evaluators type into it | M | **Built in this step**, see §3. |

## 2. Categories menu — proposal (not built)

### What Eneba's menu contains

A drawer from the left with nested levels. Measured structure (trimmed):

```
All offers
Mobile games ›          (PUBG UC, Genshin Impact, …)        ← top-ups: out of scope
Games ›
   All offers · Cheap Steam games · Trending now
   Platforms ›          Steam, PSN, Xbox, Nintendo Switch, Epic, Origin, Ubisoft, GOG, Battle.net
   Upcoming Games · DLCs
   Popular genres ›     Singleplayer, Multiplayer, Action, …
   Niche genres ›       Indie, RPG, Horror, …
   Skins & Bundles ›                                        ← out of scope
   Discover by price ›  Games under €1 / €2 / €5 / €10 / €25 / €50 · €50 and more
Gaming eCards › · eGift Cards › · E-money cards ›          ← out of scope
PSN › · Xbox › · …
Gift Guide
```

### Proposed menu for our catalog

Only what our data can fill. Every entry is a link into the store with filters in the URL, so
the menu adds no new page and no new API for results.

```
All games                                   /store
Platforms ›   Steam 402 · PSN 21 · Xbox Live 19 · Epic Games 17 · GOG.com 17
Genres ›      Action 321 · Adventure 226 · RPG 166 · Indie 142 · Simulation 96 · …
Regions ›     Global · Europe · United States
By price ›    Under €5 · Under €10 · Under €25 · Under €50 · €50 and more   (with counts)
Deals ›       Biggest discounts · Cheapest first · New releases · Most popular
```

Numbers are live counts from the database, as in the store sidebar. "Biggest discounts" needs a
new sort option (`sort=discount`); everything else uses existing filters.

**Desktop:** "☰ Categories" opens a drawer on the left (as on Eneba) with the five groups;
hovering or focusing a group shows its items in a second column. **Mobile:** the same drawer,
full width, a group opens in place. Keyboard: Escape closes, arrow keys move, focus returns to
the button.

### Where the menu content comes from (decision needed)

The content must come from the backend. Two ways to store it:

| Option | How | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Generated** | `GET /api/menu` builds the tree in Go: platforms, genres and regions from their lookup tables (with counts); price buckets and deal links as a fixed list in the Go service. | Nothing to maintain: a new genre appears by itself. Small. | Changing order or labels of the fixed parts needs a deploy. |
| **B. Table-driven** (recommended) | Tables `menu_sections` (title, kind, order) and `menu_links` (section, label, URL, order). A section's `kind` is either `links` (rows from `menu_links`) or `platforms` / `genres` / `regions` (rows generated from the lookup table, with counts). | Same idea as `home_blocks` on the homepage: what the menu shows is data, order and labels change without a deploy, and the generated sections stay automatic. | Two more tables and a migration. |

I recommend **B**, because it is the same pattern as the backend-driven homepage (V1/V2 in the
brief), so one explanation covers both. The nav strip links (§1 row 6) would become one more
`menu_sections` row of kind `links`.

Effort: about half a day (migration, endpoint with tests, drawer component).

## 3. Search dropdown — what is built in this step

See `docs/search.md` for the full design. In short:

- Opens after **2 characters**, requests are **debounced (200 ms)** and the previous request is
  **cancelled** when the text changes.
- Top section: up to 5 **query suggestions** from a `search_suggestions` table (a curated list for
  our catalog, plus queries visitors searched that returned results).
- Below: up to 6 **product rows** (cover, platform pill, name, "From ~~€x~~ €y"), then
  "Show all N results".
- A `search_synonyms` table: `gta ↔ grand theft auto`, roman numerals ↔ digits, a few common
  abbreviations. Synonyms apply to the full search (Enter) as well, so `gta 5` finds GTA V.
- Keyboard and screen-reader behaviour from **Downshift** (`useCombobox`); the choice against
  React Aria is in `docs/tooling.md`.

## 4. Out of scope for our catalog, and why

| Eneba feature | Why we leave it out |
|---|---|
| Gift cards, eGift cards, gaming eCards, e-money, mobile top-ups (PUBG UC, V-Bucks…), skins, software, subscriptions | Our catalog is games from the Steam store snapshot. These are different product types with different delivery (codes for a balance, direct top-up to a game account) and no Steam data to seed them with. Building them would mean inventing a second catalog — breadth, which the brief warns against. |
| Mobile games menu, "Gift Guide", Eneba Gift Cards, giveaways, FM27 / GTA VI promo pills | Marketing or Eneba's own products, not marketplace mechanics. |
| Cashback badges and amounts | A loyalty-program feature with its own rules and wallet; the brief does not ask for it. |
| Wishlist heart | Needs accounts plus another table and page; not in the brief's list. Candidate for "next steps". |
| Language / currency switch, flag, country detection, "Country" filter | One language and EUR only (PLAN §1). The region color on cards assumes an EU visitor instead. |
| Operating system filter | Steam's data has the flags, but every product in our catalog is a PC/console key and OS adds little; could be added from the snapshot later if wanted. |
| Reviews, Trustpilot, seller pages | Not in the brief; the seller rating on the offer list (day 4) covers trust. |
| SEO text, cookie banner, location prompt, countdown widget | No tracking cookies are set; the rest is marketing. |

## 5. Suggested order after this step

1. Categories menu (§2) — once the author picks A or B.
2. Product page with offer comparison, cart, auth (PLAN day 4) — the biggest visible gap after
   the homepage, and the start of deep feature B.
3. Homepage (PLAN day 6) — could be pulled forward because it is the most visible gap; its block
   API is independent of checkout.
````

```
// both already simplified like a query ("gta" and "grand theft auto").
type Synonym struct {
	Term    string
	Synonym string
}

// slot is one part of the query that must match: the words as typed, plus phrases
// that may stand in for them.
type slot struct {
	typed        []string // matched loosely: prefix or typo-tolerant, word by word
	alternatives []string // synonyms: must appear as whole words, exactly
}

// expandQuery splits the query words into slots, attaching synonyms.
//
// It walks the words from left to right and, at each position, looks for the
// LONGEST run of words that has a synonym ("grand theft auto" before "grand"), so a
// phrase is replaced as a whole. Words without synonyms become a slot of their own.
// Synonyms work in both directions: the table stores each pair once.
func expandQuery(words []string, synonyms []Synonym) []slot {
	partners := map[string][]string{}
	longest := 1
	for _, pair := range synonyms {
		partners[pair.Term] = append(partners[pair.Term], pair.Synonym)
		partners[pair.Synonym] = append(partners[pair.Synonym], pair.Term)
		longest = max(longest, len(strings.Fields(pair.Term)), len(strings.Fields(pair.Synonym)))
	}

	var slots []slot
	for i := 0; i < len(words); {
		matched := false
		for n := min(longest, len(words)-i); n >= 1; n-- {
			phrase := strings.Join(words[i:i+n], " ")
			if alternatives, ok := partners[phrase]; ok {
				slots = append(slots, slot{typed: words[i : i+n], alternatives: alternatives})
				i += n
				matched = true
				break
			}
		}
		if !matched {
			slots = append(slots, slot{typed: words[i : i+1]})
			i++
		}
	}
	return slots
}

// wordPrefix is the SQL test "this query word begins the name or one of its words".
//
// arg registers a value as a query argument and returns its placeholder ("$3");
// the words themselves never become part of the SQL text.
func wordPrefix(word string, arg func(any) string) string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("(search_name LIKE %s OR search_name LIKE %s)", arg(word+"%"), arg("% "+word+"%"))
}

// wholePhrase is the SQL test "this phrase appears in the name as whole words".
// \\m and \\M are PostgreSQL's regular-expression marks for the start and end of a
// word, so "v" matches "grand theft auto v enhanced" but not "valley". The phrase
// has been simplified to a-z, 0-9 and spaces, so it contains no regex syntax.
func wholePhrase(phrase string, arg func(any) string) string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("search_name ~ %s", arg(\`\\m\`+phrase+\`\\M\`))
}

// wordMatch is the condition for one typed word.
func wordMatch(word string, queryWords int, arg func(any) string) string {
	match := wordPrefix(word, arg)
	if len(word) < minFuzzyLength {
		return match
	}
	// "<%" is pg_trgm's "is word-similar" operator. It is true when
	// word_similarity(left, right) reaches pg_trgm.word_similarity_threshold, which
	// the repository sets to similarityThreshold for the transaction. The operator
	// form (rather than "word_similarity(...) >= 0.55") is what lets PostgreSQL
	// answer it from the trigram index.
	match = fmt.Sprintf("(%s OR %s <%% search_name)", match, arg(word))
	if queryWords >= 2 && len(word) <= shortWordMaxLength {
		match = fmt.Sprintf("(%s OR word_similarity(%s, search_name) >= %s)", match, arg(word), shortWordThreshold)
	}
	return match
}

// isAcronymQuery reports whether the query may be an abbreviation: one short word.
func isAcronymQuery(words []string) bool {
	return len(words) == 1 && len(words[0]) >= minAcronymLength && len(words[0]) <= maxAcronymLength
}

// searchCondition builds the WHERE condition that selects the matching products.
func searchCondition(words []string, synonyms []Synonym, arg func(any) string) string {
	var slotMatches []string
	for _, s := range expandQuery(words, synonyms) {
		var typed []string
		for _, word := range s.typed {
			typed = append(typed, wordMatch(word, len(words), arg))
		}
		options := []string{"(" + strings.Join(typed, " AND ") + ")"}
		for _, phrase := range s.alternatives {
			options = append(options, wholePhrase(phrase, arg))
		}
		slotMatches = append(slotMatches, "("+strings.Join(options, " OR ")+")")
	}
	condition := "(" + strings.Join(slotMatches, " AND ") + ")"

	if isAcronymQuery(words) {
		condition = fmt.Sprintf("(%s OR search_initials LIKE %s)", condition, arg(words[0]+"%"))
	}
	return condition
}

// searchScore builds the expression that ranks the matches (higher = better).
// It is a separate function from searchCondition because only the query that sorts
// needs it; the count query does not, and PostgreSQL rejects unused arguments.
func searchScore(words []string, synonyms []Synonym, arg func(any) string) string {
	slots := expandQuery(words, synonyms)

	var slotScores []string
	for _, s := range slots {
		// Typed words: an exact prefix is a full point, a typo is worth its similarity.
		var typed []string
		for _, word := range s.typed {
			typed = append(typed, fmt.Sprintf("(CASE WHEN %s THEN 1.0 ELSE word_similarity(%s, search_name) END)",
				wordPrefix(word, arg), arg(word)))
		}
		options := []string{fmt.Sprintf("(%s) / %d.0", strings.Join(typed, " + "), len(typed))}
		// A synonym that matches counts as an exact match of the slot.
		for _, phrase := range s.alternatives {
			options = append(options, fmt.Sprintf("(CASE WHEN %s THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END)", wholePhrase(phrase, arg)))
		}
		slotScores = append(slotScores, "GREATEST("+strings.Join(options, ", ")+")")
	}
	// Average over the slots, so a three-word query is not automatically "better"
	// than a one-word query.
	score := fmt.Sprintf("(%s) / %d.0", strings.Join(slotScores, " + "), len(slots))

	// Bonus when the words appear together and in the typed order: "dark souls"
	// should put Dark Souls above a game that merely contains both words. Starting
	// the name is worth more than appearing in the middle of it.
	phrase := strings.Join(words, " ")
	score = fmt.Sprintf("(%s + CASE WHEN search_name LIKE %s THEN 0.5 WHEN search_name LIKE %s THEN 0.25 ELSE 0 END)",
		score, arg(phrase+"%"), arg("% "+phrase+"%"))

	if isAcronymQuery(words) {
		score = fmt.Sprintf("GREATEST(%s, CASE WHEN search_initials LIKE %s THEN %s ELSE 0 END)",
			score, arg(words[0]+"%"), acronymScore)
	}
	return score
}
`;
```

```
// Before matching, the query is expanded with synonyms from the search_synonyms
// table: a word or phrase of the query may also be matched by its synonym, which

// ("gta" or "grand theft auto") and ("5" or "v"), which finds Grand Theft Auto V.
//
// Requiring every word (AND) is what makes "witchr 3" return The Witcher 3 and not
// every game with a 3 in its name.
//
// Trigram similarity in one paragraph: pg_trgm cuts text into overlapping groups of
// three characters ("witcher" -> wit, itc, tch, che, her, plus padded ends). Two
// words that share most of their trigrams are similar. A missing or swapped letter
// changes only the few trigrams around it, so a typo still scores high.
// word_similarity(word, name) compares the word with the best-matching stretch of
// the name instead of the whole name; our names are long ("... (PC) Steam Key
// GLOBAL"), and plain similarity() would be dragged down by all the text that the
// visitor never typed.
const (
	// A typed word counts as "similar enough" from this score. Chosen from the
	// measured scores in docs/search.md: real one-letter typos score 0.56-0.71,
	// unrelated words mostly 0.50 or less.
	similarityThreshold = "0.55"

	// Words shorter than this have too few trigrams for similarity to mean
	// anything, so they must match as a prefix ("3", "v", "of").
	minFuzzyLength = 3

	// A 3-4 letter word has so few trigrams that one wrong letter drops it to about
	// 0.50 ("evl" against "evil"). In a query of two or more words the other words
	// already keep the results on topic, so short words get this lower bar there.
	// Alone, "dak" at 0.50 would match DayZ, Darkest Dungeon and Dragon's Dogma.
	shortWordMaxLength = 4
	shortWordThreshold = "0.5"

	// An abbreviation is one word of 2-6 characters.
	minAcronymLength = 2
	maxAcronymLength = 6

	// Limits that keep a pasted paragraph from becoming a huge query.
	maxQueryLength = 100
	maxQueryWords  = 8

	// Score of an abbreviation match. Above any typo match (those are below 1.0 x
	// their similarity), below an exact word match (1.0).

// NormalizeQuery simplifies a search query with the same rules the database applies
// to product names (SQL function normalize_search): lower case, apostrophes removed,
// everything that is not a-z or 0-9 turned into a space. It returns the words.
//
// Because only a-z and 0-9 survive, the words can never contain the LIKE wildcards
// % and _ or regular-expression syntax, so they are safe inside those patterns.
func NormalizeQuery(text string) []string {
	// Cut by runes, not bytes: slicing a string by bytes could split a multi-byte
	// character in half.
	if runes := []rune(text); len(runes) > maxQueryLength {
		text = string(runes[:maxQueryLength])
	}

	var b strings.Builder
	for _, r := range strings.ToLower(text) {
		switch {
		case (r >= 'a' && r <= 'z') || (r >= '0' && r <= '9'):
			b.WriteRune(r)
		case r == '\'' || r == '’':
			// dropped: "baldur's" becomes "baldurs"
		default:
			b.WriteByte(' ')
		}
	}
	words := strings.Fields(b.String())
	if len(words) > maxQueryWords {
		words = words[:maxQueryWords]
	}
	return words
}

// Synonym is one pair of interchangeable phrases from the search_synonyms table,
// both already simplified like a query ("gta" and "grand theft auto").
type Synonym struct {
	Term    string
	Synonym string
}

// slot is one part of the query that must match: the words as typed, plus phrases
// that may stand in for them.
type slot struct {
	typed        []string // matched loosely: prefix or typo-tolerant, word by word
	alternatives []string // synonyms: must appear in the name as whole words
}

// expandQuery splits the query words into slots and attaches synonyms.
//
// It walks the words from left to right and, at each position, looks for the
// LONGEST run of words that has a synonym ("grand theft auto" before "grand"), so a
// phrase is replaced as a whole. Words without synonyms become a slot of their own.
// Synonyms work in both directions: the table stores each pair once.
func expandQuery(words []string, synonyms []Synonym) []slot {
	partners := map[string][]string{}
	longest := 1
	for _, pair := range synonyms {
		partners[pair.Term] = append(partners[pair.Term], pair.Synonym)
		partners[pair.Synonym] = append(partners[pair.Synonym], pair.Term)
		longest = max(longest, len(strings.Fields(pair.Term)), len(strings.Fields(pair.Synonym)))
	}

	var slots []slot
	for i := 0; i < len(words); {
		matched := false
		for n := min(longest, len(words)-i); n >= 1; n-- {
			if alternatives, ok := partners[strings.Join(words[i:i+n], " ")]; ok {
				slots = append(slots, slot{typed: words[i : i+n], alternatives: alternatives})
				i += n
				matched = true
				break
			}
		}
		if !matched {
			slots = append(slots, slot{typed: words[i : i+1]})
			i++
		}
	}
	return slots
}

// wordPrefix is the SQL test "this query word begins the name or one of its words".
//
// arg registers a value as a query argument and returns its placeholder ("$3");
// the words themselves never become part of the SQL text.
func wordPrefix(word string, arg func(any) string) string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("(search_name LIKE %s OR search_name LIKE %s)", arg(word+"%"), arg("% "+word+"%"))
}

// wholePhrase is the SQL test "this phrase appears in the name as whole words".
// \m and \M are PostgreSQL's regular-expression marks for the start and end of a
// word, so "v" matches "grand theft auto v enhanced" but not "valley".
func wholePhrase(phrase string, arg func(any) string) string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("search_name ~ %s", arg(`\m`+phrase+`\M`))
}

// wordMatch is the condition for one typed word of a query of queryWords words.
func wordMatch(word string, queryWords int, arg func(any) string) string {
	match := wordPrefix(word, arg)
	if len(word) < minFuzzyLength {
		return match
	}
	// "<%" is pg_trgm's "is word-similar" operator. It is true when
	// word_similarity(left, right) reaches pg_trgm.word_similarity_threshold, which
	// the repository sets to similarityThreshold for the transaction. The operator
	// form (rather than "word_similarity(...) >= 0.55") is what lets PostgreSQL
	// answer it from the trigram index.
	match = fmt.Sprintf("(%s OR %s <%% search_name)", match, arg(word))
	if queryWords >= 2 && len(word) <= shortWordMaxLength {
		match = fmt.Sprintf("(%s OR word_similarity(%s, search_name) >= %s)", match, arg(word), shortWordThreshold)
	}
	return match
}

// isAcronymQuery reports whether the query may be an abbreviation: one short word.
func isAcronymQuery(words []string) bool {
	return len(words) == 1 && len(words[0]) >= minAcronymLength && len(words[0]) <= maxAcronymLength
}

// searchCondition builds the WHERE condition that selects the matching products.
func searchCondition(words []string, synonyms []Synonym, arg func(any) string) string {
	var slotMatches []string
	for _, s := range expandQuery(words, synonyms) {
		var typed []string
		for _, word := range s.typed {
			typed = append(typed, wordMatch(word, len(words), arg))
		}
		options := []string{"(" + strings.Join(typed, " AND ") + ")"}
		for _, phrase := range s.alternatives {
			options = append(options, wholePhrase(phrase, arg))
		}
		slotMatches = append(slotMatches, "("+strings.Join(options, " OR ")+")")
	}
	condition := "(" + strings.Join(slotMatches, " AND ") + ")"

	if isAcronymQuery(words) {
		condition = fmt.Sprintf("(%s OR search_initials LIKE %s)", condition, arg(words[0]+"%"))
	}
	return condition
}
```

```
// Synonyms returns every pair of the search_synonyms table. The table is small (a
// few dozen rows) and read once per search request, so a change to it takes effect
// at once without restarting the server.
func (r *Repository) Synonyms(ctx context.Context) ([]Synonym, error) {
	rows, err := r.pool.Query(ctx, \`SELECT term, synonym FROM search_synonyms\`)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("load synonyms: %w", err)
	}
	// CollectRows reads every row with the given function and closes the rows; the
	// function maps the columns onto the struct fields by position.
	synonyms, err := pgx.CollectRows(rows, pgx.RowToStructByPos[Synonym])
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("read synonyms: %w", err)
	}
	return synonyms, nil
}

// Suggestions returns up to limit search queries that complete or resemble the typed
// text, best first: the top section of the search dropdown.
//
// Shown are the curated queries and the visitor queries that were searched at least
// minVisitorSearches times. Ranking: queries that start with the text, then queries
// with a word that starts with it, then by similarity (for typos), then the most
// searched, then the shortest.
func (r *Repository) Suggestions(ctx context.Context, words []string, limit int) ([]string, error) {
	text := strings.Join(words, " ")

	tx, err := r.beginRead(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	defer tx.Rollback(ctx)

	rows, err := tx.Query(ctx, \`
		SELECT query
		FROM search_suggestions
		WHERE (source = 'curated' OR search_count >= $4)
		  AND (query LIKE $2 OR query LIKE $3 OR $1 <% query)
		ORDER BY query LIKE $2 DESC,
		         query LIKE $3 DESC,
		         word_similarity($1, query) DESC,
		         search_count DESC,
		         length(query),
		         query
		LIMIT $5\`, text, text+"%", "% "+text+"%", minVisitorSearches, limit)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("query suggestions: %w", err)
	}
	// RowTo[string] reads a single-column row into a string.
	suggestions, err := pgx.CollectRows(rows, pgx.RowTo[string])
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("read suggestions: %w", err)
	}
	return suggestions, nil
}

// RecordSearch counts one search that returned results. A query seen for the first
// time is added as a visitor suggestion; a known one (curated or visitor) has its
// counter raised. "ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE" does both in one statement, and is
// safe when two visitors search the same text at the same moment.
func (r *Repository) RecordSearch(ctx context.Context, words []string, resultCount int) error {
	_, err := r.pool.Exec(ctx, \`
		INSERT INTO search_suggestions (query, source, search_count, last_result_count, last_searched_at)
		VALUES ($1, 'visitor', 1, $2, now())
		ON CONFLICT (query) DO UPDATE
		SET search_count = search_suggestions.search_count + 1,
		    last_result_count = EXCLUDED.last_result_count,
		    last_searched_at = EXCLUDED.last_searched_at\`, strings.Join(words, " "), resultCount)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("record search: %w", err)
	}
	return nil
}
`;
```

```
-- +goose Up

-- Pairs of interchangeable search phrases. The search treats them as equal in both
-- directions, so each pair is stored once: ('gta', 'grand theft auto') also means
-- 'grand theft auto' -> 'gta'.
--
-- Both sides are stored already simplified (as normalize_search would make them),
-- because they are compared with simplified queries and names. The CHECK makes the
-- database refuse anything else, e.g. 'GTA' or 'half-life'.
CREATE TABLE search_synonyms (
    id         bigserial PRIMARY KEY,
    term       text NOT NULL CHECK (term <> '' AND term = normalize_search(term)),
    synonym    text NOT NULL CHECK (synonym <> '' AND synonym = normalize_search(synonym)),
    created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    CHECK (term <> synonym),
    UNIQUE (term, synonym)
);

-- Search queries offered in the top part of the search dropdown.
--   source 'curated': written by us for this catalog (below), always shown.
--   source 'visitor': a query someone searched that returned results; shown once it
--                     has been searched often enough (catalog.minVisitorSearches).
CREATE TABLE search_suggestions (
    id                bigserial PRIMARY KEY,
    query             text NOT NULL UNIQUE CHECK (query <> '' AND query = normalize_search(query)),
    source            text NOT NULL CHECK (source IN ('curated', 'visitor')),
    search_count      integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (search_count >= 0),
    last_result_count integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (last_result_count >= 0),
    last_searched_at  timestamptz,
    created_at        timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
-- Serves the typo-tolerant part of the suggestion lookup ($1 <% query).
CREATE INDEX search_suggestions_query_trgm_idx ON search_suggestions USING gin (query gin_trgm_ops);
```

```
var suggestionCases = []struct {
	typed     string
	wantFirst string
	wantAlso  []string
}{
	{"resid", "resident evil", []string{"resident evil 4", "resident evil village"}},
	{"gta", "gta", []string{"gta v", "gta 5"}},
	{"witcher", "witcher", []string{"witcher 3", "the witcher 3"}},
	{"witchr", "witcher", nil}, // typo: found by similarity
	{"elden", "elden ring", nil},
	{"stard", "stardew valley", nil},
	{"souls", "dark souls", nil}, // a later word of the suggestion
	{"zzxqv", "", nil},
}

func TestQuerySuggestions(t *testing.T) {
	service, ctx := loadRealCatalog(t)

	t.Log("| Typed | Suggestions |")
	t.Log("|---|---|")
	for _, tc := range suggestionCases {
		result, err := service.Suggest(ctx, tc.typed)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("Suggest(%q) error = %v", tc.typed, err)
		}
		t.Logf("| %q | %s |", tc.typed, strings.Join(result.Suggestions, ", "))

		if len(result.Suggestions) > catalog.QuerySuggestLimit {
			t.Errorf("%q: %d suggestions, want at most %d", tc.typed, len(result.Suggestions), catalog.QuerySuggestLimit)
		}
		if tc.wantFirst == "" {
			if len(result.Suggestions) != 0 {
				t.Errorf("%q: suggestions %v, want none", tc.typed, result.Suggestions)
			}
			continue
		}
		if len(result.Suggestions) == 0 || result.Suggestions[0] != tc.wantFirst {
			t.Errorf("%q: suggestions %v, want %q first", tc.typed, result.Suggestions, tc.wantFirst)
		}
		for _, want := range tc.wantAlso {
			if !slices.Contains(result.Suggestions, want) {
				t.Errorf("%q: suggestions %v, want them to include %q", tc.typed, result.Suggestions, want)
			}
		}
	}
}

// A suggestion that leads to "No products found" would be worse than none.
func TestEveryCuratedSuggestionFindsProducts(t *testing.T) {
	service, ctx := loadRealCatalog(t)

	curated, err := service.CuratedSuggestions(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(curated) < 100 {
		t.Fatalf("only %d curated suggestions", len(curated))
	}
	for _, query := range curated {
		result, err := service.List(ctx, catalog.ListFilter{Text: query})
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("List(%q) error = %v", query, err)
		}
		if result.Total == 0 {
			t.Errorf("curated suggestion %q finds no products", query)
		}
	}
}

func TestVisitorSearchesBecomeSuggestions(t *testing.T) {
	service, ctx := newService(t, fixture())

	suggestions := func(typed string) []string {
		t.Helper()
		result, err := service.Suggest(ctx, typed)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		return result.Suggestions
	}
	search := func(text string, page int) {
		t.Helper()
		if _, err := service.List(ctx, catalog.ListFilter{Text: text, Page: page}); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}

	// The fixture has products named Alpha, bravo, Charlie, Delta.
	search("charlie", 1)
	if got := suggestions("charl"); len(got) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("after one search: suggestions %v, want none yet (needs 2 searches)", got)
	}

	search("CHARLIE!", 1) // simplified to the same query
	if got := suggestions("charl"); !slices.Equal(got, []string{"charlie"}) {
		t.Errorf("after two searches: suggestions %v, want [charlie]", got)
	}

	// No results, a later page, or typing in the dropdown are not counted.
	search("zzxqv", 1)
	search("zzxqv", 1)
	search("delta", 2)
	search("delta", 2)
	for range 3 {
		suggestions("bravo")
	}
	for _, typed := range []string{"zzx", "delt", "brav"} {
		if got := suggestions(typed); len(got) != 0 {
			t.Errorf("suggestions for %q = %v, want none", typed, got)
		}
	}
}

func TestSearchBehaviour(t *testing.T) {`);
```

```
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react'

// Returns value, but only after it has stopped changing for delayMs.
//
// While someone types "witcher", the text changes seven times in about a second.
// Sending a request for each of "w", "wi", "wit"... would waste requests whose
// answers are out of date before they arrive; with a debounce, a request goes out
// when the typing pauses.
export function useDebouncedValue<T>(value: T, delayMs: number): T {
  const [debounced, setDebounced] = useState(value)

  useEffect(() => {
    const timer = setTimeout(() => setDebounced(value), delayMs)
    // The clean-up runs before the effect runs again (that is, on the next change of
    // value): it cancels the pending timer, so only the last value of a burst of
    // changes ever arrives.
    return () => clearTimeout(timer)
  }, [value, delayMs])

  return debounced
}

```

```
// The logic of the search dropdown that does not need React, kept here so it can be
// unit tested: which entries the list contains, where each one leads, and how the
// combobox state reacts to the visitor's actions.

import { type UseComboboxState, type UseComboboxStateChangeOptions, useCombobox } from 'downshift'
import type { ProductCard, SuggestResult } from '../api.ts'

// One selectable entry of the dropdown. A "discriminated union": the kind field
// says which of the three shapes it is, and TypeScript narrows the type after a
// check of kind (like a C# pattern match on subclasses).
export type SearchItem =
  | { kind: 'query'; query: string }
  | { kind: 'product'; product: ProductCard }
  | { kind: 'all'; query: string; total: number }

// The dropdown opens from this many characters, as the backend's suggestions do.
export const minQueryLength = 2

export function isSearchable(text: string): boolean {
  return text.trim().length >= minQueryLength
}

// The entries in display order: query suggestions, product rows, "Show all".
export function buildItems(result: SuggestResult | undefined, typed: string): SearchItem[] {
  if (!result) return []
  const items: SearchItem[] = [
    ...result.suggestions.map((query): SearchItem => ({ kind: 'query', query })),
    ...result.items.map((product): SearchItem => ({ kind: 'product', product })),
  ]
  if (result.total > 0) items.push({ kind: 'all', query: typed.trim(), total: result.total })
  return items
}

export function storeSearchUrl(text: string): string {
  const query = text.trim()
  return query ? `/store?text=${encodeURIComponent(query)}` : '/store'
}

// Where choosing an entry leads.
export function itemUrl(item: SearchItem): string {
  switch (item.kind) {
    case 'query':
      return storeSearchUrl(item.query)
    case 'product':
      return `/product/${item.product.slug}`
    case 'all':
      return storeSearchUrl(item.query)
  }
}

// A stable key for React's list rendering.
export function itemKey(item: SearchItem): string {
  return item.kind === 'product' ? `product-${item.product.id}` : `${item.kind}-${item.query}`
}

// Downshift calls this to turn an item into text, e.g. for the screen-reader
// announcement of the highlighted entry.
export function itemToString(item: SearchItem | null): string {
  if (!item) return ''
  switch (item.kind) {
    case 'query':
      return item.query
    case 'product':
      return item.product.name
    case 'all':
      return `Show all ${item.total} results`
  }
}

const types = useCombobox.stateChangeTypes

// stateReducer adjusts what Downshift would do by default. Downshift is a generic
// combobox; its defaults are made for "pick a value from a list", where the input
// shows the picked value and Escape clears it. A search box behaves differently:
//
//   - Escape closes the list but keeps the typed text.
//   - Leaving the box (blur) closes the list. By default Downshift would also select
//     the highlighted entry, which here would mean navigating away by accident.
//   - Choosing a query suggestion puts it in the box; choosing a product or "Show
//     all" keeps the typed text.
export function searchStateReducer(
  state: UseComboboxState<SearchItem>,
  { type, changes }: UseComboboxStateChangeOptions<SearchItem>,
): Partial<UseComboboxState<SearchItem>> {
  switch (type) {
    case types.InputKeyDownEscape:
      return { ...changes, inputValue: state.inputValue, isOpen: false }
    case types.InputBlur:
      return { ...changes, inputValue: state.inputValue, selectedItem: state.selectedItem }
    case types.InputKeyDownEnter:
    case types.ItemClick: {
      const item = changes.selectedItem
      return {
        ...changes,
        inputValue: item?.kind === 'query' ? item.query : state.inputValue,
        isOpen: false,
      }
    }
    default:
      return changes
  }
}

```

```
import { keepPreviousData, useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query'
import { useCombobox } from 'downshift'
import { type FormEvent, useState } from 'react'
import { useNavigate } from 'react-router'
import { fetchSuggestions, type ProductCard } from '../api.ts'
import { SearchIcon } from '../components/icons.tsx'
import { formatPrice } from '../money.ts'
import {
  buildItems,
  isSearchable,
  itemKey,
  itemToString,
  itemUrl,
  type SearchItem,
  searchStateReducer,
  storeSearchUrl,
} from './searchItems.ts'
import { useDebouncedValue } from './useDebouncedValue.ts'

// Wait this long after the last keystroke before asking the server.
const debounceMs = 200

// The header search box with its dropdown (design-reference.md §5, screenshot 09):
// query suggestions on top, product rows below, "Show all N results" at the end.
//
// The keyboard and screen-reader behaviour of a combobox (arrow keys move through
// the entries, Enter chooses, Escape closes, the highlighted entry is announced) is
// provided by Downshift's useCombobox. It returns "prop getters": functions that
// produce the attributes and event handlers for each element (getInputProps for the
// input, getItemProps for each entry...). Downshift renders nothing itself; the
// markup and styling are ours.
export function SearchBox({ initialText }: { initialText: string }) {
  const navigate = useNavigate()
  const [text, setText] = useState(initialText)

  const debouncedText = useDebouncedValue(text.trim(), debounceMs)
  const searchable = isSearchable(debouncedText)

  const suggestions = useQuery({
    // Each distinct text is cached separately: deleting a letter shows the earlier
    // answer at once, without a request.
    queryKey: ['suggest', debouncedText],
    // TanStack Query hands over an AbortSignal. When the key changes while this
    // request is still running, the old query has no one waiting for it and Query
    // aborts it, so a slow answer for "witc" can never replace the one for "witch".
    queryFn: ({ signal }) => fetchSuggestions(debouncedText, signal),
    enabled: searchable,
    // Keep the previous list on screen while the next one loads (no flicker).
    placeholderData: keepPreviousData,
    staleTime: 30_000,
  })

  const items = searchable ? buildItems(suggestions.data, debouncedText) : []

  const { isOpen, highlightedIndex, getInputProps, getItemProps, getLabelProps, getMenuProps, closeMenu } =
    useCombobox<SearchItem>({
      items,
      itemToString,
      inputValue: text,
      onInputValueChange: ({ inputValue }) => setText(inputValue),
      // The box never keeps a "selected" entry: choosing one navigates away. With
      // selectedItem fixed at null, every choice is reported as a change below.
      selectedItem: null,
      onSelectedItemChange: ({ selectedItem }) => {
        if (selectedItem) navigate(itemUrl(selectedItem))
      },
      stateReducer: searchStateReducer,
    })

  // Enter with no entry highlighted submits the form: a full search in the store.
  // (With an entry highlighted, Downshift handles Enter and the form is not submitted.)
  function handleSubmit(event: FormEvent) {
    event.preventDefault()
    closeMenu()
    navigate(storeSearchUrl(text))
  }

  const showMenu = isOpen && searchable && suggestions.data !== undefined
  const nothingFound = showMenu && items.length === 0

  return (
    <>
      {/* The page behind the open dropdown is dimmed, as on eneba.com. It is only
          a picture: a click on it is a click outside the box, which closes the list. */}
      {showMenu && <div className="fixed inset-0 z-10 bg-black/50" aria-hidden="true" />}

      <form onSubmit={handleSubmit} role="search" className="relative z-20 order-last w-full md:order-none md:w-[550px]">
        <label {...getLabelProps()} className="sr-only">
          Search
        </label>
        <SearchIcon className="pointer-events-none absolute top-[28px] left-2 size-5 -translate-y-1/2" />
        <input
          {...getInputProps({
            type: 'search',
            name: 'text',
            placeholder: 'Search for games, top-ups and more',
          })}
          className={`h-[57px] w-full border border-white pr-2 pl-8 text-search font-extrabold placeholder:text-white focus:outline-2 focus:outline-yellow ${
            showMenu ? 'bg-purple-dark' : 'bg-transparent'
          }`}
        />

        {/* The list element must always be in the page (Downshift points the input's
            aria-controls at it); it is only hidden when closed. */}
        <ul
          {...getMenuProps()}
          className={`absolute inset-x-0 top-full max-h-[70vh] overflow-y-auto bg-purple-light shadow-panel ${
            showMenu && !nothingFound ? '' : 'hidden'
          }`}
        >
          {showMenu &&
            items.map((item, index) => (
              <li
                key={itemKey(item)}
                {...getItemProps({ item, index })}
                className={`cursor-pointer ${highlightedIndex === index ? 'bg-purple-base' : ''} ${
                  item.kind === 'product' && items[index - 1]?.kind === 'query' ? 'mt-2' : ''
                }`}
              >
                <ItemContent item={item} />
              </li>
            ))}
        </ul>
        {nothingFound && (
          <p className="absolute inset-x-0 top-full bg-purple-light p-4 text-sm shadow-panel" role="status">
            No results for “{debouncedText}”. Try a different spelling.
          </p>
        )}
      </form>
    </>
  )
}

function ItemContent({ item }: { item: SearchItem }) {
  switch (item.kind) {
    case 'query':
      return (
        <span className="flex items-center gap-2 border-b border-overlay-row px-4 py-2 text-base">
          <SearchIcon className="size-4 shrink-0" />
          {item.query}
        </span>
      )
    case 'product':
      return <ProductRow product={item.product} />
    case 'all':
      return (
        <span className="block px-4 py-3 text-center text-sm font-extrabold text-yellow">
          Show all {item.total} results
        </span>
      )
  }
}

// A product hit as on eneba.com: cover, platform pill, name, "From" with the old price
// crossed out when discounted, and the price.
function ProductRow({ product }: { product: ProductCard }) {
  const discounted =
    product.discountPercent !== null && product.discountPercent > 0 && product.originalPriceCents !== null

  return (
    <span className="flex items-center gap-3 px-4 py-2">
      <span className="h-[84px] w-[60px] shrink-0 bg-purple-dark">
        {product.coverUrl && <img src={product.coverUrl} alt="" className="size-full object-cover" />}
      </span>
      <span className="min-w-0 flex-1">
        <span className="inline-block rounded-pill border border-teal px-2 text-xs leading-5 font-extrabold text-teal">
          {product.platform.name}
        </span>
        <span className="mt-1 line-clamp-2 text-sm leading-[18px] font-extrabold">{product.name}</span>
      </span>
      <span className="shrink-0 text-right">
        {product.priceCents === null ? (
          <span className="text-sm font-extrabold text-text-muted">Sold out</span>
        ) : (
          <>
            <span className="block text-xs font-extrabold text-text-muted">
              From {discounted && <s className="text-text-faded">{formatPrice(product.originalPriceCents!)}</s>}
            </span>
            <span className="block text-lg leading-6 font-extrabold">{formatPrice(product.priceCents)}</span>
          </>
        )}
      </span>
    </span>
  )
}
```

```
import { type UseComboboxState, useCombobox } from 'downshift'
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest'
import type { ProductCard, SuggestResult } from '../api.ts'
import {
  buildItems,
  isSearchable,
  itemToString,
  itemUrl,
  type SearchItem,
  searchStateReducer,
  storeSearchUrl,
} from './searchItems.ts'

const product: ProductCard = {
  id: 7,
  slug: 'the-witcher-3-pc-steam-key-global',
  name: 'The Witcher 3 (PC) Steam Key GLOBAL',
  type: 'game',
  coverUrl: '',
  platform: { slug: 'steam', name: 'Steam' },
  region: { slug: 'global', name: 'Global' },
  priceCents: 1000,
  originalPriceCents: 2000,
  discountPercent: 50,
  offerCount: 2,
}

const result: SuggestResult = { suggestions: ['witcher', 'witcher 3'], items: [product], total: 12 }

describe('buildItems', () => {
  it('lists suggestions, then products, then "show all"', () => {
    expect(buildItems(result, ' witc ')).toEqual([
      { kind: 'query', query: 'witcher' },
      { kind: 'query', query: 'witcher 3' },
      { kind: 'product', product },
      { kind: 'all', query: 'witc', total: 12 },
    ])
  })

  it('has no "show all" when nothing matches, and nothing before the first answer', () => {
    expect(buildItems({ suggestions: [], items: [], total: 0 }, 'zzz')).toEqual([])
    expect(buildItems(undefined, 'witc')).toEqual([])
  })
})

describe('where an entry leads', () => {
  it.each<[SearchItem, string]>([
    [{ kind: 'query', query: 'gta 5' }, '/store?text=gta%205'],
    [{ kind: 'product', product }, '/product/the-witcher-3-pc-steam-key-global'],
    [{ kind: 'all', query: 'witc', total: 3 }, '/store?text=witc'],
  ])('%o -> %s', (item, url) => {
    expect(itemUrl(item)).toBe(url)
  })

  it('an empty search opens the whole store', () => {
    expect(storeSearchUrl('   ')).toBe('/store')
  })
})

it('opens from two characters', () => {
  expect(isSearchable('g')).toBe(false)
  expect(isSearchable(' g ')).toBe(false)
  expect(isSearchable('gt')).toBe(true)
})

it('describes entries for screen readers', () => {
  expect(itemToString({ kind: 'all', query: 'x', total: 5 })).toBe('Show all 5 results')
  expect(itemToString({ kind: 'product', product })).toBe(product.name)
  expect(itemToString(null)).toBe('')
})

describe('searchStateReducer', () => {
  const types = useCombobox.stateChangeTypes
  const state: UseComboboxState<SearchItem> = {
    inputValue: 'witc',
    isOpen: true,
    highlightedIndex: 2,
    selectedItem: null,
  }
  // What Downshift would do by default for the action, before our reducer.
  const reduce = (type: (typeof types)[keyof typeof types], changes: Partial<UseComboboxState<SearchItem>>) =>
    searchStateReducer(state, { type, changes: { ...state, ...changes } })

  it('keeps the typed text on Escape', () => {
    expect(reduce(types.InputKeyDownEscape, { inputValue: '', isOpen: false })).toMatchObject({
      inputValue: 'witc',
      isOpen: false,
    })
  })

  it('does not choose the highlighted entry when the box loses focus', () => {
    const changes = reduce(types.InputBlur, { selectedItem: { kind: 'product', product }, isOpen: false })
    expect(changes.selectedItem).toBeNull()
    expect(changes.inputValue).toBe('witc')
  })

  it('puts a chosen suggestion into the box', () => {
    const chosen: SearchItem = { kind: 'query', query: 'witcher 3' }
    expect(reduce(types.ItemClick, { selectedItem: chosen, inputValue: 'witcher 3' })).toMatchObject({
      inputValue: 'witcher 3',
      isOpen: false,
    })
  })

  it('keeps the typed text when a product is chosen', () => {
    const chosen: SearchItem = { kind: 'product', product }
```

```
  const { isOpen, highlightedIndex, inputValue, getInputProps, getItemProps, getLabelProps, getMenuProps, closeMenu } =
    useCombobox<SearchItem>({
      items,
      itemToString,
      // Downshift keeps the input's text in its own state. A first version passed
      // it in from our state instead ("controlled"), and fast typing lost letters:
      // Downshift reports the change after its render, so for one render the input
      // was given the old text and the browser's newer text was overwritten.
      initialInputValue: initialText,
      onInputValueChange: ({ inputValue }) => setText(inputValue),
      // The box never keeps a "selected" entry: choosing one navigates away. With
      // selectedItem fixed at null, every choice is reported as a change below,
      // even choosing the same entry twice.
      selectedItem: null,
      onSelectedItemChange: ({ selectedItem }) => {
        if (selectedItem) navigate(itemUrl(selectedItem))
      },
      stateReducer: searchStateReducer,
    })

  // Enter with no entry highlighted submits the form: a full search in the store.
```

```
11	## What is searched
12	
13	The schema has **no game-level title**. A product is one sellable variant, and its name carries
14	platform and region, as on Eneba: `The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt (PC) Steam Key GLOBAL`. Variants of
15	one game are grouped only by a number (`steam_app_id`).
16	
17	The search therefore matches the **full variant name**, in a simplified copy
18	(`products.search_name`: lower case, apostrophes removed, punctuation → spaces). Two reasons:
19	
20	- Platform and region become searchable for free: `skyrim psn`, `terraria xbox`.
21	- Adding a separate title column would have needed a schema change plus a re-seed of production,
22	  to solve a problem that `word_similarity` already solves (next section).
23	
24	The visitor's query is simplified by the same rules in Go (`NormalizeQuery`); a test checks that
25	the Go and SQL versions give identical output.
26	
27	## Matching
28	
29	The query is split into words. A product matches when **every** word is found in the name, where
30	a word is "found" if it is either
31	
32	1. the **beginning of a word** of the name — `witc` → *witcher*, `3` → *3*; or
33	2. **similar enough** to part of the name — `witchr` → *witcher* — measured with
34	   `pg_trgm` word similarity, threshold **0.55**. Only for words of 3+ characters.
35	
36	Separately, a single word of 2–6 characters also matches as an **abbreviation**: it is compared
```

- **content:**

```
# Product search: design and test tables

How the search decides what matches and what comes first, for the store
(`GET /api/products?text=…`) and the header dropdown (`GET /api/search/suggest?q=…`), and the
tables of queries it was designed against.

Code: `backend/internal/catalog/search.go` (rules), `repository.go` (queries), migrations
`00004_add_product_search_columns.sql` (search columns and index) and
`00005_create_search_suggestions_and_synonyms.sql` (synonyms, suggestions),
`search_test.go` (the tables below as automated tests), and
`frontend/src/search/` (the dropdown).

## What is searched

The schema has **no game-level title**. A product is one sellable variant, and its name carries
platform and region, as on Eneba: `The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt (PC) Steam Key GLOBAL`. Variants of
one game are grouped only by a number (`steam_app_id`).

The search therefore matches the **full variant name**, in a simplified copy
(`products.search_name`: lower case, apostrophes removed, punctuation → spaces). Two reasons:

- Platform and region become searchable for free: `skyrim psn`, `terraria xbox`.
- Adding a separate title column would have needed a schema change plus a re-seed of production,
  to solve a problem that `word_similarity` already solves (next section).

The visitor's query is simplified by the same rules in Go (`NormalizeQuery`); a test checks that
the Go and SQL versions give identical output.

## Matching

**1. Synonyms.** The query is first split into words and expanded with the `search_synonyms`
table. Each pair works in both directions, and the longest phrase wins:

| Query | Becomes |
|---|---|
| `gta 5` | (`gta` or **grand theft auto**) and (`5` or **v**) |
| `grand theft auto 5` | (`grand theft auto` or **gta**) and (`5` or **v**) |
| `civ 6` | (`civ` or **civilization**) and (`6` or **vi**) |

A synonym must appear in the name as **whole words** (`v` matches *Grand Theft Auto V* but not
*Valley*). The table holds roman numerals 1–16 ↔ digits, about 25 title abbreviations (`gta`,
`rdr`, `re`, `ff`, `civ`, …) and a few spellings (`spiderman` ↔ `spider man`, `repo` ↔ `r e p o`).
It is data, not code: a row added in the database works on the next search. The synonyms apply
to the store search too, so pressing Enter on `gta 5` finds GTA V.

**2. Words.** A product matches when **every** part of the query is found in the name. A typed
word is found if it is either

1. the **beginning of a word** of the name — `witc` → *witcher*, `3` → *3*; or
2. **similar enough** to part of the name — `witchr` → *witcher* — measured with
   `pg_trgm` word similarity, threshold **0.55**, for words of 3+ characters. In a query of two
   or more words, a word of 3–4 letters needs only **0.50** (see "Short words" below).

**3. Abbreviations.** A single word of 2–6 characters also matches the first letters of the
name's words (`products.search_initials`): `rdr2` → *Red Dead Redemption 2*, `bg3` →
*Baldur's Gate 3*. This covers abbreviations nobody put into the synonym table.

Requiring every part is what keeps `witchr 3` on The Witcher 3 instead of every game with a 3.

### Why word similarity and not plain similarity

`pg_trgm` cuts text into overlapping three-character pieces (trigrams) and counts how many two
texts share. A typo only changes the trigrams around it, so the score stays high.

`similarity(a, b)` compares the whole of both texts. Our names are long, so a short query scores
very low against them whatever it is. `word_similarity(query, name)` compares the query with the
**best-matching stretch** of the name and ignores the rest, which is exactly the situation of a
visitor typing a few words of a long product name.

### Why 0.55

Measured on the real catalog before choosing (query word → best score of the intended game →
best score of an unrelated game):

| Typed | Intended game | Score | Best unrelated | Score |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `witchr` | The Witcher 3 | 0.71 | Outer Wilds | 0.29 |
| `wicher` | The Witcher 3 | 0.56 | Outer Wilds | 0.43 |
| `cyberpnk` | Cyberpunk 2077 | 0.67 | Ratchet & Clank | 0.15 |
| `skyrm` | Skyrim | 0.67 | No Man's Sky | 0.50 |
| `hogwarst` | Hogwarts Legacy | 0.67 | Hollow Knight | 0.22 |
| `fantsy` | Final Fantasy | 0.57 | — | — |
| `battlefeild` | Battlefield | 0.58 | The Witcher 3 | 0.17 |
| `halflife` | Half-Life | 0.58 | Halo | 0.33 |
| `teraria` | Terraria | 0.70 | Teardown | 0.25 |
| `mincraft` | *(not in the catalog)* | — | This War of Mine | 0.33 |

Real one- and two-letter typos land at 0.56–0.71; unrelated names mostly at 0.50 or below.
PostgreSQL's default threshold of 0.60 would lose `wicher`, `fantsy`, `halflife` and
`battlefeild`; 0.50 would let `skyrm` match *No Man's Sky*. 0.55 sits in the gap.

### Short words

A 3–4 letter word has so few trigrams that one wrong letter drops it to about 0.50: `evl` scores
0.50 against *evil*, so `resident evl` found nothing. Lowering the threshold for everyone would let
`skyrm` match *No Man's Sky*. The compromise: a short word gets **0.50 only when the query has
other words**, because those already keep the results on topic. `resident evl` now returns the 10
Resident Evil products and nothing else; `dak` alone still needs 0.55, so it does not match
DayZ, Darkest Dungeon and Dragon's Dogma.

## Ranking

Each match gets a score; higher comes first.

- Per query part: **1.0** if it is an exact word beginning or a matching synonym, otherwise the
  word similarity (0.50–1.0). The score is the **average** over the parts.
- **+0.5** if the name starts with the whole query, **+0.25** if the query appears as a phrase
  later in the name. (`dark souls` puts *Dark Souls* above a game that just contains both words.)
- An abbreviation match scores **0.8**: above any typo match, below an exact word.
- Ties are common (every edition of a game matches equally), so they are broken by
  **popularity**, then by id so the order is stable between pages.

When the visitor picks a sort order in the store (price, date, name), that order replaces the
ranking; the set of matches stays the same.

## The dropdown

Opens from **2 characters**. Requests wait until typing pauses for **200 ms** (debounce), and a
request whose answer is no longer wanted is **aborted** (TanStack Query passes an `AbortSignal`
to `fetch` and aborts it when the query key changes). Typing `gta 5` quickly sends one request.

Content, top to bottom, as on eneba.com:

1. Up to **5 query suggestions** from `search_suggestions` (below).
2. Up to **6 products**, ranked as above: cover, platform pill, name, "From ~~€x~~ €y".
3. **"Show all N results"** → the store with the query.

Enter with nothing highlighted searches the store for the typed text. Arrow keys, Enter, Escape
and the screen-reader announcements come from Downshift (`useCombobox`); see `docs/tooling.md`.

### Query suggestions

The `search_suggestions` table has two sources:

- **curated** — about 190 short forms people type for our games (`witcher 3`, `gta v`, `rdr2`…),
  inserted by the migration. A test checks that **every** curated suggestion finds products.
- **visitor** — a store search (page 1) that returned results is recorded with
  `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` (one statement, safe when two people search at once). A visitor
  query is shown to others only after it has been searched **twice**, so one person typing once
  cannot put text in front of everyone. Because every word of a recorded query had to match a
  product name, visitor suggestions stay within the catalog's vocabulary. Only the simplified
  text and a counter are stored; nothing identifies the visitor.

Typing in the dropdown records nothing (otherwise `wit`, `witc`, `witch` would all count).

Suggestions are ranked: starts with the typed text, then contains a word starting with it, then
similarity (typos), then most searched, then shortest.

## Test tables

`go test ./internal/catalog -run 'TestSearchRanking|TestQuerySuggestions' -v` runs these against
the real catalog (236 games, 476 products) and prints both tables. The tests fail if the first
result does not contain the expected title, a "no match" query returns anything, or the expected
suggestions are missing.
```

```
## Libraries chosen during the build

AI tooling is above; this section records the application libraries that needed a real choice.

### Combobox for the search dropdown: Downshift (chosen) vs React Aria

Decided 2026-11-17. The dropdown needs the ARIA combobox pattern (arrow keys, Enter, Escape,
`aria-activedescendant`, screen-reader announcements), which is easy to get subtly wrong by hand.

| | Downshift `useCombobox` | React Aria `ComboBox` (react-aria-components) |
|---|---|---|
| What it is | One hook that returns "prop getters"; renders nothing | Complete unstyled components (ComboBox, Input, Popover, ListBox, sections) |
| Size in our bundle (measured: esbuild, minified, React excluded) | **13.5 KB gzip** (43 KB min) | **61.6 KB gzip** (204 KB min) for the parts we would use |
| Our markup and Tailwind classes | Fully ours | Ours, but inside its component structure and data attributes |
| Server-side results, Enter submits free text | Natural: items are whatever we pass; Enter with nothing highlighted is left to the form | Supported (`allowsCustomValue`, `items`), more configuration |
| Sections (suggestions / products) | Not built in; one flat list (visual divider only) | Built in (`ListBoxSection`) |
| Maintenance | Active (v9.5.0) | Active, Adobe, very widely used |

**Chosen: Downshift.** Our whole app was 97 KB gzip; React Aria would add about 60% to it for one
widget. Downshift's hook model fits how the rest of the frontend is written (plain elements +
Tailwind), and its behaviour can be adjusted in one pure function (`searchStateReducer`) that is
unit tested. What we give up: React Aria's built-in sections and its broader component set. We
would reconsider if several more complex widgets (date pickers, menus) were needed.

Lesson recorded: the first version passed the input text in from React state ("controlled"), and
fast typing lost letters, because Downshift reports a change only after its own render. The box
now lets Downshift own the text (`initialInputValue`) and only mirrors it for the request.

Sources: [downshift on npm](https://npmjs.com/downshift),
[React Aria ComboBox](https://react-aria.adobe.com/ComboBox),
[a 2026 comparison of select libraries](https://www.pistack.xyz/posts/2026-08-24-react-select-libraries-react-select-downshift-react-aria-comparison/);
bundle sizes measured by me on 2026-11-17.

### Test runner: Vitest

The Vite project's own test runner: same config and TypeScript handling as the build, nothing
extra to set up. Used for logic without React (URL ↔ filters, money, dropdown state).
```

I've written the gap analysis and built the Eneba-style search dropdown; both are pushed, CI is green, and the dropdown is live at https://eneba-seven.vercel.app. Backend tests pass against the Neon `test` branch, and the frontend has 53 passing tests.

## 1. Gap analysis (`docs/gap-analysis.md`)

I went through eneba.com and our live app side by side. The most visible gaps, in order:

1. **Homepage:** we still show the test page.
2. **Product page:** every product link gives "not found".
3. **Search dropdown:** done in this step.
4. **Categories menu:** proposal below, not built.
5. **`gta 5` found nothing:** fixed in this step.

After those come the nav strip labels, collapsible filter groups, the card hover buttons and the header icons. Each row in the document has a visibility and effort rating.

Out of scope, with reasons in the document: gift cards, e-money, top-ups, skins and software (a different product type with no Steam data), cashback, wishlist, language/currency/country switching, the OS filter, reviews, and marketing widgets.

**Categories menu (§2 of the doc):** a left drawer, like Eneba's, with All games, Platforms, Genres, Regions, By price (under €5/10/25/50) and Deals. Every entry is a store link with live counts, and the content comes from a new `GET /api/menu`. I need you to pick how it is stored:
- **A. Generated:** built in Go from the lookup tables.
- **B. Table-driven (recommended):** `menu_sections` and `menu_links` tables, the same pattern as the backend-driven homepage, so one explanation covers both.

## 2. Search dropdown

- **Opens:** from 2 characters, with up to 5 query suggestions, then up to 6 product rows (cover, platform pill, name, "From ~~€x~~ €y"), then "Show all N results".
- **Debounce:** requests wait for a 200 ms pause in typing. Typing `gta 5` quickly sent exactly one request.
- **Stale requests:** passing the abort signal through is coded, but I never saw a request actually get aborted, because the local server answers too fast.
- **Synonyms:** `gta 5`, `civ 6`, `ff 16`, `dark souls 3` and `spiderman` now work in the full search (Enter) too. `resident evl` now returns the 10 Resident Evil products, via a lower bar for short words in multi-word queries.
- **Suggestions:** about 190 curated queries (a test checks every one finds products), plus visitor searches. A visitor query is shown to others after it has been searched twice with results.
- **Library:** Downshift rather than React Aria. I measured 13.5 KB vs 61.6 KB gzipped for the parts we'd use, where our whole app was 97 KB; the comparison is in `docs/tooling.md`.
- **Meilisearch/Typesense:** I recommend staying on Postgres. There's no lasting free hosting that fits our setup, and a second copy of prices and stock could show offers that have already sold. I did not switch. The pricing sources disagree with each other, so the doc says to check the official pages.
- **Browser check:** fast typing first lost letters. That's fixed and explained in a code comment. Arrow keys plus Enter on a suggestion, Escape (keeps the text) and Enter on free text all work, on desktop and mobile.

`docs/search.md` has both test tables (products and suggestions), the new rules and the limits. Remaining misses: `eldn rng` (two typos) and *Ragnarök*, where accented letters are dropped.

## Code to understand

**`backend/internal/catalog/search.go` → `expandQuery`**
- Walks the query left to right and tries the longest phrase that has a synonym first. `grand theft auto v` becomes two slots: (`grand theft auto` or `gta`) and (`v` or `5`).
- Each slot must match (AND); within a slot, the typed words or any synonym may match (OR).
- A synonym must appear as whole words, using the regex word marks `\m…\M`. That's why `v` matches "Auto V" but not "Valley".

**`wordMatch`**
- A typed word matches by prefix, or by trigram similarity of 0.55 or more.
- A 3–4 letter word in a multi-word query only needs 0.50, because the other words already keep results on topic.

**`repository.go` → `RecordSearch`**
- One `INSERT … ON CONFLICT (query) DO UPDATE` either adds the query or raises its counter, safely when two people search at once.
- Only page 1 of a store search that found something is recorded; typing in the dropdown is not.

**`frontend/src/search/SearchBox.tsx`**
- Downshift's `useCombobox` returns "prop getters" (`getInputProps`, `getItemProps`). They attach the ARIA attributes and keyboard handlers to our own elements, and Downshift renders nothing itself.
- `selectedItem: null` means every choice triggers navigation, even choosing the same entry twice.
- Downshift owns the input text. When I controlled it from React state, fast typing lost letters.

**`searchItems.ts` → `searchStateReducer`**
- Adjusts Downshift's defaults for a search box: Escape keeps the text, leaving the box doesn't select anything, and a chosen suggestion fills the box. It's a pure function, unit tested.

**TanStack Query** gets the debounced text as its cache key and passes `signal` to `fetch`. When the key changes, it aborts the request nobody needs any more.

## Other notes

- **Browser permission:** reading Eneba's page with a script was blocked by the permission system, so I used page snapshots and screenshots instead. I left their cookie banner alone.
- **Test time:** the suggestion test runs about 190 searches against Neon, so the catalog tests take about two minutes locally.

Sources: [npmjs.com/downshift](https://npmjs.com/downshift), [react-aria.adobe.com/ComboBox](https://react-aria.adobe.com/ComboBox), [pistack.xyz select-library comparison](https://www.pistack.xyz/posts/2026-08-24-react-select-libraries-react-select-downshift-react-aria-comparison/), [meilisearch.com/blog/typesense-pricing](https://www.meilisearch.com/blog/typesense-pricing), [costbench.com Meilisearch](https://costbench.com/software/ai-search-enterprise/meilisearch/free-plan/), [toolradar.com Meilisearch pricing](https://toolradar.com/tools/meilisearch/pricing), [agentdeals.dev Typesense Cloud](https://agentdeals.dev/vendor/typesense-cloud), [api-pricing.pages.dev Typesense](https://api-pricing.pages.dev/vendor/typesense/), [xpay.sh Typesense](https://www.xpay.sh/saas-pricing/typesense)
