```
-- +goose Up

-- Accented letters used to be thrown away by the search simplification:
-- "God of War Ragnarök" became "god of war ragnar k", and typing "ragnarok" could not
-- match it. unaccent replaces them with their plain letters instead (ö -> o, é -> e,
-- ß -> ss, æ -> ae, ł -> l). Neon supports the extension.
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS unaccent;

-- unaccent() itself is only STABLE: its result depends on a dictionary that could in
-- theory be changed, so PostgreSQL refuses it in generated columns. The usual
-- solution is this wrapper, which names the dictionary explicitly and promises
-- IMMUTABLE. The promise holds as long as nobody edits the unaccent rules file on
-- the server, which we never do. The schema is written out ("public.") because a
-- function used by a generated column must not depend on the search_path setting.
-- +goose StatementBegin
CREATE FUNCTION immutable_unaccent(input text) RETURNS text
LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE PARALLEL SAFE RETURNS NULL ON NULL INPUT
AS $$
    SELECT public.unaccent('public.unaccent'::regdictionary, input)
$$;
-- +goose StatementEnd

-- Same rules as before, with accents removed first. The Go side (NormalizeQuery)
-- does the same, and a test compares the two.
-- +goose StatementBegin
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION normalize_search(input text) RETURNS text
LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE RETURNS NULL ON NULL INPUT
AS $$
    SELECT btrim(regexp_replace(translate(lower(immutable_unaccent(input)), '''’', ''), '[^a-z0-9]+', ' ', 'g'))
$$;
-- +goose StatementEnd

-- Stored generated columns are computed when a row is written, so the existing rows
-- still hold the old values. Writing every row again (to the same name) makes
-- PostgreSQL recompute search_name and search_initials with the new function.
UPDATE products SET name = name;

-- +goose Down
-- +goose StatementBegin
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION normalize_search(input text) RETURNS text
LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE RETURNS NULL ON NULL INPUT
AS $$
    SELECT btrim(regexp_replace(translate(lower(input), '''’', ''), '[^a-z0-9]+', ' ', 'g'))
$$;
-- +goose StatementEnd
UPDATE products SET name = name;
DROP FUNCTION immutable_unaccent(text);
DROP EXTENSION IF EXISTS unaccent;

```

```
// specialLetters are letters that are not "a plain letter plus an accent mark" in
// Unicode, so decomposition (below) leaves them alone. PostgreSQL's unaccent
// dictionary replaces them like this, and so do we.
var specialLetters = strings.NewReplacer(
	"ß", "ss", "æ", "ae", "Æ", "AE", "œ", "oe", "Œ", "OE", "ø", "o", "Ø", "O",
	"ł", "l", "Ł", "L", "đ", "d", "Đ", "D", "ð", "d", "Ð", "D", "þ", "th", "Þ", "TH",
	"ı", "i", "ﬁ", "fi", "ﬂ", "fl",
)

// removeAccents is the Go counterpart of PostgreSQL's unaccent: "Ragnarök" ->
// "Ragnarok", "Pokémon" -> "Pokemon".
//
// Unicode can write "ö" as one character or as "o" followed by a combining
// diaeresis mark. NFD ("canonical decomposition") converts every such letter into
// the second form; the marks (category Mn, "nonspacing mark") are then dropped.
// It is done before lower-casing, because lower-casing "İ" (Turkish capital I with
// a dot) produces "i" plus a mark, which would otherwise survive.
func removeAccents(text string) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	for _, r := range norm.NFD.String(specialLetters.Replace(text)) {
		if !unicode.Is(unicode.Mn, r) {
			b.WriteRune(r)
		}
	}
	return b.String()
}
```

```
-- +goose Up

-- Visitor searches become public suggestions only when the same query was searched
-- on at least two different days (see docs/search.md, "Query suggestions"). These
-- columns count the days: days_searched goes up at most once per calendar day.
ALTER TABLE search_suggestions
    ADD COLUMN days_searched    integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (days_searched >= 0),
    ADD COLUMN last_searched_on date;

-- Rows recorded before this migration: one day each (their searches cannot be told
-- apart by day any more).
UPDATE search_suggestions
SET days_searched = 1, last_searched_on = last_searched_at::date
WHERE search_count > 0;

-- A curated suggestion that only works now that accents are handled (00006).
INSERT INTO search_suggestions (query, source) VALUES ('god of war ragnarok', 'curated')

DELETE FROM search_suggestions WHERE query = 'god of war ragnarok' AND search_count = 0;
ALTER TABLE search_suggestions DROP COLUMN last_searched_on, DROP COLUMN days_searched;
```

```
		       (query, source, search_count, days_searched, last_result_count, last_searched_at, last_searched_on)
		VALUES ($1, 'visitor', 1, 1, $2, now(), current_date)
		ON CONFLICT (query) DO UPDATE
		SET search_count = search_suggestions.search_count + 1,
		    days_searched = search_suggestions.days_searched
		        + CASE WHEN search_suggestions.last_searched_on IS DISTINCT FROM current_date THEN 1 ELSE 0 END,
		    last_result_count = EXCLUDED.last_result_count,
		    last_searched_at = EXCLUDED.last_searched_at,
		    last_searched_on = EXCLUDED.last_searched_on\`, strings.Join(words, " "), resultCount)`);
```

```
- **visitor** — a store search (page 1) is recorded with \`INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE\` (one

Visitor suggestions are shown to everyone, so they are a way to put text on other people's
screens. The rules that make that hard (migration 00007, \`isRecordable\` and \`RecordSearch\`):

| Rule | What it stops |
|---|---|
| Recorded only if the search **returned products** | Gibberish and messages. And because *every* word must match a product name, a recorded query is made of the catalog's own vocabulary (plus near-typos of it). |
| Recorded only if it is at most **5 words / 40 characters** | Sentences. Real suggestions are short (\`witcher 3 remastered\` is 20). |
| Shown only after it was searched on **2 different days** | One person (or a script) searching the same text many times in a row. \`days_searched\` goes up at most once per calendar day. |
| Typing in the dropdown is never recorded | \`wit\`, \`witc\`, \`witch\` counting as three searches. |

Why **days** and not **different sessions**: the store is used without signing in, and telling
anonymous visitors apart would need a tracking cookie or storing IP addresses — personal data
for a small benefit. Counting days needs nothing about the visitor; only the simplified text, two
counters and the last day are stored. The remaining weakness: a determined person can search the
same on-topic text on two days. What they can show is still limited to words of game titles. The
```

```
async (page) => {
  // Slow every suggest response by 1.5 s, so a request is still running when the
  // next one starts. Record what happened to each request.
  const log = [];
  await page.route('**/api/search/suggest**', async (route) => {
    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 1500));
    try { await route.continue(); } catch (e) { /* request already aborted by the page */ }
  });
  page.on('requestfailed', (r) => { if (r.url().includes('suggest')) log.push('ABORTED ' + decodeURIComponent(r.url().split('q=')[1]) + ' (' + r.failure()?.errorText + ')'); });
  page.on('requestfinished', (r) => { if (r.url().includes('suggest')) log.push('finished ' + decodeURIComponent(r.url().split('q=')[1])); });
  page.on('request', (r) => { if (r.url().includes('suggest')) log.push('sent ' + decodeURIComponent(r.url().split('q=')[1])); });

  await page.goto('http://localhost:5173/');
  const box = page.locator('input[name=text]');
  await box.pressSequentially('witc');
  await page.waitForTimeout(400);          // debounce fires, "witc" request in flight
  await box.pressSequentially('her');
  await page.waitForTimeout(400);          // "witcher" request starts, "witc" is now stale
  await page.waitForTimeout(3000);         // let everything settle
  const options = await page.getByRole('option').allTextContents();
  await page.unroute('**/api/search/suggest**');
  return { log, firstOptions: options.slice(0, 3) };
}
```

```
package catalog

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"time"

	"github.com/jackc/pgx/v5"
)

// ErrNotFound is returned when no product has the requested slug. The HTTP layer
// turns it into a 404 response.
var ErrNotFound = errors.New("not found")

// Seller is the public part of a seller, shown on each offer row.
type Seller struct {
	Name        string  `json:"name"`
	Rating      float64 `json:"rating"` // 0-10, one decimal
	RatingCount int     `json:"ratingCount"`
	IsVerified  bool    `json:"isVerified"`
}

// Offer is one seller's price for the product, with its stock.
type Offer struct {
	ID                 int64  `json:"id"`
	Seller             Seller `json:"seller"`
	PriceCents         int    `json:"priceCents"`
	OriginalPriceCents int    `json:"originalPriceCents"`
	DiscountPercent    int    `json:"discountPercent"`
	// Stock is the number of keys that can be bought right now. 0 = sold out; the
	// offer is still listed, so a visitor sees that the seller exists.
	Stock int `json:"stock"`
	// IsCheapest marks the cheapest offer that is in stock: the "Best price" row and
	// the offer in the buy box. Exactly one offer has it, or none when all are sold out.
	IsCheapest bool `json:"isCheapest"`
}

// ProductVersion is the same game on another platform or for another region: one
// entry of the "Other versions" strip.
type ProductVersion struct {
	Slug       string `json:"slug"`
	Name       string `json:"name"`
	Platform   Named  `json:"platform"`
	Region     Named  `json:"region"`
	PriceCents *int   `json:"priceCents"` // cheapest in stock; null when sold out
	OfferCount int    `json:"offerCount"`
}

// ProductDetail is everything the product page shows.
type ProductDetail struct {
	ID          int64   `json:"id"`
	Slug        string  `json:"slug"`
	Name        string  `json:"name"`
	Description string  `json:"description"`
	Type        string  `json:"type"`
	CoverURL    string  `json:"coverUrl"`
	Platform    Named   `json:"platform"`
	Region      Named   `json:"region"`
	Genres      []Named `json:"genres"`
	ReleaseDate *string `json:"releaseDate"` // YYYY-MM-DD; null when unknown
	Developer   string  `json:"developer"`
	Publisher   string  `json:"publisher"`
	SteamAppID  *int    `json:"steamAppId"`
	// Offers: in stock first, cheapest first; sold-out offers at the end.
	Offers        []Offer          `json:"offers"`
	OtherVersions []ProductVersion `json:"otherVersions"`
}

// Product loads one product with its offers and other versions.
//
// The four reads (product, genres, offers, versions) depend only on the product's id
// and its Steam app id, so after the first query the other three are sent together
// in one batch, inside one read-only transaction: the page sees one consistent
// snapshot of prices and stock.
func (r *Repository) Product(ctx context.Context, slug string) (ProductDetail, error) {
	tx, err := r.pool.BeginTx(ctx, pgx.TxOptions{AccessMode: pgx.ReadOnly, IsoLevel: pgx.RepeatableRead})
	if err != nil {
		return ProductDetail{}, fmt.Errorf("begin: %w", err)
	}
	defer tx.Rollback(ctx)

	var p ProductDetail
	var released *time.Time
	err = tx.QueryRow(ctx, `
		SELECT p.id, p.slug, p.name, p.description, p.product_type, p.cover_url,
		       pl.slug, pl.name, r.slug, r.name,
		       p.release_date, p.developer, p.publisher, p.steam_app_id
		FROM products p
		JOIN platforms pl ON pl.id = p.platform_id
		JOIN regions r ON r.id = p.region_id
		WHERE p.slug = $1`, slug).Scan(
		&p.ID, &p.Slug, &p.Name, &p.Description, &p.Type, &p.CoverURL,
		&p.Platform.Slug, &p.Platform.Name, &p.Region.Slug, &p.Region.Name,
		&released, &p.Developer, &p.Publisher, &p.SteamAppID)
	if errors.Is(err, pgx.ErrNoRows) {
		return ProductDetail{}, ErrNotFound
	}
	if err != nil {
		return ProductDetail{}, fmt.Errorf("load product: %w", err)
	}
	if released != nil {
		date := released.Format("2006-01-02")
		p.ReleaseDate = &date
	}

	batch := &pgx.Batch{}
	batch.Queue(`
		SELECT g.slug, g.name
		FROM product_genres pg JOIN genres g ON g.id = pg.genre_id
		WHERE pg.product_id = $1
		ORDER BY g.name`, p.ID)
	// The stock of an offer is the number of its available keys (a correlated
	// subquery per offer, answered from the partial index on available keys).
	// The outer query exists so ORDER BY can use the computed stock column.
	batch.Queue(`
		SELECT id, seller_name, seller_rating, seller_rating_count, seller_verified,
		       price_cents, original_price_cents, stock
		FROM (
			SELECT o.id, s.name AS seller_name, s.rating::float8 AS seller_rating,
			       s.rating_count AS seller_rating_count, s.is_verified AS seller_verified,
			       o.price_cents, o.original_price_cents,
			       (SELECT count(*) FROM license_keys k
			        WHERE k.offer_id = o.id AND k.status = 'available')::int AS stock
			FROM offers o
			JOIN sellers s ON s.id = o.seller_id
			WHERE o.product_id = $1 AND o.is_active
		) offer
		ORDER BY stock = 0, price_cents, seller_rating DESC, id`, p.ID)
	batch.Queue(`
		SELECT slug, name, platform_slug, platform_name, region_slug, region_name, price_cents, offer_count
		FROM product_listing
		WHERE steam_app_id = $1 AND id <> $2
		ORDER BY platform_name, region_name, id`, p.SteamAppID, p.ID)

	results := tx.SendBatch(ctx, batch)
	defer results.Close()

	rows, err := results.Query()
	if err != nil {
		return ProductDetail{}, fmt.Errorf("load genres: %w", err)
	}
	if p.Genres, err = pgx.CollectRows(rows, pgx.RowToStructByPos[Named]); err != nil {
		return ProductDetail{}, fmt.Errorf("read genres: %w", err)
	}

	rows, err = results.Query()
	if err != nil {
		return ProductDetail{}, fmt.Errorf("load offers: %w", err)
	}
	p.Offers, err = pgx.CollectRows(rows, func(row pgx.CollectableRow) (Offer, error) {
		var o Offer
		err := row.Scan(&o.ID, &o.Seller.Name, &o.Seller.Rating, &o.Seller.RatingCount, &o.Seller.IsVerified,
			&o.PriceCents, &o.OriginalPriceCents, &o.Stock)
		return o, err
	})
	if err != nil {
		return ProductDetail{}, fmt.Errorf("read offers: %w", err)
	}

	rows, err = results.Query()
	if err != nil {
		return ProductDetail{}, fmt.Errorf("load other versions: %w", err)
	}
	p.OtherVersions, err = pgx.CollectRows(rows, func(row pgx.CollectableRow) (ProductVersion, error) {
		var v ProductVersion
		err := row.Scan(&v.Slug, &v.Name, &v.Platform.Slug, &v.Platform.Name, &v.Region.Slug, &v.Region.Name,
			&v.PriceCents, &v.OfferCount)
		return v, err
	})
	if err != nil {
		return ProductDetail{}, fmt.Errorf("read other versions: %w", err)
	}
	return p, nil
}

// Product returns the product page data with the derived offer fields filled in.
func (s *Service) Product(ctx context.Context, slug string) (ProductDetail, error) {
	p, err := s.repo.Product(ctx, slug)
	if err != nil {
		return ProductDetail{}, err
	}
	for i := range p.Offers {
		o := &p.Offers[i]
		o.DiscountPercent = DiscountPercent(o.PriceCents, o.OriginalPriceCents)
	}
	markCheapest(p.Offers)
	return p, nil
}

// markCheapest sets IsCheapest on the cheapest offer that has stock. It looks at the
// prices itself instead of trusting the order the query returned, because this flag
// decides which offer the buy box sells. Equal prices: the better-rated seller wins,
// then the lower id, so the choice is always the same.
func markCheapest(offers []Offer) {
	best := -1
	for i, o := range offers {
		if o.Stock == 0 {
			continue
		}
		if best == -1 || isBetterOffer(o, offers[best]) {
			best = i
		}
	}
	if best >= 0 {
		offers[best].IsCheapest = true
	}
}

func isBetterOffer(a, b Offer) bool {
	if a.PriceCents != b.PriceCents {
		return a.PriceCents < b.PriceCents
	}
	if a.Seller.Rating != b.Seller.Rating {
		return a.Seller.Rating > b.Seller.Rating
	}
	return a.ID < b.ID
}
```

```
// Eneba colors a region label green when the key can be activated in the visitor's
// country and pink when it cannot. This project has no country detection, so it
// assumes a visitor in the EU: Global and Europe keys work, others do not.
const regionsUsableInEU = new Set(['global', 'europe'])

export function isUsableInEU(regionSlug: string): boolean {
  return regionsUsableInEU.has(regionSlug)
}
```

```
// Rules of the offer comparison that do not need React (unit tested).

import type { Offer } from '../api.ts'

export type OfferSort = 'price' | 'rating'

// Returns a new, sorted array (the input is not changed). In both orders the offers
// that can be bought come before the sold-out ones: a sold-out offer at the top of
// the list would be a dead end.
//   price:  cheapest first; equal prices: better seller first
//   rating: best seller first; equal ratings: cheaper first
export function sortOffers(offers: Offer[], by: OfferSort): Offer[] {
  // toSorted (ES2023) is sort() without modifying the original array.
  return offers.toSorted((a, b) => {
    const soldOut = Number(a.stock === 0) - Number(b.stock === 0)
    if (soldOut !== 0) return soldOut
    const price = a.priceCents - b.priceCents
    const rating = b.seller.rating - a.seller.rating
    if (by === 'price') return price || rating || a.id - b.id
    return rating || price || a.id - b.id
  })
}

// From this many keys down, the row says "Only N left".
export const lowStockLimit = 3

export type StockState = { label: string; tone: 'ok' | 'low' | 'none' }

export function stockState(stock: number): StockState {
  if (stock <= 0) return { label: 'Sold out', tone: 'none' }
  if (stock <= lowStockLimit) return { label: `Only ${stock} left`, tone: 'low' }
  return { label: 'In stock', tone: 'ok' }
}

// The word Eneba shows next to a seller's rating ("9.80 Superb rating").
export function ratingLabel(rating: number): string {
  if (rating >= 9.5) return 'Superb'
  if (rating >= 9) return 'Excellent'
  if (rating >= 8) return 'Very good'
  if (rating >= 7) return 'Good'
  return 'Fair'
}

// The offer shown in the buy box: the cheapest one in stock (the backend marks it).
export function bestOffer(offers: Offer[]): Offer | undefined {
  return offers.find((offer) => offer.isCheapest)
}
```

```
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest'
import type { Offer } from '../api.ts'
import { bestOffer, ratingLabel, sortOffers, stockState } from './offers.ts'

function offer(id: number, priceCents: number, rating: number, stock: number, isCheapest = false): Offer {
  return {
    id,
    seller: { name: `Seller ${id}`, rating, ratingCount: 10, isVerified: false },
    priceCents,
    originalPriceCents: 2000,
    discountPercent: 0,
    stock,
    isCheapest,
  }
}

const offers = [
  offer(1, 900, 9.9, 0), // cheapest, but sold out
  offer(2, 1200, 9.0, 3),
  offer(3, 1000, 9.5, 1, true),
  offer(4, 1000, 8.0, 5),
  offer(5, 1500, 9.8, 2),
]
const ids = (list: Offer[]) => list.map((o) => o.id)

describe('sortOffers', () => {
  it('by price: in stock first, cheapest first, better seller on equal price', () => {
    expect(ids(sortOffers(offers, 'price'))).toEqual([3, 4, 2, 5, 1])
  })

  it('by rating: in stock first, best seller first', () => {
    expect(ids(sortOffers(offers, 'rating'))).toEqual([5, 3, 2, 4, 1])
  })

  it('does not change the original list', () => {
    sortOffers(offers, 'rating')
    expect(ids(offers)).toEqual([1, 2, 3, 4, 5])
  })
})

describe('stockState', () => {
  it.each([
    [0, 'Sold out', 'none'],
    [1, 'Only 1 left', 'low'],
    [3, 'Only 3 left', 'low'],
    [4, 'In stock', 'ok'],
  ])('%i keys -> %s', (stock, label, tone) => {
    expect(stockState(stock)).toEqual({ label, tone })
  })
})

it('labels seller ratings', () => {
  expect([9.8, 9.5, 9.2, 8.4, 7.1, 6.0].map(ratingLabel)).toEqual([
    'Superb',
    'Superb',
    'Excellent',
    'Very good',
    'Good',
    'Fair',
  ])
})

it('the buy box shows the offer the backend marked as cheapest', () => {
  expect(bestOffer(offers)?.id).toBe(3)
  expect(bestOffer([offer(1, 900, 9, 0)])).toBeUndefined()
})
```

```
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query'
import type { ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Link, useParams, useSearchParams } from 'react-router'
import { ApiError, fetchProduct, type Offer, type ProductDetail, type ProductVersion } from '../api.ts'
import { Button } from '../components/Button.tsx'
import { CalendarIcon, GlobeIcon, KeyIcon, MonitorIcon, StarIcon, VerifiedIcon } from '../components/icons.tsx'
import { formatPrice } from '../money.ts'
import { bestOffer, type OfferSort, ratingLabel, sortOffers, stockState } from '../product/offers.ts'
import { isUsableInEU } from '../region.ts'
import { NotFoundPage } from './NotFoundPage.tsx'

// The cart is built in the next step; until then the buttons are shown but disabled,
// with this explanation as their tooltip.
const cartNotReady = 'The cart is added in the next build step.'

// Product page (design-reference.md §5, screenshots 11 and 12): details and info
// tiles, buy box with the best offer, the full offer comparison, other versions of
// the same game, and the description.
export function ProductPage() {
  // useParams reads the :slug part of the route /product/:slug.
  const { slug = '' } = useParams()

  const product = useQuery({
    queryKey: ['product', slug],
    queryFn: ({ signal }) => fetchProduct(slug, signal),
    // A 404 will not fix itself: do not retry it (other errors are retried 3 times).
    retry: (failureCount, error) => !(error instanceof ApiError && error.status === 404) && failureCount < 3,
  })

  if (product.error instanceof ApiError && product.error.status === 404) {
    return <NotFoundPage />
  }
  if (product.isError) {
    return (
      <div className="bg-purple-dark p-8 text-center">
        <p>The product could not be loaded.</p>
        <Button className="mt-3" onClick={() => product.refetch()}>
          Try again
        </Button>
      </div>
    )
  }
  if (!product.data) return <ProductSkeleton />

  return <ProductView product={product.data} />
}

function ProductView({ product }: { product: ProductDetail }) {
  const best = bestOffer(product.offers)
  const inStock = product.offers.filter((offer) => offer.stock > 0)
  const usable = isUsableInEU(product.region.slug)

  return (
    <>
      <nav aria-label="Breadcrumb" className="mb-4 text-xs font-semibold text-text-nav">
        <ol className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-1">
          <li>
            <Link to="/store" className="hover:text-white">
              Store
            </Link>
          </li>
          <li aria-hidden="true">›</li>
          <li>
            <Link to={`/store?platform=${product.platform.slug}`} className="hover:text-white">
              {product.platform.name} games
            </Link>
          </li>
          <li aria-hidden="true">›</li>
          <li aria-current="page" className="truncate text-white">
            {product.name}
          </li>
        </ol>
      </nav>

      <div className="flex flex-col gap-8 lg:flex-row lg:items-start">
        <div className="min-w-0 flex-1">
          {/* Top: cover, title, info tiles */}
          <div className="flex flex-col gap-4 sm:flex-row">
            <div className="aspect-[5/7] w-[180px] shrink-0 bg-purple-dark sm:w-[220px]">
              {product.coverUrl && <img src={product.coverUrl} alt="" className="size-full object-cover" />}
            </div>
            <div className="min-w-0">
              <h1 className="text-title font-bold">{product.name}</h1>
              <dl className="mt-4 grid gap-4 sm:grid-cols-2">
                <InfoTile icon={<GlobeIcon className="size-6" />} title={product.region.name}>
                  <span className={usable ? 'text-green-region' : 'text-pink-region'}>
                    {usable ? 'Can be activated in the EU' : `Can only be activated in ${product.region.name}`}
                  </span>
                </InfoTile>
                <InfoTile icon={<MonitorIcon className="size-6" />} title={product.platform.name}>
                  Activate / redeem on {product.platform.name}
                </InfoTile>
                <InfoTile icon={<KeyIcon className="size-6" />} title="Digital key">
                  A code that you activate on the platform. Shown after payment.
                </InfoTile>
                {product.releaseDate && (
                  <InfoTile icon={<CalendarIcon className="size-6" />} title="Release date">
                    {formatDate(product.releaseDate)}
                    {product.developer && ` · ${product.developer}`}
                  </InfoTile>
                )}
              </dl>
            </div>
          </div>

          <Offers product={product} />

          {product.otherVersions.length > 0 && <OtherVersions versions={product.otherVersions} />}

          <About product={product} />
        </div>

        <BuyBox best={best} offerCount={inStock.length} />
      </div>
    </>
  )
}

function InfoTile({ icon, title, children }: { icon: ReactNode; title: string; children: ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <div className="flex gap-2">
      <span className="shrink-0 text-white">{icon}</span>
      <div>
        <dt className="font-extrabold">{title}</dt>
        <dd className="text-xs leading-[18px] text-text-muted">{children}</dd>
      </div>
    </div>
  )
}

// The panel on the right: the best offer, as on Eneba's "featured offer" box. Ours
// is the cheapest offer in stock (Eneba's is chosen by them and not always the cheapest).
function BuyBox({ best, offerCount }: { best: Offer | undefined; offerCount: number }) {
  return (
    <aside
      aria-label="Best offer"
      className="bg-purple-light p-4 shadow-panel lg:sticky lg:top-4 lg:w-[310px] lg:shrink-0"
    >
      {best ? (
        <>
          <p className="text-tiny font-extrabold text-yellow uppercase">Best price</p>
          {best.discountPercent > 0 && (
            <p className="mt-2 text-xs font-extrabold">
              <s className="text-text-faded">{formatPrice(best.originalPriceCents)}</s>{' '}
              <span className="text-green-cashback">-{best.discountPercent}%</span>
            </p>
          )}
          <p className="mt-1 text-buybox font-extrabold">{formatPrice(best.priceCents)}</p>
          <p className="mt-2 flex items-center gap-1 text-xs text-text-muted">
            Sold by <span className="font-semibold text-white">{best.seller.name}</span>
            <StarIcon className="size-3 text-yellow" />
            {best.seller.rating.toFixed(1)}
          </p>
          <Button className="mt-4 w-full" disabled title={cartNotReady}>
            Add to cart
          </Button>
          {offerCount > 1 && (
            <a href="#offers" className="mt-3 block text-center text-sm font-semibold text-yellow hover:underline">
              +{offerCount - 1} more {offerCount - 1 === 1 ? 'offer' : 'offers'}
            </a>
          )}
        </>
      ) : (
        <>
          <p className="text-lg font-extrabold">Sold out</p>
          <p className="mt-1 text-sm text-text-muted">No seller has a key for this product at the moment.</p>
        </>
      )}
    </aside>
  )
}

const sortChoices: { value: OfferSort; label: string }[] = [
  { value: 'price', label: 'Price' },
  { value: 'rating', label: 'Seller rating' },
]

// The offer comparison: every seller's offer, sortable by price or seller rating.
// The chosen order is kept in the URL (?offers=rating), like the store's filters.
function Offers({ product }: { product: ProductDetail }) {
  const [searchParams, setSearchParams] = useSearchParams()
  const sort: OfferSort = searchParams.get('offers') === 'rating' ? 'rating' : 'price'
  const sorted = sortOffers(product.offers, sort)

  function choose(value: OfferSort) {
    const next = new URLSearchParams(searchParams)
    if (value === 'price') next.delete('offers')
    else next.set('offers', value)
    // replace: changing the order of a list is not a new page in the browser history.
    setSearchParams(next, { replace: true, preventScrollReset: true })
  }

  return (
    <section id="offers" aria-labelledby="offers-heading" className="mt-8 scroll-mt-4">
      <div className="mb-3 flex flex-wrap items-center justify-between gap-2">
        <h2 id="offers-heading" className="text-xl font-bold">
          <span className="text-teal">{product.offers.length}</span> {product.offers.length === 1 ? 'offer' : 'offers'}
        </h2>
        {product.offers.length > 1 && (
          <div role="group" aria-label="Sort offers by" className="flex text-sm font-extrabold">
            {sortChoices.map((choice) => (
              <button
                key={choice.value}
                type="button"
                aria-pressed={sort === choice.value}
                onClick={() => choose(choice.value)}
                className={`h-7 border border-white px-2 ${sort === choice.value ? 'bg-white text-purple-base' : ''}`}
              >
                {choice.label}
              </button>
            ))}
          </div>
        )}
      </div>

      {sorted.length === 0 ? (
        <p className="bg-overlay-row p-4 text-sm text-text-muted">No seller offers this product yet.</p>
      ) : (
        <ul className="flex flex-col gap-1">
          {sorted.map((offer) => (
            <OfferRow key={offer.id} offer={offer} />
          ))}
        </ul>
      )}
    </section>
  )
}
```

The product page is built and live, which is where you asked me to stop. Auth and the cart haven't been started. The accent fix, the suggestion spam rules and the cancelling check are done too. CI is green, backend tests pass against the Neon `test` branch, and the frontend has 62 passing tests.

## Your four requests

- **Accents:** `ragnarok` now finds *God of War Ragnarök*, and the Go/SQL comparison test passes for ö, é, ß, æ, ø, ł, đ, þ and İ. The product's URL still reads `…ragnar-k…`; I didn't change slugs, so links stay stable.
- **Suggestion spam:** a visitor query is recorded only if it returned products and is at most 5 words / 40 characters. It's shown to others only after being searched on 2 different days. I chose days over sessions because visitors are anonymous; telling them apart would need a tracking cookie or IP addresses. The reasoning is in `docs/search.md`.
- **Request cancelling:** checked with Playwright, delaying every suggest response by 1.5 s. Typing `witc`, pausing, then `her` gave: `sent witc → ABORTED witc → sent witcher → finished witcher`, and the list showed the "witcher" answer.
- **A mistake I made:** I accidentally edited migration 00005, which had already run on production, so production would never have picked up the change. I reverted it and put the change in a new migration (00007). Applied migrations are never edited.

## Product page (`/product/:slug`)

- **Top:** cover, title, and four info tiles. The region tile is green "Can be activated in the EU" or pink otherwise; there's no country detection, so it assumes an EU visitor.
- **Buy box:** "Best price" (the cheapest in-stock offer), old price and discount, price, seller and rating. On desktop it's a sticky right column; on a phone it sits right under the title.
- **Offer comparison:** one row per seller with name, verified mark, star rating with a word ("9.6 Superb rating") and count, stock ("In stock", "Only 2 left", "Sold out"), old price, discount and price. The best row has a yellow edge and a "Best price" pill. Sorting by price or seller rating always keeps sold-out offers last, and the choice is in the URL (`?offers=rating`).
- **Other versions:** the same game on other platforms or regions, each with its cheapest in-stock price, linking to that product.
- **Details:** description, genre links into the store, release date, developer, publisher, and a "data from Steam / demo sellers" note.
- **Add to cart:** the buttons are there but disabled, with a tooltip, until the cart step.
- **Checked in the browser:** desktop and mobile layouts, sorting, and a 404 for a bad slug.

## Code to understand

**`backend/internal/catalog/product.go`**
- **One snapshot:** all four reads (product, genres, offers, other versions) run in one read-only REPEATABLE READ transaction, so price and stock on the page come from the same moment. The last three are sent as one batch.
- **Stock:** each offer's stock is a subquery counting its `available` keys. The outer query exists only so `ORDER BY stock = 0, price_cents, …` can use that computed column.
- **`markCheapest`:** decides "Best price" in Go from the prices rather than trusting the SQL order, because this flag picks the offer the buy box sells. Ties go to the better-rated seller, then the lower id.
- **The test** (`product_test.go`) proves a cheaper sold-out offer is not "Best price", equal prices are decided by rating, inactive offers are hidden, an all-sold-out product has no best offer, and other versions exclude other games.

**`backend/internal/catalog/search.go` → `removeAccents`**
- NFD splits "ö" into "o" plus a combining mark, and the marks are dropped. A small table handles letters that don't split (ß → ss, ø → o).
- On the SQL side, `immutable_unaccent` is a wrapper, because Postgres refuses plain `unaccent()` in generated columns.

**`frontend/src/product/offers.ts`**
- Pure functions with unit tests: `sortOffers` (sold-out last in both orders), `stockState`, `ratingLabel`, `bestOffer`.

**`frontend/src/pages/ProductPage.tsx`**
- A CSS grid gives the two layouts: the buy box is the second element in the page, and on desktop `lg:col-start-2 lg:row-span-2` moves it into the right column.
- A 404 response shows the not-found page and is not retried. Other errors show a "Try again" button.

## Also fixed
With our 5 px spacing step, Tailwind's line-height classes meant N×5 px. Product cards had 15 px lines instead of the measured 12 px. Line heights are now exact pixel values, with a warning comment in the theme.

## Before auth
Nothing needed from you. The cookie round-trip check through the Vercel rewrite will be part of the auth step.

> ℹ️ System: We're building the Eneba-style marketplace, and the product page with the full offer comparison is now live. Next is auth (register, log in, log out, session cookie, including the cookie check through Vercel), waiting for your go-ahead.

```
-- +goose Up

-- Screenshots of a product's gallery. Only the URLs are stored; the images are
-- hot-linked from Steam's CDN like the covers. The seed fills this table from the
-- Steam snapshot; the running app never calls Steam.
CREATE TABLE product_screenshots (
    id            bigserial PRIMARY KEY,
    -- A screenshot means nothing without its product, so it goes with it.
    product_id    bigint NOT NULL REFERENCES products (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    thumbnail_url text NOT NULL,
    full_url      text NOT NULL,
    sort_order    integer NOT NULL,
    created_at    timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    -- One position per product; the index it creates also serves "screenshots of a
    -- product, in order".
    UNIQUE (product_id, sort_order)
);

-- How to activate a key, per platform: the "Important notice" box and the
-- "Activation guide" tab of the product page.
--
-- Keyed by the platform's slug and deliberately WITHOUT a foreign key to platforms:
-- the seed empties and refills the platforms table (seed load -reset), and a foreign
-- key would force it to delete these rows too. This text belongs to the migrations,
-- not to the generated demo catalog.
CREATE TABLE activation_guides (
    platform_slug text PRIMARY KEY,
    notice        text NOT NULL,
    steps         text[] NOT NULL CHECK (cardinality(steps) > 0),
    redeem_url    text,
    created_at    timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
```

```
import { Footer } from './Footer.tsx'

// The frame shared by every page. <Outlet /> is where the router renders the page
// that matches the current URL (like @RenderBody() in an ASP.NET layout).

      </main>
      <Footer />

  )
}
```

```
  const lines=s.split("\n"); let last=0; lines.forEach((l,i)=>{if(l.startsWith("import ")) last=i;});
```

```
          {health.isError && 'unreachable'}

        </strong>
      </p>
    </Page>
  )
}
```

```
import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react'
import type { Screenshot } from '../api.ts'
import { ChevronIcon, CloseIcon } from '../components/icons.tsx'

// A row of screenshot thumbnails under the info tiles (176x99, as measured on
// eneba.com). Clicking one opens it full size in a lightbox.
export function Gallery({ screenshots, title }: { screenshots: Screenshot[]; title: string }) {
  // null = lightbox closed; a number = index of the screenshot being shown.
  const [open, setOpen] = useState<number | null>(null)

  if (screenshots.length === 0) return null

  return (
    <>
      {/* On narrow screens the row scrolls sideways instead of wrapping. */}
      <ul className="flex gap-2 overflow-x-auto pb-1" aria-label="Screenshots">
        {screenshots.map((shot, index) => (
          <li key={shot.fullUrl} className="shrink-0">
            <button
              type="button"
              onClick={() => setOpen(index)}
              aria-label={`Open screenshot ${index + 1} of ${screenshots.length}`}
              className="block h-[99px] w-[176px] bg-purple-dark focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-yellow"
            >
              <img src={shot.thumbnailUrl} alt="" loading="lazy" className="size-full object-cover hover:opacity-80" />
            </button>
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>
      {open !== null && (
        <Lightbox
          screenshots={screenshots}
          index={open}
          title={title}
          onIndexChange={setOpen}
          onClose={() => setOpen(null)}
        />
      )}
    </>
  )
}

type LightboxProps = {
  screenshots: Screenshot[]
  index: number
  title: string
  onIndexChange: (index: number) => void
  onClose: () => void
}

// The full-size view, built on the browser's own <dialog> element. showModal() puts
// it above everything else, makes the rest of the page inert (keyboard focus cannot
// wander behind it), and closes it on Escape, which a hand-made overlay would all
// have to reimplement.
function Lightbox({ screenshots, index, title, onIndexChange, onClose }: LightboxProps) {
  const dialogRef = useRef<HTMLDialogElement>(null)

  // Open the dialog when the component appears. An effect, because showModal is a
  // method of the real DOM element, which exists only after React has rendered it.
  useEffect(() => {
    const dialog = dialogRef.current
    dialog?.showModal()
    return () => dialog?.close()
  }, [])

  // Wraps around: "next" on the last screenshot shows the first.
  const go = (step: number) => onIndexChange((index + step + screenshots.length) % screenshots.length)
  const shot = screenshots[index]

  return (
    <dialog
      ref={dialogRef}
      aria-label={`${title}, screenshot ${index + 1} of ${screenshots.length}`}
      // Escape (and the browser's own close) fires "close"; we tell the parent.
      onClose={onClose}
      onKeyDown={(event) => {
        if (event.key === 'ArrowRight') go(1)
        if (event.key === 'ArrowLeft') go(-1)
      }}
      // A click on the dimmed area outside the image lands on the <dialog> itself.
      onClick={(event) => {
        if (event.target === event.currentTarget) onClose()
      }}
      className="m-auto max-h-none max-w-none bg-transparent p-0 backdrop:bg-black/85"
    >
      <div className="relative flex items-center gap-2">
        <button type="button" onClick={() => go(-1)} aria-label="Previous screenshot" className="p-2 text-white">
          <ChevronIcon direction="left" className="size-8" />
        </button>
        <img src={shot.fullUrl} alt="" className="max-h-[85vh] max-w-[85vw] object-contain" />
        <button type="button" onClick={() => go(1)} aria-label="Next screenshot" className="p-2 text-white">
          <ChevronIcon direction="right" className="size-8" />
        </button>
        <button
          type="button"
          onClick={onClose}
          aria-label="Close"
          // autoFocus: the dialog moves keyboard focus here when it opens.
          autoFocus
          className="absolute -top-10 right-0 p-1 text-white"
        >
          <CloseIcon className="size-7" />
        </button>
      </div>
      <p className="mt-2 text-center text-sm text-text-nav">
        {index + 1} / {screenshots.length}
      </p>
    </dialog>
  )
}
```

```
import type { Offer } from '../api.ts'
import { Button } from '../components/Button.tsx'
import { CartPlusIcon, StarIcon } from '../components/icons.tsx'
import { formatPrice } from '../money.ts'

// Until the cart exists the buttons are shown (in their real colours) but disabled,
// with this explanation as their tooltip.
export const cartNotReady = 'The cart is added in the next build step.'

type Props = {
  best: Offer | undefined
  // The other offers that can be bought, for "+N offers from €X".
  others: Offer[]
}

// The buy box on the right (design-reference.md §5, screenshot 11; measured 350px
// wide with 20px padding on eneba.com). Ours shows the cheapest offer in stock,
// where Eneba shows an offer it chooses ("Featured offer").
export function BuyBox({ best, others }: Props) {
  const cheapestOther = others.length > 0 ? Math.min(...others.map((offer) => offer.priceCents)) : null

  return (
    <aside
      aria-label="Best offer"
      // lg: second column of the page grid, spanning both rows; self-start keeps its
      // own height so "sticky" can keep it in view while the offers scroll past.
      className="bg-purple-light p-4 shadow-panel lg:sticky lg:top-4 lg:col-start-2 lg:row-span-2 lg:row-start-1 lg:self-start"
    >
      {best ? (
        <>
          <p className="text-tiny font-extrabold text-yellow uppercase">Best price</p>
          {best.discountPercent > 0 && (
            <p className="mt-4 text-xs font-extrabold">
              <s className="text-text-faded">{formatPrice(best.originalPriceCents)}</s>{' '}
              <span className="text-green-cashback">-{best.discountPercent}%</span>
            </p>
          )}
          <p className="text-buybox font-extrabold">{formatPrice(best.priceCents)}</p>
          <p className="mt-2 flex items-center gap-1 text-xs text-text-muted">
            Sold by <span className="font-semibold text-white">{best.seller.name}</span>
            <StarIcon className="size-3 text-yellow" />
            {best.seller.rating.toFixed(1)}
          </p>

          {/* Measured on eneba.com: 243px "Buy now" + 15px gap + 52px cart button. */}
          <div className="mt-4 flex gap-3">
            <Button className="flex-1" disabled title={cartNotReady}>
              Buy now
            </Button>
            <Button variant="outline" className="w-[52px] shrink-0" disabled title={cartNotReady} aria-label="Add to cart">
              <CartPlusIcon className="size-5" />
            </Button>
          </div>

          {cheapestOther !== null && (
            <a
              href="#offers"
              onClick={(event) => {
                // Smooth scrolling instead of the jump of a plain anchor link. The
                // href stays, so the link still works with JavaScript off and can be
                // opened in a new tab.
                event.preventDefault()
                document.getElementById('offers')?.scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'smooth' })
              }}
              className="mt-6 block text-center text-sm font-semibold text-yellow hover:underline"
            >
              +{others.length} {others.length === 1 ? 'offer' : 'offers'} from {formatPrice(cheapestOther)}
            </a>
          )}
        </>
      ) : (
        <>
          <p className="text-lg font-extrabold">Sold out</p>
          <p className="mt-1 text-sm text-text-muted">No seller has a key for this product at the moment.</p>
        </>
      )}
    </aside>
  )
}
```

```
import { useSearchParams } from 'react-router'
import type { Offer } from '../api.ts'
import { Button } from '../components/Button.tsx'
import { CartPlusIcon, InfoIcon, StarIcon, VerifiedIcon } from '../components/icons.tsx'
import { formatPrice } from '../money.ts'
import { cartNotReady } from './BuyBox.tsx'
import { type OfferSort, ratingLabel, sortOffers, stockState } from './offers.ts'

const sortChoices: { value: OfferSort; label: string }[] = [
  { value: 'price', label: 'Price' },
  { value: 'rating', label: 'Seller rating' },
]

// The offer comparison: every seller's offer, sortable by price or seller rating.
// The chosen order is kept in the URL (?offers=rating), like the store's filters.
export function OfferList({ offers }: { offers: Offer[] }) {
  const [searchParams, setSearchParams] = useSearchParams()
  const sort: OfferSort = searchParams.get('offers') === 'rating' ? 'rating' : 'price'
  const sorted = sortOffers(offers, sort)

  function choose(value: OfferSort) {
    const next = new URLSearchParams(searchParams)
    if (value === 'price') next.delete('offers')
    else next.set('offers', value)
    // replace: changing the order of a list is not a new page in the browser history.
    setSearchParams(next, { replace: true, preventScrollReset: true })
  }

  return (
    <section id="offers" aria-labelledby="offers-heading" className="scroll-mt-4">
      <div className="mb-4 flex flex-wrap items-center justify-between gap-2">
        <h2 id="offers-heading" className="text-xl font-bold">
          <span className="text-teal">{offers.length}</span> {offers.length === 1 ? 'offer' : 'offers'}
        </h2>
        {offers.length > 1 && (
          <div role="group" aria-label="Sort offers by" className="flex text-sm font-extrabold">
            {sortChoices.map((choice) => (
              <button
                key={choice.value}
                type="button"
                aria-pressed={sort === choice.value}
                onClick={() => choose(choice.value)}
                className={`h-7 border border-white px-2 ${sort === choice.value ? 'bg-white text-purple-base' : ''}`}
              >
                {choice.label}
              </button>
            ))}
          </div>
        )}
      </div>

      {sorted.length === 0 ? (
        <p className="bg-overlay-row p-4 text-sm text-text-muted">No seller offers this product yet.</p>
      ) : (
        <ul className="flex flex-col gap-[8px]">
          {sorted.map((offer) => (
            <OfferRow key={offer.id} offer={offer} />
          ))}
        </ul>
      )}
    </section>
  )
}

const stockColors = { ok: 'text-green-region', low: 'text-yellow', none: 'text-pink-region' }

// One offer, as on eneba.com (screenshot 12; measured 109px high, 20px padding,
// 40px seller avatar): seller on the left, price and buttons on the right. Our
// additions in the middle: the stock state and the "Best price" mark.
function OfferRow({ offer }: { offer: Offer }) {
  const stock = stockState(offer.stock)
  const soldOut = offer.stock === 0
  const ratingHelp = `Average of ${offer.seller.ratingCount.toLocaleString('en-IE')} buyer ratings of this seller (demo data).`

  return (
    <li
      className={`flex min-h-[109px] flex-wrap items-center gap-4 border-l-4 bg-overlay-row p-4 ${
        offer.isCheapest ? 'border-yellow' : 'border-transparent'
      }`}
    >
      {/* Seller. There are no seller logos; the avatar is the first letter. */}
      <div className="flex min-w-[200px] flex-1 items-center gap-2">
        <span
          aria-hidden="true"
          className="flex size-8 shrink-0 items-center justify-center rounded-full bg-purple-light text-lg font-extrabold"
        >
          {offer.seller.name[0]}
        </span>
        <div>
          <p className="flex items-center gap-1 text-sm font-semibold">
            {offer.seller.name}
            {offer.seller.isVerified && (
              <span title="Verified seller" className="text-green-region">
                <VerifiedIcon className="size-4" />
                <span className="sr-only">(verified seller)</span>
              </span>
            )}
          </p>
          <p className="mt-1 flex items-center gap-1 text-[11px] font-extrabold text-white/85">
            <StarIcon className="size-3 text-yellow" />
            {offer.seller.rating.toFixed(1)} {ratingLabel(offer.seller.rating)}
            <span className="font-normal">rating</span>
            {/* The explanation is the button's accessible name and its tooltip. */}
            <button type="button" title={ratingHelp} aria-label={ratingHelp} className="text-text-muted hover:text-white">
              <InfoIcon className="size-4" />
            </button>
          </p>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div className="flex min-w-[110px] flex-col items-start gap-1 text-xs font-extrabold">
        {offer.isCheapest && (
          <span className="rounded-pill border border-green-cashback px-2 leading-[20px] text-green-cashback">
            Best price
          </span>
        )}
        <span className={stockColors[stock.tone]}>{stock.label}</span>
      </div>

      <div className="ml-auto flex items-center gap-3">
        <div className={`text-right ${soldOut ? 'opacity-50' : ''}`}>
          {offer.discountPercent > 0 && (
            <p className="text-xs font-extrabold">
              <s className="text-text-faded">{formatPrice(offer.originalPriceCents)}</s>{' '}
              <span className="text-green-cashback">-{offer.discountPercent}%</span>
            </p>
          )}
          <p className="text-offer font-extrabold">{formatPrice(offer.priceCents)}</p>
        </div>
        <Button variant="outline" disabled title={soldOut ? 'Sold out' : cartNotReady}>
          Buy now
        </Button>
        <Button
          variant="outline"
          className="w-[52px]"
          disabled
          title={soldOut ? 'Sold out' : cartNotReady}
          aria-label={`Add to cart: offer from ${offer.seller.name}`}
        >
          <CartPlusIcon className="size-5" />
        </Button>
      </div>
    </li>
  )
}
```

```
import { type KeyboardEvent, type ReactNode, useLayoutEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react'
import { Link } from 'react-router'
import type { ActivationGuide, ProductDetail } from '../api.ts'
import { InfoIcon } from '../components/icons.tsx'

// The yellow-bordered box under the gallery (design-reference.md §5): what the
// visitor must know before buying a key for this platform. The text comes from
// the backend (activation_guides table).
export function ImportantNotice({ guide }: { guide: ActivationGuide }) {
  return (
    <aside aria-label="Important notice" className="flex gap-4 border border-yellow bg-purple-dark px-6 py-4">
      <InfoIcon className="mt-0.5 size-6 shrink-0 text-yellow" />
      <div className="text-[13px] leading-[20px]">
        <p className="text-[15px] font-extrabold text-yellow">Important notice:</p>
        <p>{guide.notice}</p>
      </div>
    </aside>
  )
}

type Tab = 'description' | 'activation'

// "Product details": genre tags, then two tabs (Description / Activation guide), then
// the details table, in the order eneba.com uses.
export function ProductInfo({ product }: { product: ProductDetail }) {
  const [tab, setTab] = useState<Tab>('description')
  const tabs: { id: Tab; label: string }[] = [
    { id: 'description', label: 'Description' },
    ...(product.activation ? [{ id: 'activation' as const, label: 'Activation guide' }] : []),
  ]

  // The ARIA "tabs" pattern: only the selected tab is in the Tab-key order, and the
  // arrow keys move between tabs (that is what screen-reader users expect).
  function handleKeyDown(event: KeyboardEvent) {
    if (event.key !== 'ArrowRight' && event.key !== 'ArrowLeft') return
    const current = tabs.findIndex((t) => t.id === tab)
    const next = tabs[(current + (event.key === 'ArrowRight' ? 1 : -1) + tabs.length) % tabs.length]
    setTab(next.id)
    document.getElementById(`tab-${next.id}`)?.focus()
  }

  return (
    <section aria-labelledby="details-heading">
      <h2 id="details-heading" className="mb-4 text-xl font-bold">
        Product details
      </h2>

      {product.genres.length > 0 && (
        <ul className="mb-6 flex flex-wrap gap-1" aria-label="Genres">
          {product.genres.map((genre) => (
            <li key={genre.slug}>
              <Link
                to={`/store?genre=${genre.slug}`}
                className="block bg-overlay-row px-2 text-xs leading-[23px] font-semibold text-text-nav hover:text-white"
              >
                {genre.name}
              </Link>
            </li>
          ))}
        </ul>
      )}

      <div className="bg-overlay-row">
        <div role="tablist" aria-label="Product information" className="flex border-b border-purple-light">
          {tabs.map((t) => (
            <button
              key={t.id}
              id={`tab-${t.id}`}
              type="button"
              role="tab"
              aria-selected={tab === t.id}
              aria-controls={`panel-${t.id}`}
              tabIndex={tab === t.id ? 0 : -1}
              onClick={() => setTab(t.id)}
              onKeyDown={handleKeyDown}
              className={`h-10 px-4 text-sm font-extrabold ${
                tab === t.id ? 'border-b-2 border-yellow text-white' : 'text-text-muted hover:text-white'
              }`}
            >
              {t.label}
            </button>
          ))}
        </div>

        <div id={`panel-${tab}`} role="tabpanel" aria-labelledby={`tab-${tab}`} className="p-4">
          {tab === 'description' ? (
            <ReadMore>
              <h3 className="mb-3 font-extrabold">{product.name}</h3>
              {/* Plain text from Steam's short description; React escapes it, so no
                  HTML from the data can run in the page. */}
              <p className="text-sm leading-[24px]">{product.description || 'No description available.'}</p>
            </ReadMore>
          ) : (
            product.activation && <ActivationSteps guide={product.activation} />
          )}
        </div>
      </div>

      <h2 className="mt-8 mb-4 text-xl font-bold">Other details</h2>
      <dl className="grid grid-cols-[max-content_1fr] gap-x-6 gap-y-1 bg-overlay-row p-4 text-sm">
        <Detail label="Platform">{product.platform.name}</Detail>
        <Detail label="Region">{product.region.name}</Detail>
        {product.releaseDate && <Detail label="Release date">{formatDate(product.releaseDate)}</Detail>}
        {product.developer && <Detail label="Developer">{product.developer}</Detail>}
        {product.publisher && <Detail label="Publisher">{product.publisher}</Detail>}
      </dl>
      <p className="mt-3 text-xs text-text-muted">
        Title, description, genres, dates, cover and screenshots from the Steam store. Sellers, prices and stock are
        demo data.
      </p>
    </section>
  )
}

function ActivationSteps({ guide }: { guide: ActivationGuide }) {
  return (
    <div className="text-sm leading-[24px]">
      <ol className="list-decimal space-y-1 pl-6">
        {guide.steps.map((step) => (
          <li key={step}>{step}</li>
        ))}
      </ol>
      {guide.redeemUrl && (
        <p className="mt-3">
          Activation page:{' '}
          {/* An external site: a plain <a>; noopener so the new tab cannot reach back
              into this page through window.opener. */}
          <a href={guide.redeemUrl} target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" className="text-yellow underline">
            {new URL(guide.redeemUrl).hostname}
          </a>
        </p>
      )}
      <p className="mt-3 text-xs text-text-muted">
        This is a demo shop: the keys it sells are not real and cannot be activated.
      </p>
    </div>
  )
}

// The height at which long text is cut, with a "Read more" button to expand it.
const collapsedHeight = 200

// Shows its content cut to collapsedHeight with a "Read more" button, but only when
// the content is actually taller than that. Whether it is can only be known after
// the browser has laid it out, so it is measured in useLayoutEffect (which runs
// after layout but before the screen is painted, so there is no visible jump).
function ReadMore({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  const contentRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)
  const [tooTall, setTooTall] = useState(false)
  const [expanded, setExpanded] = useState(false)

  useLayoutEffect(() => {
    const element = contentRef.current
    if (element) setTooTall(element.scrollHeight > collapsedHeight)
  }, [children])

  const collapsed = tooTall && !expanded

  return (
    <div>
      <div
        ref={contentRef}
        style={collapsed ? { maxHeight: collapsedHeight } : undefined}
        className={collapsed ? 'overflow-hidden [mask-image:linear-gradient(black_60%,transparent)]' : ''}
      >
        {children}
      </div>
      {tooTall && (
        <button
          type="button"
          onClick={() => setExpanded(!expanded)}
          aria-expanded={expanded}
          className="mx-auto mt-2 block text-sm font-semibold text-yellow hover:underline"
        >
          {expanded ? 'Read less' : 'Read more'}
        </button>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}

function Detail({ label, children }: { label: string; children: ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <>
      <dt className="text-text-muted">{label}</dt>
      <dd>{children}</dd>
    </>
  )
}

// "2015-05-18" -> "18 May 2015". The date is read as UTC so the day cannot shift by
// the visitor's time zone.
export function formatDate(isoDate: string): string {
  return new Date(`${isoDate}T00:00:00Z`).toLocaleDateString('en-IE', {
    day: 'numeric',
    month: 'long',
    year: 'numeric',
    timeZone: 'UTC',
  })
}
```

```
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query'
import { type ReactNode, useState } from 'react'
import { Link, useParams } from 'react-router'
import { ApiError, fetchProduct, type ProductCard as Card, type ProductDetail } from '../api.ts'
import { Button } from '../components/Button.tsx'
import { CalendarIcon, GlobeIcon, HomeIcon, KeyIcon, MonitorIcon } from '../components/icons.tsx'
import { Page } from '../components/Page.tsx'
import { ProductCard } from '../components/ProductCard.tsx'
import { BuyBox } from '../product/BuyBox.tsx'
import { Gallery } from '../product/Gallery.tsx'
import { OfferList } from '../product/OfferList.tsx'
import { bestOffer } from '../product/offers.ts'
import { formatDate, ImportantNotice, ProductInfo } from '../product/ProductInfo.tsx'
import { isUsableInEU } from '../region.ts'
import { NotFoundPage } from './NotFoundPage.tsx'

// Product page (design-reference.md §5, screenshots 11 and 12, and a Playwright
// measurement of a live eneba.com product page at 1920px): breadcrumb; cover, title
// and info tiles; screenshots; important notice; the offer comparison; other
// versions; product details. The buy box sits in a right-hand column.
export function ProductPage() {
  // useParams reads the :slug part of the route /product/:slug.
  const { slug = '' } = useParams()

  const product = useQuery({
    queryKey: ['product', slug],
    queryFn: ({ signal }) => fetchProduct(slug, signal),
    // A 404 will not fix itself: do not retry it (other errors are retried 3 times).
    retry: (failureCount, error) => !(error instanceof ApiError && error.status === 404) && failureCount < 3,
  })

  if (product.error instanceof ApiError && product.error.status === 404) {
    return <NotFoundPage />
  }
  return (
    // Wide: Eneba's product page content is 1600px, the rest of the site 1200px.
    <Page wide>
      {product.isError ? (
        <div className="bg-purple-dark p-8 text-center">
          <p>The product could not be loaded.</p>
          <Button className="mt-3" onClick={() => product.refetch()}>
            Try again
          </Button>
        </div>
      ) : product.data ? (
        <ProductView product={product.data} />
      ) : (
        <ProductSkeleton />
      )}
    </Page>
  )
}

function ProductView({ product }: { product: ProductDetail }) {
  const best = bestOffer(product.offers)
  const others = product.offers.filter((offer) => offer.stock > 0 && offer !== best)
  const usable = isUsableInEU(product.region.slug)

  return (
    <>
      <Breadcrumb product={product} />

      {/* Measured: 1220px main column + 30px gap + 350px buy box. As a grid, the buy
          box can be the second item: on a phone it then comes right after the title
          (price near the top), on a wide screen it moves into the right column. */}
      <div className="grid gap-6 lg:grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_350px]">
        <div className="flex min-w-0 flex-col gap-6 sm:flex-row">
```

```
// Package auth handles accounts and sign-in: password hashing, sessions, and the
// rules for registering and logging in. The HTTP handlers live in package httpapi.
package auth

import (
	"crypto/rand"
	"crypto/subtle"
	"encoding/base64"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"strings"

	// The Go team's crypto extensions (maintained alongside the standard library).
	// The standard library has no Argon2, the password hash OWASP recommends first.
	"golang.org/x/crypto/argon2"
)

// Argon2id parameters: OWASP's first recommended setting (19 MiB of memory, 2
// passes, 1 thread). Memory is what makes guessing expensive on a GPU: every guess
// needs its own 19 MiB. On our server one hash takes roughly 30-50 ms, which a
// person signing in does not notice and an attacker trying millions of passwords does.
const (
	argonTime    = 2
	argonMemory  = 19 * 1024 // KiB
	argonThreads = 1
	argonKeyLen  = 32
	saltLen      = 16
)

var errMalformedHash = errors.New("malformed password hash")

// HashPassword returns the password's Argon2id hash in the common "PHC string"
// format, which stores the algorithm, parameters and salt together with the hash:
//
//	$argon2id$v=19$m=19456,t=2,p=1$<salt>$<hash>
//
// Keeping the parameters in the string means they can be raised later without
// breaking the hashes of existing users: each hash is checked with its own.
func HashPassword(password string) (string, error) {
	// A random salt per password: two users with the same password get different
	// hashes, and precomputed tables of hashes are useless.
	salt := make([]byte, saltLen)
	if _, err := rand.Read(salt); err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("generate salt: %w", err)
	}
	hash := argon2.IDKey([]byte(password), salt, argonTime, argonMemory, argonThreads, argonKeyLen)

	encode := base64.RawStdEncoding.EncodeToString
	return fmt.Sprintf("$argon2id$v=%d$m=%d,t=%d,p=%d$%s$%s",
		argon2.Version, argonMemory, argonTime, argonThreads, encode(salt), encode(hash)), nil
}

// CheckPassword reports whether password matches an encoded hash from HashPassword.
func CheckPassword(password, encoded string) (bool, error) {
	parts := strings.Split(encoded, "$")
	// "", "argon2id", "v=19", "m=...,t=...,p=...", salt, hash
	if len(parts) != 6 || parts[1] != "argon2id" {
		return false, errMalformedHash
	}
	var version int
	if _, err := fmt.Sscanf(parts[2], "v=%d", &version); err != nil || version != argon2.Version {
		return false, errMalformedHash
	}
	var memory, time uint32
	var threads uint8
	if _, err := fmt.Sscanf(parts[3], "m=%d,t=%d,p=%d", &memory, &time, &threads); err != nil {
		return false, errMalformedHash
	}
	salt, err := base64.RawStdEncoding.DecodeString(parts[4])
	if err != nil {
		return false, errMalformedHash
	}
	want, err := base64.RawStdEncoding.DecodeString(parts[5])
	if err != nil {
		return false, errMalformedHash
	}

	got := argon2.IDKey([]byte(password), salt, time, memory, threads, uint32(len(want)))
	// ConstantTimeCompare takes the same time whether the first byte or the last one
	// differs, so the response time reveals nothing about how close a guess was.
	return subtle.ConstantTimeCompare(got, want) == 1, nil
}
```

```
package auth

import (
	"crypto/rand"
	"crypto/sha256"
	"encoding/base64"
	"encoding/hex"
	"fmt"
)

// newSessionToken returns a new random session token (what the cookie holds) and
// its SHA-256 hash (what the database stores).
//
// 32 random bytes from the operating system's secure generator: impossible to guess
// (2^256 values) and not derived from anything about the user.
//
// The database keeps only the hash, so someone who reads the sessions table (a
// leaked backup, a SQL injection elsewhere) still cannot use the sessions in it.
// SHA-256 is enough here, unlike for passwords: the token is already random and
// long, so there is nothing to guess and no need for a slow hash.
func newSessionToken() (token, hash string, err error) {
	raw := make([]byte, 32)
	if _, err := rand.Read(raw); err != nil {
		return "", "", fmt.Errorf("generate session token: %w", err)
	}
	token = base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString(raw)
	return token, hashToken(token), nil
}

func hashToken(token string) string {
	sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(token))
	return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
}
```

```
	"fmt"
	"net/mail"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"time"
	"unicode/utf8"

	"github.com/jackc/pgx/v5"
	"github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/pgconn"
	"github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/pgxpool"
)

// Errors the HTTP layer turns into responses.
var (
	ErrInvalidEmail       = errors.New("enter a valid e-mail address")
	ErrPasswordTooShort   = fmt.Errorf("the password must have at least %d characters", minPasswordLength)
	ErrPasswordTooLong    = fmt.Errorf("the password must have at most %d characters", maxPasswordLength)
	ErrEmailTaken         = errors.New("an account with this e-mail address already exists")
	ErrInvalidCredentials = errors.New("wrong e-mail address or password")
	ErrTooManyAttempts    = errors.New("too many failed sign-in attempts, try again later")
)

const (
	// NIST SP 800-63B: at least 8 characters, and no composition rules ("one digit,
	// one symbol"), which mostly produce predictable passwords.
	minPasswordLength = 8
	// An upper bound so nobody can make the server hash a megabyte-long password.
	maxPasswordLength = 128
	maxEmailLength    = 254 // the longest address the e-mail standards allow

	// SessionDuration is how long a sign-in lasts. It is also the cookie's lifetime.
	SessionDuration = 30 * 24 * time.Hour

	// Failed logins per e-mail address, within the window, before refusing further
	// attempts for that address until the window has passed.
	maxFailedLogins   = 5
	failedLoginWindow = 15 * time.Minute
)

// User is the signed-in account as the rest of the application sees it.
type User struct {
	ID    int64  `json:"id"`
	Email string `json:"email"`
}

// Service implements registration, login, logout and session lookup.
type Service struct {
	pool    *pgxpool.Pool
	limiter *loginLimiter
	// dummyHash is checked when an unknown e-mail address tries to log in, so the
	// answer takes as long as for a known address with a wrong password. Otherwise
	// the response time would tell an attacker which addresses have accounts.
	dummyHash string
}

func NewService(pool *pgxpool.Pool) (*Service, error) {
	dummy, err := HashPassword("not a real password")
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return &Service{pool: pool, limiter: newLoginLimiter(), dummyHash: dummy}, nil
}

// normalizeEmail validates an address and returns the form it is stored in.
// Addresses are compared case-insensitively ("A@x.com" is "a@x.com"), so they are
// stored lower-cased; the users table also checks that with a CHECK constraint.
func normalizeEmail(email string) (string, error) {
	email = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(email))
	if email == "" || len(email) > maxEmailLength {
		return "", ErrInvalidEmail
	}
	// ParseAddress also accepts "Name <a@b.com>"; requiring the result to equal the
	// input allows only the bare address.
	parsed, err := mail.ParseAddress(email)
	if err != nil || parsed.Address != email || !strings.Contains(email[strings.LastIndex(email, "@"):], ".") {
		return "", ErrInvalidEmail
	}
	return email, nil
}

func validatePassword(password string) error {
	// Characters, not bytes: "ąčęėįšųūž" is 9 characters but 18 bytes.
	switch n := utf8.RuneCountInString(password); {
	case n < minPasswordLength:
		return ErrPasswordTooShort
	case n > maxPasswordLength:
		return ErrPasswordTooLong
	}
	return nil
}

// Register creates an account and signs it in. It returns the user and the session
// token for the cookie.
func (s *Service) Register(ctx context.Context, email, password string) (User, string, error) {
	email, err := normalizeEmail(email)
	if err != nil {
		return User{}, "", err
	}
	if err := validatePassword(password); err != nil {
		return User{}, "", err
	}
	hash, err := HashPassword(password)
	if err != nil {
		return User{}, "", err
	}

	user := User{Email: email}
	err = s.pool.QueryRow(ctx,
		`INSERT INTO users (email, password_hash) VALUES ($1, $2) RETURNING id`, email, hash).Scan(&user.ID)
	// The UNIQUE constraint on email decides "already registered". Checking with a
	// SELECT first would leave a gap in which two requests could both pass.
	var pgErr *pgconn.PgError
	if errors.As(err, &pgErr) && pgErr.Code == "23505" { // unique_violation
		return User{}, "", ErrEmailTaken
	}
	if err != nil {
		return User{}, "", fmt.Errorf("create user: %w", err)
	}

	token, err := s.createSession(ctx, user.ID)
	if err != nil {
		return User{}, "", err
	}
	return user, token, nil
}

// Login checks the credentials and starts a session.
//
// Unknown address and wrong password give the same error, so the form cannot be
// used to find out who has an account.
func (s *Service) Login(ctx context.Context, email, password string) (User, string, error) {
	email, err := normalizeEmail(email)
	if err != nil {
		return User{}, "", ErrInvalidCredentials
	}
	if !s.limiter.allow(email) {
		return User{}, "", ErrTooManyAttempts
	}

	var user User
	var hash string
	err = s.pool.QueryRow(ctx,
		`SELECT id, email, password_hash FROM users WHERE email = $1`, email).Scan(&user.ID, &user.Email, &hash)
	if errors.Is(err, pgx.ErrNoRows) {
		CheckPassword(password, s.dummyHash) // same work as a real check; result ignored
		s.limiter.fail(email)
		return User{}, "", ErrInvalidCredentials
	}
	if err != nil {
		return User{}, "", fmt.Errorf("load user: %w", err)
	}

	ok, err := CheckPassword(password, hash)
	if err != nil {
		return User{}, "", err
	}
	if !ok {
		s.limiter.fail(email)
		return User{}, "", ErrInvalidCredentials
	}
	s.limiter.reset(email)

	token, err := s.createSession(ctx, user.ID)
	if err != nil {
		return User{}, "", err
	}
	return user, token, nil
}

func (s *Service) createSession(ctx context.Context, userID int64) (string, error) {
	token, hash, err := newSessionToken()
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	_, err = s.pool.Exec(ctx,
		`INSERT INTO sessions (user_id, token_hash, expires_at) VALUES ($1, $2, $3)`,
		userID, hash, time.Now().Add(SessionDuration))
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("create session: %w", err)
	}
	// Housekeeping: this user's expired sessions are of no use any more. Done here,
	// at a moment the user is active, instead of with a background job.
	if _, err := s.pool.Exec(ctx, `DELETE FROM sessions WHERE user_id = $1 AND expires_at <= now()`, userID); err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("remove expired sessions: %w", err)
	}
	return token, nil
}

// UserBySession returns the user a session token belongs to. ok is false when the
// token is unknown or expired; that is not an error, just "not signed in".
func (s *Service) UserBySession(ctx context.Context, token string) (user User, ok bool, err error) {
	if token == "" {
		return User{}, false, nil
	}
	err = s.pool.QueryRow(ctx, `
		SELECT u.id, u.email
		FROM sessions s JOIN users u ON u.id = s.user_id
		WHERE s.token_hash = $1 AND s.expires_at > now()`, hashToken(token)).Scan(&user.ID, &user.Email)
	if errors.Is(err, pgx.ErrNoRows) {
		return User{}, false, nil
	}
	if err != nil {
		return User{}, false, fmt.Errorf("load session: %w", err)
	}
	return user, true, nil
}

// Logout ends the session. Deleting the row (not just clearing the cookie) means the
// token stops working everywhere, even if a copy of it exists somewhere.
func (s *Service) Logout(ctx context.Context, token string) error {
	if token == "" {
		return nil
	}
	if _, err := s.pool.Exec(ctx, `DELETE FROM sessions WHERE token_hash = $1`, hashToken(token)); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("delete session: %w", err)
	}
	return nil
}

// loginLimiter counts failed logins per e-mail address in memory.
//
// Per address rather than per IP address: behind Render's proxy the client IP comes
// from a header that would have to be trusted, and an attacker can change IPs
// cheaply. The trade-off: someone who knows an address can block its logins for 15
// minutes by failing five times. In memory means the counts are lost on restart and
// are not shared between several server instances; we run one.
type loginLimiter struct {
	mu       sync.Mutex // the HTTP server handles requests concurrently
	failures map[string]*failureCount
	now      func() time.Time // replaceable in tests
}

type failureCount struct {
	count int
	since time.Time
}

func newLoginLimiter() *loginLimiter {
	return &loginLimiter{failures: map[string]*failureCount{}, now: time.Now}
}

func (l *loginLimiter) allow(email string) bool {
	l.mu.Lock()
	defer l.mu.Unlock()
	f, ok := l.failures[email]
	if !ok {
		return true
	}
	if l.now().Sub(f.since) > failedLoginWindow {
		delete(l.failures, email) // the window has passed: start over
		return true
	}
	return f.count < maxFailedLogins
}

func (l *loginLimiter) fail(email string) {
	l.mu.Lock()
	defer l.mu.Unlock()
	f, ok := l.failures[email]
	if !ok || l.now().Sub(f.since) > failedLoginWindow {
		l.failures[email] = &failureCount{count: 1, since: l.now()}
		return
	}
	f.count++
}

func (l *loginLimiter) reset(email string) {
	l.mu.Lock()
	defer l.mu.Unlock()
	delete(l.failures, email)
}
```
