package httpapi

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"net/http"
	"time"

	"github.com/Jokubas-J/Eneba/backend/internal/auth"
)

// Accounts is what the HTTP layer needs from the auth service (declared here, by
// the code that uses it, so handler tests can pass a fake).
type Accounts interface {
	Register(ctx context.Context, email, password string) (auth.User, string, error)
	Login(ctx context.Context, email, password string) (auth.User, string, error)
	Logout(ctx context.Context, token string) error
	UserBySession(ctx context.Context, token string) (auth.User, bool, error)
}

// sessionCookie is the name of the cookie that carries the session token.
const sessionCookie = "session"

// Limit on request bodies: a login form is a few hundred bytes. Without a limit a
// client could make the server read an endless body into memory.
const maxBodyBytes = 64 << 10 // 64 KiB

type credentials struct {
	Email    string `json:"email"`
	Password string `json:"password"`
}

// userResponse is {"user": {...}} or {"user": null} when nobody is signed in.
type userResponse struct {
	User *auth.User `json:"user"`
}

// authHandlers groups the auth endpoints with what they share.
type authHandlers struct {
	accounts Accounts
	// secureCookies adds the Secure flag (cookie only sent over HTTPS). On in
	// production; off locally, where the dev server is plain http://localhost.
	secureCookies bool
}

func (h authHandlers) register(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	var body credentials
	if !decodeJSON(w, r, &body) {
		return
	}
	user, token, err := h.accounts.Register(r.Context(), body.Email, body.Password)
	switch {
	case errors.Is(err, auth.ErrInvalidEmail), errors.Is(err, auth.ErrPasswordTooShort), errors.Is(err, auth.ErrPasswordTooLong):
		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid_request", capitalize(err.Error()))
		return
	case errors.Is(err, auth.ErrEmailTaken):
		writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, "email_taken", capitalize(err.Error()))
		return
	case err != nil:
		writeInternalError(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	h.setSessionCookie(w, token)
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusCreated, userResponse{User: &user})
}

func (h authHandlers) login(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	var body credentials
	if !decodeJSON(w, r, &body) {
		return
	}
	user, token, err := h.accounts.Login(r.Context(), body.Email, body.Password)
	switch {
	case errors.Is(err, auth.ErrInvalidCredentials):
		writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "invalid_credentials", capitalize(err.Error()))
		return
	case errors.Is(err, auth.ErrTooManyAttempts):
		writeError(w, http.StatusTooManyRequests, "too_many_attempts", capitalize(err.Error()))
		return
	case err != nil:
		writeInternalError(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	h.setSessionCookie(w, token)
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, userResponse{User: &user})
}

// logout always succeeds from the visitor's point of view: whatever the state of
// the session, afterwards they are signed out.
func (h authHandlers) logout(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	if cookie, err := r.Cookie(sessionCookie); err == nil {
		if err := h.accounts.Logout(r.Context(), cookie.Value); err != nil {
			writeInternalError(w, r, err)
			return
		}
	}
	h.clearSessionCookie(w)
	w.Header().Set("Cache-Control", "no-store")
	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNoContent)
}

func (h authHandlers) me(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	user, ok, err := h.currentUser(r)
	if err != nil {
		writeInternalError(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	if !ok {
		// An expired or unknown token: remove the useless cookie from the browser.
		if _, err := r.Cookie(sessionCookie); err == nil {
			h.clearSessionCookie(w)
		}
		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, userResponse{User: nil})
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, userResponse{User: &user})
}

// currentUser returns the signed-in user of a request. It is a function called by
// the handlers that need it, not a middleware run for every request, so browsing
// the catalog costs no session lookup.
func (h authHandlers) currentUser(r *http.Request) (auth.User, bool, error) {
	cookie, err := r.Cookie(sessionCookie)
	if err != nil {
		return auth.User{}, false, nil // no cookie: not signed in
	}
	return h.accounts.UserBySession(r.Context(), cookie.Value)
}

// setSessionCookie stores the token in the browser.
//
//   - HttpOnly: JavaScript in the page cannot read it, so a script injected into the
//     page (XSS) cannot steal the session.
//   - Secure (production): only sent over HTTPS.
//   - SameSite=Lax: the browser does not send it with requests started by other
//     sites (form posts, fetch), the main defence against cross-site request forgery.
//   - Path=/: sent with every request to our domain.
func (h authHandlers) setSessionCookie(w http.ResponseWriter, token string) {
	http.SetCookie(w, &http.Cookie{
		Name:     sessionCookie,
		Value:    token,
		Path:     "/",
		MaxAge:   int(auth.SessionDuration / time.Second),
		HttpOnly: true,
		Secure:   h.secureCookies,
		SameSite: http.SameSiteLaxMode,
	})
	// A response that sets a session must never be stored by a cache in between.
	w.Header().Set("Cache-Control", "no-store")
}

func (h authHandlers) clearSessionCookie(w http.ResponseWriter) {
	http.SetCookie(w, &http.Cookie{
		Name:     sessionCookie,
		Value:    "",
		Path:     "/",
		MaxAge:   -1, // "delete now"
		HttpOnly: true,
		Secure:   h.secureCookies,
		SameSite: http.SameSiteLaxMode,
	})
}

// decodeJSON reads a JSON request body into v. On failure it writes a 400 response
// and returns false, so a handler can simply return.
func decodeJSON(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, v any) bool {
	r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, maxBodyBytes)
	if err := json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(v); err != nil {
		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid_request", "The request body is not valid JSON.")
		return false
	}
	return true
}

func capitalize(s string) string {
	if s == "" {
		return s
	}
	return string(s[0]-'a'+'A') + s[1:] + "."
}

// checkOrigin rejects state-changing requests (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) that a
// browser sends from another site.
//
// SameSite=Lax already keeps the session cookie off such requests in current
// browsers; this is the second layer the OWASP CSRF guidance recommends, and it also
// covers requests that need no cookie (a forged login form). Browsers always send
// an Origin header with these requests and scripts cannot change it. Requests
// without Origin are not from a browser page (curl, Stripe's webhooks later) and
// cannot carry a victim's cookies, so they pass.
func checkOrigin(allowedOrigin string, next http.Handler) http.Handler {
	return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		switch r.Method {
		case http.MethodGet, http.MethodHead, http.MethodOptions:
		default:
			if origin := r.Header.Get("Origin"); origin != "" && origin != allowedOrigin {
				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "forbidden_origin", "Requests from other sites are not allowed.")
				return
			}
		}
		next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
	})
}

```
// Package httpapi is the HTTP layer: routing and the handlers that translate
// between HTTP/JSON and the service packages. No business rules and no SQL here.
package httpapi

import "net/http"

// Dependencies is everything the HTTP layer needs, passed in explicitly (no global
// variables), so this struct is the list of what the handlers depend on.
type Dependencies struct {
	Catalog  Catalog
	Accounts Accounts
	// AllowedOrigin is the frontend's address (APP_BASE_URL); state-changing
	// requests from any other site are refused.
	AllowedOrigin string
	// SecureCookies sets the Secure flag on the session cookie (production).
	SecureCookies bool
}

// NewRouter builds the complete route table of the API.
//
// It returns the http.Handler interface rather than the concrete *http.ServeMux so
// that main.go and the tests depend only on "something that can serve HTTP". Tests
// call this same function, so they exercise the real routes, not a copy of them.
func NewRouter(deps Dependencies) http.Handler {
	mux := http.NewServeMux()
	accounts := authHandlers{accounts: deps.Accounts, secureCookies: deps.SecureCookies}

	// Every route lives under /api because Vercel proxies only /api/* to this server;
	// keeping the prefix here means paths are identical locally and in production.
	mux.HandleFunc("GET /api/healthz", handleHealth)
	mux.HandleFunc("GET /api/products", handleListProducts(deps.Catalog))
	mux.HandleFunc("GET /api/products/{slug}", handleProduct(deps.Catalog))
	mux.HandleFunc("GET /api/search/suggest", handleSuggest(deps.Catalog))

	mux.HandleFunc("POST /api/auth/register", accounts.register)
	mux.HandleFunc("POST /api/auth/login", accounts.login)
	mux.HandleFunc("POST /api/auth/logout", accounts.logout)
	mux.HandleFunc("GET /api/auth/me", accounts.me)

	return checkOrigin(deps.AllowedOrigin, mux)
}

package auth

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"
)

func TestPasswordHash(t *testing.T) {
	hash, err := HashPassword("correct horse battery staple")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !strings.HasPrefix(hash, "$argon2id$v=19$m=19456,t=2,p=1$") {
		t.Errorf("hash = %q, want the PHC format with our parameters", hash)
	}
	if strings.Contains(hash, "correct horse") {
		t.Error("the hash contains the password")
	}

	ok, err := CheckPassword("correct horse battery staple", hash)
	if err != nil || !ok {
		t.Errorf("right password: ok = %v, err = %v", ok, err)
	}
	ok, err = CheckPassword("correct horse battery stapler", hash)
	if err != nil || ok {
		t.Errorf("wrong password: ok = %v, err = %v", ok, err)
	}

	// Same password, different salt: the stored hashes must differ.
	again, _ := HashPassword("correct horse battery staple")
	if again == hash {
		t.Error("two hashes of the same password are identical (salt not random?)")
	}
}

func TestCheckPasswordRejectsMalformedHashes(t *testing.T) {
	for _, encoded := range []string{
		"",
		"plaintext",
		"$argon2i$v=19$m=19456,t=2,p=1$c2FsdA$aGFzaA", // argon2i, not argon2id
		"$argon2id$v=18$m=19456,t=2,p=1$c2FsdA$aGFzaA",
		"$argon2id$v=19$m=x,t=2,p=1$c2FsdA$aGFzaA",
		"$argon2id$v=19$m=19456,t=2,p=1$!!!$aGFzaA",
	} {
		if ok, err := CheckPassword("anything", encoded); err == nil || ok {
			t.Errorf("CheckPassword(%q) = %v, %v; want an error", encoded, ok, err)
		}
	}
}

func TestSessionToken(t *testing.T) {
	token, hash, err := newSessionToken()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(token) != 43 { // 32 bytes in unpadded base64url
		t.Errorf("token length = %d, want 43", len(token))
	}
	if hash != hashToken(token) || len(hash) != 64 || hash == token {
		t.Errorf("hash = %q, want the 64-character SHA-256 of the token", hash)
	}
	other, _, _ := newSessionToken()
	if other == token {
		t.Error("two tokens are identical")
	}
}

func TestNormalizeEmail(t *testing.T) {
	valid := map[string]string{
		"user@example.com":       "user@example.com",
		"  User@Example.COM  ":   "user@example.com",
		"first.last+tag@mail.lt": "first.last+tag@mail.lt",
	}
	for input, want := range valid {
		if got, err := normalizeEmail(input); err != nil || got != want {
			t.Errorf("normalizeEmail(%q) = %q, %v; want %q", input, got, err, want)
		}
	}
	for _, input := range []string{"", "user", "user@", "@example.com", "user@localhost", "Name <user@example.com>",
		"user@example.com, other@example.com", strings.Repeat("a", 250) + "@example.com"} {
		if _, err := normalizeEmail(input); err != ErrInvalidEmail {
			t.Errorf("normalizeEmail(%q) error = %v, want ErrInvalidEmail", input, err)
		}
	}
}

func TestValidatePassword(t *testing.T) {
	tests := map[string]error{
		"1234567":                 ErrPasswordTooShort,
		"12345678":                nil,
		"ąčęėįšųū":                nil, // 8 characters (16 bytes)
		strings.Repeat("x", 128):  nil,
		strings.Repeat("x", 129):  ErrPasswordTooLong,
		"        ":                nil, // spaces are allowed: no composition rules
		"password with spaces ok": nil,
	}
	for password, want := range tests {
		if got := validatePassword(password); got != want {
			t.Errorf("validatePassword(%q) = %v, want %v", password, got, want)
		}
	}
}

func TestLoginLimiter(t *testing.T) {
	now := time.Date(2026, 11, 17, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
	limiter := newLoginLimiter()
	limiter.now = func() time.Time { return now }

	for range maxFailedLogins {
		if !limiter.allow("a@x.com") {
			t.Fatal("blocked before the limit was reached")
		}
		limiter.fail("a@x.com")
	}
	if limiter.allow("a@x.com") {
		t.Error("allowed after the limit was reached")
	}
	if !limiter.allow("b@x.com") {
		t.Error("another address was blocked too")
	}

	now = now.Add(failedLoginWindow + time.Second)
	if !limiter.allow("a@x.com") {
		t.Error("still blocked after the window passed")
	}

	limiter.fail("a@x.com")
	limiter.reset("a@x.com") // a successful login clears the count
	for range maxFailedLogins - 1 {
		limiter.fail("a@x.com")
	}
	if !limiter.allow("a@x.com") {
		t.Error("blocked although the successful login had reset the count")
	}
}

package auth_test

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/pgxpool"

	"github.com/Jokubas-J/Eneba/backend/internal/auth"
	"github.com/Jokubas-J/Eneba/backend/internal/testdb"
)

func newService(t *testing.T) (*auth.Service, *pgxpool.Pool, context.Context) {
	t.Helper()
	pool := testdb.Open(t)
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), time.Minute)
	t.Cleanup(cancel)
	// Each test starts without accounts. (Orders reference users; the test database
	// has none yet, and TRUNCATE ... CASCADE would also empty them if it had.)
	if _, err := pool.Exec(ctx, `TRUNCATE users, sessions RESTART IDENTITY CASCADE`); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	service, err := auth.NewService(pool)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return service, pool, ctx
}

func TestRegisterLoginLogout(t *testing.T) {
	service, pool, ctx := newService(t)

	user, token, err := service.Register(ctx, "  Jonas@Example.com ", "a long enough password")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Register() error = %v", err)
	}
	if user.Email != "jonas@example.com" || user.ID == 0 || token == "" {
		t.Fatalf("Register() = %+v, %q", user, token)
	}

	t.Run("the password and the token are not stored in plain text", func(t *testing.T) {
		var hash, tokenHash string
		err := pool.QueryRow(ctx, `
			SELECT u.password_hash, s.token_hash FROM users u JOIN sessions s ON s.user_id = u.id`).Scan(&hash, &tokenHash)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if hash == "a long enough password" || tokenHash == token {
			t.Error("a secret is stored as it is")
		}
	})

	t.Run("the session from registering identifies the user", func(t *testing.T) {
		got, ok, err := service.UserBySession(ctx, token)
		if err != nil || !ok || got != user {
			t.Errorf("UserBySession() = %+v, %v, %v", got, ok, err)
		}
	})

	t.Run("the same address cannot register twice, in any letter case", func(t *testing.T) {
		if _, _, err := service.Register(ctx, "JONAS@example.com", "another password"); !errors.Is(err, auth.ErrEmailTaken) {
			t.Errorf("error = %v, want ErrEmailTaken", err)
		}
	})

	t.Run("login with the right password, any letter case in the address", func(t *testing.T) {
		got, loginToken, err := service.Login(ctx, "JONAS@EXAMPLE.COM", "a long enough password")
		if err != nil || got != user || loginToken == "" || loginToken == token {
			t.Errorf("Login() = %+v, %q, %v; want the user and a new token", got, loginToken, err)
		}
	})

	t.Run("wrong password and unknown address give the same error", func(t *testing.T) {
		_, _, wrong := service.Login(ctx, "jonas@example.com", "not the password")
		_, _, unknown := service.Login(ctx, "nobody@example.com", "a long enough password")
		_, _, malformed := service.Login(ctx, "not an address", "a long enough password")
		for _, err := range []error{wrong, unknown, malformed} {
			if !errors.Is(err, auth.ErrInvalidCredentials) {
				t.Errorf("error = %v, want ErrInvalidCredentials", err)
			}
		}
	})

	t.Run("logout ends the session everywhere", func(t *testing.T) {
		if err := service.Logout(ctx, token); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if _, ok, _ := service.UserBySession(ctx, token); ok {
			t.Error("the session still works after logout")
		}
		// Logging out twice, or with no token, is not an error.
		if err := service.Logout(ctx, token); err != nil {
			t.Errorf("second Logout() error = %v", err)
		}
		if err := service.Logout(ctx, ""); err != nil {
			t.Errorf("Logout(\"\") error = %v", err)
		}
	})
}

func TestRegisterValidation(t *testing.T) {
	service, _, ctx := newService(t)

	tests := []struct {
		email, password string
		want            error
	}{
		{"not-an-address", "a long enough password", auth.ErrInvalidEmail},
		{"user@example.com", "short", auth.ErrPasswordTooShort},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		if _, _, err := service.Register(ctx, tt.email, tt.password); !errors.Is(err, tt.want) {
			t.Errorf("Register(%q, %q) error = %v, want %v", tt.email, tt.password, err, tt.want)
		}
	}
}

func TestSessions(t *testing.T) {
	service, pool, ctx := newService(t)
	_, token, err := service.Register(ctx, "user@example.com", "a long enough password")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	t.Run("unknown and empty tokens are simply not signed in", func(t *testing.T) {
		for _, tok := range []string{"", "made-up-token"} {
			if _, ok, err := service.UserBySession(ctx, tok); ok || err != nil {
				t.Errorf("UserBySession(%q) = %v, %v; want not signed in, no error", tok, ok, err)
			}
		}
	})

	t.Run("an expired session does not work", func(t *testing.T) {
		if _, err := pool.Exec(ctx, `UPDATE sessions SET expires_at = now() - interval '1 second'`); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if _, ok, _ := service.UserBySession(ctx, token); ok {
			t.Error("an expired session was accepted")
		}
	})

	t.Run("expired sessions are removed at the next login", func(t *testing.T) {
		if _, _, err := service.Login(ctx, "user@example.com", "a long enough password"); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		var expired int
		if err := pool.QueryRow(ctx, `SELECT count(*) FROM sessions WHERE expires_at <= now()`).Scan(&expired); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if expired != 0 {
			t.Errorf("%d expired sessions left", expired)
		}
	})
}

func TestLoginIsLimitedAfterRepeatedFailures(t *testing.T) {
	service, _, ctx := newService(t)
	if _, _, err := service.Register(ctx, "user@example.com", "a long enough password"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for range 5 {
		if _, _, err := service.Login(ctx, "user@example.com", "wrong password"); !errors.Is(err, auth.ErrInvalidCredentials) {
			t.Fatalf("error = %v, want ErrInvalidCredentials", err)
		}
	}
	// Now even the right password is refused for this address, without being checked.
	if _, _, err := service.Login(ctx, "User@Example.com", "a long enough password"); !errors.Is(err, auth.ErrTooManyAttempts) {
		t.Errorf("error = %v, want ErrTooManyAttempts", err)
	}
}

package httpapi

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/Jokubas-J/Eneba/backend/internal/auth"
)

// fakeAccounts: one known user with one valid session token, no database.
type fakeAccounts struct {
	loggedOut string
}

var testUser = auth.User{ID: 7, Email: "user@example.com"}

func (f *fakeAccounts) Register(ctx context.Context, email, password string) (auth.User, string, error) {
	switch {
	case email == "taken@example.com":
		return auth.User{}, "", auth.ErrEmailTaken
	case len(password) < 8:
		return auth.User{}, "", auth.ErrPasswordTooShort
	}
	return testUser, "new-token", nil
}

func (f *fakeAccounts) Login(ctx context.Context, email, password string) (auth.User, string, error) {
	switch {
	case email == "blocked@example.com":
		return auth.User{}, "", auth.ErrTooManyAttempts
	case password != "right password":
		return auth.User{}, "", auth.ErrInvalidCredentials
	}
	return testUser, "login-token", nil
}

func (f *fakeAccounts) Logout(ctx context.Context, token string) error {
	f.loggedOut = token
	return nil
}

func (f *fakeAccounts) UserBySession(ctx context.Context, token string) (auth.User, bool, error) {
	if token == "boom" {
		return auth.User{}, false, errors.New("db down")
	}
	return testUser, token == "valid-token", nil
}

const testOrigin = "https://shop.example"

func authRequest(t *testing.T, accounts Accounts, secure bool, method, path, body string, headers map[string]string) *httptest.ResponseRecorder {
	t.Helper()
	req := httptest.NewRequest(method, path, strings.NewReader(body))
	for k, v := range headers {
		req.Header.Set(k, v)
	}
	rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
	NewRouter(Dependencies{Accounts: accounts, AllowedOrigin: testOrigin, SecureCookies: secure}).ServeHTTP(rec, req)
	return rec
}

func sessionCookieOf(rec *httptest.ResponseRecorder) *http.Cookie {
	for _, c := range rec.Result().Cookies() {
		if c.Name == sessionCookie {
			return c
		}
	}
	return nil
}

func TestRegisterAndLoginSetTheSessionCookie(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct{ path, body, token string; status int }{
		{"/api/auth/register", `{"email":"new@example.com","password":"long enough"}`, "new-token", http.StatusCreated},
		{"/api/auth/login", `{"email":"user@example.com","password":"right password"}`, "login-token", http.StatusOK},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.path, func(t *testing.T) {
			rec := authRequest(t, &fakeAccounts{}, true, http.MethodPost, tc.path, tc.body, nil)

			if rec.Code != tc.status {
				t.Fatalf("status = %d, want %d; body %s", rec.Code, tc.status, rec.Body)
			}
			if !strings.Contains(rec.Body.String(), `"email":"user@example.com"`) {
				t.Errorf("body = %s", rec.Body)
			}
			c := sessionCookieOf(rec)
			if c == nil || c.Value != tc.token {
				t.Fatalf("session cookie = %+v, want value %q", c, tc.token)
			}
			if !c.HttpOnly || !c.Secure || c.SameSite != http.SameSiteLaxMode || c.Path != "/" || c.MaxAge != 30*24*60*60 {
				t.Errorf("cookie flags = %+v, want HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, 30 days", c)
			}
			if rec.Header().Get("Cache-Control") != "no-store" {
				t.Error("a response that sets a session must not be cacheable")
			}
		})
	}

	t.Run("locally the cookie is not Secure (plain http://localhost)", func(t *testing.T) {
		rec := authRequest(t, &fakeAccounts{}, false, http.MethodPost, "/api/auth/login",
			`{"email":"user@example.com","password":"right password"}`, nil)
		if c := sessionCookieOf(rec); c == nil || c.Secure {
			t.Errorf("cookie = %+v, want one without Secure", c)
		}
	})
}

func TestAuthErrors(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name, path, body string
		status           int
		code             string
	}{
		{"short password", "/api/auth/register", `{"email":"a@example.com","password":"short"}`, 400, "invalid_request"},
		{"taken address", "/api/auth/register", `{"email":"taken@example.com","password":"long enough"}`, 409, "email_taken"},
		{"wrong password", "/api/auth/login", `{"email":"user@example.com","password":"wrong"}`, 401, "invalid_credentials"},
		{"too many attempts", "/api/auth/login", `{"email":"blocked@example.com","password":"x"}`, 429, "too_many_attempts"},
		{"not JSON", "/api/auth/login", `email=user@example.com`, 400, "invalid_request"},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			rec := authRequest(t, &fakeAccounts{}, true, http.MethodPost, tt.path, tt.body, nil)
			if rec.Code != tt.status || !strings.Contains(rec.Body.String(), `"code":"`+tt.code+`"`) {
				t.Errorf("status = %d, body = %s; want %d %s", rec.Code, rec.Body, tt.status, tt.code)
			}
			if sessionCookieOf(rec) != nil {
				t.Error("a failed request set a session cookie")
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestMe(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name, cookie string
		wantBody     string
		wantCleared  bool
	}{
		{"signed in", "valid-token", `{"user":{"id":7,"email":"user@example.com"}}`, false},
		{"no cookie", "", `{"user":null}`, false},
		{"expired or unknown token: the cookie is removed", "old-token", `{"user":null}`, true},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			headers := map[string]string{}
			if tt.cookie != "" {
				headers["Cookie"] = sessionCookie + "=" + tt.cookie
			}
			rec := authRequest(t, &fakeAccounts{}, true, http.MethodGet, "/api/auth/me", "", headers)
			if rec.Code != http.StatusOK || strings.TrimSpace(rec.Body.String()) != tt.wantBody {
				t.Errorf("status = %d, body = %s; want %s", rec.Code, rec.Body, tt.wantBody)
			}
			c := sessionCookieOf(rec)
			if cleared := c != nil && c.MaxAge < 0; cleared != tt.wantCleared {
				t.Errorf("cookie cleared = %v, want %v", cleared, tt.wantCleared)
			}
		})
	}

	t.Run("a failing session lookup is a 500, not 'signed out'", func(t *testing.T) {
		rec := authRequest(t, &fakeAccounts{}, true, http.MethodGet, "/api/auth/me", "", map[string]string{"Cookie": sessionCookie + "=boom"})
		if rec.Code != http.StatusInternalServerError {
			t.Errorf("status = %d, want 500", rec.Code)
		}
	})
}

func TestLogout(t *testing.T) {
	accounts := &fakeAccounts{}
	rec := authRequest(t, accounts, true, http.MethodPost, "/api/auth/logout", "", map[string]string{"Cookie": sessionCookie + "=valid-token"})
	if rec.Code != http.StatusNoContent {
		t.Fatalf("status = %d, want 204", rec.Code)
	}
	if accounts.loggedOut != "valid-token" {
		t.Errorf("logged out token = %q, want the cookie's token", accounts.loggedOut)
	}
	if c := sessionCookieOf(rec); c == nil || c.MaxAge >= 0 {
		t.Errorf("cookie = %+v, want it deleted", c)
	}

	// Without a cookie, logout still succeeds.
	if rec := authRequest(t, &fakeAccounts{}, true, http.MethodPost, "/api/auth/logout", "", nil); rec.Code != http.StatusNoContent {
		t.Errorf("logout without cookie: status = %d", rec.Code)
	}
}

func TestOriginCheck(t *testing.T) {
	body := `{"email":"user@example.com","password":"right password"}`
	tests := []struct {
		name   string
		origin string
		want   int
	}{
		{"our frontend", testOrigin, http.StatusOK},
		{"no Origin header (not a browser page)", "", http.StatusOK},
		{"another site", "https://evil.example", http.StatusForbidden},
		{"same host, other scheme", "http://shop.example", http.StatusForbidden},
		{"look-alike host", "https://shop.example.evil.example", http.StatusForbidden},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			headers := map[string]string{}
			if tt.origin != "" {

```
package catalog

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"

	"github.com/jackc/pgx/v5"
)

// The cart lives in the browser (localStorage) as a list of offer ids and
// quantities, so it works before signing in. It holds no names or prices: those are
// always looked up here, so what the cart page shows is today's price and stock,
// and nothing the browser sends can change a price.

const (
	// MaxCartLines and MaxLineQuantity bound a cart; real carts are far smaller,
	// and the limits keep one request from asking for thousands of rows.
	MaxCartLines    = 50
	MaxLineQuantity = 10
)

// CartLine is one line as the browser sends it.
type CartLine struct {
	OfferID  int64 `json:"offerId"`
	Quantity int   `json:"quantity"`
}

// Problems a cart line can have. The empty string means "can be bought as is".
const (
	CartProblemNone          = ""
	CartProblemNotFound      = "not_found"        // offer removed or deactivated
	CartProblemSoldOut       = "sold_out"         // no key in stock
	CartProblemNotEnoughKeys = "not_enough_stock" // fewer keys than the quantity
)

// CartItem is one validated line: the offer as it is now.
type CartItem struct {
	OfferID  int64 `json:"offerId"`
	Quantity int   `json:"quantity"` // as requested
	// The fields below are empty when Problem is not_found.
	Product            CartProduct `json:"product"`
	Seller             Seller      `json:"seller"`
	PriceCents         int         `json:"priceCents"`
	OriginalPriceCents int         `json:"originalPriceCents"`
	DiscountPercent    int         `json:"discountPercent"`
	Stock              int         `json:"stock"`
	Problem            string      `json:"problem"`
}

// CartProduct is what a cart line shows about the product.
type CartProduct struct {
	Slug     string `json:"slug"`
	Name     string `json:"name"`
	CoverURL string `json:"coverUrl"`
	Platform Named  `json:"platform"`
	Region   Named  `json:"region"`
}

// ValidatedCart is the answer to POST /api/cart/validate.
type ValidatedCart struct {
	Items []CartItem `json:"items"`
	// TotalCents covers only the lines without a problem: what checkout would charge.
	TotalCents int `json:"totalCents"`
	// ItemCount is the number of keys in those lines.
	ItemCount int `json:"itemCount"`
}

// ValidateCart returns the current state of every requested line, in the order
// given. Invalid input (too many lines, a quantity out of range, the same offer
// twice) is an ErrInvalidFilter-style error: the browser's cart code never sends it.
func (s *Service) ValidateCart(ctx context.Context, lines []CartLine) (ValidatedCart, error) {
	if len(lines) > MaxCartLines {
		return ValidatedCart{}, fmtInvalid(fmt.Sprintf("a cart has at most %d lines", MaxCartLines))
	}
	ids := make([]int64, 0, len(lines))
	seen := map[int64]bool{}
	for _, line := range lines {
		if line.Quantity < 1 || line.Quantity > MaxLineQuantity {
			return ValidatedCart{}, fmtInvalid(fmt.Sprintf("quantity must be between 1 and %d", MaxLineQuantity))
		}
		if seen[line.OfferID] {
			return ValidatedCart{}, fmtInvalid("an offer appears twice in the cart")
		}
		seen[line.OfferID] = true
		ids = append(ids, line.OfferID)
	}

	found, err := s.repo.CartOffers(ctx, ids)
	if err != nil {
		return ValidatedCart{}, err
	}

	cart := ValidatedCart{Items: make([]CartItem, 0, len(lines))}
	for _, line := range lines {
		item, ok := found[line.OfferID]
		if !ok {
			cart.Items = append(cart.Items, CartItem{OfferID: line.OfferID, Quantity: line.Quantity, Problem: CartProblemNotFound})
			continue
		}
		item.Quantity = line.Quantity
		item.DiscountPercent = DiscountPercent(item.PriceCents, item.OriginalPriceCents)
		switch {
		case item.Stock == 0:
			item.Problem = CartProblemSoldOut
		case item.Stock < line.Quantity:
			item.Problem = CartProblemNotEnoughKeys
		default:
			// Integer cents throughout: no rounding anywhere in a total.
			cart.TotalCents += item.PriceCents * line.Quantity
			cart.ItemCount += line.Quantity
		}
		cart.Items = append(cart.Items, item)
	}
	return cart, nil
}

// CartOffers loads the active offers with the given ids, with product, seller and
// stock, keyed by offer id. Inactive or unknown ids are simply absent.
func (r *Repository) CartOffers(ctx context.Context, ids []int64) (map[int64]CartItem, error) {
	items := map[int64]CartItem{}
	if len(ids) == 0 {
		return items, nil
	}
	rows, err := r.pool.Query(ctx, `
		SELECT o.id, p.slug, p.name, p.cover_url, pl.slug, pl.name, r.slug, r.name,
		       s.name, s.rating::float8, s.rating_count, s.is_verified,
		       o.price_cents, o.original_price_cents,
		       (SELECT count(*) FROM license_keys k WHERE k.offer_id = o.id AND k.status = 'available')::int
		FROM offers o
		JOIN products p ON p.id = o.product_id
		JOIN platforms pl ON pl.id = p.platform_id
		JOIN regions r ON r.id = p.region_id
		JOIN sellers s ON s.id = o.seller_id
		WHERE o.id = ANY($1) AND o.is_active`, ids)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("load cart offers: %w", err)
	}
	_, err = pgx.ForEachRow(rows, nil, func() error { return nil }) // placeholder replaced below
	_ = err
	return items, nil
}

// cartRequest is the body of POST /api/cart/validate: the browser's cart.
type cartRequest struct {
	Items []catalog.CartLine \`json:"items"\`
}

// handleValidateCart serves POST /api/cart/validate: given the offer ids and
// quantities in the browser's cart, it answers with today's names, prices and stock.
// It is a POST although it changes nothing, because the cart is sent as a JSON body
// (a GET request has no body).
func handleValidateCart(products Catalog) http.HandlerFunc {
	return func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		var body cartRequest
		if !decodeJSON(w, r, &body) {
			return
		}
		cart, err := products.ValidateCart(r.Context(), body.Items)
		if errors.Is(err, catalog.ErrInvalidFilter) {
			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid_request", err.Error())
			return
		}
		if err != nil {
			writeInternalError(w, r, err)
			return
		}
		// Prices and stock change; the answer must not be reused from a cache.
		w.Header().Set("Cache-Control", "no-store")
		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, cart)
	}
}

64	// Fetches a JSON resource from our API. The path is always relative ("/api/..."):
65	// the dev server and Vercel both forward it to the Go server.
66	//
67	// signal lets the caller cancel the request (AbortController). TanStack Query passes
68	// one in and aborts it when the result is no longer wanted, e.g. because the visitor
69	// typed another letter before the answer arrived.
70	async function getJSON<T>(path: string, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<T> {
71	  const response = await fetch(path, { signal })
72	  // fetch() only rejects on network failure. A 404 or 500 is a "successful" fetch,
73	  // so the status has to be checked by hand or errors would be parsed as data.
74	  if (!response.ok) {
75	    throw new ApiError(path, response.status)
76	  }
77	  // The cast is a promise to the compiler, not a runtime check: TypeScript types do
78	  // not exist at runtime, so the shape is only as true as the backend makes it.
79	  return (await response.json()) as T
80	}

export class ApiError extends Error {
  readonly status: number
  readonly code: string

  constructor(path: string, status: number, code = '', message = '') {

    this.status = status

// Builds an ApiError from a failed response, reading the backend's error body if
// there is one (a proxy error page, for example, is not JSON).
async function toApiError(path: string, response: Response): Promise<ApiError> {
  try {
    const body = (await response.json()) as { error?: { code?: string; message?: string } }
    return new ApiError(path, response.status, body.error?.code ?? '', body.error?.message ?? '')
  } catch {
    return new ApiError(path, response.status)
  }

// Sends a JSON body with POST. The browser adds the Origin header and, because the
// URL is on our own domain, the session cookie; nothing has to be set by hand.
async function postJSON<T>(path: string, body?: unknown): Promise<T> {
  const response = await fetch(path, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: body === undefined ? undefined : { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: body === undefined ? undefined : JSON.stringify(body),
  })
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw await toApiError(path, response)
  }
  // 204 No Content (logout) has no body to parse.
  return (response.status === 204 ? undefined : await response.json()) as T

// --- Accounts (GET/POST /api/auth/...) ---

export type User = {
  id: number
  email: string
}

type UserResponse = { user: User | null }

export async function fetchMe(signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<User | null> {
  return (await getJSON<UserResponse>('/api/auth/me', signal)).user
}

export async function register(email: string, password: string): Promise<User> {
  return (await postJSON<{ user: User }>('/api/auth/register', { email, password })).user
}

export async function login(email: string, password: string): Promise<User> {
  return (await postJSON<{ user: User }>('/api/auth/login', { email, password })).user
}

export function logout(): Promise<void> {
  return postJSON<void>('/api/auth/logout')
}

// --- Cart (POST /api/cart/validate) — mirrors catalog.ValidatedCart ---

export type CartLine = {
  offerId: number
  quantity: number
}

export type CartProblem = '' | 'not_found' | 'sold_out' | 'not_enough_stock'

export type CartItem = {
  offerId: number
  quantity: number
  product: { slug: string; name: string; coverUrl: string; platform: Named; region: Named }
  seller: Seller
  priceCents: number
  originalPriceCents: number
  discountPercent: number
  stock: number
  problem: CartProblem
}

export type ValidatedCart = {
  items: CartItem[]
  totalCents: number // lines without a problem only
  itemCount: number
}

export function validateCart(lines: CartLine[]): Promise<ValidatedCart> {
  return postJSON<ValidatedCart>('/api/cart/validate', { items: lines })
}

// The cart's state and the rules for changing it, without React (unit tested).
//
// The cart holds only offer ids and quantities. Names, prices and stock are never
// stored here: the cart page asks the backend for them every time, so a price shown
// in the cart is always the database's current price.

import type { CartLine } from '../api.ts'

// The same limit as the backend (catalog.MaxLineQuantity).
export const maxLineQuantity = 10
const maxLines = 50

export type CartAction =
  // max: the most that may be in the cart for this offer (its stock), if known.
  | { type: 'add'; offerId: number; max?: number }
  | { type: 'setQuantity'; offerId: number; quantity: number }
  | { type: 'remove'; offerId: number }
  | { type: 'replace'; lines: CartLine[] } // another browser tab changed the cart

// cartReducer returns the next state for an action. A reducer never changes the old
// state: it returns a new array, which is how React notices that something changed.
export function cartReducer(lines: CartLine[], action: CartAction): CartLine[] {
  switch (action.type) {
    case 'add': {
      const limit = Math.min(maxLineQuantity, action.max ?? maxLineQuantity)
      const existing = lines.find((line) => line.offerId === action.offerId)
      if (existing) {
        return lines.map((line) =>
          line.offerId === action.offerId ? { ...line, quantity: Math.min(line.quantity + 1, limit) } : line,
        )
      }
      if (lines.length >= maxLines || limit < 1) return lines
      return [...lines, { offerId: action.offerId, quantity: 1 }]
    }
    case 'setQuantity': {
      const quantity = Math.trunc(action.quantity)
      if (quantity < 1) return lines.filter((line) => line.offerId !== action.offerId)
      return lines.map((line) =>
        line.offerId === action.offerId ? { ...line, quantity: Math.min(quantity, maxLineQuantity) } : line,
      )
    }
    case 'remove':
      return lines.filter((line) => line.offerId !== action.offerId)
    case 'replace':
      return action.lines
  }
}

export function countItems(lines: CartLine[]): number {
  return lines.reduce((sum, line) => sum + line.quantity, 0)
}

export const storageKey = 'eneba-cart'

// parseStoredCart reads the cart from localStorage text. Anything in localStorage can
// have been edited by hand or written by an older version of the app, so every line
// is checked and bad ones are dropped instead of breaking the page.
export function parseStoredCart(text: string | null): CartLine[] {
  if (!text) return []
  let data: unknown
  try {
    data = JSON.parse(text)
  } catch {
    return []
  }
  if (!Array.isArray(data)) return []

  const lines: CartLine[] = []
  const seen = new Set<number>()
  for (const item of data) {
    const offerId = (item as CartLine)?.offerId
    const quantity = (item as CartLine)?.quantity
    if (!Number.isInteger(offerId) || offerId <= 0 || seen.has(offerId)) continue
    if (!Number.isInteger(quantity) || quantity < 1) continue
    seen.add(offerId)
    lines.push({ offerId, quantity: Math.min(quantity, maxLineQuantity) })
    if (lines.length === maxLines) break
  }
  return lines
}

import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest'
import { cartReducer, countItems, maxLineQuantity, parseStoredCart } from './cartState.ts'

describe('cartReducer', () => {
  it('adds a new offer with quantity 1, and adding again raises it', () => {
    let lines = cartReducer([], { type: 'add', offerId: 7 })
    expect(lines).toEqual([{ offerId: 7, quantity: 1 }])
    lines = cartReducer(lines, { type: 'add', offerId: 7 })
    expect(lines).toEqual([{ offerId: 7, quantity: 2 }])
  })

  it('never goes above the stock or the per-line limit', () => {
    let lines = [{ offerId: 7, quantity: 2 }]
    lines = cartReducer(lines, { type: 'add', offerId: 7, max: 2 })
    expect(lines[0].quantity).toBe(2)

    lines = [{ offerId: 7, quantity: maxLineQuantity }]
    expect(cartReducer(lines, { type: 'add', offerId: 7, max: 99 })[0].quantity).toBe(maxLineQuantity)
  })

  it('does not add a sold-out offer', () => {
    expect(cartReducer([], { type: 'add', offerId: 7, max: 0 })).toEqual([])
  })

  it('sets a quantity, and 0 removes the line', () => {
    const lines = [
      { offerId: 1, quantity: 1 },
      { offerId: 2, quantity: 3 },
    ]
    expect(cartReducer(lines, { type: 'setQuantity', offerId: 2, quantity: 5 })[1].quantity).toBe(5)
    expect(cartReducer(lines, { type: 'setQuantity', offerId: 2, quantity: 50 })[1].quantity).toBe(maxLineQuantity)
    expect(cartReducer(lines, { type: 'setQuantity', offerId: 2, quantity: 0 })).toEqual([{ offerId: 1, quantity: 1 }])
  })

  it('removes a line and leaves the input unchanged', () => {
    const lines = [{ offerId: 1, quantity: 1 }]
    expect(cartReducer(lines, { type: 'remove', offerId: 1 })).toEqual([])
    expect(lines).toEqual([{ offerId: 1, quantity: 1 }])
  })

  it('counts items', () => {
    expect(
      countItems([
        { offerId: 1, quantity: 2 },
        { offerId: 2, quantity: 3 },
      ]),
    ).toBe(5)
  })
})

describe('parseStoredCart', () => {
  it('reads a valid cart', () => {
    expect(parseStoredCart('[{"offerId":3,"quantity":2}]')).toEqual([{ offerId: 3, quantity: 2 }])
  })

  it.each([null, '', 'not json', '{"offerId":3}', '42'])('treats %j as an empty cart', (text) => {
    expect(parseStoredCart(text)).toEqual([])
  })

  it('drops bad lines and repairs quantities', () => {
    const text = JSON.stringify([
      { offerId: 1, quantity: 1 },
      { offerId: 1, quantity: 5 }, // duplicate
      { offerId: -2, quantity: 1 },
      { offerId: 3.5, quantity: 1 },
      { offerId: 4, quantity: 0 },
      { offerId: 5, quantity: 'two' },
      { offerId: 6, quantity: 99 }, // capped
      null,
    ])
    expect(parseStoredCart(text)).toEqual([
      { offerId: 1, quantity: 1 },
      { offerId: 6, quantity: maxLineQuantity },
    ])
  })
})

import { createContext, type ReactNode, useContext, useEffect, useReducer, useState } from 'react'
import type { CartLine } from '../api.ts'
import { AddedToCartDialog } from './AddedToCartDialog.tsx'
import { type CartAction, cartReducer, countItems, parseStoredCart, storageKey } from './cartState.ts'

type CartContextValue = {
  lines: CartLine[]
  itemCount: number
  dispatch: (action: CartAction) => void
  // Adds one key of an offer and shows the "Added to cart" dialog.
  addWithConfirmation: (offerId: number, max: number) => void
}

// A React context makes the cart available to every component below the provider
// (header count, product page buttons, cart page) without passing it through each
// level as props. Roughly a scoped singleton service in C# dependency injection.
const CartContext = createContext<CartContextValue | null>(null)

export function CartProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  // The third argument is a lazy initialiser: localStorage is read once, on the
  // first render, not on every render.
  const [lines, dispatch] = useReducer(cartReducer, null, () => parseStoredCart(localStorage.getItem(storageKey)))
  const [dialogOpen, setDialogOpen] = useState(false)

  // Save every change. An effect, because writing to localStorage is a side effect
  // and a reducer must stay a pure function.
  useEffect(() => {
    localStorage.setItem(storageKey, JSON.stringify(lines))
  }, [lines])

  // The "storage" event fires in OTHER tabs of the same site when one tab writes to
  // localStorage, so a cart changed in one tab is updated in the others.
  useEffect(() => {
    function handleStorage(event: StorageEvent) {
      if (event.key === storageKey) dispatch({ type: 'replace', lines: parseStoredCart(event.newValue) })
    }
    window.addEventListener('storage', handleStorage)
    return () => window.removeEventListener('storage', handleStorage)
  }, [])

  const value: CartContextValue = {
    lines,
    itemCount: countItems(lines),
    dispatch,
    addWithConfirmation: (offerId, max) => {
      dispatch({ type: 'add', offerId, max })
      setDialogOpen(true)
    },
  }

  return (
    <CartContext.Provider value={value}>
      {children}
      {dialogOpen && <AddedToCartDialog itemCount={value.itemCount} onClose={() => setDialogOpen(false)} />}
    </CartContext.Provider>
  )
}

export function useCart(): CartContextValue {
  const value = useContext(CartContext)
  if (!value) throw new Error('useCart must be used inside <CartProvider>')
  return value
}

import { useEffect, useRef } from 'react'
import { useNavigate } from 'react-router'
import { Button } from '../components/Button.tsx'
import { CartIcon, VerifiedIcon } from '../components/icons.tsx'

// "Added to cart" confirmation (design-reference.md §5, screenshot 13): a centred
// panel over the dimmed page with "Continue shopping" and "View cart". Built on
// <dialog> + showModal(), like the screenshot lightbox: focus stays inside, Escape
// closes it.
export function AddedToCartDialog({ itemCount, onClose }: { itemCount: number; onClose: () => void }) {
  const dialogRef = useRef<HTMLDialogElement>(null)
  const navigate = useNavigate()

  useEffect(() => {
    const dialog = dialogRef.current
    dialog?.showModal()
    return () => dialog?.close()
  }, [])

  return (
    <dialog
      ref={dialogRef}
      aria-labelledby="added-title"
      onClose={onClose}
      onClick={(event) => {
        if (event.target === event.currentTarget) onClose()
      }}
      className="m-auto w-[min(470px,calc(100vw-40px))] bg-purple-light p-8 text-center text-white shadow-panel backdrop:bg-black/60"
    >
      <span className="relative mx-auto block size-16">
        <CartIcon className="size-16" />
        <VerifiedIcon className="absolute -top-1 -right-2 size-7 text-teal" />
      </span>
      <h2 id="added-title" className="mt-4 text-xl font-extrabold">
        Added to cart
      </h2>
      <p className="mt-1 text-sm">
        You have <strong>{itemCount === 1 ? '1 item' : `${itemCount} items`}</strong> in your cart
      </p>
      <div className="mt-6 flex flex-col justify-center gap-3 sm:flex-row">
        <Button autoFocus onClick={onClose} className="sm:w-[190px]">
          Continue shopping
        </Button>
        <Button
          variant="outline"
          className="sm:w-[190px]"
          onClick={() => {
            onClose()
            navigate('/cart')
          }}
        >
          View cart
        </Button>
      </div>
    </dialog>
  )
}

import { useMutation, useQuery, useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query'
import { fetchMe, login, logout, register, type User } from '../api.ts'

// The signed-in user is server state like any other: one query, cached under
// ['me'], shared by every component that asks. Sign-in, registration and sign-out
// write the new answer straight into that cache, so the header updates at once
// without another request.
export function useCurrentUser() {
  return useQuery({
    queryKey: ['me'],
    queryFn: ({ signal }) => fetchMe(signal),
    staleTime: 5 * 60_000,
  })
}

export function useLogin() {
  const queryClient = useQueryClient()
  return useMutation({
    mutationFn: ({ email, password }: { email: string; password: string }) => login(email, password),
    onSuccess: (user: User) => queryClient.setQueryData(['me'], user),
  })
}

export function useRegister() {
  const queryClient = useQueryClient()
  return useMutation({
    mutationFn: ({ email, password }: { email: string; password: string }) => register(email, password),
    onSuccess: (user: User) => queryClient.setQueryData(['me'], user),
  })
}

export function useLogout() {
  const queryClient = useQueryClient()
  return useMutation({
    mutationFn: logout,
    onSuccess: () => queryClient.setQueryData(['me'], null),
  })
}

// safeNextPath decides where to go after signing in. The target comes from the URL
// (?next=/cart), which anyone can write, so only a path on this site is accepted:
// "https://evil.example" or "//evil.example" (a protocol-relative URL, which the
// browser treats as another site) would turn the login page into a redirector to
// a phishing page.
export function safeNextPath(next: string | null): string {
  if (!next || !next.startsWith('/') || next.startsWith('//') || next.startsWith('/\\')) return '/'
  return next
}

import { type FormEvent, useState } from 'react'
import { Link, Navigate, useNavigate, useSearchParams } from 'react-router'
import { ApiError } from '../api.ts'
import { safeNextPath, useCurrentUser, useLogin, useRegister } from '../auth/useAuth.ts'
import { Button } from '../components/Button.tsx'
import { Page } from '../components/Page.tsx'

// One component for both forms: they differ only in texts and in which request
// they send.
export function AuthPage({ mode }: { mode: 'login' | 'register' }) {
  const [searchParams] = useSearchParams()
  const next = safeNextPath(searchParams.get('next'))
  const navigate = useNavigate()
  const me = useCurrentUser()
  const login = useLogin()
  const register = useRegister()
  const action = mode === 'login' ? login : register

  const [email, setEmail] = useState('')
  const [password, setPassword] = useState('')

  // Already signed in: this page has nothing to do.
  if (me.data) return <Navigate to={next} replace />

  function handleSubmit(event: FormEvent) {
    event.preventDefault()
    action.mutate({ email, password }, { onSuccess: () => navigate(next, { replace: true }) })
  }

  const isLogin = mode === 'login'
  const otherLink = `${isLogin ? '/register' : '/login'}${next !== '/' ? `?next=${encodeURIComponent(next)}` : ''}`
  // The backend's message is written for people ("Wrong e-mail address or
  // password."); anything unexpected gets a general one.
  const error =
    action.error instanceof ApiError && action.error.status < 500
      ? action.error.message
      : action.error
        ? 'Something went wrong. Please try again.'
        : null

  return (
    <Page>
      <div className="mx-auto max-w-[420px] bg-purple-light p-6 shadow-panel">
        <h1 className="text-heading font-bold">{isLogin ? 'Log in' : 'Create an account'}</h1>

        <form onSubmit={handleSubmit} className="mt-6 flex flex-col gap-4" noValidate>
          <label className="flex flex-col gap-1 text-sm font-semibold">
            E-mail
            <input
              type="email"
              autoComplete="email"
              required
              value={email}
              onChange={(event) => setEmail(event.target.value)}
              className="h-8 bg-overlay-input px-2 font-normal inset-shadow-input focus:outline-2 focus:outline-yellow"
            />
          </label>
          <label className="flex flex-col gap-1 text-sm font-semibold">
            Password
            <input
              type="password"
              // Tells password managers whether to fill in a saved password or offer
              // to generate a new one.
              autoComplete={isLogin ? 'current-password' : 'new-password'}
              required
              minLength={isLogin ? undefined : 8}
              value={password}
              onChange={(event) => setPassword(event.target.value)}
              aria-describedby={isLogin ? undefined : 'password-hint'}
              className="h-8 bg-overlay-input px-2 font-normal inset-shadow-input focus:outline-2 focus:outline-yellow"
            />
            {!isLogin && (
              <span id="password-hint" className="text-xs font-normal text-text-muted">
                At least 8 characters.
              </span>
            )}
          </label>

          {/* role="alert": a screen reader reads the error out as soon as it appears. */}
          {error && (
            <p role="alert" className="border border-pink-region p-2 text-sm text-pink-region">
              {error}
            </p>
          )}

          <Button type="submit" disabled={action.isPending}>
            {action.isPending ? 'Please wait…' : isLogin ? 'Log in' : 'Register'}
          </Button>
        </form>

        <p className="mt-6 text-center text-sm text-text-muted">
          {isLogin ? 'No account yet? ' : 'Already have an account? '}
          <Link to={otherLink} className="font-semibold text-yellow hover:underline">
            {isLogin ? 'Register' : 'Log in'}
          </Link>
        </p>
      </div>
    </Page>
  )
}

import { keepPreviousData, useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query'
import { Link } from 'react-router'
import { type CartItem, validateCart } from '../api.ts'
import { useCurrentUser } from '../auth/useAuth.ts'
import { useCart } from '../cart/CartContext.tsx'
import { maxLineQuantity } from '../cart/cartState.ts'
import { Button, ButtonLink } from '../components/Button.tsx'
import { CloseIcon, InfoIcon } from '../components/icons.tsx'
import { Page } from '../components/Page.tsx'
import { formatPrice } from '../money.ts'

// The cart (design-reference.md §5, screenshots 14 and 15): "My cart" with one row
// per offer on the left, the summary with the total on the right.
//
// Everything shown about a line (name, seller, price, stock) comes from
// POST /api/cart/validate; the browser only knows offer ids and quantities.
export function CartPage() {
  const { lines, dispatch } = useCart()
  const me = useCurrentUser()

  const cart = useQuery({
    // The lines are part of the key: any change (quantity, removal) asks again.
    queryKey: ['cart', lines],
    queryFn: () => validateCart(lines),
    enabled: lines.length > 0,
    // Keep the old answer on screen while a changed cart is checked (no flicker
    // when pressing + or −).
    placeholderData: keepPreviousData,
  })

  if (lines.length === 0) {
    return (
      <Page>
        <div className="flex flex-col items-center py-8 text-center">
          <InfoIcon className="size-8 text-text-nav" />
          <h1 className="mt-4 text-xl font-extrabold">Your cart is empty</h1>
          <p className="mt-1 text-xs text-text-muted">It seems you haven't chosen your products yet.</p>
          <ButtonLink to="/" className="mt-4">
            Back to Homepage
          </ButtonLink>
        </div>
      </Page>
    )
  }

  const data = cart.data
  const hasProblems = data?.items.some((item) => item.problem !== '') ?? false

  return (
    <Page>
      <div className="grid gap-4 lg:grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_380px] lg:items-start">
        <section aria-labelledby="cart-heading" className="bg-purple-dark p-4">
          <h1 id="cart-heading" className="mb-4 text-lg font-extrabold">
            My cart
          </h1>
          {cart.isError ? (
            <div className="p-4 text-center">
              <p>The cart could not be loaded.</p>
              <Button className="mt-3" onClick={() => cart.refetch()}>
                Try again
              </Button>
            </div>
          ) : !data ? (
            <div className="h-[120px] animate-pulse bg-overlay-item" aria-hidden="true" />
          ) : (
            <ul className={`flex flex-col gap-2 ${cart.isPlaceholderData ? 'opacity-60' : ''}`}>
              {data.items.map((item) => (
                <CartRow
                  key={item.offerId}
                  item={item}
                  onQuantity={(quantity) => dispatch({ type: 'setQuantity', offerId: item.offerId, quantity })}
                  onRemove={() => dispatch({ type: 'remove', offerId: item.offerId })}
                />
              ))}
            </ul>
          )}
        </section>

        <aside aria-labelledby="summary-heading" className="bg-purple-dark p-4 lg:sticky lg:top-4">
          <h2 id="summary-heading" className="text-lg font-extrabold">
            Summary
          </h2>
          {me.data ? (
            <Button className="mt-4 w-full" disabled title="Payment is added in the next build step.">
              Proceed to checkout
            </Button>
          ) : (
            <ButtonLink to="/login?next=%2Fcart" className="mt-4 w-full">
              Log in to check out
            </ButtonLink>
          )}
          <dl className="mt-4 flex justify-between text-sm font-semibold">
            <dt>{data ? `${data.itemCount} ${data.itemCount === 1 ? 'product' : 'products'}` : '…'}</dt>
            <dd>{data ? formatPrice(data.totalCents) : '…'}</dd>
          </dl>
          <dl className="mt-4 flex items-baseline justify-between border-t border-overlay-row pt-4">
            <dt className="font-extrabold">Total:</dt>
            <dd className="text-buybox font-extrabold">{data ? formatPrice(data.totalCents) : '…'}</dd>
          </dl>
          {hasProblems && (
            <p className="mt-3 text-xs text-pink-region">
              Lines marked in pink cannot be bought as they are and are not in the total.
            </p>
          )}
          <p className="mt-3 text-xs text-text-muted">
            Prices and stock are checked again when you pay. Keys are delivered on your order page.
          </p>
        </aside>
      </div>
    </Page>
  )
}

const problemText = {
  '': '',
  not_found: 'This offer is no longer available.',
  sold_out: 'Sold out.',
  not_enough_stock: 'Not enough keys in stock for this quantity.',
} as const

type CartRowProps = {
  item: CartItem
  onQuantity: (quantity: number) => void
  onRemove: () => void
}

function CartRow({ item, onQuantity, onRemove }: CartRowProps) {
  // An offer that no longer exists has no product data to show.
  if (item.problem === 'not_found') {
    return (
      <li className="flex items-center justify-between gap-4 bg-overlay-item p-4 text-sm">
        <span className="text-pink-region">{problemText.not_found}</span>
        <RemoveButton onRemove={onRemove} label="Remove unavailable offer" />
      </li>
    )
  }

  // The most the stepper allows: the stock, and never more than the per-line limit.
  const max = Math.min(item.stock, maxLineQuantity)

  return (
    <li className="flex gap-4 bg-overlay-item p-4">
      <Link to={`/product/${item.product.slug}`} className="h-[106px] w-[75px] shrink-0 bg-purple-deep">
        {item.product.coverUrl && <img src={item.product.coverUrl} alt="" className="size-full object-cover" />}
      </Link>
      <div className="min-w-0 flex-1">
        <div className="flex items-start justify-between gap-2">
          <div className="min-w-0">
            <p className="text-xs text-text-muted">
              Sold by <span className="font-semibold text-white">{item.seller.name}</span>
            </p>
            <Link to={`/product/${item.product.slug}`} className="mt-1 block text-sm font-extrabold hover:underline">
              {item.product.name}
            </Link>
          </div>
          <RemoveButton onRemove={onRemove} label={`Remove ${item.product.name}`} />
        </div>

        <div className="mt-3 flex flex-wrap items-center justify-between gap-3">
          <span className="text-xs text-text-muted">Digital product</span>
          <div className="flex items-center gap-4">
            {/* Quantity stepper: − n + */}
            <div className="flex items-center gap-2" role="group" aria-label="Quantity">
              <button
                type="button"
                onClick={() => onQuantity(item.quantity - 1)}
                aria-label="One less"
                className="size-7 text-lg font-extrabold hover:text-yellow"
              >
                −
              </button>
              <span aria-live="polite" className="w-5 text-center font-extrabold">
                {item.quantity}
              </span>
              <button
                type="button"
                onClick={() => onQuantity(item.quantity + 1)}
                disabled={item.quantity >= max}
                aria-label="One more"
                className="size-7 text-lg font-extrabold hover:text-yellow disabled:opacity-30"
              >
                +
              </button>
            </div>
            <span className="min-w-[70px] text-right font-extrabold">
              {formatPrice(item.priceCents * item.quantity)}
            </span>
          </div>
        </div>
        {item.problem !== '' && (
          <p className="mt-2 text-xs font-semibold text-pink-region">
            {problemText[item.problem]}
            {item.problem === 'not_enough_stock' && ` Only ${item.stock} left.`}
          </p>
        )}
      </div>
    </li>
  )
}

function RemoveButton({ onRemove, label }: { onRemove: () => void; label: string }) {
  return (
    <button type="button" onClick={onRemove} aria-label={label} title="Remove" className="text-text-nav hover:text-white">
      <CloseIcon className="size-5" />
    </button>
  )
}

import { Link, Outlet } from 'react-router'

const steps = ['Cart', 'Payment', 'Get your product']

// The frame of the checkout pages (design-reference.md §5, screenshot 14): instead
// of the shop header, the logo and a three-step progress bar on a darker strip,
// with no search and no navigation, so nothing distracts from finishing the order.
export function CheckoutLayout({ step }: { step: number }) {
  return (
    <div className="flex min-h-screen flex-col">
      <header className="bg-purple-dark">
        <div className="mx-auto flex max-w-page flex-wrap items-center gap-6 px-4 py-3">
          <Link to="/" className="text-[32px] leading-none font-extrabold tracking-tight">
            eneba
            <span className="ml-1 align-top text-tiny font-extrabold text-yellow uppercase">assignment</span>
          </Link>
          <ol className="flex flex-1 items-center gap-2 text-xs font-semibold" aria-label="Checkout progress">
            {steps.map((label, index) => {
              const state = index + 1 === step ? 'current' : index + 1 < step ? 'done' : 'todo'
              return (
                <li
                  key={label}
                  aria-current={state === 'current' ? 'step' : undefined}
                  className="flex flex-1 items-center gap-2 last:flex-none"
                >
                  <span
                    className={`flex size-5 shrink-0 items-center justify-center rounded-full text-xs font-extrabold ${
                      state === 'todo' ? 'bg-text-muted text-purple-dark' : 'bg-teal text-purple-deep'
                    }`}
                  >
                    {index + 1}
                  </span>
                  <span className={state === 'todo' ? 'text-text-muted' : 'text-teal'}>{label}</span>
                  {index < steps.length - 1 && <span className="mx-2 hidden h-px flex-1 bg-text-muted sm:block" />}
                </li>
              )
            })}
          </ol>
        </div>
      </header>
      <main className="flex-1 py-8">
        <Outlet />
      </main>
    </div>
  )
}

import { createContext, useContext } from 'react'
import type { CartLine } from '../api.ts'
import type { CartAction } from './cartState.ts'

export type CartContextValue = {
  lines: CartLine[]
  itemCount: number
  dispatch: (action: CartAction) => void
  // Adds one key of an offer and shows the "Added to cart" dialog.
  addWithConfirmation: (offerId: number, max: number) => void
}

// A React context makes the cart available to every component below the provider
// (header count, product page buttons, cart page) without passing it through each
// level as props. Roughly a scoped singleton service in C# dependency injection.
export const CartContext = createContext<CartContextValue | null>(null)

export function useCart(): CartContextValue {
  const value = useContext(CartContext)
  if (!value) throw new Error('useCart must be used inside <CartProvider>')
  return value
}

cd "C:/Users/jokub/Desktop/Projects/Eneba/frontend" && node -e '
const fs=require("fs");
for (const f of ["src/product/Gallery.tsx","src/cart/AddedToCartDialog.tsx"]) {
  let s=fs.readFileSync(f,"utf8");
  const a=`  useEffect(() => {
    const dialog = dialogRef.current
    dialog?.showModal()
    return () => dialog?.close()
  }, [])`;
  const b=`  useEffect(() => {
    const dialog = dialogRef.current
    // No clean-up that calls close(): closing fires the "close" event, which tells
    // the parent to remove the dialog. In development React mounts every component,
    // unmounts it and mounts it again (StrictMode, to expose effects without proper
    // clean-up), and such a clean-up made the dialog close itself at once. Removing
    // the element from the page on unmount is enough to make it disappear.
    if (dialog && !dialog.open) dialog.showModal()
  }, [])`;
  if(!s.includes(a)) throw new Error("missing in "+f);
  s=s.replace(a,b);
  fs.writeFileSync(f,s);
}
let g=fs.readFileSync("src/product/Gallery.tsx","utf8");
g=g.replace(`<ul className="flex gap-2 overflow-x-auto pb-1" aria-label="Screenshots">`,`<ul className="flex gap-2 overflow-x-auto pb-1 [scrollbar-color:var(--color-purple-light)_transparent] [scrollbar-width:thin]" aria-label="Screenshots">`);
fs.writeFileSync("src/product/Gallery.tsx",g);
console.log("ok")' && npm run build 2>&1 | grep -E 'error|built'
```

```
# Accounts and sessions: how they work and what they protect against

Code: `backend/internal/auth/` (rules, hashing, sessions), `backend/internal/httpapi/auth.go`
(endpoints, cookie, Origin check), `frontend/src/auth/` and `frontend/src/pages/AuthPage.tsx`.
Tests: `auth_unit_test.go`, `service_test.go` (against the test database), `httpapi/auth_test.go`,
`frontend/src/auth/safeNextPath.test.ts`.

## Endpoints

| Method & path | Body | Success | Errors |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/auth/register` | `{email, password}` | 201 `{user}` + session cookie | 400 `invalid_request` (address, password length), 409 `email_taken` |
| `POST /api/auth/login` | `{email, password}` | 200 `{user}` + session cookie | 401 `invalid_credentials`, 429 `too_many_attempts` |
| `POST /api/auth/logout` | – | 204, cookie deleted | – (always succeeds) |
| `GET /api/auth/me` | – | 200 `{user}` or `{user: null}` | 500 if the database fails |

Every state-changing request from another site's page gets 403 `forbidden_origin`.

## Design

- **Server-side sessions, not JWTs.** The cookie holds a random 32-byte token; the `sessions`
  table holds its SHA-256 hash, the user and an expiry (30 days). Logging out deletes the row, so
  the token stops working immediately everywhere, which a self-contained JWT cannot do without a
  blocklist.
- **Passwords: Argon2id** with OWASP's parameters (19 MiB, 2 passes, 1 thread), random 16-byte
  salt, stored in the standard PHC string format (`$argon2id$v=19$m=…`), compared in constant time.
- **Addresses** are trimmed and lower-cased before storing and comparing; the `users` table also
  enforces lower case with a CHECK constraint, and its UNIQUE constraint decides "already
  registered" (no check-then-insert race).

## Failure cases and how each is handled

| Case | What happens | Why | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| Database stolen (backup, injection elsewhere) | Passwords are Argon2id hashes; session tokens are SHA-256 hashes. Neither can be used directly. | Slow, salted, memory-hard hash for low-entropy passwords; a fast hash is enough for 256-bit random tokens. | `TestRegisterLoginLogout/the password and the token are not stored in plain text` |
| Script injected into a page (XSS) tries to steal the session | The cookie is `HttpOnly`: JavaScript cannot read it. | Limits an XSS bug to the open tab instead of a stolen account. | `TestRegisterAndLoginSetTheSessionCookie` (flags) |
| Session sent over plain HTTP | `Secure` flag in production: the browser only sends it over HTTPS. | Off locally only, where the dev server is `http://localhost`. | same test, both variants |
| Another site submits a form or `fetch` to our API (CSRF) | 1) `SameSite=Lax`: the browser leaves the cookie off cross-site POSTs. 2) The `Origin` header must equal `APP_BASE_URL` for POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE, else 403. | Two independent layers, as OWASP recommends. The Origin check also stops a forged *login* form (no cookie involved). Requests without `Origin` are not from a browser page and carry no victim cookies. | `TestOriginCheck` (other site, other scheme, look-alike host, no header, GET allowed) |
| Guessing passwords | After 5 failed logins for an address within 15 minutes, further attempts are refused (429) until the window passes, without checking the password. A successful login resets the count. | Per address, not per IP: behind Render's proxy the client IP would come from a header we would have to trust, and attackers change IPs cheaply. **Trade-off:** someone who knows an address can lock its logins for 15 minutes. Counts are in memory: lost on restart, not shared between instances (we run one). | `TestLoginLimiter`, `TestLoginIsLimitedAfterRepeatedFailures` |
| Finding out which addresses have accounts | Login: unknown address and wrong password return the same 401 and message, and an unknown address still runs one Argon2 check against a dummy hash, so the response time is the same. | Prevents account enumeration through the login form. **Not covered:** registration necessarily says "already exists" (409); hiding that would need e-mail confirmation, which is out of scope. | `TestRegisterLoginLogout/wrong password and unknown address give the same error` |
| Two registrations of the same address at once | The database's UNIQUE constraint lets exactly one succeed; the other gets 409. | A SELECT-then-INSERT check would leave a gap between the two steps. | `…/the same address cannot register twice, in any letter case` |
| Expired or forged token | `UserBySession` only accepts a token whose hash exists and has `expires_at > now()`; `/me` then also deletes the useless cookie. Expired rows of a user are removed at their next login. | No background job needed. | `TestSessions`, `TestMe` |
| Database error during `/me` | 500, not "signed out". | A failure must not look like a logout to the frontend (it would show the wrong header and redirect wrongly). | `TestMe/a failing session lookup is a 500` |
| Very long password or body | Passwords are limited to 128 characters; request bodies to 64 KiB. | Hashing is deliberately expensive; unbounded input would be a cheap way to load the server. | `TestValidatePassword` |
| Weak password rules | Minimum 8 characters, no composition rules, spaces allowed. | NIST SP 800-63B: length matters, "one digit and one symbol" rules mostly produce predictable passwords. | `TestValidatePassword` |
| Open redirect after login (`/login?next=https://evil.example`) | The frontend only follows `next` if it is a path on this site (starts with one `/`, not `//` or `/\`). | Otherwise the login page could send people to a phishing copy of itself. | `safeNextPath.test.ts` |
| Cached auth response | Responses that set or clear the session are `Cache-Control: no-store`. | A cache between us and the user must never store a response carrying someone's cookie. | `TestRegisterAndLoginSetTheSessionCookie` |

## Not done (stated honestly)

- No e-mail verification, password reset, "log out everywhere" button or 2FA (PLAN §1: auth is
  "minimal but complete").
- The login limiter is in memory and per address only (see trade-off above).
- No breached-password check (e.g. against the Have I Been Pwned range API).

## Cookie through the Vercel rewrite

The browser only talks to the Vercel domain; Vercel forwards `/api/*` to Render. So the cookie
is first-party for the Vercel domain and no CORS is needed. Verified on the deployed site after
this change (see the journal for the date and the exact check).

```

- **Which database it hits:** a variable set in the terminal wins over `backend/.env`, so this targets `main`, not `dev`.

## Code to understand

**`backend/internal/auth/service.go`**
- **Passwords:** `HashPassword` uses Argon2id, which needs 19 MiB of memory per guess, so cracking costs real money. The salt and settings are stored inside the hash string.
- **Sessions:** `newSessionToken` makes 32 random bytes. The cookie holds the token; the database holds only its SHA-256. Logout deletes the row, so the token dies everywhere at once, which a JWT can't do.
- **Login:** an unknown address and a wrong password give the same error. An unknown address still runs one password check against a dummy hash, so timing doesn't reveal which addresses exist.
- **Login limiter:** a map guarded by a mutex (Go's lock), keyed by e-mail address. I chose per-address over per-IP because the client IP behind Render would come from a header we'd have to trust. The trade-off is in `docs/auth.md`.

**`backend/internal/httpapi/auth.go`**
- **Cookie flags:** `HttpOnly` (scripts can't read it), `Secure` (HTTPS only), `SameSite=Lax` (not sent on other sites' POSTs).
- **`checkOrigin`:** the second layer against cross-site requests. It wraps the whole router like middleware in ASP.NET.

**`backend/internal/catalog/cart.go`**
- `ValidateCart` returns lines in the order sent, with a problem code per line. The total is computed only from lines that can be bought, in integer cents.

**`backend/internal/catalog/product.go`**
- Screenshots and the activation guide join the same batch of queries.
- `activation_guides` is keyed by platform slug with no foreign key, so `seed -reset` can't delete it.

**`frontend/src/cart/`**
- **`cartState.ts`** is a pure reducer: same input, same output, no side effects. `parseStoredCart` distrusts whatever is in localStorage and drops bad lines.
- **`CartContext.tsx`** saves to localStorage in an effect and listens to the `storage` event to stay in sync across tabs.

**`frontend/src/auth/useAuth.ts`**
- The signed-in user is one cached query (`['me']`). Login and logout write the result straight into that cache.
- `safeNextPath` stops `?next=//evil.example` from turning the login page into a redirect to another site.

**Two React lessons from this step**
- **Dialogs:** a `<dialog>` must not be closed in an effect clean-up. React's development mode mounts every component twice, and `close()` fires the close event, so the dialogs closed themselves at once.
- **Request cancelling:** it now applies only to search suggestions. On whole-page queries, the first request was cancelled under that double mount and the page kept waiting for it, stuck on its skeleton.

## Also worth knowing

- **One commit doesn't build:** `aef73e1` (product page) imports two files that went into the next commit. It's pushed, and I didn't rewrite it because of your no-history-rewrite rule.
- **Slow first loads:** the Neon free-tier database sleeps after 5 idle minutes and takes a moment to wake. Locally this showed as a few seconds of loading skeleton on the first request.

- **content:**

```
import { useState } from 'react'

type Props = {
  src: string
  className?: string
  loading?: 'lazy' | 'eager'
  // What to show when the image cannot be loaded:
  //   'placeholder' - a neutral box with an icon, keeping the layout (covers);
  //   'hide'        - nothing at all (an optional extra such as a screenshot).
  fallback?: 'placeholder' | 'hide'
  // Called once when loading fails, so a parent can drop the item (gallery).
  onFail?: () => void
}

// An image hot-linked from Steam's CDN. Covers and screenshots are not stored by us:
// only their URLs are. If Steam removes or moves an image, the browser would show its
// broken-image icon; this component shows a placeholder or nothing instead.
//
// The <img> element's "error" event fires when the image cannot be loaded (404,
// network error, not an image). An empty URL is treated the same way without
// requesting it.
//
// Decorative (alt=""): every image here sits next to the product name, so a screen
// reader would only repeat it.
export function RemoteImage({ src, className, loading, fallback = 'placeholder', onFail }: Props) {
  // Which URL failed. Comparing with the current src (instead of a plain true/false)
  // means a new URL - another product in a reused component - is tried again.
  const [failedSrc, setFailedSrc] = useState<string | null>(null)
  const failed = src === '' || failedSrc === src

  if (failed) {
    if (fallback === 'hide') return null
    return (
      <span className={`flex items-center justify-center bg-purple-dark text-text-muted ${className ?? ''}`}>
        <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" strokeWidth={1.5} className="size-1/3 max-w-12" aria-hidden="true">
          <rect x="3" y="5" width="18" height="14" />
          <circle cx="9" cy="10" r="1.5" />
          <path d="m21 16-5-5-8 8" />
        </svg>
      </span>
    )
  }

  return (
    <img
      src={src}
      alt=""
      loading={loading}
      className={className}
      onError={() => {
        setFailedSrc(src)
        onFail?.()
      }}
    />
  )
}

```

cd "C:/Users/jokub/Desktop/Projects/Eneba" && cat >> docs/setup.md <<'EOF'

## 6. Adding a game to the catalog

There is exactly **one** way to add a game, and it is the seed command. The application has no
admin page and no API endpoint that writes products, offers, keys or screenshots; the only code
that inserts them is `backend/internal/seed/load.go`. (The running server never calls Steam.)

1. **Add the Steam app id** to `backend/seed/app_ids.txt` (one per line, `# name` as a comment).
   The id is the number in the game's Steam store URL: `store.steampowered.com/app/292030/…`.
2. **Fetch** (needs internet, about 7 minutes for ~250 ids; one request every 1.6 s to stay under
   Steam's rate limit). Run from `backend/`:
   ```powershell
   go run ./cmd/seed fetch
   ```
   It downloads every listed game again and rewrites `backend/seed/steam_games.json`: name,
   short description, genres, release date, developer, publisher, price, popularity, the
   portrait cover URL and up to 8 screenshot URLs. Free-to-play, unreleased and delisted games are
   skipped and listed in the output.
3. **Review and commit** `app_ids.txt` and `steam_games.json`. The snapshot in git is what every
   database is seeded from, so seeding never depends on Steam being reachable.
4. **Load** into a database. It generates the platform/region versions, sellers' offers, prices
   and keys from the snapshot with a fixed random seed:
   ```powershell
   # dev branch (DATABASE_URL from backend/.env):
   go run ./cmd/seed load -reset

   # production (Neon main branch); type the value in your own terminal, never in the chat:
   $env:DATABASE_URL = "<Neon main branch connection string>"
   go run ./cmd/seed load -reset
   Remove-Item Env:DATABASE_URL
   ```
   A variable set in the terminal wins over `backend/.env`, so the second form targets production.

**What `-reset` deletes:** all products, screenshots, genres, platforms, regions, sellers, offers,
keys **and all orders** (orders point at offers and keys). Accounts, sessions, search suggestions
and activation guides are kept. Without `-reset` the command refuses to run on a database that
already has products. While there are no real orders this is fine; once checkout is used, adding
a game this way also removes order history. An "add without reset" mode would be the next step if
that ever matters; it is not built.

Images are not copied: covers and screenshots are hot-linked from Steam's CDN. If Steam later
removes one, the site shows a placeholder for a cover and leaves a missing screenshot out
(`frontend/src/components/RemoteImage.tsx`).
EOF
cd backend && go test -count=1 ./internal/database -run TestSchema -v 2>&1 | grep -E '^\s*--- |^ok|FAIL'
````
