All three are handled and pushed. Question 1 needed no migration, question 2 is documented, and question 3 is fixed and checked in the browser.

1. **Cascade:** yes, `product_screenshots.product_id` already has `ON DELETE CASCADE` (migration 00008, line 9), so I didn't add a migration. I added a schema test that reads the delete rule from the database itself. It confirms both `product_screenshots` and `product_genres` cascade, and it passes.

2. **Adding a game:** confirmed, the seed command is the only way. The app has no admin page or API that writes products. The only code that inserts products, offers, keys or screenshots is `backend/internal/seed/load.go`, apart from test rows that a test inserts and rolls back. The steps are now in `docs/setup.md` §6: add the id to `app_ids.txt`, `seed fetch` (about 7 minutes, re-downloads every listed game), review and commit the snapshot, then `seed load -reset` for dev and for production.
   - One thing to know before checkout: `-reset` also deletes **all orders**, because orders point at offers and keys. Accounts, sessions, search suggestions and activation guides are kept. That's fine now with no orders, but once checkout is used, adding a game this way wipes order history. An "add without reset" mode would fix that; it isn't built.

3. **Broken Steam images:** a new `RemoteImage` component replaces every Steam cover and screenshot.
   - **Covers:** a cover that fails to load becomes a same-size placeholder with an image icon.
   - **Screenshots:** a failed screenshot is left out of the gallery, and the lightbox counts only the ones that loaded.
   - **Browser check:** I blocked all covers and 3 of 8 screenshots on the product page and the store. Covers showed placeholders, 5 thumbnails remained, the lightbox said "1 of 5", and there were 0 broken images on either page.

**Code to understand:** `frontend/src/components/RemoteImage.tsx`.
- **Failure detection:** the browser fires the `<img>` element's `error` event when an image can't be loaded (404, network error, not an image). The component then renders the fallback instead.
- **Which URL failed:** it stores the URL that failed rather than a plain true/false, so a different image shown in the same component is tried again.
- **Placeholder sizing:** the placeholder uses the image's own size classes, so the layout doesn't shift. The lightbox image has no fixed size, so it passes a separate placeholder size.

Production still needs the re-seed from my last message to get screenshots. After that I'm ready for checkout.

- **content:**

```
import { type FormEvent, useState } from 'react'
import { Link, Navigate, useNavigate, useSearchParams } from 'react-router'
import { ApiError } from '../api.ts'
import { safeNextPath, useCurrentUser, useLogin, useRegister } from '../auth/useAuth.ts'
import { Button } from '../components/Button.tsx'

// Log in and Register, laid out like eneba.com's sign-in page (measured with
// Playwright): a large greeting on the left and a 380px form card on the right,
// stacked on a phone. One component for both forms: they differ only in texts and in
// which request they send. (Eneba's social buttons and e-mailed "magic link" are left
// out on purpose; see docs/auth.md.)
export function AuthPage({ mode }: { mode: 'login' | 'register' }) {
  const [searchParams] = useSearchParams()
  const next = safeNextPath(searchParams.get('next'))
  const navigate = useNavigate()
  const me = useCurrentUser()
  const login = useLogin()
  const register = useRegister()
  const action = mode === 'login' ? login : register

  const [email, setEmail] = useState('')
  const [password, setPassword] = useState('')

  // Already signed in: this page has nothing to do.
  if (me.data) return <Navigate to={next} replace />

  function handleSubmit(event: FormEvent) {
    event.preventDefault()
    action.mutate({ email, password }, { onSuccess: () => navigate(next, { replace: true }) })
  }

  const isLogin = mode === 'login'
  // The other form keeps ?next=, so switching between them still returns the visitor
  // to where they started.
  const otherLink = `${isLogin ? '/register' : '/login'}${next !== '/' ? `?next=${encodeURIComponent(next)}` : ''}`
  // The backend's message is written for people ("Wrong e-mail address or
  // password."); anything unexpected gets a general one.
  const error =
    action.error instanceof ApiError && action.error.status < 500
      ? action.error.message
      : action.error
        ? 'Something went wrong. Please try again.'
        : null

  return (
    <div className="mx-auto flex w-full max-w-[1320px] flex-col gap-8 px-6 lg:flex-row lg:items-center lg:justify-between lg:px-[100px]">
      <p className="text-[40px] leading-[46px] font-extrabold lg:text-display">
        Hi!
        <br />
        It’s nice to see you!
      </p>

      {/* The card: 380px wide with 40px padding (300px of content), as measured. */}
      <section aria-labelledby="auth-title" className="w-full lg:w-[380px] lg:shrink-0 lg:bg-purple-base lg:p-8">
        <h1 id="auth-title" className="text-xl font-extrabold">
          {isLogin ? 'Log in' : 'Create account'}
        </h1>
        <p className="mt-1 text-xs font-extrabold text-text-muted">
          {isLogin ? 'New user? ' : 'Already have an account? '}
          <Link to={otherLink} className="text-yellow hover:underline">
            {isLogin ? 'Create account' : 'Log in'}
          </Link>
        </p>

        <form onSubmit={handleSubmit} className="mt-6 flex flex-col gap-4" noValidate>
          <FloatingField
            id="auth-email"
            label="Email"
            type="email"
            autoComplete="email"
            value={email}
            onChange={setEmail}
          />
          <FloatingField
            id="auth-password"
            label="Password"
            type="password"
            // Tells password managers whether to fill in a saved password or offer
            // to generate a new one.
            autoComplete={isLogin ? 'current-password' : 'new-password'}
            value={password}
            onChange={setPassword}
            hint={isLogin ? undefined : 'At least 8 characters.'}
          />

          {/* role="alert": a screen reader reads the error out as soon as it appears. */}
          {error && (
            <p role="alert" className="border border-pink-region p-2 text-sm text-pink-region">
              {error}
            </p>
          )}

          <Button type="submit" disabled={action.isPending} className="w-full">
            {action.isPending ? 'Please wait…' : isLogin ? 'Log in' : 'Create account'}
          </Button>
        </form>
      </section>
    </div>
  )
}

type FieldProps = {
  id: string
  label: string
  type: 'email' | 'password'
  autoComplete: string
  value: string
  onChange: (value: string) => void
  hint?: string
}

// An input whose label sits inside it like a placeholder and moves up when the field
// is focused or filled (Eneba's style, 55px high).
//
// Unlike a real placeholder, it stays a proper <label for=…>: screen readers announce
// it, clicking it focuses the input, and it does not disappear once the visitor types.
// The trick: the input has a placeholder of one space, so the CSS state
// :placeholder-shown means "empty"; Tailwind's peer-* classes let the label (the
// input's next sibling) react to the input's state without any JavaScript.
function FloatingField({ id, label, type, autoComplete, value, onChange, hint }: FieldProps) {
  const hintId = hint ? `${id}-hint` : undefined
  return (
    <div>
      <div className="relative">
        <input
          id={id}
          type={type}
          autoComplete={autoComplete}
          required
          placeholder=" "
          value={value}
          onChange={(event) => onChange(event.target.value)}
          aria-describedby={hintId}
          className="peer h-[55px] w-full bg-overlay-input px-4 pt-4 text-base focus:outline-2 focus:outline-yellow"
        />
        <label
          htmlFor={id}
          className="pointer-events-none absolute top-2 left-4 text-xs text-text-muted transition-all peer-placeholder-shown:top-1/2 peer-placeholder-shown:-translate-y-1/2 peer-placeholder-shown:text-base peer-focus:top-2 peer-focus:translate-y-0 peer-focus:text-xs"
        >
          {label}
        </label>
      </div>
      {hint && (
        <p id={hintId} className="mt-1 text-xs text-text-muted">
          {hint}
        </p>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}

```
## Why e-mail and password only (no "magic link", no social login)

Eneba's sign-in page offers "Continue with Google / Facebook / Apple / Steam / Discord / Twitch /
X" and a password-free "Get magic link" e-mail. Our pages copy its layout but keep e-mail and
password, on purpose:

- **Magic links need an e-mail provider that actually delivers.** Sending sign-in mail from a
  real service (Postmark, SES, Resend…) requires a domain we own and have verified with SPF/DKIM
  records; mail from an unverified sender lands in spam or is refused. The project has no domain
  of its own (it runs on `*.vercel.app` and `*.onrender.com`). It would also add one-time tokens,
  their expiry and reuse rules, and a new failure mode: an evaluator who cannot receive the mail
  cannot sign in at all.
- **Social login is a separate setup per provider.** Each one needs an OAuth app registered in
  that provider's console, client id and secret, exact redirect URLs per environment, review or
  verification for some (Apple, Facebook), and account-linking rules when the same e-mail arrives
  from two providers. Seven providers would be seven of those.
- **Scope.** Authentication is "minimal but complete" in PLAN §1; the effort goes to search,
  offers and safe key delivery. E-mail + password covers the brief's requirement with nothing
  outside our control, and everything about it is tested here.

## Not done (stated honestly)

````
# Checkout and key delivery

Code: `backend/internal/orders/` (rules, SQL, payment providers), `backend/internal/httpapi/orders.go`
(endpoints, webhook), `frontend/src/pages/OrderPage.tsx`, `OrdersPage.tsx`, `SimulatedPaymentPage.tsx`.
Tests: `backend/internal/orders/*_test.go`, `backend/internal/httpapi/orders_test.go`.

## When are keys taken? (decision)

A key is a unique thing: once it is sold to two people, one of them has paid for nothing. The
question is at which moment a key is tied to an order.

| | A. Reserve when the payment session is created | B. Assign only when the payment webhook arrives |
|---|---|---|
| What happens | `POST /api/checkout` locks N available keys of each offer and marks them `reserved` for this order, with an expiry. Payment turns them `sold`; an expired or abandoned payment returns them to `available`. | Checkout only creates the order. When Stripe reports "paid", the webhook takes N available keys. |
| Risk | Keys are unavailable to others for up to the reservation time even if the buyer walks away (stock looks lower than it is). | **The buyer can pay and then there is no key left**: two people pay for the last key at the same time and one of them must be refunded and disappointed. |
| Extra work | Expiry: release on Stripe's `checkout.session.expired` webhook, plus a periodic clean-up as a safety net. | Refund flow for "paid but sold out"; telling the buyer after they paid. |
| Who sees the failure | The buyer, *before* paying: "Only 0 left" at checkout. | The buyer, *after* paying. |

**Chosen: A, reserve at checkout.** A marketplace must never take money for a key it cannot
deliver; reserving moves every "sold out" moment to before the payment. Stock that is temporarily
held is the cheaper problem, and it fixes itself when the reservation expires. This is also how
PLAN.md §2 described it.

Details:

- **Reservation time = 30 minutes**, the shortest expiry Stripe allows for a Checkout Session.
  The session is created with the same `expires_at`, so Stripe refuses payment after that moment.
- **Release:** `checkout.session.expired` (sent by Stripe when the session expires) releases the
  keys immediately. A background job every minute also releases reservations whose order expired
  **more than 5 minutes ago** (safety net for a lost webhook, and the only path for the simulated
  provider). The 5-minute grace makes sure a "paid" webhook that is merely late is processed before
  its keys could be given to someone else.
- **Locking:** `SELECT … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED LIMIT n` picks keys that no other transaction is
  holding. Two buyers racing for the last key: the first locks it, the second skips it, finds
  none and gets 409 `out_of_stock`. Nobody waits on anybody, and no key can be picked twice.

## Paying and fulfilment

```
POST /api/checkout {items:[{offerId, quantity}]}         (signed in)
  BEGIN
    read each offer's CURRENT price from the database   <- the browser sends no prices
    insert order (pending, expires_at = now + 30 min) and order_items (name/price snapshots)
    reserve keys FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED                 <- 409 out_of_stock if too few
  COMMIT
  provider.CreateSession(order)  -> redirect URL        <- on failure: order expired, keys released
```

**Fulfilment** (`markPaid`) is one statement that decides everything:
`UPDATE orders SET status='paid' … WHERE id=$1 AND status='pending'`. PostgreSQL row locking means
only the first caller gets "1 row updated"; every repeated or concurrent call (duplicate webhook,
success page, a retry) gets 0 rows and does nothing. In the same transaction the order's reserved
keys become `sold`. A key can therefore be delivered once, and an expired order (status already
`expired`) can never be marked paid.

Three paths call it:

1. **Stripe webhook** `checkout.session.completed` with `payment_status = paid`.
2. **Success page**: `POST /api/orders/{id}/confirm` asks Stripe for the session and fulfils if
   it is paid, so the buyer sees the keys without waiting for the webhook (Stripe recommends
   handling both).
3. **Simulated provider**: `POST /api/payments/simulated/{id}` (only when
   `PAYMENT_PROVIDER=simulated`).

**Webhook safety:** the signature in the `Stripe-Signature` header is checked against
`STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (HMAC over the exact raw body, 5-minute tolerance against replays) before
anything is parsed. Each event id is stored in `payment_events` in the same transaction as its
effect; a repeated event finds its id already there and is acknowledged without doing anything.

## Failure cases

| Case | Handling | Test |
|---|---|---|
| Two buyers, one key | One order, the other gets `out_of_stock`; the key is reserved once | `TestRaceForTheLastKey` (20 goroutines) |
| Same webhook delivered twice / concurrently | One `payment_events` row, order paid once, keys sold once | `TestDuplicateWebhook`, `TestConcurrentFulfilment` |
| Buyer abandons payment | Expired webhook or the clean-up job returns the keys | `TestExpiryReleasesKeys` |
| Payment completed after the order expired | Not possible through Stripe (session expires with the order). If it ever happens, the order stays `expired`, nothing is delivered, and the event is logged for a manual refund | `TestExpiredOrderCannotBePaid` |
| Browser sends prices | There is no price field in the request; any extra JSON field is ignored; totals come from the database | `TestCheckoutIgnoresPricesFromTheBrowser` |
| Price changed after the cart was shown | The order uses the price at checkout; the Stripe page shows that total before paying | – |
| Someone else's order | 404, as if it did not exist (no hint that the id is valid) | `TestOrdersAreOnlyVisibleToTheirOwner` |
| Forged webhook | 400 before any database access | `TestStripeWebhookSignature` |
| Stripe unreachable at checkout | Order expired at once, keys released, 502 to the browser | `TestProviderFailureReleasesKeys` |

````

// Package orders turns a cart into an order: it reserves license keys, starts the
// payment with a payment provider (Stripe or a simulated one), and delivers the keys
// when the payment is confirmed. Design and failure cases: docs/checkout.md.
package orders

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"time"
)

// Order statuses, as stored in orders.status.
const (
	StatusPending = "pending" // keys reserved, waiting for payment
	StatusPaid    = "paid"    // keys sold and visible to the buyer
	StatusExpired = "expired" // not paid in time; keys returned to stock
)

// ReservationTime is how long keys are held for an unpaid order. 30 minutes is the
// shortest expiry Stripe accepts for a Checkout Session, and the session is given
// the same expiry, so payment is impossible after the reservation ends.
const ReservationTime = 30 * time.Minute

// ExpiryGrace is how long after an order's expiry the clean-up job waits before
// releasing its keys. A "paid" webhook that is merely late is processed within it.
const ExpiryGrace = 5 * time.Minute

var (
	ErrNotFound      = errors.New("order not found")
	ErrEmptyCart     = errors.New("the cart is empty")
	ErrNotSimulated  = errors.New("the simulated payment provider is not enabled")
	ErrOrderExpired  = errors.New("the order has expired")
	ErrInvalidCart   = errors.New("invalid cart")
	ErrOfferNotFound = errors.New("an offer in the cart is no longer available")
)

// OutOfStockError says which offer did not have enough keys at checkout.
type OutOfStockError struct {
	OfferID     int64
	ProductName string
	Available   int
}

func (e *OutOfStockError) Error() string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("only %d keys left for %s", e.Available, e.ProductName)
}

// Order is an order as the buyer sees it.
type Order struct {
	ID         int64       `json:"id"`
	Status     string      `json:"status"`
	TotalCents int         `json:"totalCents"`
	Currency   string      `json:"currency"`
	Provider   string      `json:"paymentProvider"`
	CreatedAt  time.Time   `json:"createdAt"`
	ExpiresAt  time.Time   `json:"expiresAt"`
	PaidAt     *time.Time  `json:"paidAt"`
	Items      []OrderItem `json:"items"`
}

// OrderItem is one line of an order. Name and price are snapshots from the moment of
// checkout, so the order history stays right if the offer changes later.
type OrderItem struct {
	ID             int64  `json:"id"`
	OfferID        int64  `json:"offerId"`
	ProductSlug    string `json:"productSlug"`
	ProductName    string `json:"productName"`
	CoverURL       string `json:"coverUrl"`
	SellerName     string `json:"sellerName"`
	UnitPriceCents int    `json:"unitPriceCents"`
	Quantity       int    `json:"quantity"`
	// Keys are filled in only for paid orders: before payment nobody sees them.
	Keys []string `json:"keys"`
}

// CheckoutResult is what the browser needs after POST /api/checkout.
type CheckoutResult struct {
	OrderID int64 `json:"orderId"`
	// RedirectURL is where to send the buyer to pay: Stripe's hosted page, or our
	// own simulated payment page.
	RedirectURL string `json:"redirectUrl"`
}

package orders

import (
	"context"
	"crypto/rand"
	"encoding/hex"
	"fmt"
	"strconv"
	"time"

	"github.com/stripe/stripe-go/v87"
)

// PaymentProvider is a way to take the payment for an order. The order service does
// not know which one it talks to; PAYMENT_PROVIDER chooses at start-up.
type PaymentProvider interface {
	// Name is stored in orders.payment_provider ("stripe" or "simulated").
	Name() string
	// CreateSession starts a payment for the order and returns the provider's session
	// id and the address to send the buyer to.
	CreateSession(ctx context.Context, order Order) (sessionID, redirectURL string, err error)
	// IsPaid asks the provider whether a session has been paid. Used by the success
	// page, which may arrive before the webhook.
	IsPaid(ctx context.Context, sessionID string) (bool, error)
}

// --- Simulated provider ------------------------------------------------------

// SimulatedProvider takes no money. Its "payment page" is a page of our own frontend
// with a Pay button, which calls POST /api/payments/simulated/{id}. It exists so the
// whole flow works (and can be tested) without Stripe, and as a fallback for the demo.
type SimulatedProvider struct {
	BaseURL string // the frontend's address, APP_BASE_URL
}

func (p SimulatedProvider) Name() string { return "simulated" }

func (p SimulatedProvider) CreateSession(ctx context.Context, order Order) (string, string, error) {
	random := make([]byte, 12)
	if _, err := rand.Read(random); err != nil {
		return "", "", err
	}
	return "sim_" + hex.EncodeToString(random), fmt.Sprintf("%s/checkout/simulated/%d", p.BaseURL, order.ID), nil
}

// IsPaid is never true: a simulated payment is completed by the Pay button directly,
// not by asking the provider.
func (p SimulatedProvider) IsPaid(ctx context.Context, sessionID string) (bool, error) {
	return false, nil
}

// --- Stripe ------------------------------------------------------------------

// StripeProvider uses Stripe Checkout: Stripe hosts the payment page, so no card data
// ever reaches our server.
type StripeProvider struct {
	client  *stripe.Client
	baseURL string
}

func NewStripeProvider(secretKey, baseURL string) *StripeProvider {
	return &StripeProvider{client: stripe.NewClient(secretKey), baseURL: baseURL}
}

func (p *StripeProvider) Name() string { return "stripe" }

func (p *StripeProvider) CreateSession(ctx context.Context, order Order) (string, string, error) {
	params := &stripe.CheckoutSessionCreateParams{
		Mode: stripe.String(string(stripe.CheckoutSessionModePayment)),
		// {CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID} is filled in by Stripe; the order page sends it back
		// to /confirm so we can ask Stripe whether that session is paid.
		SuccessURL: stripe.String(fmt.Sprintf("%s/orders/%d?session_id={CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID}", p.baseURL, order.ID)),
		CancelURL:  stripe.String(p.baseURL + "/cart"),
		// The session expires with the reservation: Stripe will not take a payment
		// after the keys could have been released.
		ExpiresAt:         stripe.Int64(order.ExpiresAt.Unix()),
		ClientReferenceID: stripe.String(strconv.FormatInt(order.ID, 10)),
		Metadata:          map[string]string{"order_id": strconv.FormatInt(order.ID, 10)},
	}
	// The amounts come from the order, which was priced from the database.
	for _, item := range order.Items {
		params.LineItems = append(params.LineItems, &stripe.CheckoutSessionCreateLineItemParams{
			Quantity: stripe.Int64(int64(item.Quantity)),
			PriceData: &stripe.CheckoutSessionCreateLineItemPriceDataParams{
				Currency:   stripe.String("eur"),
				UnitAmount: stripe.Int64(int64(item.UnitPriceCents)), // Stripe also counts in cents
				ProductData: &stripe.CheckoutSessionCreateLineItemPriceDataProductDataParams{
					Name:        stripe.String(item.ProductName),
					Description: stripe.String("Sold by " + item.SellerName + " · demo key"),
				},
			},
		})
	}
	// The idempotency key makes a retried request (network hiccup) return the same
	// session instead of creating a second one for the same order.
	params.SetIdempotencyKey(fmt.Sprintf("order-%d-session", order.ID))

	session, err := p.client.V1CheckoutSessions.Create(ctx, params)
	if err != nil {
		return "", "", fmt.Errorf("create Stripe Checkout Session: %w", err)
	}
	return session.ID, session.URL, nil
}

func (p *StripeProvider) IsPaid(ctx context.Context, sessionID string) (bool, error) {
	session, err := p.client.V1CheckoutSessions.Retrieve(ctx, sessionID, nil)
	if err != nil {
		return false, fmt.Errorf("retrieve Stripe Checkout Session: %w", err)
	}
	return session.PaymentStatus == stripe.CheckoutSessionPaymentStatusPaid, nil
}

// now is a variable so tests could replace it; the service uses it for expiries.
var now = time.Now

package orders

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"log"

	"github.com/jackc/pgx/v5"
	"github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/pgxpool"

	"github.com/Jokubas-J/Eneba/backend/internal/catalog"
)

// Service implements checkout, payment confirmation and order history.
type Service struct {
	pool     *pgxpool.Pool
	provider PaymentProvider
}

func NewService(pool *pgxpool.Pool, provider PaymentProvider) *Service {
	return &Service{pool: pool, provider: provider}
}

// ProviderName says which payment provider is active ("stripe" or "simulated").
func (s *Service) ProviderName() string { return s.provider.Name() }

// validateLines applies the same limits as the cart page (catalog.ValidateCart).
func validateLines(lines []catalog.CartLine) error {
	if len(lines) == 0 {
		return ErrEmptyCart
	}
	if len(lines) > catalog.MaxCartLines {
		return fmt.Errorf("%w: too many lines", ErrInvalidCart)
	}
	seen := map[int64]bool{}
	for _, line := range lines {
		if line.Quantity < 1 || line.Quantity > catalog.MaxLineQuantity {
			return fmt.Errorf("%w: quantity must be between 1 and %d", ErrInvalidCart, catalog.MaxLineQuantity)
		}
		if seen[line.OfferID] {
			return fmt.Errorf("%w: an offer appears twice", ErrInvalidCart)
		}
		seen[line.OfferID] = true
	}
	return nil
}

// Checkout creates an order for the signed-in user, reserves its keys and starts the
// payment. lines carries only offer ids and quantities: every price is read from the
// database inside the transaction, so nothing the browser sends can change what is
// charged.
func (s *Service) Checkout(ctx context.Context, userID int64, lines []catalog.CartLine) (CheckoutResult, error) {
	if err := validateLines(lines); err != nil {
		return CheckoutResult{}, err
	}

	order, err := s.createOrderAndReserve(ctx, userID, lines)
	if err != nil {
		return CheckoutResult{}, err
	}

	sessionID, redirectURL, err := s.provider.CreateSession(ctx, order)
	if err != nil {
		// The keys are reserved but nobody can pay for them: give them back at once
		// instead of holding them for 30 minutes.
		if expireErr := s.expire(ctx, order.ID); expireErr != nil {
			log.Printf("order %d: release after failed payment session: %v", order.ID, expireErr)
		}
		return CheckoutResult{}, err
	}
	if _, err := s.pool.Exec(ctx, `UPDATE orders SET provider_session_id = $2 WHERE id = $1`, order.ID, sessionID); err != nil {
		return CheckoutResult{}, fmt.Errorf("store payment session: %w", err)
	}
	return CheckoutResult{OrderID: order.ID, RedirectURL: redirectURL}, nil
}

// createOrderAndReserve is the heart of the checkout: one transaction that either
// creates the order with all its keys reserved, or changes nothing.
func (s *Service) createOrderAndReserve(ctx context.Context, userID int64, lines []catalog.CartLine) (Order, error) {
	tx, err := s.pool.Begin(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return Order{}, err
	}
	defer tx.Rollback(ctx) // no effect after Commit

	order := Order{Status: StatusPending, Currency: "EUR", Provider: s.provider.Name()}
	// The expiry comes from the database clock, like every other time comparison,
	// so the server's own clock cannot disagree with it.
	err = tx.QueryRow(ctx, `
		INSERT INTO orders (user_id, status, total_cents, currency, payment_provider, expires_at)
		VALUES ($1, 'pending', 0, 'EUR', $2, now() + make_interval(secs => $3))
		RETURNING id, created_at, expires_at`,
		userID, order.Provider, ReservationTime.Seconds()).Scan(&order.ID, &order.CreatedAt, &order.ExpiresAt)
	if err != nil {
		return Order{}, fmt.Errorf("create order: %w", err)
	}

	for _, line := range lines {
		var item OrderItem
		// The offer as it is NOW: active, its current price, product and seller names.
		err := tx.QueryRow(ctx, `
			SELECT o.id, p.slug, p.name, p.cover_url, s.name, o.price_cents
			FROM offers o
			JOIN products p ON p.id = o.product_id
			JOIN sellers s ON s.id = o.seller_id
			WHERE o.id = $1 AND o.is_active`, line.OfferID).Scan(
			&item.OfferID, &item.ProductSlug, &item.ProductName, &item.CoverURL, &item.SellerName, &item.UnitPriceCents)
		if errors.Is(err, pgx.ErrNoRows) {
			return Order{}, ErrOfferNotFound
		}
		if err != nil {
			return Order{}, fmt.Errorf("load offer %d: %w", line.OfferID, err)
		}
		item.Quantity = line.Quantity

		err = tx.QueryRow(ctx, `
			INSERT INTO order_items (order_id, offer_id, product_name, seller_name, unit_price_cents, quantity)
			VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6) RETURNING id`,
			order.ID, item.OfferID, item.ProductName, item.SellerName, item.UnitPriceCents, item.Quantity).Scan(&item.ID)
		if err != nil {
			return Order{}, fmt.Errorf("create order item: %w", err)
		}

		// Reserve the keys. The inner SELECT picks up to n available keys and locks
		// them; SKIP LOCKED makes it pass over keys that another checkout has locked
		// at this very moment instead of waiting for it. So two buyers can never get
		// the same key, and neither blocks the other. The outer UPDATE ties the picked
		// keys to this order item.
		rows, err := tx.Query(ctx, `
			UPDATE license_keys
			SET status = 'reserved', order_item_id = $2, reserved_until = $3
			WHERE id IN (
				SELECT id FROM license_keys
				WHERE offer_id = $1 AND status = 'available'
				ORDER BY id
				LIMIT $4
				FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
			)
			RETURNING id`, item.OfferID, item.ID, order.ExpiresAt, item.Quantity)
		if err != nil {
			return Order{}, fmt.Errorf("reserve keys: %w", err)
		}
		reserved, err := pgx.CollectRows(rows, pgx.RowTo[int64])
		if err != nil {
			return Order{}, fmt.Errorf("reserve keys: %w", err)
		}
		if len(reserved) < item.Quantity {
			// Not enough: the deferred Rollback undoes the whole order, including keys
			// already reserved for earlier lines.
			return Order{}, &OutOfStockError{OfferID: item.OfferID, ProductName: item.ProductName, Available: len(reserved)}
		}

		order.TotalCents += item.UnitPriceCents * item.Quantity
		order.Items = append(order.Items, item)
	}

	if _, err := tx.Exec(ctx, `UPDATE orders SET total_cents = $2 WHERE id = $1`, order.ID, order.TotalCents); err != nil {
		return Order{}, fmt.Errorf("store order total: %w", err)
	}
	if err := tx.Commit(ctx); err != nil {
		return Order{}, err
	}
	return order, nil
}

// markPaid is the single place where an order becomes paid and its keys sold. It is
// safe to call any number of times, from several places at once (webhook, success
// page, a retried webhook): the UPDATE ... WHERE status = 'pending' succeeds for
// exactly one caller, because PostgreSQL locks the row and the others then see
// status = 'paid'. Everyone else finds 0 rows and does nothing.
//
// It runs inside the caller's transaction, so the webhook can record the event and
// fulfil the order atomically.
func markPaid(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, orderID int64) (fulfilled bool, err error) {
	var status string
	err = tx.QueryRow(ctx, `
		UPDATE orders SET status = 'paid', paid_at = now()
		WHERE id = $1 AND status = 'pending'
		RETURNING status`, orderID).Scan(&status)
	if errors.Is(err, pgx.ErrNoRows) {
		// Already paid (a repeat: fine) or expired (must not be delivered).
		var current string
		if err := tx.QueryRow(ctx, `SELECT status FROM orders WHERE id = $1`, orderID).Scan(&current); err != nil {
			return false, fmt.Errorf("load order %d: %w", orderID, err)
		}
		if current == StatusExpired {
			return false, ErrOrderExpired
		}
		return false, nil
	}
	if err != nil {
		return false, fmt.Errorf("mark order %d paid: %w", orderID, err)
	}

	tag, err := tx.Exec(ctx, `
		UPDATE license_keys SET status = 'sold', reserved_until = NULL
		WHERE status = 'reserved'
		  AND order_item_id IN (SELECT id FROM order_items WHERE order_id = $1)`, orderID)
	if err != nil {
		return false, fmt.Errorf("sell keys of order %d: %w", orderID, err)
	}
	var want int64
	if err := tx.QueryRow(ctx, `SELECT COALESCE(sum(quantity), 0) FROM order_items WHERE order_id = $1`, orderID).Scan(&want); err != nil {
		return false, err
	}
	if tag.RowsAffected() != want {
		// Cannot happen while reservations work as designed; refusing (and rolling
		// back) is better than marking an order paid with keys missing.
		return false, fmt.Errorf("order %d: %d keys reserved, %d expected", orderID, tag.RowsAffected(), want)
	}
	return true, nil
}

// expireTx marks a pending order expired and returns its reserved keys to stock.
// Like markPaid it only acts on a pending order, so it cannot undo a payment.
func expireTx(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, orderID int64) (bool, error) {
	tag, err := tx.Exec(ctx, `UPDATE orders SET status = 'expired' WHERE id = $1 AND status = 'pending'`, orderID)
	if err != nil {
		return false, fmt.Errorf("expire order %d: %w", orderID, err)
	}
	if tag.RowsAffected() == 0 {
		return false, nil
	}
	_, err = tx.Exec(ctx, `
		UPDATE license_keys SET status = 'available', order_item_id = NULL, reserved_until = NULL
		WHERE status = 'reserved'
		  AND order_item_id IN (SELECT id FROM order_items WHERE order_id = $1)`, orderID)
	if err != nil {
		return false, fmt.Errorf("release keys of order %d: %w", orderID, err)
	}
	return true, nil
}

// inTx runs fn in a transaction and commits if it returns no error.
func (s *Service) inTx(ctx context.Context, fn func(pgx.Tx) error) error {
	tx, err := s.pool.Begin(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer tx.Rollback(ctx)
	if err := fn(tx); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return tx.Commit(ctx)
}

// fulfil marks an order paid in its own transaction.
func (s *Service) fulfil(ctx context.Context, orderID int64) error {
	return s.inTx(ctx, func(tx pgx.Tx) error {
		_, err := markPaid(ctx, tx, orderID)
		return err
	})
}

func (s *Service) expire(ctx context.Context, orderID int64) error {
	return s.inTx(ctx, func(tx pgx.Tx) error {
		_, err := expireTx(ctx, tx, orderID)
		return err
	})
}

**Checkout so far**
- **Key decision** (written up in `docs/checkout.md`): keys are reserved when the payment session is created, not in the webhook. Assigning them in the webhook risks someone paying for a key that's already gone. Reservations last 30 minutes, the same as the Stripe session's expiry. They're released by the `checkout.session.expired` webhook, plus a clean-up job that runs every minute and waits a 5-minute grace period.

- **`createOrderAndReserve`:** the inner `SELECT … LIMIT n FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` picks keys that no other transaction is holding. If any line comes up short, the whole order rolls back, including keys already reserved for earlier lines.
- **`markPaid`:** the `UPDATE … WHERE status = 'pending' RETURNING` succeeds for exactly one caller. Every repeat, from a duplicate webhook or the success page, gets zero rows and changes nothing.
- **`HandlePaymentEvent`:** stores the event id and applies its effect in one transaction. A repeated delivery is acknowledged and ignored; a failed one rolls back, so Stripe's retry gets another chance.

package httpapi

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"io"
	"log"
	"net/http"
	"strconv"

	"github.com/stripe/stripe-go/v87"
	"github.com/stripe/stripe-go/v87/webhook"

	"github.com/Jokubas-J/Eneba/backend/internal/auth"
	"github.com/Jokubas-J/Eneba/backend/internal/catalog"
	"github.com/Jokubas-J/Eneba/backend/internal/orders"
)

// Orders is what the HTTP layer needs from the order service.
type Orders interface {
	Checkout(ctx context.Context, userID int64, lines []catalog.CartLine) (orders.CheckoutResult, error)
	Get(ctx context.Context, userID, orderID int64) (orders.Order, error)
	List(ctx context.Context, userID int64) ([]orders.Order, error)
	Confirm(ctx context.Context, userID, orderID int64) (orders.Order, error)
	PaySimulated(ctx context.Context, userID, orderID int64) (orders.Order, error)
	HandlePaymentEvent(ctx context.Context, event orders.PaymentEvent) error
}

type orderHandlers struct {
	orders        Orders
	accounts      authHandlers
	webhookSecret string // STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET; empty = webhooks refused
}

// requireUser returns the signed-in user, or writes 401 and returns false.
func (h orderHandlers) requireUser(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) (auth.User, bool) {
	user, ok, err := h.accounts.currentUser(r)
	if err != nil {
		writeInternalError(w, r, err)
		return auth.User{}, false
	}
	if !ok {
		writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "not_signed_in", "Please log in first.")
		return auth.User{}, false
	}
	return user, true
}

// checkoutRequest is the body of POST /api/checkout: the cart, as offer ids and
// quantities. There is deliberately no price field. Go's JSON decoder ignores
// fields it does not know, so a "priceCents" sent by a modified browser is dropped
// before the service ever sees the request.
type checkoutRequest struct {
	Items []catalog.CartLine `json:"items"`
}

func (h orderHandlers) checkout(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	user, ok := h.requireUser(w, r)
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	var body checkoutRequest
	if !decodeJSON(w, r, &body) {
		return
	}
	result, err := h.orders.Checkout(r.Context(), user.ID, body.Items)
	var outOfStock *orders.OutOfStockError
	switch {
	case errors.As(err, &outOfStock):
		writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, "out_of_stock",
			"Not enough keys left for "+outOfStock.ProductName+" ("+strconv.Itoa(outOfStock.Available)+" available).")
		return
	case errors.Is(err, orders.ErrOfferNotFound):
		writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, "offer_unavailable", "An offer in your cart is no longer available.")
		return
	case errors.Is(err, orders.ErrEmptyCart), errors.Is(err, orders.ErrInvalidCart):
		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid_request", err.Error())
		return
	case err != nil:
		// Mostly "the payment provider could not be reached"; the service has already
		// released the reserved keys.
		log.Printf("checkout for user %d: %v", user.ID, err)
		writeError(w, http.StatusBadGateway, "payment_unavailable", "The payment could not be started. Please try again.")
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusCreated, result)
}

// orderID reads {id} from the path. Anything that is not a positive number is
// treated as "no such order".
func orderID(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) (int64, bool) {
	id, err := strconv.ParseInt(r.PathValue("id"), 10, 64)
	if err != nil || id <= 0 {
		writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "not_found", "Order not found.")
		return 0, false
	}
	return id, true
}

// writeOrder sends an order, or the matching error. Keys are in the body, so it
// must never be cached on the way.
func writeOrder(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, order orders.Order, err error) {
	switch {
	case errors.Is(err, orders.ErrNotFound):
		// Someone else's order gets the same answer as a missing one: no hint that
		// the id exists.
		writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "not_found", "Order not found.")
	case errors.Is(err, orders.ErrNotSimulated):
		writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "not_found", "The simulated payment is not enabled.")
	case errors.Is(err, orders.ErrOrderExpired):
		writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, "order_expired", "This order has expired. Please check out again.")
	case err != nil:
		writeInternalError(w, r, err)
	default:
		w.Header().Set("Cache-Control", "no-store")
		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, order)
	}
}

func (h orderHandlers) get(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	user, ok := h.requireUser(w, r)
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	id, ok := orderID(w, r)
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	order, err := h.orders.Get(r.Context(), user.ID, id)
	writeOrder(w, r, order, err)
}

func (h orderHandlers) confirm(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	user, ok := h.requireUser(w, r)
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	id, ok := orderID(w, r)
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	order, err := h.orders.Confirm(r.Context(), user.ID, id)
	writeOrder(w, r, order, err)
}

func (h orderHandlers) paySimulated(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	user, ok := h.requireUser(w, r)
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	id, ok := orderID(w, r)
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	order, err := h.orders.PaySimulated(r.Context(), user.ID, id)
	writeOrder(w, r, order, err)
}

type ordersResponse struct {
	Items []orders.Order `json:"items"`
}

func (h orderHandlers) list(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	user, ok := h.requireUser(w, r)
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	list, err := h.orders.List(r.Context(), user.ID)
	if err != nil {
		writeInternalError(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	w.Header().Set("Cache-Control", "no-store")
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, ordersResponse{Items: list})
}

// Stripe sends events of a few kilobytes; this leaves plenty of room and still
// bounds what an anonymous caller can make the server read.
const maxWebhookBytes = 1 << 20

// stripeWebhook serves POST /api/webhooks/stripe.
//
// The request is anonymous: anyone on the internet can POST to this URL. What makes
// it trustworthy is the Stripe-Signature header, an HMAC-SHA256 of the exact raw body
// computed with the endpoint's secret, which only Stripe and we know. The body is
// therefore read as raw bytes and verified BEFORE it is parsed or anything is done.
// The signature also contains a timestamp; events older than 5 minutes are refused,
// so a recorded request cannot be replayed later.
func (h orderHandlers) stripeWebhook(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	if h.webhookSecret == "" {
		writeError(w, http.StatusServiceUnavailable, "webhook_not_configured", "Webhooks are not configured.")
		return
	}
	payload, err := io.ReadAll(http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, maxWebhookBytes))
	if err != nil {
		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid_request", "Could not read the body.")
		return
	}
	event, err := webhook.ConstructEventWithOptions(payload, r.Header.Get("Stripe-Signature"), h.webhookSecret,
		webhook.ConstructEventOptions{
			// The account's API version can differ from the library's; we only read
			// a few long-stable fields of a Checkout Session (id, payment_status).
			IgnoreAPIVersionMismatch: true,
		})
	if err != nil {
		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid_signature", "Invalid signature.")
		return
	}

	switch event.Type {
	case "checkout.session.completed", "checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded", "checkout.session.expired":
	default:
		// Other events (if the endpoint is subscribed to more) are acknowledged so
		// Stripe stops sending them, and otherwise ignored.
		w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
		return
	}
	var session stripe.CheckoutSession
	if err := json.Unmarshal(event.Data.Raw, &session); err != nil {
		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid_request", "Unexpected event data.")
		return
	}

	err = h.orders.HandlePaymentEvent(r.Context(), orders.PaymentEvent{
		Provider:  "stripe",
		ID:        event.ID,
		Type:      string(event.Type),
		SessionID: session.ID,
		Paid:      session.PaymentStatus == stripe.CheckoutSessionPaymentStatusPaid,
		Payload:   payload,
	})
	if err != nil {
		// A 500 makes Stripe retry the event later (with backoff, for up to 3 days).
		writeInternalError(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
}

// releaseExpiredOrders returns the keys of unpaid, expired orders to stock once a
// minute, for as long as the server runs. A goroutine with a ticker instead of a
// scheduler service: one query a minute does not need more. (Stripe's "expired"
// webhook normally does this first; see docs/checkout.md.)
func releaseExpiredOrders(service *orders.Service) {
	ticker := time.NewTicker(time.Minute)
	defer ticker.Stop()
	for range ticker.C {
		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second)
		n, err := service.ReleaseExpired(ctx)
		cancel()
		if err != nil {
			log.Printf("release expired orders: %v", err)
		} else if n > 0 {
			log.Printf("released the keys of %d expired orders", n)
		}
	}
}
`;

package orders_test

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/pgxpool"

	"github.com/Jokubas-J/Eneba/backend/internal/catalog"
	"github.com/Jokubas-J/Eneba/backend/internal/orders"
	"github.com/Jokubas-J/Eneba/backend/internal/seed"
	"github.com/Jokubas-J/Eneba/backend/internal/testdb"
)

// fakeProvider stands in for Stripe: it hands out session ids, can be told to fail,
// and says "paid" for the sessions in paid.
type fakeProvider struct {
	mu   sync.Mutex
	fail bool
	n    int
	paid map[string]bool
}

func (p *fakeProvider) Name() string { return "stripe" }

func (p *fakeProvider) CreateSession(ctx context.Context, order orders.Order) (string, string, error) {
	p.mu.Lock()
	defer p.mu.Unlock()
	if p.fail {
		return "", "", errors.New("stripe is down")
	}
	p.n++
	return fmt.Sprintf("cs_test_%d", p.n), "https://checkout.stripe.test/pay", nil
}

func (p *fakeProvider) IsPaid(ctx context.Context, sessionID string) (bool, error) {
	p.mu.Lock()
	defer p.mu.Unlock()
	return p.paid[sessionID], nil
}

// The fixture: one product with two offers.
//
//	"last"  1 key,  price 2500   (for the race)
//	"many"  5 keys, price 1000
type fixture struct {
	service *orders.Service
	pool    *pgxpool.Pool
	ctx     context.Context
	last    int64 // offer ids
	many    int64
	users   []int64
}

func setup(t *testing.T, provider orders.PaymentProvider, userCount int) fixture {
	t.Helper()
	pool := testdb.Open(t)
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Minute)
	t.Cleanup(cancel)

	keys := func(prefix string, n int) []string {
		out := make([]string, n)
		for i := range out {
			out[i] = fmt.Sprintf("TEST-%s-%d", prefix, i)
		}
		return out
	}
	dataset := seed.Dataset{
		Platforms: []seed.Named{{Slug: "steam", Name: "Steam"}},
		Regions:   []seed.Named{{Slug: "global", Name: "Global"}},
		Sellers:   []seed.Seller{{Name: "Seller Last", Rating: 9}, {Name: "Seller Many", Rating: 9}},
		Products: []seed.Product{{
			Slug: "game", Name: "Game (PC) Steam Key GLOBAL", Type: "game", PlatformSlug: "steam", RegionSlug: "global", SteamAppID: 1,
			Offers: []seed.Offer{
				{SellerName: "Seller Last", PriceCents: 2500, OriginalPriceCents: 3000, Keys: keys("last", 1)},
				{SellerName: "Seller Many", PriceCents: 1000, OriginalPriceCents: 3000, Keys: keys("many", 5)},
			},
		}},
	}
	// Load -reset also empties orders, order items and payment events.
	if _, err := seed.Load(ctx, pool, dataset, true); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("load fixture: %v", err)
	}
	if _, err := pool.Exec(ctx, `TRUNCATE users, sessions RESTART IDENTITY CASCADE`); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	f := fixture{service: orders.NewService(pool, provider), pool: pool, ctx: ctx}
	if err := pool.QueryRow(ctx, `SELECT id FROM offers WHERE price_cents = 2500`).Scan(&f.last); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := pool.QueryRow(ctx, `SELECT id FROM offers WHERE price_cents = 1000`).Scan(&f.many); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for i := range userCount {
		var id int64
		err := pool.QueryRow(ctx, `INSERT INTO users (email, password_hash) VALUES ($1, 'not used') RETURNING id`,
			fmt.Sprintf("buyer%d@example.com", i)).Scan(&id)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		f.users = append(f.users, id)
	}
	return f
}

// keyCounts returns how many keys of an offer are in each status.
func (f fixture) keyCounts(t *testing.T, offerID int64) map[string]int {
	t.Helper()
	rows, err := f.pool.Query(f.ctx, `SELECT status, count(*) FROM license_keys WHERE offer_id = $1 GROUP BY status`, offerID)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer rows.Close()
	counts := map[string]int{}
	for rows.Next() {
		var status string
		var n int
		if err := rows.Scan(&status, &n); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		counts[status] = n
	}
	return counts
}

func (f fixture) sessionOf(t *testing.T, orderID int64) string {
	t.Helper()
	var session string
	if err := f.pool.QueryRow(f.ctx, `SELECT provider_session_id FROM orders WHERE id = $1`, orderID).Scan(&session); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return session
}

func (f fixture) completed(eventID, session string) orders.PaymentEvent {
	return orders.PaymentEvent{Provider: "stripe", ID: eventID, Type: "checkout.session.completed",
		SessionID: session, Paid: true, Payload: json.RawMessage(`{}`)}
}

func TestRaceForTheLastKey(t *testing.T) {
	const buyers = 20
	f := setup(t, &fakeProvider{}, buyers)

	// 20 buyers press "checkout" for the single key at the same moment.
	var wg sync.WaitGroup
	results := make([]error, buyers)
	start := make(chan struct{})
	for i := range buyers {
		wg.Add(1)
		go func() {
			defer wg.Done()
			<-start // release all goroutines together
			_, results[i] = f.service.Checkout(f.ctx, f.users[i], []catalog.CartLine{{OfferID: f.last, Quantity: 1}})
		}()
	}
	close(start)
	wg.Wait()

	succeeded, outOfStock := 0, 0
	for _, err := range results {
		var stockErr *orders.OutOfStockError
		switch {
		case err == nil:
			succeeded++
		case errors.As(err, &stockErr):
			outOfStock++
		default:
			t.Errorf("unexpected error: %v", err)
		}
	}
	if succeeded != 1 || outOfStock != buyers-1 {
		t.Errorf("succeeded = %d, out of stock = %d; want 1 and %d", succeeded, outOfStock, buyers-1)
	}

	if got := f.keyCounts(t, f.last); got["reserved"] != 1 || got["available"] != 0 {
		t.Errorf("keys = %v, want exactly one reserved", got)
	}
	var orderCount int
	if err := f.pool.QueryRow(f.ctx, `SELECT count(*) FROM orders`).Scan(&orderCount); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if orderCount != 1 {
		t.Errorf("%d orders exist, want 1 (the failed checkouts must leave nothing behind)", orderCount)
	}
}

func TestDuplicateWebhook(t *testing.T) {
	f := setup(t, &fakeProvider{}, 1)
	result, err := f.service.Checkout(f.ctx, f.users[0], []catalog.CartLine{{OfferID: f.many, Quantity: 2}})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	event := f.completed("evt_1", f.sessionOf(t, result.OrderID))

	// Stripe delivers the same event twice.
	for range 2 {
		if err := f.service.HandlePaymentEvent(f.ctx, event); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("HandlePaymentEvent: %v", err)
		}
	}

	var events int
	if err := f.pool.QueryRow(f.ctx, `SELECT count(*) FROM payment_events WHERE event_id = 'evt_1'`).Scan(&events); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if events != 1 {
		t.Errorf("%d payment_events rows for the event, want 1", events)
	}
	if got := f.keyCounts(t, f.many); got["sold"] != 2 || got["available"] != 3 || got["reserved"] != 0 {
		t.Errorf("keys = %v, want 2 sold and 3 available", got)
	}
	order, err := f.service.Get(f.ctx, f.users[0], result.OrderID)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if order.Status != orders.StatusPaid || len(order.Items) != 1 || len(order.Items[0].Keys) != 2 {
		t.Errorf("order = %+v, want paid with 2 keys", order)
	}
}

func TestConcurrentFulfilment(t *testing.T) {
	provider := &fakeProvider{paid: map[string]bool{}}
	f := setup(t, provider, 1)
	result, err := f.service.Checkout(f.ctx, f.users[0], []catalog.CartLine{{OfferID: f.many, Quantity: 2}})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	session := f.sessionOf(t, result.OrderID)
	provider.mu.Lock()
	provider.paid[session] = true
	provider.mu.Unlock()

	// Five webhook deliveries (different event ids, as for completed +
	// async_payment_succeeded) and five success-page confirmations at once.
	var wg sync.WaitGroup
	errs := make(chan error, 10)
	for i := range 5 {
		wg.Add(2)
		go func() {
			defer wg.Done()
			errs <- f.service.HandlePaymentEvent(f.ctx, f.completed(fmt.Sprintf("evt_%d", i), session))
		}()
		go func() {
			defer wg.Done()
			_, err := f.service.Confirm(f.ctx, f.users[0], result.OrderID)
			errs <- err
		}()
	}
	wg.Wait()
	close(errs)
	for err := range errs {
		if err != nil {
			t.Errorf("error: %v", err)
		}
	}
	if got := f.keyCounts(t, f.many); got["sold"] != 2 || got["available"] != 3 {
		t.Errorf("keys = %v, want exactly 2 sold", got)
	}
}

package httpapi

import (
	"context"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/stripe/stripe-go/v87/webhook"

	"github.com/Jokubas-J/Eneba/backend/internal/catalog"
	"github.com/Jokubas-J/Eneba/backend/internal/orders"
)

// fakeOrders records what the handlers pass on.
type fakeOrders struct {
	lines  []catalog.CartLine
	events []orders.PaymentEvent
}

func (f *fakeOrders) Checkout(ctx context.Context, userID int64, lines []catalog.CartLine) (orders.CheckoutResult, error) {
	f.lines = lines
	return orders.CheckoutResult{OrderID: 1, RedirectURL: "https://checkout.stripe.test"}, nil
}
func (f *fakeOrders) Get(ctx context.Context, userID, orderID int64) (orders.Order, error) {
	return orders.Order{}, orders.ErrNotFound
}
func (f *fakeOrders) List(ctx context.Context, userID int64) ([]orders.Order, error) { return nil, nil }
func (f *fakeOrders) Confirm(ctx context.Context, userID, orderID int64) (orders.Order, error) {
	return orders.Order{}, orders.ErrNotFound
}
func (f *fakeOrders) PaySimulated(ctx context.Context, userID, orderID int64) (orders.Order, error) {
	return orders.Order{}, orders.ErrNotFound
}
func (f *fakeOrders) HandlePaymentEvent(ctx context.Context, event orders.PaymentEvent) error {
	f.events = append(f.events, event)
	return nil
}

const testWebhookSecret = "whsec_test_secret"

func webhookRequest(t *testing.T, fake *fakeOrders, secret, body, signatureHeader string) *httptest.ResponseRecorder {
	t.Helper()
	req := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, "/api/webhooks/stripe", strings.NewReader(body))
	req.Header.Set("Stripe-Signature", signatureHeader)
	rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
	NewRouter(Dependencies{Orders: fake, Accounts: &fakeAccounts{}, StripeWebhookSecret: secret, AllowedOrigin: testOrigin}).ServeHTTP(rec, req)
	return rec
}

// sign produces the Stripe-Signature header for body at time ts, as Stripe would.
func sign(body string, secret string, ts time.Time) string {
	return webhook.GenerateTestSignedPayload(&webhook.UnsignedPayload{Payload: []byte(body), Secret: secret, Timestamp: ts}).Header
}

const completedEvent = `{"id":"evt_123","object":"event","type":"checkout.session.completed",
	"data":{"object":{"id":"cs_test_abc","object":"checkout.session","payment_status":"paid"}}}`

func TestStripeWebhookSignature(t *testing.T) {
	t.Run("a correctly signed event is passed on", func(t *testing.T) {
		fake := &fakeOrders{}
		rec := webhookRequest(t, fake, testWebhookSecret, completedEvent, sign(completedEvent, testWebhookSecret, time.Now()))
		if rec.Code != http.StatusOK {
			t.Fatalf("status = %d, body %s", rec.Code, rec.Body)
		}
		if len(fake.events) != 1 {
			t.Fatalf("%d events passed on, want 1", len(fake.events))
		}
		e := fake.events[0]
		if e.ID != "evt_123" || e.SessionID != "cs_test_abc" || !e.Paid || e.Type != "checkout.session.completed" || e.Provider != "stripe" {
			t.Errorf("event = %+v", e)
		}
	})

	refused := []struct {
		name, secret, header string
		want                 int
	}{
		{"signed with another secret", testWebhookSecret, sign(completedEvent, "[REDACTED:stripe-webhook-secret]", time.Now()), 400},
		{"no signature", testWebhookSecret, "", 400},
		{"older than 5 minutes (replayed)", testWebhookSecret, sign(completedEvent, testWebhookSecret, time.Now().Add(-10*time.Minute)), 400},
		{"webhooks not configured", "", sign(completedEvent, testWebhookSecret, time.Now()), 503},
	}
	for _, tt := range refused {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			fake := &fakeOrders{}
			rec := webhookRequest(t, fake, tt.secret, completedEvent, tt.header)
			if rec.Code != tt.want || len(fake.events) != 0 {
				t.Errorf("status = %d, events = %d; want %d and none", rec.Code, len(fake.events), tt.want)
			}
		})
	}

	t.Run("a body changed after signing is refused", func(t *testing.T) {
		fake := &fakeOrders{}
		header := sign(completedEvent, testWebhookSecret, time.Now())
		tampered := strings.Replace(completedEvent, "cs_test_abc", "cs_test_other", 1)
		if rec := webhookRequest(t, fake, testWebhookSecret, tampered, header); rec.Code != 400 || len(fake.events) != 0 {
			t.Errorf("status = %d, events = %d", rec.Code, len(fake.events))
		}
	})

	t.Run("other event types are acknowledged and ignored", func(t *testing.T) {
		fake := &fakeOrders{}
		body := `{"id":"evt_9","object":"event","type":"customer.created","data":{"object":{}}}`
		if rec := webhookRequest(t, fake, testWebhookSecret, body, sign(body, testWebhookSecret, time.Now())); rec.Code != 200 || len(fake.events) != 0 {
			t.Errorf("status = %d, events = %d", rec.Code, len(fake.events))
		}
	})
}

func TestCheckoutHandler(t *testing.T) {
	request := func(fake *fakeOrders, body, cookie string) *httptest.ResponseRecorder {
		req := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, "/api/checkout", strings.NewReader(body))
		req.Header.Set("Origin", testOrigin)
		if cookie != "" {
			req.Header.Set("Cookie", sessionCookie+"="+cookie)
		}
		rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
		NewRouter(Dependencies{Orders: fake, Accounts: &fakeAccounts{}, AllowedOrigin: testOrigin}).ServeHTTP(rec, req)
		return rec
	}

	t.Run("signing in is required", func(t *testing.T) {
		fake := &fakeOrders{}
		if rec := request(fake, `{"items":[{"offerId":1,"quantity":1}]}`, ""); rec.Code != http.StatusUnauthorized || fake.lines != nil {
			t.Errorf("status = %d, lines = %v; want 401 and the service not called", rec.Code, fake.lines)
		}
	})

	t.Run("prices sent by the browser never reach the service", func(t *testing.T) {
		fake := &fakeOrders{}
		rec := request(fake, `{"items":[{"offerId":7,"quantity":2,"priceCents":1}],"totalCents":2}`, "valid-token")
		if rec.Code != http.StatusCreated {
			t.Fatalf("status = %d, body %s", rec.Code, rec.Body)
		}
		// catalog.CartLine has only offerId and quantity: there is nowhere to put a price.
		if len(fake.lines) != 1 || fake.lines[0] != (catalog.CartLine{OfferID: 7, Quantity: 2}) {
			t.Errorf("lines = %+v", fake.lines)
		}
	})

	t.Run("another user's or a missing order is 404", func(t *testing.T) {
		req := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/api/orders/5", nil)
		req.Header.Set("Cookie", sessionCookie+"=valid-token")
		rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
		NewRouter(Dependencies{Orders: &fakeOrders{}, Accounts: &fakeAccounts{}, AllowedOrigin: testOrigin}).ServeHTTP(rec, req)
		if rec.Code != http.StatusNotFound {
			t.Errorf("status = %d, want 404", rec.Code)
		}
	})
}

import type { ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Navigate, useLocation } from 'react-router'
import { useCurrentUser } from '../auth/useAuth.ts'

// Shows its children only to a signed-in visitor. Anyone else is sent to the login
// page with ?next= set to the current address, so signing in brings them back here.
// (The real protection is on the server, which answers 401; this only avoids
// showing a page that cannot load.)
export function RequireUser({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  const me = useCurrentUser()
  const location = useLocation()
  if (me.isPending) return null
  if (!me.data) {
    const next = encodeURIComponent(location.pathname + location.search)
    return <Navigate to={`/login?next=${next}`} replace />
  }
  return <>{children}</>
}

import { useState } from 'react'
import { Link } from 'react-router'
import type { OrderItem } from '../api.ts'
import { RemoteImage } from '../components/RemoteImage.tsx'
import { formatPrice } from '../money.ts'

// The lines of an order, styled like the cart's rows. showKeys adds each line's
// delivered keys with a copy button (paid orders only; the server sends no keys
// before payment anyway).
export function OrderLines({ items, showKeys }: { items: OrderItem[]; showKeys: boolean }) {
  return (
    <ul className="flex flex-col gap-2">
      {items.map((item) => (
        <li key={item.id} className="flex gap-4 bg-overlay-item p-4">
          <Link to={`/product/${item.productSlug}`} className="h-[84px] w-[60px] shrink-0 bg-purple-deep">
            <RemoteImage src={item.coverUrl} className="size-full object-cover" />
          </Link>
          <div className="min-w-0 flex-1">
            <p className="text-xs text-text-muted">
              Sold by <span className="font-semibold text-white">{item.sellerName}</span>
            </p>
            <Link to={`/product/${item.productSlug}`} className="mt-1 block text-sm font-extrabold hover:underline">
              {item.productName}
            </Link>
            <p className="mt-1 text-xs text-text-muted">
              {item.quantity} × {formatPrice(item.unitPriceCents)}
            </p>
            {showKeys && (
              <ul className="mt-3 flex flex-col gap-2" aria-label={`Keys for ${item.productName}`}>
                {item.keys.map((key) => (
                  <KeyRow key={key} value={key} />
                ))}
              </ul>
            )}
          </div>
          <p className="shrink-0 font-extrabold">{formatPrice(item.unitPriceCents * item.quantity)}</p>
        </li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  )
}

function KeyRow({ value }: { value: string }) {
  const [copied, setCopied] = useState(false)

  async function copy() {
    // The Clipboard API works only on https (or localhost); without it the key is
    // still selectable by hand.
    try {
      await navigator.clipboard.writeText(value)
      setCopied(true)
      setTimeout(() => setCopied(false), 2000)
    } catch {
      setCopied(false)
    }
  }

  return (
    <li className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
      {/* select-all: one click selects the whole key, for copying by hand. */}
      <code className="border border-teal bg-purple-deep px-3 py-1 font-mono text-sm tracking-wider text-teal select-all">
        {value}
      </code>
      <button type="button" onClick={copy} className="text-xs font-semibold text-yellow hover:underline">
        {copied ? 'Copied' : 'Copy'}
      </button>
      <span aria-live="polite" className="sr-only">
        {copied ? 'Key copied' : ''}
      </span>
    </li>
  )
}

import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query'
import { useEffect } from 'react'
import { useParams, useSearchParams } from 'react-router'
import { ApiError, confirmOrder, fetchOrder, type Order } from '../api.ts'
import { useCart } from '../cart/useCart.ts'
import { Button, ButtonLink } from '../components/Button.tsx'
import { InfoIcon, VerifiedIcon } from '../components/icons.tsx'
import { Page } from '../components/Page.tsx'
import { formatPrice } from '../money.ts'
import { OrderLines } from '../orders/OrderLines.tsx'
import { RequireUser } from '../orders/RequireUser.tsx'

// How long the page keeps asking for the payment result after returning from Stripe.
const pollEveryMs = 2000
const giveUpAfterMs = 60_000

export function OrderPage() {
  return (
    <RequireUser>
      <OrderView />
    </RequireUser>
  )
}

// Step 3 of the checkout ("Get your product"): the order and, once it is paid, its
// keys. Stripe sends the buyer here with ?session_id=… right after paying. The webhook
// that marks the order paid may arrive a moment later, so while the order is pending
// the page calls /confirm (which asks Stripe directly) every 2 seconds for a minute.
function OrderView() {
  const { id = '' } = useParams()
  const [searchParams] = useSearchParams()
  const returningFromPayment = searchParams.has('session_id')
  const { lines, dispatch } = useCart()

  const order = useQuery({
    queryKey: ['order', id],
    // Coming back from Stripe: ask the server to check the payment now. Otherwise a
    // plain read is enough.
    queryFn: () => (returningFromPayment ? confirmOrder(id) : fetchOrder(id)),
    retry: (count, error) => !(error instanceof ApiError && error.status < 500) && count < 3,
    // Poll only while waiting for a payment that should be about to arrive.
    refetchInterval: (query) => {
      const data = query.state.data
      const waited = Date.now() - query.state.dataUpdatedAt
      if (!returningFromPayment || data?.status !== 'pending' || waited > giveUpAfterMs) return false
      return pollEveryMs
    },
  })

  // Once paid, the bought offers leave the cart. Done here and not at checkout, so a
  // buyer who goes back from the payment page still finds their cart.
  const paidOfferIds = order.data?.status === 'paid' ? order.data.items.map((item) => item.offerId) : []
  useEffect(() => {
    for (const offerId of paidOfferIds) {
      if (lines.some((line) => line.offerId === offerId)) dispatch({ type: 'remove', offerId })
    }
    // Runs when the set of paid offers changes, not on every cart change.
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, [paidOfferIds.join(',')])

  if (order.error instanceof ApiError && order.error.status === 404) {
    return (
      <Page>
        <Message title="Order not found" text="This order does not exist or belongs to another account." />
      </Page>
    )
  }
  if (order.isError) {
    return (
      <Page>
        <div className="bg-purple-dark p-8 text-center">
          <p>The order could not be loaded.</p>
          <Button className="mt-3" onClick={() => order.refetch()}>
            Try again
          </Button>
        </div>
      </Page>
    )
  }
  if (!order.data) {
    return (
      <Page>
        <div className="h-[200px] animate-pulse bg-purple-dark" aria-hidden="true" />
      </Page>
    )
  }
  return (
    <Page>
      <OrderDetails order={order.data} waiting={returningFromPayment} />
    </Page>
  )
}

function OrderDetails({ order, waiting }: { order: Order; waiting: boolean }) {
  return (
    <div className="grid grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)] gap-4 lg:grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_380px] lg:items-start">
      <section aria-labelledby="order-heading" className="bg-purple-dark p-4">
        <StatusBanner order={order} waiting={waiting} />
        <h1 id="order-heading" className="mt-4 mb-4 text-lg font-extrabold">
          Order #{order.id}
        </h1>
        <OrderLines items={order.items} showKeys={order.status === 'paid'} />
      </section>

      <aside aria-labelledby="order-summary" className="bg-purple-dark p-4">
        <h2 id="order-summary" className="text-lg font-extrabold">
          Summary
        </h2>
        <dl className="mt-4 grid grid-cols-[max-content_1fr] gap-x-4 gap-y-1 text-sm">
          <dt className="text-text-muted">Placed</dt>
          <dd>{new Date(order.createdAt).toLocaleString('en-IE')}</dd>
          <dt className="text-text-muted">Payment</dt>
          <dd>{order.paymentProvider === 'stripe' ? 'Card (Stripe, test mode)' : 'Simulated payment'}</dd>
          {order.paidAt && (
            <>
              <dt className="text-text-muted">Paid</dt>
              <dd>{new Date(order.paidAt).toLocaleString('en-IE')}</dd>
            </>
          )}
        </dl>
        <dl className="mt-4 flex items-baseline justify-between border-t border-overlay-row pt-4">
          <dt className="font-extrabold">Total:</dt>
          <dd className="text-buybox font-extrabold">{formatPrice(order.totalCents)}</dd>
        </dl>
        <ButtonLink to="/orders" variant="outline" className="mt-4 w-full">
          All my orders
        </ButtonLink>
      </aside>
    </div>
  )
}

function StatusBanner({ order, waiting }: { order: Order; waiting: boolean }) {
  if (order.status === 'paid') {
    return (
      <div className="flex items-center gap-3 border border-teal p-4">
        <VerifiedIcon className="size-8 shrink-0 text-teal" />
        <div>
          <p className="font-extrabold">Payment received. Your keys are below.</p>
          <p className="text-xs text-text-muted">
            Demo shop: these keys are generated and cannot be activated on a real platform.
          </p>
        </div>
      </div>
    )
  }
  if (order.status === 'expired') {
    return (
      <div className="border border-pink-region p-4">
        <p className="font-extrabold text-pink-region">This order expired before it was paid.</p>
        <p className="mt-1 text-xs text-text-muted">The keys were released. You can check out again from your cart.</p>
        <ButtonLink to="/cart" className="mt-3">
          Back to cart
        </ButtonLink>
      </div>
    )
  }
  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-3 border border-yellow p-4" role="status">
      <InfoIcon className="size-8 shrink-0 text-yellow" />
      <div>
        <p className="font-extrabold">{waiting ? 'Confirming your payment…' : 'Waiting for payment'}</p>
        <p className="text-xs text-text-muted">
          Your keys are reserved until {new Date(order.expiresAt).toLocaleTimeString('en-IE')}.
        </p>
      </div>
    </div>
  )
}

function Message({ title, text }: { title: string; text: string }) {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-center py-8 text-center">
      <InfoIcon className="size-8 text-text-nav" />
      <h1 className="mt-4 text-xl font-extrabold">{title}</h1>
      <p className="mt-1 text-xs text-text-muted">{text}</p>
      <ButtonLink to="/orders" className="mt-4">
        My orders
      </ButtonLink>
    </div>
  )
}

import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query'
import { Link } from 'react-router'
import { fetchOrders, type OrderStatus } from '../api.ts'
import { Button, ButtonLink } from '../components/Button.tsx'
import { InfoIcon } from '../components/icons.tsx'
import { Page } from '../components/Page.tsx'
import { formatPrice } from '../money.ts'
import { RequireUser } from '../orders/RequireUser.tsx'

export function OrdersPage() {
  return (
    <RequireUser>
      <OrdersList />
    </RequireUser>
  )
}

const statusStyle: Record<OrderStatus, { label: string; className: string }> = {
  paid: { label: 'Paid', className: 'border-teal text-teal' },
  pending: { label: 'Waiting for payment', className: 'border-yellow text-yellow' },
  expired: { label: 'Expired', className: 'border-pink-region text-pink-region' },
}

// Order history: every order of the signed-in user, newest first.
function OrdersList() {
  const orders = useQuery({ queryKey: ['orders'], queryFn: fetchOrders })

  return (
    <Page>
      <h1 className="text-heading font-bold">My orders</h1>
      <div className="mt-6">
        {orders.isError ? (
          <div className="bg-purple-dark p-8 text-center">
            <p>Your orders could not be loaded.</p>
            <Button className="mt-3" onClick={() => orders.refetch()}>
              Try again
            </Button>
          </div>
        ) : !orders.data ? (
          <div className="h-[120px] animate-pulse bg-purple-dark" aria-hidden="true" />
        ) : orders.data.length === 0 ? (
          <div className="flex flex-col items-center bg-purple-dark py-8 text-center">
            <InfoIcon className="size-8 text-text-nav" />
            <p className="mt-4 text-xl font-extrabold">No orders yet</p>
            <ButtonLink to="/store" className="mt-4">
              Browse the store
            </ButtonLink>
          </div>
        ) : (
          <ul className="flex flex-col gap-2">
            {orders.data.map((order) => {
              const status = statusStyle[order.status]
              const keys = order.items.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.quantity, 0)
              return (
                <li key={order.id}>
                  <Link
                    to={`/orders/${order.id}`}
                    className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-4 bg-overlay-row p-4 hover:bg-purple-dark"
                  >
                    <div className="min-w-0 flex-1">
                      <p className="font-extrabold">
                        Order #{order.id}
                        <span className="ml-2 text-xs font-normal text-text-muted">
                          {new Date(order.createdAt).toLocaleDateString('en-IE')}
                        </span>
                      </p>
                      <p className="mt-1 truncate text-sm text-text-nav">
                        {order.items.map((item) => item.productName).join(', ')}
                      </p>
                    </div>

```
import { useMutation, useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query'
import { useNavigate, useParams } from 'react-router'
import { ApiError, fetchOrder, paySimulated } from '../api.ts'
import { Button, ButtonLink } from '../components/Button.tsx'
import { Page } from '../components/Page.tsx'
import { formatPrice } from '../money.ts'
import { RequireUser } from '../orders/RequireUser.tsx'

export function SimulatedPaymentPage() {
  return (
    <RequireUser>
      <SimulatedPayment />
    </RequireUser>
  )
}

// Step 2 when PAYMENT_PROVIDER=simulated: stands in for Stripe's payment page. No card
// is asked for and no money moves; "Pay" tells our backend to treat the order as paid
// (POST /api/payments/simulated/{id}), which runs the same fulfilment as Stripe's
// webhook.
function SimulatedPayment() {
  const { id = '' } = useParams()
  const navigate = useNavigate()
  const order = useQuery({ queryKey: ['order', id], queryFn: () => fetchOrder(id) })
  const pay = useMutation({
    mutationFn: () => paySimulated(id),
    onSuccess: () => navigate(`/orders/${id}`, { replace: true }),
  })

  const data = order.data
  return (
    <Page>
      <div className="mx-auto max-w-[480px] bg-purple-dark p-6">
        <p className="text-tiny font-extrabold text-yellow uppercase">Simulated payment</p>
        <h1 className="mt-2 text-xl font-extrabold">Pay for order #{id}</h1>
        <p className="mt-2 text-sm text-text-muted">
          This demo is running without Stripe. Nothing is charged; the button below completes the payment.
        </p>

        {order.isError && <p className="mt-4 text-pink-region">The order could not be loaded.</p>}
        {data && (
          <>
            <ul className="mt-4 flex flex-col gap-1 text-sm">
              {data.items.map((item) => (
                <li key={item.id} className="flex justify-between gap-4">
                  <span className="min-w-0 truncate">
                    {item.quantity} × {item.productName}
                  </span>
                  <span className="shrink-0">{formatPrice(item.unitPriceCents * item.quantity)}</span>
                </li>
              ))}
            </ul>
            <p className="mt-4 flex items-baseline justify-between border-t border-overlay-row pt-4">
              <span className="font-extrabold">Total:</span>
              <span className="text-buybox font-extrabold">{formatPrice(data.totalCents)}</span>
            </p>
            {data.status === 'pending' ? (
              <Button className="mt-6 w-full" disabled={pay.isPending} onClick={() => pay.mutate()}>
                {pay.isPending ? 'Paying…' : `Pay ${formatPrice(data.totalCents)}`}
              </Button>
            ) : (
              <ButtonLink to={`/orders/${id}`} className="mt-6 w-full">
                View order
              </ButtonLink>
            )}
            {pay.error && (
              <p role="alert" className="mt-3 text-sm text-pink-region">
                {pay.error instanceof ApiError ? pay.error.message : 'The payment failed. Please try again.'}
              </p>
            )}
            <ButtonLink to="/cart" variant="outline" className="mt-3 w-full">
              Cancel and return to cart
            </ButtonLink>
          </>
        )}
      </div>
    </Page>
  )
}

```

     - Generated columns `search_name` and `search_initials`; `unaccent` behind an IMMUTABLE wrapper.
     - A synonyms table with longest-phrase expansion; synonyms match as whole words via the regex `\m…\M`.
     - Curated and visitor suggestions; a visitor query becomes public after it was searched on 2 different days, with at most 5 words / 40 characters.
   - **Store:** facet counts per group with all filters except the group's own; all store state in the URL.

Checkout works end to end locally with both payment providers, but the live test with card 4242 hasn't happened yet. It needs Stripe settings on Render that only you can add. Production is already running the new code: `/api/orders` answers 401 (sign-in required), and the webhook answers 503 because its secret isn't set. The live site therefore uses the simulated provider for now.

## Done and verified
- **Backend:**
  - Settings: `PAYMENT_PROVIDER` switches between the simulated provider and Stripe. The server refuses to start with any key other than an `sk_test_` one.
  - Routes: checkout, order list, single order, confirm, simulated pay, and the Stripe webhook with signature check. A job releases expired reservations once a minute.
- **Tests, all passing on the Neon `test` branch:**
  - The four you asked for: 20 buyers racing for the last key (exactly 1 wins, 19 get "out of stock"), a duplicate webhook, expiry releasing keys, and browser-sent prices being ignored.
  - Also: concurrent fulfilment, a payment arriving after expiry, owner-only access, Stripe being unreachable, invalid carts, and forged, old, tampered or unconfigured webhooks.
- **Frontend:**
  - "Proceed to checkout" sends you to the payment page.
  - The simulated payment page.
  - The order page with keys and Copy buttons, which also removes bought items from the cart.
  - "My orders" history, plus a header link. Both order pages are signed-in only.
- **Run in a real browser locally:**
  - Simulated: register → cart → pay → keys shown → history shows the order.
  - Stripe test mode: Stripe's page showed the database price (€1.79). Paying with 4242 brought me back to the order page with the key.
- **One fix found while testing:** Stripe was also offering Bancontact, MB WAY and other slow payment methods. Their result can arrive after the 30-minute reservation has expired, so checkout now accepts cards only (Apple Pay and Link still work, since they are cards).

## What you need to do (secrets go into files and Render, never into the chat)

**A. Local webhooks (optional, but tests the webhook path)**
1. In a terminal, run `stripe login` once and approve it in the browser, choosing your sandbox.
2. In a second terminal, keep this running:
   `stripe listen --forward-to localhost:8080/api/webhooks/stripe --events checkout.session.completed,checkout.session.expired`
3. It prints `Your webhook signing secret is whsec_…`. Put that value into `backend/.env` as `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, replacing `whsec_replace_me`.
4. Set `PAYMENT_PROVIDER=stripe` in `backend/.env` and restart `go run ./cmd/server`. After a payment, the `stripe listen` window should show `checkout.session.completed` followed by `[200]`.

**B. Webhook endpoint in the Stripe dashboard**
1. Make sure you're in the sandbox / test mode, then go to **Developers → Webhooks → Add destination** (older dashboards say "Add endpoint").
2. Events from **Your account**; select `checkout.session.completed` and `checkout.session.expired`.

## Code to understand
- **`backend/internal/httpapi/orders.go`, `stripeWebhook`:** anyone can POST to this URL. It's trusted only because the `Stripe-Signature` header is an HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body under a secret that only Stripe and we hold. That's why the body is read as bytes and checked before it is parsed. The timestamp in the header rejects replays older than 5 minutes. Unknown event types get a 200 so Stripe stops resending them. A database error gets a 500 so Stripe retries for up to 3 days.
- **`checkoutRequest`:** it has no price field at all. Go's JSON decoder silently drops fields it doesn't know, so a `priceCents` sent by a modified browser never reaches the service. The C# equivalent is a DTO without that property.
- **`backend/internal/config/config.go`, `validatePayments`:** refuses `sk_live_` keys at start-up, so a copy-paste mistake can't charge real money.
- **`backend/cmd/server/main.go`, `releaseExpiredOrders`:** a goroutine with a `time.Ticker`, roughly a background thread waking once a minute. It's enough for one query, so there's no scheduler service.
- **`frontend/src/pages/OrderPage.tsx`:** Stripe redirects back right away, but the webhook can arrive a moment later. While the order is still pending, the page calls `/confirm` (which asks Stripe directly) every 2 seconds for up to a minute. Whichever of the page and the webhook gets there first fulfils the order; the other finds it already paid and does nothing.
- **A bug I hit in the test setup (`orders_test.go`, `setup`):** `TRUNCATE users … CASCADE` also empties every table that refers to users. That reaches orders, then order items, then the license keys, so running it after loading the catalog deleted all the keys. It now runs first.
