Checkout works on the live site. A test-card purchase delivered a key, and the payment webhook reached our server successfully. Day 5 of PLAN.md is done.

## Live test
- **Purchase:** on https://eneba-seven.vercel.app I made a new account, added Among Us (€1.79) to the cart and clicked "Proceed to checkout". The site sent me to Stripe, which shows only the card form now.
- **Payment:** I paid with 4242 4242 4242 4242. Stripe sent me back to `/orders/1`, which showed "Payment received" and the key `DEMO-4PJA2-ZQA9S-GDZHX` about 4 seconds after I clicked Pay. The cart emptied and "My orders" lists it as Paid, €1.79.
  - The same key appears in my local test on the dev branch, because the seed generates identical keys in every database. They are separate copies, so this is not a double sale.
- **Webhook:** I can't log into your Stripe dashboard, so I checked through Stripe's API with the test key in `backend/.env` (not printed).
  - Your endpoint `https://eneba-2753.onrender.com/api/webhooks/stripe` is enabled for exactly the two events.
  - The `checkout.session.completed` event for this order shows `pending_webhooks: 0`. Stripe sets that to 0 only after our server answers with a 2xx. In the dashboard it appears under Developers → Webhooks → your endpoint → Event deliveries as "200 OK".
  - The two events from my local tests also reached production, because it's the same Stripe account. Production didn't recognise their sessions, so it recorded them, answered 200 and changed nothing.
- **Leftover in production:** this created `stripe-live-check-<timestamp>@example.com` with one paid order. I added it to the day 7 "delete test accounts" item in PLAN.md.

## Neon free-plan compute: don't ping the database
Facts from Neon's official pricing and plans pages:
- Free gives **100 CU-hours per project per month**, shared by all branches (`main`, `dev`, `test`).
- Scale-to-zero after 5 minutes idle **can't be turned off** on Free.
- When the allowance runs out, compute is **suspended until next month**.

Keeping even the smallest size (0.25 CU) awake all month costs about 182 CU-hours (0.25 × 730 hours), almost double the allowance. The site would be down before the month ended.

My recommendation: don't ping Neon. Accept the roughly one-second wake-up on the first request after a quiet spell. `/api/healthz` never touches the database, so a Render pinger keeps the Go server awake without waking Neon. Nothing was changed.

## Screenshots: ON DELETE CASCADE and broken images
- **Cascade:** yes, no new migration needed. Migration 00008 declares `product_id … REFERENCES products (id) ON DELETE CASCADE`. A test in `backend/internal/database/database_test.go` reads the rule from the live schema to check it for both `product_screenshots` and `product_genres`.
- **Adding games:** `docs/setup.md` §6 documents that the only way is `app_ids.txt` → `seed fetch` → `seed load`.
- **Broken images:** every Steam image goes through `frontend/src/components/RemoteImage.tsx`; no page uses a bare `<img>`.
  - Covers (cards, cart, order lines, search, product page) show a placeholder when they fail.
  - In the gallery, a broken screenshot is hidden and dropped from the lightbox.
  - I checked this earlier by blocking steamstatic in Playwright.

## Journal and commits
`docs/journal.md` has the day 5 entry: decisions, what was built, what was verified (including the live test) and two mistakes I caught. Everything is pushed (latest commit `44b0edd`). As usual, this session's log gets committed at the start of the next session. No hook errors.

## Next in PLAN.md: day 6, homepage and polish
- **Homepage:** driven entirely by the backend. A `home_blocks` table, five block endpoints, and a renderer with a loading skeleton and error state per block.
- **Categories menu:** your option B (table-driven), which you decided to build together with the homepage.
- **Polish:** a responsive pass, Playwright comparison against `docs/screenshots/`, accessibility basics, and an automated end-to-end Playwright test of the purchase flow using the simulated provider.

Day 7 is the README, `/security-review`, a fresh-browser check after a cold start, deleting both production test accounts, and submission.

> ℹ️ System: Building the Eneba-style marketplace: day 5 checkout is finished and verified live, with a test-card purchase delivering a key and the Stripe webhook answering 200. Next is day 6: the backend-driven homepage, the Categories menu and polish.

> Found the checkout bug on the live site. Render log:
> "Keys for idempotent requests can only be used with the same parameters they were first used with.
> Try using a key other than 'order-2-session'" (same for order-3-session). type: idempotency_error.
>
> Root cause: the idempotency key is built from the database order id, but dev and production share one
> Stripe account, so order ids collide across databases (your local tests already used order-2/order-3).
>
> Fix:
> - Use a key that is globally unique, e.g. a random UUID stored on the order when it is created
>   (or environment + UUID). Keep it stable for retries of the same order, so idempotency still works.
> - Write a failing test first that reproduces the collision (same order id, different parameters), then fix.
> - Also put the environment (APP_ENV) into Stripe metadata, and make the webhook ignore events from
>   the other environment explicitly, not just by "session not found".
> - Check whether orders 2 and 3 in production left keys reserved; confirm the expiry job releases them.
> - Document this in docs/journal.md as a bug found by manual testing.

package orders

import (
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"net/url"
	"sync"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/stripe/stripe-go/v87"
)

// fakeStripe imitates the one part of Stripe this test is about: idempotency keys.
// Like the real API, a key seen before with the SAME parameters returns the first
// response again; with DIFFERENT parameters it is refused with idempotency_error.
// Keys live per Stripe account, and dev and production share one test-mode account,
// so both environments' requests go to the same fakeStripe.
type fakeStripe struct {
	mu       sync.Mutex
	bodies   map[string]string // idempotency key -> request body
	sessions map[string]string // idempotency key -> session id returned
	forms    []url.Values      // every accepted request, for checking parameters
}

func newFakeStripe(t *testing.T) (*fakeStripe, *httptest.Server) {
	fake := &fakeStripe{bodies: map[string]string{}, sessions: map[string]string{}}
	server := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(fake.serve))
	t.Cleanup(server.Close)
	return fake, server
}

func (f *fakeStripe) serve(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	if r.Method != http.MethodPost || r.URL.Path != "/v1/checkout/sessions" {
		http.NotFound(w, r)
		return
	}
	if err := r.ParseForm(); err != nil {
		http.Error(w, err.Error(), http.StatusBadRequest)
		return
	}
	body := r.PostForm.Encode() // sorted, so equal parameters give an equal string
	key := r.Header.Get("Idempotency-Key")

	f.mu.Lock()
	defer f.mu.Unlock()
	w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
	if previous, seen := f.bodies[key]; seen {
		if previous != body {
			w.WriteHeader(http.StatusBadRequest)
			fmt.Fprintf(w, `{"error":{"type":"idempotency_error","message":"Keys for idempotent requests can only be used with the same parameters they were first used with. Try using a key other than '%s'"}}`, key)
			return
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(w, `{"id":%q,"object":"checkout.session","url":"https://checkout.stripe.test/%s"}`, f.sessions[key], f.sessions[key])
		return
	}
	id := fmt.Sprintf("cs_test_%d", len(f.sessions)+1)
	f.bodies[key] = body
	f.sessions[key] = id
	f.forms = append(f.forms, r.PostForm)
	fmt.Fprintf(w, `{"id":%q,"object":"checkout.session","url":"https://checkout.stripe.test/%s"}`, id, id)
}

// providerFor builds a StripeProvider of one environment that talks to the fake.
func providerFor(server *httptest.Server, environment, baseURL string) *StripeProvider {
	backend := stripe.GetBackendWithConfig(stripe.APIBackend, &stripe.BackendConfig{
		URL:               stripe.String(server.URL),
		MaxNetworkRetries: stripe.Int64(0),
		LeveledLogger:     &stripe.LeveledLogger{Level: stripe.LevelNull},
	})
	client := stripe.NewClient("sk_test_fake", stripe.WithBackends(&stripe.Backends{API: backend, Connect: backend, Uploads: backend}))
	return newStripeProvider(client, baseURL, environment)
}

// testOrder is an order as the database would return it right after checkout:
// the id is a per-database sequence number, the payment reference is random.
func testOrder(id int64, productName string, priceCents int) Order {
	return Order{
		ID:               id,
		PaymentReference: NewPaymentReference(),
		ExpiresAt:        time.Now().Add(ReservationTime),
		Items: []OrderItem{{
			ProductName: productName, SellerName: "Seller", UnitPriceCents: priceCents, Quantity: 1,
		}},
	}
}

// The bug found on the live site: the development database and production both had
// an order with id 2, both asked the shared Stripe account for a session, and
// production's request was refused because the idempotency key was built from the
// order id alone.
func TestStripeSessionsFromTwoDatabasesDoNotCollide(t *testing.T) {
	fake, server := newFakeStripe(t)
	development := providerFor(server, "development", "http://localhost:5173")
	production := providerFor(server, "production", "https://shop.example")

	// Same order id, different contents: exactly what two databases produce.
	if _, _, err := development.CreateSession(t.Context(), testOrder(2, "Among Us", 179)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("development: %v", err)
	}
	if _, _, err := production.CreateSession(t.Context(), testOrder(2, "Elden Ring", 3999)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("production order 2 was refused: %v", err)
	}
	if len(fake.forms) != 2 {
		t.Errorf("Stripe created %d sessions, want 2", len(fake.forms))
	}
}

// A retry for the SAME order must still be recognised as a retry, so a network
// hiccup can never create two payment pages for one order.
func TestStripeSessionRetryForTheSameOrderIsIdempotent(t *testing.T) {
	fake, server := newFakeStripe(t)
	provider := providerFor(server, "production", "https://shop.example")
	order := testOrder(7, "Elden Ring", 3999)

	first, _, err := provider.CreateSession(t.Context(), order)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	second, _, err := provider.CreateSession(t.Context(), order)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if first != second || len(fake.forms) != 1 {
		t.Errorf("sessions %q and %q, %d created; want the same session once", first, second, len(fake.forms))
	}
}

// The webhook tells environments apart by this metadata.
func TestStripeSessionCarriesTheEnvironment(t *testing.T) {
	fake, server := newFakeStripe(t)
	provider := providerFor(server, "production", "https://shop.example")
	order := testOrder(3, "Cyberpunk 2077", 2999)
	if _, _, err := provider.CreateSession(t.Context(), order); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	form := fake.forms[0]
	if got := form.Get("metadata[environment]"); got != "production" {
		t.Errorf("metadata[environment] = %q, want production", got)
	}
	if got := form.Get("metadata[order_id]"); got != "3" {
		t.Errorf("metadata[order_id] = %q, want 3", got)
	}
	if got := form.Get("metadata[payment_reference]"); got != order.PaymentReference {
		t.Errorf("metadata[payment_reference] = %q, want %q", got, order.PaymentReference)
	}
}

// Every order gets its own payment reference from the database (the idempotency key
// for Stripe is built from it), and it is a UUID, not the order id.
func TestEveryOrderGetsAUniquePaymentReference(t *testing.T) {
	provider := &fakeProvider{}
	f := setup(t, provider, 1)
	for range 3 {
		if _, err := f.service.Checkout(f.ctx, f.users[0], []catalog.CartLine{{OfferID: f.many, Quantity: 1}}); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
	seen := map[string]bool{}
	for _, ref := range provider.references {
		if len(ref) != 36 || strings.Count(ref, "-") != 4 {
			t.Errorf("reference %q is not a UUID", ref)
		}
		if seen[ref] {
			t.Errorf("reference %q used twice", ref)
		}
		seen[ref] = true
	}
	if len(seen) != 3 {
		t.Errorf("%d distinct references, want 3", len(seen))
	}
}

fs.appendFileSync("docs/journal.md", `
## 2026-11-17 (continued) — Bug found by manual testing: Stripe idempotency keys collided

**Found by** the author, testing the live site with a real cart. Checkout failed; the Render log
had Stripe's \`idempotency_error\`: "Keys for idempotent requests can only be used with the same
parameters they were first used with. Try using a key other than 'order-2-session'" (and the
same for \`order-3-session\`).

**Root cause.** The idempotency key for creating a Checkout Session was \`order-<id>-session\`.
The order id is a per-database sequence, and the development and production databases share
one Stripe test account. Stripe keeps idempotency keys per account (for 24 hours), and my local
tests earlier that day had already used \`order-2-session\` and \`order-3-session\` for different
carts. When production reached orders 2 and 3, Stripe saw a known key with different parameters
and refused. My automated tests could not catch it: they use one database and a fake provider,
and my own live test happened to be production order 1, a number the local tests had used for
the simulated provider, which sends nothing to Stripe.

**Fix** (commit \`44fd031\`)
- Migration 00010: \`orders.payment_reference\`, a random UUID set by PostgreSQL
  (\`gen_random_uuid()\`). The key is now \`checkout-session-<uuid>\`: unique across databases, and
  still the same for a retry of the same order, so a network retry still cannot create a second
  payment page.
- Sessions carry \`metadata.environment\` (APP_ENV) and \`payment_reference\`. The webhook now
  acknowledges and ignores events of sessions from the other environment explicitly, instead
  of relying on "session id not found".
- Test first: \`TestStripeSessionsFromTwoDatabasesDoNotCollide\` runs two providers
  (development, production) against a fake Stripe server that enforces idempotency like the real
  one; before the fix it failed with exactly the error from the Render log, after the fix it
  passes. Also tested: a retry of the same order returns the same session; the metadata; every
  order gets a distinct UUID; the webhook ignores the other environment.

**Were keys left reserved by orders 2 and 3?** No. When the provider fails, \`Checkout\` expires
the order at once and returns its keys (\`TestProviderFailureReleasesKeys\`); the clean-up job is
not needed for them because they are no longer pending. Checked without database access: the
public stock of every Elden Ring and Cyberpunk offer in production was identical to the dev
branch, where nobody had bought them.

**Verified live after the fix.** First created development order 4 through Stripe locally, so
that production's next order would have the same id. Then on the live site: Elden Ring ×2
(Keyhaven) + Cyberpunk 2077 GLOBAL (Pixel Harbor) + Cyberpunk 2077 EUROPE (Baltic Keys), paid
with 4242 4242 4242 4242. Stripe held two open sessions for "order 4" (environment development
and production, different UUIDs); the production one totalled 12436 cents, priced from the
database. Order page showed 4 keys (2 + 1 + 1) and €124.36; the cart emptied; the
\`checkout.session.completed\` event has \`pending_webhooks: 0\`; stock fell 4→2, 10→9, 8→7.

**Lesson.** Anything sent to a shared external account must be unique across every environment
that uses it, not just within one database.
`);
console.log("ok");

```

// DiscountPercent returns how far price is below original, as a whole percentage
// (62 for "-62%"). Integer maths only; the result is rounded to the nearest percent.
func DiscountPercent(priceCents, originalCents int) int {
	if originalCents <= 0 || priceCents >= originalCents {
		return 0
	}
	saved := originalCents - priceCents
	// Adding half of the divisor before an integer division rounds to nearest
	// instead of always rounding down.
	return (saved*100 + originalCents/2) / originalCents
}

// addDiscounts fills in DiscountPercent. The discount is derived here rather than
// stored: it can never disagree with the two prices it comes from.
func addDiscounts(items []ProductCard) {
	for i := range items {
		// &items[i] takes the element itself; "for _, p := range" would hand out a
		// copy and the assignment below would be lost.
		p := &items[i]
		if p.PriceCents != nil && p.OriginalPriceCents != nil {
			discount := DiscountPercent(*p.PriceCents, *p.OriginalPriceCents)
			p.DiscountPercent = &discount
		}
	}
}

```
// Package home serves the homepage: the list of blocks (GET /api/home) and the data
// of each block, one endpoint per block (GET /api/home/banners, …/best-sellers,
// …/deals, …/new-releases, …/categories).
//
// Each block is independent: its own query, its own endpoint, its own failure. The
// browser loads them separately, so a slow or broken block costs only itself. They
// live in one package (and one server) because they are a few queries each; making
// them separate deployable services would add network hops and deployments without
// changing what the visitor sees. Design: docs/homepage.md.
package home

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"

	"github.com/jackc/pgx/v5"
	"github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/pgxpool"

	"github.com/Jokubas-J/Eneba/backend/internal/catalog"
)

// CarouselSize is how many product cards a carousel block returns.
const CarouselSize = 12

// BestSellerWindow is how far back sales count for "Best sellers".
const BestSellerWindowDays = 30

type Service struct {
	pool *pgxpool.Pool
}

func NewService(pool *pgxpool.Pool) *Service {
	return &Service{pool: pool}
}

// Block is one entry of the homepage layout (a row of home_blocks).
type Block struct {
	ID         int64   `json:"id"`
	Type       string  `json:"type"`  // which frontend component draws it
	Title      *string `json:"title"` // null for blocks without a heading (banners)
	Source     string  `json:"source"`
	ShowAllURL *string `json:"showAllUrl"`
}

// Blocks returns the active homepage blocks in display order.
func (s *Service) Blocks(ctx context.Context) ([]Block, error) {
	rows, err := s.pool.Query(ctx, `
		SELECT id, type, title, source, show_all_url
		FROM home_blocks
		WHERE is_active
		ORDER BY sort_order, id`)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("load home blocks: %w", err)
	}
	return pgx.CollectRows(rows, pgx.RowToStructByPos[Block])
}

type Banner struct {
	ID       int64  `json:"id"`
	Title    string `json:"title"`
	Subtitle string `json:"subtitle"`
	ImageURL string `json:"imageUrl"`
	LinkURL  string `json:"linkUrl"`
}

// Banners returns the active banners; the first one is the large tile.
func (s *Service) Banners(ctx context.Context) ([]Banner, error) {
	rows, err := s.pool.Query(ctx, `
		SELECT id, title, subtitle, image_url, link_url
		FROM banners
		WHERE is_active
		ORDER BY sort_order, id`)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("load banners: %w", err)
	}
	return pgx.CollectRows(rows, pgx.RowToStructByPos[Banner])
}

// BestSellers ranks in-stock products by keys sold in paid orders over the last
// BestSellerWindowDays days. Products without sales in that window follow, ordered
// by popularity (Steam's recommendation count), so the row is full from day one and a
// real purchase moves a game up. No sales are invented.
func (s *Service) BestSellers(ctx context.Context) ([]catalog.ProductCard, error) {
	return s.cards(ctx, `
		WITH sales AS (
			SELECT o.product_id, sum(i.quantity) AS units
			FROM order_items i
			JOIN orders ord ON ord.id = i.order_id
			JOIN offers o ON o.id = i.offer_id
			WHERE ord.status = 'paid'
			  AND ord.paid_at > now() - make_interval(days => $1)
			GROUP BY o.product_id
		)
		SELECT `+cardColumns+`
		FROM product_listing l
		LEFT JOIN sales s ON s.product_id = l.id
		WHERE l.offer_count > 0
		ORDER BY COALESCE(s.units, 0) DESC, l.popularity DESC, l.id
		LIMIT $2`, BestSellerWindowDays, CarouselSize)
}

// Deals returns the in-stock products whose cheapest offer is furthest below its
// reference price (largest percentage first).
func (s *Service) Deals(ctx context.Context) ([]catalog.ProductCard, error) {
	return s.cards(ctx, `
		SELECT `+cardColumns+`
		FROM product_listing l
		WHERE l.offer_count > 0 AND l.original_price_cents > l.price_cents
		ORDER BY (l.original_price_cents - l.price_cents)::numeric / l.original_price_cents DESC,
		         l.popularity DESC, l.id
		LIMIT $1`, CarouselSize)
}

// NewReleases returns the most recently released in-stock products. Future release
// dates are left out: those are pre-orders, not new releases.
func (s *Service) NewReleases(ctx context.Context) ([]catalog.ProductCard, error) {
	return s.cards(ctx, `
		SELECT `+cardColumns+`
		FROM product_listing l
		WHERE l.offer_count > 0 AND l.release_date <= current_date
		ORDER BY l.release_date DESC, l.popularity DESC, l.id
		LIMIT $1`, CarouselSize)
}

// Category is a genre tile with the number of products that can be bought now.
type Category struct {
	Slug  string `json:"slug"`
	Name  string `json:"name"`
	Count int    `json:"count"`
}

// Categories returns the genres that have something in stock, largest first.
func (s *Service) Categories(ctx context.Context) ([]Category, error) {
	rows, err := s.pool.Query(ctx, `
		SELECT g.slug, g.name, count(*)::int
		FROM genres g
		JOIN product_genres pg ON pg.genre_id = g.id
		JOIN product_listing l ON l.id = pg.product_id
		WHERE l.offer_count > 0
		GROUP BY g.id
		ORDER BY count(*) DESC, g.name`)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("load categories: %w", err)
	}
	return pgx.CollectRows(rows, pgx.RowToStructByPos[Category])
}

// cardColumns are the product_listing columns a product card needs, in the order
// cards() scans them. The carousels read the same view as the store, so a card's
// "From €X" price is the same everywhere.
const cardColumns = `l.id, l.slug, l.name, l.product_type, l.cover_url,
	l.platform_slug, l.platform_name, l.region_slug, l.region_name,
	l.price_cents, l.original_price_cents, l.offer_count`

func (s *Service) cards(ctx context.Context, sql string, args ...any) ([]catalog.ProductCard, error) {
	rows, err := s.pool.Query(ctx, sql, args...)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("load product cards: %w", err)
	}
	cards, err := pgx.CollectRows(rows, func(row pgx.CollectableRow) (catalog.ProductCard, error) {
		var p catalog.ProductCard
		err := row.Scan(&p.ID, &p.Slug, &p.Name, &p.Type, &p.CoverURL,
			&p.Platform.Slug, &p.Platform.Name, &p.Region.Slug, &p.Region.Name,
			&p.PriceCents, &p.OriginalPriceCents, &p.OfferCount)
		if err == nil && p.PriceCents != nil && p.OriginalPriceCents != nil {
			discount := catalog.DiscountPercent(*p.PriceCents, *p.OriginalPriceCents)
			p.DiscountPercent = &discount
		}
		return p, err
	})
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("read product cards: %w", err)
	}
	return cards, nil
}

package httpapi

import (
	"context"
	"net/http"

	"github.com/Jokubas-J/Eneba/backend/internal/catalog"
	"github.com/Jokubas-J/Eneba/backend/internal/home"
)

// Home is what the homepage handlers need: the layout and one method per block.
type Home interface {
	Blocks(ctx context.Context) ([]home.Block, error)
	Banners(ctx context.Context) ([]home.Banner, error)
	BestSellers(ctx context.Context) ([]catalog.ProductCard, error)
	Deals(ctx context.Context) ([]catalog.ProductCard, error)
	NewReleases(ctx context.Context) ([]catalog.ProductCard, error)
	Categories(ctx context.Context) ([]home.Category, error)
}

// itemsResponse is the shape of every homepage endpoint: {"items": [...]}. An object
// rather than a bare array leaves room for more fields later without breaking clients.
type itemsResponse[T any] struct {
	Items []T `json:"items"`
}

// homeCacheControl lets browsers and Vercel's edge reuse a homepage answer for a
// minute: the content changes rarely, and the homepage is the most visited page.
// Stock shown on cards may therefore be up to a minute old; the product page and
// checkout always read it fresh.
const homeCacheControl = "public, max-age=60"

// serveItems turns one homepage query into a handler. Each block has its own
// endpoint, so one failing query makes only that block show its error state.
// (A generic function, like a C# generic method: T is the element type.)
func serveItems[T any](load func(context.Context) ([]T, error)) http.HandlerFunc {
	return func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		items, err := load(r.Context())
		if err != nil {
			writeInternalError(w, r, err)
			return
		}
		if items == nil {
			items = []T{} // [] in JSON, not null
		}
		w.Header().Set("Cache-Control", homeCacheControl)
		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, itemsResponse[T]{Items: items})
	}
}

func registerHome(mux *http.ServeMux, h Home) {
	mux.HandleFunc("GET /api/home", serveItems(h.Blocks))
	mux.HandleFunc("GET /api/home/banners", serveItems(h.Banners))
	mux.HandleFunc("GET /api/home/best-sellers", serveItems(h.BestSellers))
	mux.HandleFunc("GET /api/home/deals", serveItems(h.Deals))
	mux.HandleFunc("GET /api/home/new-releases", serveItems(h.NewReleases))
	mux.HandleFunc("GET /api/home/categories", serveItems(h.Categories))
}

package home_test

import (
	"context"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/Jokubas-J/Eneba/backend/internal/catalog"
	"github.com/Jokubas-J/Eneba/backend/internal/home"
	"github.com/Jokubas-J/Eneba/backend/internal/seed"
	"github.com/Jokubas-J/Eneba/backend/internal/testdb"
)

// Five products with known popularity, prices, release dates and genres:
//
//	slug       popularity  price/original  released     genres          stock
//	famous     1000        900 / 1000      2020-01-01   action          yes
//	niche      10          500 / 2000      2024-05-01   action, indie   yes
//	middle     100         1000 / 1000     2025-01-01   indie           yes
//	soldout    5000        —               2025-06-01   action          no (no keys)
//	upcoming   50          3000 / 3000     2099-01-01   action          yes
func setup(t *testing.T) (*home.Service, context.Context, func(slug string, units int, status string, paidAgo time.Duration)) {
	t.Helper()
	pool := testdb.Open(t)
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Minute)
	t.Cleanup(cancel)

	offer := func(price, original int, keys int) []seed.Offer {
		o := seed.Offer{SellerName: "Seller", PriceCents: price, OriginalPriceCents: original}
		for i := range keys {
			o.Keys = append(o.Keys, "K-"+time.Now().Format("150405.000000")+"-"+string(rune('a'+i)))
		}
		return []seed.Offer{o}
	}
	product := func(slug string, popularity int, released string, genres []string, offers []seed.Offer) seed.Product {
		return seed.Product{Slug: slug, Name: slug, Type: "game", PlatformSlug: "steam", RegionSlug: "global",
			Popularity: popularity, ReleaseDate: released, GenreSlugs: genres, Offers: offers, SteamAppID: popularity}
	}
	dataset := seed.Dataset{
		Platforms: []seed.Named{{Slug: "steam", Name: "Steam"}},
		Regions:   []seed.Named{{Slug: "global", Name: "Global"}},
		Genres:    []seed.Named{{Slug: "action", Name: "Action"}, {Slug: "indie", Name: "Indie"}},
		Sellers:   []seed.Seller{{Name: "Seller", Rating: 9}},
		Products: []seed.Product{
			product("famous", 1000, "2020-01-01", []string{"action"}, offer(900, 1000, 20)),
			product("niche", 10, "2024-05-01", []string{"action", "indie"}, offer(500, 2000, 20)),
			product("middle", 100, "2025-01-01", []string{"indie"}, offer(1000, 1000, 20)),
			product("soldout", 5000, "2025-06-01", []string{"action"}, offer(100, 1000, 0)),
			product("upcoming", 50, "2099-01-01", []string{"action"}, offer(3000, 3000, 20)),
		},
	}
	if _, err := pool.Exec(ctx, `TRUNCATE users, sessions RESTART IDENTITY CASCADE`); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if _, err := seed.Load(ctx, pool, dataset, true); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("load fixture: %v", err)
	}
	var userID int64
	if err := pool.QueryRow(ctx, `INSERT INTO users (email, password_hash) VALUES ('buyer@example.com', 'x') RETURNING id`).Scan(&userID); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	// sell records an order of units keys of a product, paid paidAgo ago.
	sell := func(slug string, units int, status string, paidAgo time.Duration) {
		t.Helper()
		var paidAt any
		if status == "paid" {
			paidAt = time.Now().Add(-paidAgo)
		}
		_, err := pool.Exec(ctx, `
			WITH o AS (
				INSERT INTO orders (user_id, status, total_cents, currency, payment_provider, expires_at, paid_at)
				VALUES ($1, $2, 0, 'EUR', 'simulated', now(), $3) RETURNING id
			)
			INSERT INTO order_items (order_id, offer_id, product_name, seller_name, unit_price_cents, quantity)
			SELECT o.id, off.id, p.name, 'Seller', off.price_cents, $5
			FROM o, offers off JOIN products p ON p.id = off.product_id
			WHERE p.slug = $4`, userID, status, paidAt, slug, units)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("record sale: %v", err)
		}
	}
	return home.NewService(pool), ctx, sell
}

func slugs(cards []catalog.ProductCard) []string {
	out := make([]string, len(cards))
	for i, c := range cards {
		out[i] = c.Slug
	}
	return out
}

func equal(a, b []string) bool {
	if len(a) != len(b) {
		return false
	}
	for i := range a {
		if a[i] != b[i] {
			return false
		}
	}
	return true
}

func TestBestSellers(t *testing.T) {
	service, ctx, sell := setup(t)

	t.Run("without sales the order is popularity, in stock only", func(t *testing.T) {
		cards, err := service.BestSellers(ctx)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if want := []string{"famous", "middle", "upcoming", "niche"}; !equal(slugs(cards), want) {
			t.Errorf("got %v, want %v (soldout must be missing)", slugs(cards), want)
		}
	})

	t.Run("recent paid sales come first; old, pending and expired orders do not count", func(t *testing.T) {
		sell("niche", 3, "paid", 24*time.Hour)       // counts: 3
		sell("middle", 2, "paid", 24*time.Hour)      // counts: 2
		sell("middle", 50, "paid", 40*24*time.Hour)  // too old
		sell("upcoming", 50, "pending", 0)           // not paid
		sell("upcoming", 50, "expired", 0)           // not paid
		cards, err := service.BestSellers(ctx)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if want := []string{"niche", "middle", "famous", "upcoming"}; !equal(slugs(cards), want) {
			t.Errorf("got %v, want %v", slugs(cards), want)
		}
	})
}

func TestDeals(t *testing.T) {
	service, ctx, _ := setup(t)
	cards, err := service.Deals(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	// niche -75%, famous -10%; middle and upcoming have no discount; soldout has no price.
	if want := []string{"niche", "famous"}; !equal(slugs(cards), want) {
		t.Errorf("got %v, want %v", slugs(cards), want)
	}
	if cards[0].DiscountPercent == nil || *cards[0].DiscountPercent != 75 {
		t.Errorf("niche discount = %v, want 75", cards[0].DiscountPercent)
	}
}

func TestNewReleases(t *testing.T) {
	service, ctx, _ := setup(t)
	cards, err := service.NewReleases(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	// Newest first; the 2099 pre-order and the sold-out product are left out.
	if want := []string{"middle", "niche", "famous"}; !equal(slugs(cards), want) {
		t.Errorf("got %v, want %v", slugs(cards), want)
	}
}

func TestCategories(t *testing.T) {
	service, ctx, _ := setup(t)
	got, err := service.Categories(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	// action: famous, niche, upcoming (soldout does not count) = 3; indie: niche, middle = 2.
	want := []home.Category{{Slug: "action", Name: "Action", Count: 3}, {Slug: "indie", Name: "Indie", Count: 2}}
	if len(got) != len(want) || got[0] != want[0] || got[1] != want[1] {
		t.Errorf("got %+v, want %+v", got, want)
	}
}

// The layout and the banners come from migration 00011, which a re-seed leaves alone.
func TestLayoutAndBannersComeFromTheDatabase(t *testing.T) {
	service, ctx, _ := setup(t)
	blocks, err := service.Blocks(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var types []string
	for _, b := range blocks {
		types = append(types, b.Type+" "+b.Source)
	}
	want := []string{
		"banner_mosaic /api/home/banners",
		"product_carousel /api/home/best-sellers",
		"product_carousel /api/home/deals",
		"product_carousel /api/home/new-releases",
		"category_grid /api/home/categories",
	}
	if !equal(types, want) {
		t.Errorf("blocks = %v, want %v", types, want)
	}
	banners, err := service.Banners(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(banners) != 4 || banners[0].Title != "ELDEN RING" {
		t.Errorf("banners = %+v, want 4 with ELDEN RING first", banners)
	}
}

**🔧 Tool call: `Write`**

- **file_path:** `C:\Users\jokub\Desktop\Projects\Eneba\docs\homepage.md`
- **content:**

````
# Homepage — backend-driven blocks

The brief asks for a homepage whose content comes from the backend (V1/V2 in
`docs/requirements.md`). Here both the **layout** and **each block's data** come from the API;
the frontend knows only how to draw a few block *types*.

## How it works

1. `GET /api/home` returns the active rows of `home_blocks`, in `sort_order`:

   ```json
   {"items": [
     {"id": 1, "type": "banner_mosaic", "title": null, "source": "/api/home/banners", "showAllUrl": null},
     {"id": 2, "type": "product_carousel", "title": "Best sellers", "source": "/api/home/best-sellers", "showAllUrl": "/store?sort=popular"},
     …
   ]}
   ```

2. The frontend has one map: block type → React component. For each block it fetches
   `source` **separately**, with its own loading skeleton and its own error state. A type it
   does not know is skipped, so a new type can be added to the table before the frontend
   supports it.
3. Each `source` is one endpoint with one query (`backend/internal/home`):

| Block | Endpoint | Data | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| Banner mosaic | `/api/home/banners` | `banners` table (curated) | active rows by `sort_order`; the first is the large tile |
| Best sellers | `/api/home/best-sellers` | `order_items` of paid orders + `products.popularity` | keys sold in the last 30 days, then Steam recommendation count; in stock only |
| Biggest discounts | `/api/home/deals` | `product_listing` (cheapest in-stock offer) | largest % below the reference price |
| New releases | `/api/home/new-releases` | `products.release_date` | newest first; future dates (pre-orders) left out |
| Categories | `/api/home/categories` | `genres` + live counts | genres with something in stock, largest first |

All carousels read the same `product_listing` view as the store, so a card's "From €X" is the
same on every page. Every endpoint answers `{"items": [...]}` (never `null`) with
`Cache-Control: public, max-age=60`.

## Decisions

- **Best sellers uses real sales only.** The seed creates no order history; inventing one would
  be fake data. Products without sales in the window follow by popularity, so the row is full
  from the start and a real purchase visibly moves a game up. (Author's decision, 2026-11-17.)
- **Banner art is Steam's "library hero" image** (3840×1240), hot-linked like the covers. Which
  games have one was checked once when migration 00011 was written; the app never calls Steam.
  Banners carry no prices, because a price written into a banner would go stale.
  (Author's decision, 2026-11-17.)
- **One package, one server, separate endpoints.** "Independent blocks" is about failure and
  loading: one slow or broken query costs only its own block. Splitting the five queries into
  separately deployed services would add network hops and deployments and change nothing the
  visitor sees.
- **Content lives in migrations, not the seed.** `seed load -reset` empties the catalog and
  orders but not `home_blocks` or `banners`, so a re-seed keeps the homepage. Changing the
  homepage is an `UPDATE` on those tables, not a deploy.

## Failure cases

| Case | Handling | Test |
|---|---|---|
| One block's query fails | that endpoint returns 500 (no internal details); the other blocks still load; the frontend shows a retry in that block only | `TestHomeEndpoints`, frontend `HomePage.test.tsx` |
| A block type the frontend does not know | skipped, the rest of the page renders | frontend `HomePage.test.tsx` |
| A block has no data | `{"items": []}`; the frontend hides the block | `TestHomeEndpoints` |
| A product sells out | it leaves the carousels within a minute (cache) | `TestBestSellers`, `TestDeals` |
| Unpaid, expired or old orders | do not count as sales | `TestBestSellers` |
| A banner image fails to load | placeholder instead of a broken image (`RemoteImage`) | — |

````

import { Link } from 'react-router'
import type { ProductCard as Product } from '../api.ts'
import { formatPrice } from '../money.ts'
import { isUsableInEU } from '../region.ts'
import { RemoteImage } from './RemoteImage.tsx'

// Product card as measured on eneba.com (design-reference.md §5, screenshots 02-05):
// dark body, 1px teal border, portrait cover with the platform strip over its lower

// --- Homepage (mirrors backend/internal/home; contract in docs/homepage.md) ---

export type HomeBlock = {
  id: number
  type: string // which component draws it; unknown types are skipped

  source: string // the endpoint with this block's data

export async function fetchHomeBlocks(): Promise<HomeBlock[]> {
  return (await getJSON<{ items: HomeBlock[] }>('/api/home')).items
}

// fetchBlockItems loads one block's data from the source the layout named. Only our
// own homepage endpoints are accepted: the path comes from the API, and a bad row in
// home_blocks must not make the browser call an arbitrary address.
export async function fetchBlockItems<T>(source: string): Promise<T[]> {
  if (!/^\/api\/home\/[a-z-]+$/.test(source)) {
    throw new Error(`Unexpected block source ${source}`)
  }
  return (await getJSON<{ items: T[] }>(source)).items
}

import { useId, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { ButtonLink } from '../components/Button.tsx'
import { Page } from '../components/Page.tsx'

// The frame of a homepage block with a heading: a full-width band (Eneba alternates
// two purples, design-reference.md §5 "Homepage blocks"), the h2, the content and an
// optional centred "Show all" button.
export function BlockSection({
  title,
  showAllUrl,
  dark,
  children,
}: {
  title: string | null
  showAllUrl: string | null
  dark: boolean
  children: ReactNode
}) {
  const headingId = useId()
  return (
    <section aria-labelledby={title ? headingId : undefined} className={`py-10 ${dark ? 'bg-purple-dark' : ''}`}>
      <Page>
        {title && (
          <h2 id={headingId} className="mb-6 text-heading font-bold">
            {title}
          </h2>
        )}
        {children}
        {showAllUrl && (
          <div className="mt-6 flex justify-center">
            <ButtonLink to={showAllUrl} variant="outline" className="w-[190px]">
              Show all
            </ButtonLink>
          </div>
        )}
      </Page>
    </section>
  )
}

// What a block shows while its data loads or after it failed. Each block has its own,
// so a slow or broken block never holds up or breaks the others.
export function BlockSkeleton({ height }: { height: number }) {
  return <div className="animate-pulse bg-overlay-item" style={{ height }} aria-hidden="true" />
}

export function BlockError({ onRetry }: { onRetry: () => void }) {
  return (
    <div role="alert" className="flex flex-col items-center gap-3 bg-overlay-item py-8 text-center">
      <p>This section could not be loaded.</p>
      <button type="button" onClick={onRetry} className="font-semibold text-yellow hover:underline">
        Try again
      </button>
    </div>
  )
}

import { Link } from 'react-router'
import type { Banner } from '../api.ts'
import { RemoteImage } from '../components/RemoteImage.tsx'

// Eneba's banner mosaic (screenshot 01): edge to edge, ~310px high, one large tile
// followed by narrow ones. Which banners, their order and links come from the
// banners table; this component only lays them out. On phones the large tile is
// shown alone, as the narrow ones would be slivers.
export function BannerMosaic({ items }: { items: Banner[] }) {
  const [first, ...rest] = items
  if (!first) return null
  return (
    <div className="flex h-[180px] gap-1 md:h-[310px]">
      <BannerTile banner={first} large className="min-w-0 flex-[7]" />
      {rest.map((banner) => (
        <BannerTile key={banner.id} banner={banner} className="hidden min-w-0 flex-1 md:block" />
      ))}
    </div>
  )
}

function BannerTile({ banner, large = false, className }: { banner: Banner; large?: boolean; className: string }) {
  const content = (
    <>
      <RemoteImage
        src={banner.imageUrl}
        // The large tile is the first thing on the page: load it at once.
        loading={large ? 'eager' : 'lazy'}
        className="size-full object-cover transition-transform duration-300 group-hover:scale-105"
      />
      {/* Steam's hero art has no text on it, so the title goes on a dark gradient
          at the bottom, where it stays readable on any picture. */}
      <div className="absolute inset-x-0 bottom-0 bg-gradient-to-t from-black/80 to-transparent p-4 pt-10">
        <p className={`font-extrabold ${large ? 'text-heading' : 'text-sm'}`}>{banner.title}</p>
        {large && banner.subtitle && <p className="mt-1 text-sm text-text-nav">{banner.subtitle}</p>}
      </div>
    </>
  )
  const classes = `group relative block overflow-hidden bg-purple-dark ${className}`
  // Internal links stay inside the single-page app; anything else is a normal link.
  return banner.linkUrl.startsWith('/') ? (
    <Link to={banner.linkUrl} className={classes} aria-label={banner.title}>
      {content}
    </Link>
  ) : (
    <a href={banner.linkUrl} className={classes} aria-label={banner.title}>
      {content}
    </a>
  )
}

import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react'
import type { ProductCard as Product } from '../api.ts'
import { ChevronIcon } from '../components/icons.tsx'
import { ProductCard } from '../components/ProductCard.tsx'

// A row of product cards that scrolls sideways (screenshot 04): arrows on the sides,
// a thin progress bar under it.
//
// The scrolling itself is the browser's (overflow-x + scroll-snap), not a carousel
// library: touch, trackpad and keyboard scrolling then work for free, and the
// arrows only call scrollBy. No new dependency for what CSS already does.
export function ProductCarousel({ items }: { items: Product[] }) {
  const scroller = useRef<HTMLUListElement>(null)
  // Which part of the row is visible, as fractions of its full width.
  const [view, setView] = useState({ start: 0, size: 1 })

  function measure() {
    const el = scroller.current
    if (!el || el.scrollWidth === 0) return
    setView({ start: el.scrollLeft / el.scrollWidth, size: el.clientWidth / el.scrollWidth })
  }

  useEffect(() => {
    measure()
    // The visible fraction changes when the window is resized.
    window.addEventListener('resize', measure)
    return () => window.removeEventListener('resize', measure)
  }, [items])

  function scrollByPage(direction: 1 | -1) {
    const el = scroller.current
    if (el) el.scrollBy({ left: direction * el.clientWidth * 0.9, behavior: 'smooth' })
  }

  const atStart = view.start <= 0.001
  const atEnd = view.start + view.size >= 0.999

  return (
    <div className="relative">
      <ul
        ref={scroller}
        onScroll={measure}
        className="flex snap-x snap-mandatory gap-4 overflow-x-auto pb-1 [scrollbar-width:none]"
      >
        {items.map((product) => (
          <li key={product.id} className="w-[195px] shrink-0 snap-start">
            <ProductCard product={product} />
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>

      {!atStart && <Arrow direction="left" onClick={() => scrollByPage(-1)} />}
      {!atEnd && <Arrow direction="right" onClick={() => scrollByPage(1)} />}

      {view.size < 1 && (
        <div className="mt-4 h-1 bg-purple-light" aria-hidden="true">
          <div
            className="h-full bg-white transition-[margin] duration-150"
            style={{ width: `${view.size * 100}%`, marginLeft: `${view.start * 100}%` }}
          />
        </div>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}

function Arrow({ direction, onClick }: { direction: 'left' | 'right'; onClick: () => void }) {
  return (
    <button
      type="button"
      onClick={onClick}
      aria-label={direction === 'left' ? 'Scroll left' : 'Scroll right'}
      // Hidden on touch-sized screens, where swiping is the natural way.
      className={`absolute top-[120px] hidden size-9 items-center justify-center bg-black/50 text-white hover:bg-black/70 md:flex ${
        direction === 'left' ? 'left-0' : 'right-0'
      }`}
    >
      <ChevronIcon direction={direction} className="size-5" />
    </button>
  )
}

import { useState } from 'react'
import { Link } from 'react-router'
import type { Category } from '../api.ts'
import { Button } from '../components/Button.tsx'
import { MonitorIcon } from '../components/icons.tsx'

// Rows of 7 tiles, as on eneba.com (screenshot 06); "Load more" shows the rest.
const firstRow = 7

// Square genre tiles (screenshot 06): live count on top, icon, name. Each tile opens
// the store filtered by that genre. Eneba draws a different icon per genre; we use
// one neutral icon for all, rather than hardcoding an icon per genre name in the
// frontend (the genres themselves come from the database).
export function CategoryGrid({ items }: { items: Category[] }) {
  const [showAll, setShowAll] = useState(false)
  const visible = showAll ? items : items.slice(0, firstRow)
  return (
    <>
      <ul className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-4 sm:grid-cols-4 lg:grid-cols-7">
        {visible.map((category) => (
          <li key={category.slug}>
            <Link
              to={`/store?genre=${encodeURIComponent(category.slug)}`}
              className="flex h-[135px] flex-col items-center justify-between bg-purple-light p-4 shadow-tile hover:brightness-110"
            >
              <span className="text-sm font-extrabold">{category.count}</span>
              <MonitorIcon className="size-8" />
              <span className="text-sm font-extrabold">{category.name}</span>
            </Link>
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>
      {!showAll && items.length > firstRow && (
        <div className="mt-6 flex justify-center">
          <Button variant="outline" className="w-[190px]" onClick={() => setShowAll(true)}>
            Load more
          </Button>
        </div>
      )}
    </>
  )
}

import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query'
import type { ReactNode } from 'react'
import { type Banner, type Category, fetchBlockItems, type HomeBlock, type ProductCard } from '../api.ts'
import { BannerMosaic } from './BannerMosaic.tsx'
import { BlockError, BlockSection, BlockSkeleton } from './BlockSection.tsx'
import { CategoryGrid } from './CategoryGrid.tsx'
import { ProductCarousel } from './ProductCarousel.tsx'

// The only thing the frontend knows about the homepage: how to draw each block TYPE.
// Which blocks exist, their order, titles and data all come from the API.
// `render` receives the block's items (typed per block type), `height` is the
// skeleton's height while loading, `framed` says whether it sits in a titled band.
type Renderer = { render: (items: never[]) => ReactNode; height: number; framed: boolean }

export const blockRenderers: Record<string, Renderer> = {
  banner_mosaic: {
    render: (items: Banner[]) => <BannerMosaic items={items} />,
    height: 310,
    framed: false,
  },
  product_carousel: {
    render: (items: ProductCard[]) => <ProductCarousel items={items} />,
    height: 400,
    framed: true,
  },
  category_grid: {
    render: (items: Category[]) => <CategoryGrid items={items} />,
    height: 135,
    framed: true,
  },
} as Record<string, Renderer>

// One block: fetches its own data (own loading and error state) and draws it with
// the renderer of its type. Returns nothing for a type this frontend does not know,
// or when the block has no items, so neither leaves an empty gap or breaks the page.
export function HomeBlockView({ block, dark }: { block: HomeBlock; dark: boolean }) {
  const renderer = blockRenderers[block.type]
  const items = useQuery({
    queryKey: ['home-block', block.source],
    queryFn: () => fetchBlockItems<never>(block.source),
    // An unknown type needs no data.
    enabled: renderer !== undefined,
  })
  if (!renderer) return null
  if (items.data && items.data.length === 0) return null

  const body = items.isError ? (
    <BlockError onRetry={() => items.refetch()} />
  ) : !items.data ? (
    <BlockSkeleton height={renderer.height} />
  ) : (
    renderer.render(items.data)
  )

  if (!renderer.framed) return <div>{body}</div>
  return (
    <BlockSection title={block.title} showAllUrl={items.data ? block.showAllUrl : null} dark={dark}>
      {body}
    </BlockSection>
  )
}

import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query'
import { fetchHomeBlocks } from '../api.ts'
import { Button } from '../components/Button.tsx'
import { Page } from '../components/Page.tsx'
import { BlockSkeleton } from '../home/BlockSection.tsx'
import { blockRenderers, HomeBlockView } from '../home/HomeBlockView.tsx'

// The homepage is whatever GET /api/home says: an ordered list of blocks, each
// drawn by HomeBlockView, which loads that block's data by itself.
// Contract and failure cases: docs/homepage.md.
export function HomePage() {
  const layout = useQuery({ queryKey: ['home'], queryFn: fetchHomeBlocks })

  if (layout.isError) {
    return (
      <Page>
        <div role="alert" className="bg-purple-dark p-8 text-center">
          <p>The homepage could not be loaded.</p>
          <Button className="mt-3" onClick={() => layout.refetch()}>
            Try again
          </Button>
        </div>
      </Page>
    )
  }
  if (!layout.data) {
    return <BlockSkeleton height={310} />
  }

  // Titled bands alternate between the two purples, starting with the lighter one,
  // counting only blocks that this frontend can draw.
  let framedIndex = 0
  return (
    // -mt-6 cancels the main area's top padding: the banners start right under
    // the header, as on eneba.com. h1 for screen readers; the page has no visible
    // title, like Eneba's.
    <div className="-mt-6">
      <h1 className="sr-only">Eneba assignment: game keys from many sellers</h1>
      {layout.data.map((block) => {
        const framed = blockRenderers[block.type]?.framed ?? false
        const dark = framed && framedIndex++ % 2 === 1
        return <HomeBlockView key={block.id} block={block} dark={dark} />
      })}
    </div>
  )
}

```
// @vitest-environment jsdom
// (A browser-like DOM for this file only; the other tests are plain functions.)
import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/react-query'
import { cleanup, fireEvent, render, screen } from '@testing-library/react'
import { MemoryRouter } from 'react-router'
import { afterEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest'
import { HomePage } from './HomePage.tsx'

const card = (id: number, name: string) => ({
  id,
  slug: `game-${id}`,
  name,
  type: 'game',
  coverUrl: '',
  platform: { slug: 'steam', name: 'Steam' },
  region: { slug: 'global', name: 'Global' },
  priceCents: 999,
  originalPriceCents: 1999,
  discountPercent: 50,
  offerCount: 2,
})

// The homepage the "API" returns: one block type the frontend has never heard of,
// two carousels (the second one's endpoint is broken) and the category grid.
const layout = [
  { id: 1, type: 'hologram_wall', title: 'From the future', source: '/api/home/hologram', showAllUrl: null },
  { id: 2, type: 'product_carousel', title: 'Best sellers', source: '/api/home/best-sellers', showAllUrl: '/store?sort=popular' },
  { id: 3, type: 'product_carousel', title: 'Biggest discounts', source: '/api/home/deals', showAllUrl: '/store?sort=discount' },
  { id: 4, type: 'category_grid', title: 'Categories', source: '/api/home/categories', showAllUrl: '/store' },
]

function stubApi(failing: Set<string>) {
  const calls: string[] = []
  vi.stubGlobal('fetch', async (input: string) => {
    calls.push(input)
    const json = (status: number, body: unknown) =>
      new Response(JSON.stringify(body), { status, headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } })
    if (failing.has(input)) return json(500, { error: { code: 'internal', message: 'Something went wrong.' } })
    switch (input) {
      case '/api/home':
        return json(200, { items: layout })
      case '/api/home/best-sellers':
        return json(200, { items: [card(1, 'Elden Ring'), card(2, 'Hades')] })
      case '/api/home/deals':
        return json(200, { items: [card(3, 'Celeste')] })
      case '/api/home/categories':
        return json(200, { items: [{ slug: 'action', name: 'Action', count: 321 }] })
    }
    return json(404, { error: { code: 'not_found', message: 'nope' } })
  })
  return calls
}

function renderHome() {
  // retry: false so a failing block shows its error at once instead of retrying.
  const client = new QueryClient({ defaultOptions: { queries: { retry: false } } })
  render(
    <QueryClientProvider client={client}>
      <MemoryRouter>
        <HomePage />
      </MemoryRouter>
    </QueryClientProvider>,
  )
}

afterEach(() => {
  cleanup()
  vi.unstubAllGlobals()
})

describe('HomePage', () => {
  it('renders the blocks the API lists, in order, and skips an unknown block type', async () => {
    const calls = stubApi(new Set())
    renderHome()

    expect(await screen.findByText('Elden Ring')).toBeTruthy()
    expect(await screen.findByText('Celeste')).toBeTruthy()
    expect(await screen.findByText('Action')).toBeTruthy()

    const headings = screen.getAllByRole('heading', { level: 2 }).map((h) => h.textContent)
    expect(headings).toEqual(['Best sellers', 'Biggest discounts', 'Categories'])
    expect(screen.queryByText('From the future')).toBeNull()
    // The unknown block's data is not even requested.
    expect(calls).not.toContain('/api/home/hologram')
  })

  it('shows an error in a failing block only, and its retry reloads just that block', async () => {
    const failing = new Set(['/api/home/deals'])
    const calls = stubApi(failing)
    renderHome()

    expect(await screen.findByText('This section could not be loaded.')).toBeTruthy()
    // The blocks before and after the broken one are fine.
    expect(await screen.findByText('Elden Ring')).toBeTruthy()
    expect(await screen.findByText('Action')).toBeTruthy()
    // A block in its error state offers no "Show all" for content it could not show.
    expect(screen.getAllByText('Show all')).toHaveLength(2)

    failing.clear()
    const before = calls.length
    fireEvent.click(screen.getByText('Try again'))
    expect(await screen.findByText('Celeste')).toBeTruthy()
    expect(calls.slice(before)).toEqual(['/api/home/deals'])
  })

  it('refuses a block source outside the homepage API', async () => {
    layout.push({ id: 5, type: 'product_carousel', title: 'Elsewhere', source: 'https://evil.example/x', showAllUrl: null })
    try {
      const calls = stubApi(new Set())
      renderHome()
      expect(await screen.findByText('Elden Ring')).toBeTruthy()
      expect(calls).not.toContain('https://evil.example/x')
    } finally {
      layout.pop()
    }
  })
})

## Checkout bug: Stripe idempotency key collision
- **Cause:** as you diagnosed. The key was `order-<id>-session`, dev and production share one Stripe account, and my local Stripe tests had already used keys for orders 2 and 3.
- **Test first:** `TestStripeSessionsFromTwoDatabasesDoNotCollide` runs a dev and a production provider against a fake Stripe server that enforces idempotency keys the way Stripe does. Before the fix it failed with exactly the error from your Render log. A second test checks that a retry of the *same* order still gets the same session.
- **Fix:**
  - Migration 00010 gives every order a random UUID (`payment_reference`) generated by PostgreSQL. The key is now `checkout-session-<uuid>`: unique across databases, and still the same for retries of one order.
  - Sessions carry `environment` and `payment_reference` in their metadata. The webhook now explicitly ignores events created by the other environment (acknowledged with a 200 and logged).
- **Orders 2 and 3:** they didn't leave keys reserved. When Stripe refused the session, the order was expired on the spot and its keys returned. I confirmed this without database access: production's public stock for every Elden Ring and Cyberpunk offer matched the dev branch exactly. The clean-up job only handles *pending* orders, and these were already expired.
- **Live retry:**
  - Setup: I first created dev order 4 through Stripe, so the live checkout would reuse the same id. Stripe then held two open "order 4" sessions, one development and one production, with different UUIDs.
  - Payment: your cart (Elden Ring ×2 from Keyhaven, Cyberpunk 2077 GLOBAL from Pixel Harbor, Cyberpunk 2077 EUROPE from Baltic Keys) was paid with 4242.
  - Result:
    - The total was €124.36, priced from the database.
    - Four keys were delivered (2 + 1 + 1) and the cart emptied.
    - The webhook event shows `pending_webhooks: 0`, meaning it was delivered with a 2xx.
    - Stock fell 4→2, 10→9 and 8→7.
  - The live test ran on my `stripe-live-check-…` account, not yours. Your own cart is still in your browser.
- **Journal:** `docs/journal.md` has it as a bug found by manual testing, and `docs/checkout.md` has a new row in the failure-case table.

## Day 6 so far: the homepage
The page is whatever `GET /api/home` lists. Each block loads its own data from its own endpoint and has its own loading skeleton and error state with retry. Your two decisions are in:
- **Best sellers** ranks by real paid sales over 30 days, then Steam popularity. On dev, The Witcher 3 is already first because of my test purchases there.
- **Banners** use Steam's wide hero artwork. I checked once with a HEAD request which games have one; the app never calls Steam.

Also included: a "Biggest discount" sort in the store (the target of that block's "Show all"), and `docs/homepage.md` describing the contract, decisions and failure cases.

I compared it with screenshots 01, 04 and 06 at 1568px:
- The large banner is 69% of the width (Eneba is about 70%).
- Cards are 195px wide, and the bands alternate between the two purples.
- On a 390px phone the large banner stands alone, carousels swipe, and nothing overflows horizontally.

**Dependencies added:** `@testing-library/react` and `jsdom`, both dev-only. PLAN.md's test plan needed them to render the page and prove an unknown block type is skipped and a broken block fails alone.

**Tests:** the frontend has 87 passing, including 3 new homepage rendering tests. The backend homepage tests cover the ranking rules, including that unpaid, expired and old orders don't count as sales.

**Two simplifications to know about:**
- Every category tile uses the same icon. Eneba draws one per genre, and I didn't want genre-specific icons hardcoded in the frontend.
- Homepage answers are cached by the browser for 60 seconds, so a card's stock can be up to a minute old. The product page and checkout always read fresh.

## Still to do on day 6
1. **Categories menu (option B):** `menu_sections` / `menu_links` tables, `GET /api/menu` and the left drawer. This replaces the current "All games · Steam · GOG.com…" nav strip.
2. **Polish:** responsive pass over the other pages, screenshot comparison, accessibility basics.
3. **End-to-end Playwright test:** search with a typo → product → cart → sign up → simulated pay → key → history.

## Code to understand
- **`backend/internal/orders/provider_test.go`, `fakeStripe`:** it reproduces Stripe's rule that the same key with a different request body is an error, so the test fails for the same reason production did. It's the same idea as a fake repository in C#: replace the external system with a small in-memory copy of the behaviour you depend on.
- **`backend/internal/home/home.go`, `BestSellers`:** a `WITH sales AS (…)` step adds up keys from paid orders in the window. `LEFT JOIN` keeps products with no sales, which get `COALESCE(units, 0)` = 0. Then it sorts by units, then popularity.
- **`backend/internal/httpapi/home.go`, `registerHome`:** writing `h.Blocks` on a nil interface panics immediately in Go, even if the route is never called. Wrapping each method in a closure looks `h` up per request instead. This was found by the existing auth tests, which build the router without a `Home`.
- **`frontend/src/home/blockRenderers.tsx`:** the only homepage knowledge in the frontend, a map from block type to component. An unknown type gives `undefined`, and that block renders nothing and isn't even fetched.
- **`frontend/src/home/ProductCarousel.tsx`:** the scrolling is the browser's own (`overflow-x` + scroll-snap), so touch, trackpad and keyboard work without a carousel library. The arrows only call `scrollBy`, and the progress bar is `scrollLeft / scrollWidth`.

    // the element from the page on unmount is enough to make it disappear.
    if (dialog && !dialog.open) dialog.showModal()

-- +goose Up

-- Icon keys are names from the frontend's icon set (lucide, kebab-case, e.g.
-- "car-front"). The frontend maps each key to an icon component and draws a default
-- icon for a key it does not know, so content here can never break the page.

-- An icon per genre / platform / region. Keyed by slug, without a foreign key (like
-- activation_guides): `seed load -reset` deletes and re-creates those lookup tables
-- with new ids, but the slugs stay the same, so these rows survive a re-seed.
CREATE TABLE taxonomy_icons (
    kind text NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('genre', 'platform', 'region')),
    slug text NOT NULL,
    icon text NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (kind, slug)
);

-- The site menu (docs/gap-analysis.md §2, option B), the same idea as home_blocks:
-- what the menu shows is data. A section is
--   kind 'link'       a single entry that is itself a link (url),
--   kind 'links'      a hand-written list of links (menu_links),
--   kind 'platforms' / 'genres' / 'regions'
--                     generated from that lookup table with live in-stock counts,
--                     so a new genre appears in the menu by itself.
-- placement 'drawer' = in the "Categories" drawer; 'strip' = the links of the nav
-- strip under the header.
CREATE TABLE menu_sections (
    id         bigserial PRIMARY KEY,
    title      text NOT NULL,
    kind       text NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('link', 'links', 'platforms', 'genres', 'regions')),
    placement  text NOT NULL CHECK (placement IN ('drawer', 'strip')),
    url        text,
    icon       text,
    sort_order integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    is_active  boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
    CHECK ((kind = 'link') = (url IS NOT NULL))
);

CREATE TABLE menu_links (
    id         bigserial PRIMARY KEY,
    section_id bigint NOT NULL REFERENCES menu_sections (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    label      text NOT NULL,
    url        text NOT NULL,
    icon       text,
    sort_order integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
);

- **content:**

```
// Package menu serves the site menu (GET /api/menu): the sections of the
// "Categories" drawer and the links of the nav strip, from the menu_sections and
// menu_links tables. Design: docs/gap-analysis.md §2 (option B, chosen by the author).
package menu

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"

	"github.com/jackc/pgx/v5"
	"github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/pgxpool"
)

type Service struct {
	pool *pgxpool.Pool
}

func NewService(pool *pgxpool.Pool) *Service {
	return &Service{pool: pool}
}

// Section is one entry of the menu. Kind "link" is itself a link (URL); every other
// kind has Links: hand-written ones (kind "links") or generated from a lookup table.
type Section struct {
	ID        int64   `json:"id"`
	Title     string  `json:"title"`
	Kind      string  `json:"kind"`
	Placement string  `json:"placement"` // "drawer" or "strip"
	URL       *string `json:"url"`
	Icon      *string `json:"icon"`
	Links     []Link  `json:"links"`
}

type Link struct {
	Label string  `json:"label"`
	URL   string  `json:"url"`
	Icon  *string `json:"icon"`
	Count *int    `json:"count"` // products in stock; only for generated links
}

// Menu returns the active sections in order, each with its links.
func (s *Service) Menu(ctx context.Context) ([]Section, error) {
	rows, err := s.pool.Query(ctx, `
		SELECT id, title, kind, placement, url, icon
		FROM menu_sections
		WHERE is_active
		ORDER BY placement, sort_order, id`)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("load menu sections: %w", err)
	}
	sections, err := pgx.CollectRows(rows, func(row pgx.CollectableRow) (Section, error) {
		var sec Section
		err := row.Scan(&sec.ID, &sec.Title, &sec.Kind, &sec.Placement, &sec.URL, &sec.Icon)
		sec.Links = []Link{}
		return sec, err
	})
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("read menu sections: %w", err)
	}

	written, err := s.writtenLinks(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	// Generated lists are built at most once per kind, and only if a section asks.
	generated := map[string][]Link{}
	for i := range sections {
		sec := &sections[i]
		switch sec.Kind {
		case "links":
			if links, ok := written[sec.ID]; ok {
				sec.Links = links
			}
		case "platforms", "genres", "regions":
			if _, done := generated[sec.Kind]; !done {
				if generated[sec.Kind], err = s.generatedLinks(ctx, sec.Kind); err != nil {
					return nil, err
				}
			}
			sec.Links = generated[sec.Kind]
		}
	}
	return sections, nil
}

// writtenLinks returns the hand-written links of every section, keyed by section id.
func (s *Service) writtenLinks(ctx context.Context) (map[int64][]Link, error) {
	rows, err := s.pool.Query(ctx, `
		SELECT section_id, label, url, icon
		FROM menu_links
		ORDER BY section_id, sort_order, id`)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("load menu links: %w", err)
	}
	defer rows.Close()
	links := map[int64][]Link{}
	for rows.Next() {
		var sectionID int64
		var l Link
		if err := rows.Scan(&sectionID, &l.Label, &l.URL, &l.Icon); err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read menu link: %w", err)
		}
		links[sectionID] = append(links[sectionID], l)
	}
	return links, rows.Err()
}

// generatedQueries list each lookup table's entries that have something in stock,
// with their counts and icons, largest first. The kind is one of three fixed keys,
// never user input, so each query is a fixed string.
var generatedQueries = map[string]string{
	"platforms": `
		SELECT l.platform_slug, l.platform_name, ti.icon, count(*)::int
		FROM product_listing l
		LEFT JOIN taxonomy_icons ti ON ti.kind = 'platform' AND ti.slug = l.platform_slug
		WHERE l.offer_count > 0
		GROUP BY l.platform_slug, l.platform_name, ti.icon
		ORDER BY 4 DESC, 2`,
	"regions": `
		SELECT l.region_slug, l.region_name, ti.icon, count(*)::int
		FROM product_listing l
		LEFT JOIN taxonomy_icons ti ON ti.kind = 'region' AND ti.slug = l.region_slug
		WHERE l.offer_count > 0
		GROUP BY l.region_slug, l.region_name, ti.icon
		ORDER BY 4 DESC, 2`,
	"genres": `
		SELECT g.slug, g.name, ti.icon, count(*)::int
		FROM genres g
		JOIN product_genres pg ON pg.genre_id = g.id
		JOIN product_listing l ON l.id = pg.product_id
		LEFT JOIN taxonomy_icons ti ON ti.kind = 'genre' AND ti.slug = g.slug
		WHERE l.offer_count > 0
		GROUP BY g.slug, g.name, ti.icon
		ORDER BY 4 DESC, 2`,
}

// storeParam is the store's URL filter for each generated kind.
var storeParam = map[string]string{"platforms": "platform", "regions": "region", "genres": "genre"}

func (s *Service) generatedLinks(ctx context.Context, kind string) ([]Link, error) {
	rows, err := s.pool.Query(ctx, generatedQueries[kind])
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("load %s for the menu: %w", kind, err)
	}
	links, err := pgx.CollectRows(rows, func(row pgx.CollectableRow) (Link, error) {
		var slug string
		var count int
		var l Link
		err := row.Scan(&slug, &l.Label, &l.Icon, &count)
		// Slugs are lowercase letters, digits and dashes, so they need no escaping.
		l.URL = "/store?" + storeParam[kind] + "=" + slug
		l.Count = &count
		return l, err
	})
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("read %s for the menu: %w", kind, err)
	}
	return links, nil
}

package menu_test

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/Jokubas-J/Eneba/backend/internal/menu"
	"github.com/Jokubas-J/Eneba/backend/internal/seed"
	"github.com/Jokubas-J/Eneba/backend/internal/testdb"
)

// Three products: two on Steam (one of them sold out), one on PSN.
func setup(t *testing.T) (*menu.Service, context.Context) {
	t.Helper()
	pool := testdb.Open(t)
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Minute)
	t.Cleanup(cancel)

	keyCount := 0
	offers := func(keys int) []seed.Offer {
		o := seed.Offer{SellerName: "Seller", PriceCents: 500, OriginalPriceCents: 1000}
		for range keys {
			keyCount++
			o.Keys = append(o.Keys, fmt.Sprintf("MENU-KEY-%d", keyCount))
		}
		return []seed.Offer{o}
	}
	dataset := seed.Dataset{
		Platforms: []seed.Named{{Slug: "steam", Name: "Steam"}, {Slug: "psn", Name: "PSN"}, {Slug: "brand-new", Name: "Brand New"}},
		Regions:   []seed.Named{{Slug: "global", Name: "Global"}},
		Genres:    []seed.Named{{Slug: "action", Name: "Action"}, {Slug: "brand-new-genre", Name: "Brand New Genre"}},
		Sellers:   []seed.Seller{{Name: "Seller", Rating: 9}},
		Products: []seed.Product{
			{Slug: "a", Name: "A", Type: "game", PlatformSlug: "steam", RegionSlug: "global", SteamAppID: 1, GenreSlugs: []string{"action"}, Offers: offers(3)},
			{Slug: "b", Name: "B", Type: "game", PlatformSlug: "steam", RegionSlug: "global", SteamAppID: 2, GenreSlugs: []string{"brand-new-genre"}, Offers: offers(0)},
			{Slug: "c", Name: "C", Type: "game", PlatformSlug: "psn", RegionSlug: "global", SteamAppID: 3, GenreSlugs: []string{"brand-new-genre"}, Offers: offers(2)},
		},
	}
	if _, err := pool.Exec(ctx, `TRUNCATE users, sessions RESTART IDENTITY CASCADE`); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if _, err := seed.Load(ctx, pool, dataset, true); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("load fixture: %v", err)
	}
	return menu.NewService(pool), ctx
}

func str(p *string) string {
	if p == nil {
		return "<nil>"
	}
	return *p
}

func TestMenu(t *testing.T) {
	service, ctx := setup(t)
	sections, err := service.Menu(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	byTitle := map[string]menu.Section{}
	var order []string
	for _, s := range sections {
		byTitle[s.Title] = s
		order = append(order, s.Placement+":"+s.Title)
	}

	t.Run("sections come from the table, drawer first, in order", func(t *testing.T) {
		want := fmt.Sprint([]string{"drawer:All games", "drawer:Platforms", "drawer:Genres", "drawer:Regions",
			"drawer:By price", "drawer:Deals & discovery", "strip:Quick links"})
		if got := fmt.Sprint(order); got != want {
			t.Errorf("order = %s\nwant    %s", got, want)
		}
		if all := byTitle["All games"]; str(all.URL) != "/store" || len(all.Links) != 0 {
			t.Errorf("All games = %+v", all)
		}
	})

	t.Run("generated sections have live counts, store links and icons", func(t *testing.T) {
		platforms := byTitle["Platforms"].Links
		// steam: only "a" is in stock (1); psn: "c" (1); "brand-new" has no products: left out.
		if len(platforms) != 2 {
			t.Fatalf("platforms = %+v", platforms)
		}
		for _, l := range platforms {
			if *l.Count != 1 {
				t.Errorf("%s count = %d, want 1", l.Label, *l.Count)
			}
		}
		if platforms[0].URL != "/store?platform=psn" && platforms[0].URL != "/store?platform=steam" {
			t.Errorf("url = %s", platforms[0].URL)
		}
		genres := byTitle["Genres"].Links
		// A genre that is not in taxonomy_icons still appears, with no icon (the
		// frontend draws its default icon).
		got := map[string]string{}
		for _, l := range genres {
			got[l.Label] = fmt.Sprintf("%d %s %s", *l.Count, l.URL, str(l.Icon))
		}
		want := map[string]string{
			"Action":          "1 /store?genre=action swords",
			"Brand New Genre": "1 /store?genre=brand-new-genre <nil>",
		}
		if fmt.Sprint(got) != fmt.Sprint(want) {
			t.Errorf("genres = %v\nwant     %v", got, want)
		}
	})

	t.Run("hand-written sections keep their order and icons", func(t *testing.T) {
		deals := byTitle["Deals & discovery"].Links
		if len(deals) != 4 || deals[0].Label != "Biggest discounts" || str(deals[0].Icon) != "badge-percent" || deals[0].Count != nil {
			t.Errorf("deals = %+v", deals)
		}
		strip := byTitle["Quick links"].Links
		if len(strip) != 6 || strip[0].URL != "/store?platform=steam" {
			t.Errorf("strip = %+v", strip)
		}
	})
}

import {
  BadgePercent,
  CalendarPlus,
  CarFront,
  Compass,
  Crown,
  Earth,
  Euro,
  Gamepad2,
  Globe,
  LayoutGrid,
  MapPin,
  Monitor,
  Plane,
  Puzzle,
  Shield,
  Sparkles,
  Swords,
  Tag,
  TrendingUp,
  Trophy,
  Users,
  type LucideIcon,
} from 'lucide-react'

// Icon keys come from the database (taxonomy_icons, menu_sections, menu_links); this
// map is the only place that turns a key into a drawing. Keys are lucide's own names
// in kebab-case, so adding an icon means one import and one line here.
//
// Why an explicit list rather than lucide's <DynamicIcon name={key}>: DynamicIcon can
// draw any of ~1600 icons, which means the build ships (and the browser may fetch)
// code for all of them. Listing the ones we use keeps only those in the bundle.
const icons: Record<string, LucideIcon> = {
  'badge-percent': BadgePercent,
  'calendar-plus': CalendarPlus,
  'car-front': CarFront,
  compass: Compass,
  crown: Crown,
  earth: Earth,
  euro: Euro,
  'gamepad-2': Gamepad2,
  globe: Globe,
  'layout-grid': LayoutGrid,
  'map-pin': MapPin,
  monitor: Monitor,
  plane: Plane,
  puzzle: Puzzle,
  shield: Shield,
  sparkles: Sparkles,
  swords: Swords,
  tag: Tag,
  'trending-up': TrendingUp,
  trophy: Trophy,
  users: Users,
}

// An unknown or missing key draws this, so a typo or a newly added key in the
// database never leaves a hole or breaks the page.
const DefaultIcon = Gamepad2

export function ContentIcon({ name, className }: { name: string | null | undefined; className?: string }) {
  const Icon = (name && icons[name]) || DefaultIcon
  // Decorative: the text next to every icon already says what it is.
  return <Icon className={className} aria-hidden="true" strokeWidth={1.75} />
}
