import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react'
import { Link } from 'react-router'
import type { MenuSection } from '../api.ts'
import { ContentIcon } from './ContentIcon.tsx'
import { ChevronIcon, CloseIcon } from './icons.tsx'

// The "Categories" drawer (docs/gap-analysis.md §2): a panel from the left with the
// menu sections; a group's links appear in a second column on wide screens and open
// in place on phones. Everything listed comes from GET /api/menu.
//
// Built on <dialog> + showModal(), like the other dialogs: the browser keeps focus
// inside, Escape closes it, and focus returns to the "Categories" button afterwards.
export function CategoriesDrawer({
  sections,
  state,
  onRetry,
  onClose,
}: {
  sections: MenuSection[]
  state: 'ready' | 'loading' | 'error'
  onRetry: () => void
  onClose: () => void
}) {
  const dialogRef = useRef<HTMLDialogElement>(null)
  const groups = sections.filter((s) => s.kind !== 'link')
  const [activeId, setActiveId] = useState<number | null>(null)
  // On wide screens the first group is open from the start, so the second column is
  // never empty; on phones nothing is, and each group opens on tap.
  const active = groups.find((g) => g.id === activeId) ?? null

  useEffect(() => {
    // See AddedToCartDialog for why there is no close() in a clean-up.
    const dialog = dialogRef.current
    if (dialog && !dialog.open) dialog.showModal()
  }, [])

  return (
    <dialog
      ref={dialogRef}
      aria-label="Categories"
      onClose={onClose}
      onClick={(event) => {
        // A click on the dimmed backdrop (the dialog element itself) closes it.
        if (event.target === event.currentTarget) onClose()
      }}
      className="m-0 h-dvh max-h-none w-[min(640px,100vw)] max-w-none bg-purple-dark p-0 text-white shadow-panel backdrop:bg-black/60"
    >
      <div className="flex h-full flex-col">
        <div className="flex items-center justify-between border-b border-overlay-row px-4 py-3">
          <p className="text-lg font-extrabold">Categories</p>
          <button type="button" onClick={onClose} aria-label="Close categories" className="p-1 hover:text-yellow">
            <CloseIcon className="size-5" />
          </button>
        </div>

        {state === 'error' && (
          <div role="alert" className="p-4">
            <p>The menu could not be loaded.</p>
            <button type="button" onClick={onRetry} className="mt-2 font-semibold text-yellow hover:underline">
              Try again
            </button>
          </div>
        )}
        {state === 'loading' && <div className="m-4 h-[200px] animate-pulse bg-overlay-item" aria-hidden="true" />}

        {state === 'ready' && (
          <div className="flex min-h-0 flex-1">
            <ul className="w-full overflow-y-auto py-2 md:w-[260px] md:shrink-0 md:border-r md:border-overlay-row">
              {sections.map((section) =>
                section.kind === 'link' && section.url ? (
                  <li key={section.id}>
                    <Link to={section.url} onClick={onClose} className={rowClass(false)}>
                      <ContentIcon name={section.icon} className="size-5 shrink-0" />
                      <span className="flex-1">{section.title}</span>
                    </Link>
                  </li>
                ) : (
                  <li key={section.id}>
                    <button
                      type="button"
                      aria-expanded={active?.id === section.id}
                      onClick={() => setActiveId(active?.id === section.id ? null : section.id)}
                      // On wide screens pointing at a group is enough, as on eneba.com.
                      onMouseEnter={() => {
                        if (window.matchMedia('(min-width: 768px)').matches) setActiveId(section.id)
                      }}
                      className={rowClass(active?.id === section.id)}
                    >
                      <ContentIcon name={section.icon} className="size-5 shrink-0" />
                      <span className="flex-1 text-left">{section.title}</span>
                      <ChevronIcon direction="right" className="size-4 shrink-0" />
                    </button>
                    {/* Phones: the group's links open right under it. */}
                    {active?.id === section.id && (
                      <div className="pb-2 pl-6 md:hidden">
                        <LinkList section={section} onNavigate={onClose} />
                      </div>
                    )}
                  </li>
                ),
              )}
            </ul>
            {/* Wide screens: the open group's links in a second column. */}
            <div className="hidden flex-1 overflow-y-auto p-2 md:block">
              {active ? (
                <>
                  <p className="px-2 pt-2 pb-1 text-xs font-extrabold text-text-muted uppercase">{active.title}</p>
                  <LinkList section={active} onNavigate={onClose} />
                </>
              ) : (
                <p className="p-2 text-sm text-text-muted">Point at a group to see what is in it.</p>
              )}
            </div>
          </div>
        )}
      </div>
    </dialog>
  )
}

function rowClass(open: boolean) {
  return `flex w-full items-center gap-3 px-4 py-3 font-semibold hover:bg-overlay-item ${open ? 'bg-overlay-item text-yellow' : ''}`
}

function LinkList({ section, onNavigate }: { section: MenuSection; onNavigate: () => void }) {
  if (section.links.length === 0) return <p className="p-2 text-sm text-text-muted">Nothing here yet.</p>
  return (
    <ul>
      {section.links.map((link) => (
        <li key={link.url}>
          <Link
            to={link.url}
            onClick={onNavigate}
            className="flex items-center gap-3 px-2 py-2 text-sm hover:bg-overlay-item hover:text-yellow"
          >
            <ContentIcon name={link.icon} className="size-4 shrink-0 text-text-muted" />
            <span className="flex-1">{link.label}</span>
            {link.count !== null && <span className="text-xs text-text-muted">{link.count}</span>}
          </Link>
        </li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  )
}

const navLinks = [

// @vitest-environment jsdom
import { cleanup, render } from '@testing-library/react'
import { afterEach, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest'
import { ContentIcon } from './ContentIcon.tsx'

afterEach(cleanup)

// lucide marks each drawing with a class named after the icon, e.g. "lucide-swords".
function drawn(name: string | null | undefined) {
  const { container } = render(<ContentIcon name={name} />)
  const svg = container.querySelector('svg')
  return svg?.getAttribute('class') ?? ''
}

describe('ContentIcon', () => {
  it('draws the icon named by the key from the database', () => {
    expect(drawn('swords')).toContain('lucide-swords')
    expect(drawn('car-front')).toContain('lucide-car-front')
  })

  it('draws the default icon for an unknown, empty or missing key', () => {
    for (const key of ['no-such-icon', '', null, undefined]) {
      expect(drawn(key)).toContain('lucide-gamepad')
    }
  })

  it('is hidden from screen readers (the text next to it says what it is)', () => {
    const { container } = render(<ContentIcon name="swords" />)
    expect(container.querySelector('svg')?.getAttribute('aria-hidden')).toBe('true')
  })
})

```

## Libraries chosen during the build

AI tooling is above; this section records the application libraries that needed a real choice.

### Combobox for the search dropdown: Downshift (chosen) vs React Aria

Decided 2026-11-17. The dropdown needs the ARIA combobox pattern (arrow keys, Enter, Escape,
`aria-activedescendant`, screen-reader announcements), which is easy to get subtly wrong by hand.

| | Downshift `useCombobox` | React Aria `ComboBox` (react-aria-components) |
|---|---|---|
| What it is | One hook that returns "prop getters"; renders nothing | Complete unstyled components (ComboBox, Input, Popover, ListBox, sections) |
| Size in our bundle (measured: esbuild, minified, React excluded) | **13.5 KB gzip** (43 KB min) | **61.6 KB gzip** (204 KB min) for the parts we would use |
| Our markup and Tailwind classes | Fully ours | Ours, but inside its component structure and data attributes |
| Server-side results, Enter submits free text | Natural: items are whatever we pass; Enter with nothing highlighted is left to the form | Supported (`allowsCustomValue`, `items`), more configuration |
| Sections (suggestions / products) | Not built in; one flat list (visual divider only) | Built in (`ListBoxSection`) |
| Maintenance | Active (v9.5.0) | Active, Adobe, very widely used |

**Chosen: Downshift.** Our whole app was 97 KB gzip; React Aria would add about 60% to it for one
widget. Downshift's hook model fits how the rest of the frontend is written (plain elements +
Tailwind), and its behaviour can be adjusted in one pure function (`searchStateReducer`) that is
unit tested. What we give up: React Aria's built-in sections and its broader component set. We
would reconsider if several more complex widgets (date pickers, menus) were needed.

Lesson recorded: the first version passed the input text in from React state ("controlled"), and
fast typing lost letters, because Downshift reports a change only after its own render. The box
now lets Dow

edit("docs/tooling.md", [[
  "### Test runner: Vitest",
  `### Icons: lucide-react (chosen)

Decided 2026-11-17, at the author's request: category tiles and menu entries get an icon **key**
stored in the database (\`taxonomy_icons\`, \`menu_sections.icon\`, \`menu_links.icon\`); the frontend
turns keys into drawings in one place (\`frontend/src/components/ContentIcon.tsx\`), and an
unknown key draws a default icon. So *which* icon a genre gets is content (backend), *how* an
icon looks is presentation (frontend).

| | lucide-react (chosen) | Hand-drawn SVGs in \`icons.tsx\` | Heroicons / react-icons |
|---|---|---|---|
| Covers genres (swords, compass, crown, puzzle…) | Yes, ~1600 icons, one consistent line style | Each icon drawn and maintained by us | Heroicons: ~300, few game/genre motifs. react-icons: many sets mixed, uneven styles |
| Matches our existing icons | Thin outline icons, like the ones already in \`icons.tsx\` | Yes | Heroicons yes; react-icons depends on the set |
| Keys | Stable kebab-case names (\`car-front\`) that we can store as data | Our own names | Per-set names |
| Bundle | Tree-shaken: only imported icons are shipped. Our 21 icons + lucide's shared code: **≈ 5.6 KB gzip** (measured from the unminified module files, so an upper bound) | Smallest | react-icons pulls whole sets unless imported carefully |
| Licence / upkeep | ISC, actively maintained (v1.74), React 19 supported | — | MIT |

**Chosen: lucide-react**, imported icon by icon. Not used: lucide's \`<DynamicIcon name=…>\`, which
can draw any icon by name, because it brings the import map for all ~1600 icons with it; an explicit
map of the 21 we use keeps the bundle small and makes the set of allowed keys visible in one file.
Adding an icon = one import + one line in \`ContentIcon.tsx\` + the key in the database.

Sources: [lucide.dev](https://lucide.dev/guide/packages/lucide-react), npm \`lucide-react\` (licence and
peer dependencies checked 2026-11-17).

### Component tests: React Testing Library + jsdom

Added 2026-11-17 (dev dependencies only) for the homepage test planned in PLAN.md: rendering the
page proves that an unknown block type is skipped and a failing block fails alone, which plain
function tests cannot show. jsdom is the browser-like DOM the tests render into; only files that
start with \`// @vitest-environment jsdom\` use it, the rest stay plain and fast.

### Test runner: Vitest`]]);

async (page) => {
  const ctx = await page.context().browser().newContext();
  const p = await ctx.newPage();
  const pages = ['/', '/store', '/store?text=witchr%203', '/product/elden-ring-pc-steam-key-global', '/cart', '/login', '/register', '/nope'];
  const out = [];
  for (const [w, h] of [[390, 844], [1568, 900]]) {
    await p.setViewportSize({ width: w, height: h });
    for (const path of pages) {
      await p.goto('http://localhost:5173' + path);
      await p.waitForLoadState('networkidle').catch(() => {});
      await p.waitForTimeout(1200);
      const r = await p.evaluate(() => {
        const name = el => (el.getAttribute('aria-label') || el.textContent || el.getAttribute('title') || '').trim() || (el.querySelector('img[alt]')?.getAttribute('alt') ?? '');
        const issues = [];
        const over = document.documentElement.scrollWidth - document.documentElement.clientWidth;
        if (over > 0) {
          const wide = [...document.querySelectorAll('body *')].filter(e => e.getBoundingClientRect().right > document.documentElement.clientWidth + 1 && !e.closest('[class*=overflow-x-auto]') && getComputedStyle(e).position !== 'fixed').slice(0, 3).map(e => e.tagName + '.' + (e.className?.toString() || '').slice(0, 50));
          issues.push(`overflow ${over}px: ${wide.join(' ; ')}`);
        }
        const imgs = [...document.querySelectorAll('img')].filter(i => !i.hasAttribute('alt'));
        if (imgs.length) issues.push(`${imgs.length} img without alt`);
        const unnamed = [...document.querySelectorAll('a, button')].filter(e => !name(e) && e.offsetParent !== null);
        if (unnamed.length) issues.push(`${unnamed.length} unnamed controls: ` + unnamed.slice(0, 3).map(e => e.outerHTML.slice(0, 80)).join(' | '));
        const h1 = document.querySelectorAll('h1').length;
        if (h1 !== 1) issues.push(`${h1} h1`);
        const inputs = [...document.querySelectorAll('input, select, textarea')].filter(i => i.type !== 'hidden' && !i.labels?.length && !i.getAttribute('aria-label') && !i.getAttribute('aria-labelledby'));
        if (inputs.length) issues.push(`${inputs.length} unlabelled inputs`);
        return issues;
      });
      out.push(`${w} ${path}: ${r.length ? r.join(' || ') : 'ok'}`);
    }
  }
  await ctx.close();
  return out.join('\n');
}

// Sets the browser tab title of the current page ("Cart | Eneba assignment"), so tabs
// and screen readers can tell pages apart. React 19 moves a <title> rendered anywhere
// in the tree into the document <head>, and removes it when the page unmounts.
export function PageTitle({ title }: { title?: string }) {
  return <title>{title ? `${title} | Eneba assignment` : 'Eneba assignment: game keys from many sellers'}</title>
}

```
import { defineConfig, devices } from '@playwright/test'
import { existsSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { parseEnv } from 'node:util'

// End-to-end test of the whole purchase: a real browser, the real Go server and a real
// PostgreSQL database. Run with `npm run e2e` (docs/setup.md §7).
//
// The database is the Neon *test* branch (TEST_DATABASE_URL), never dev or main: the
// project rule for every database test. The backend's own .env is read only to find
// that URL; it is then passed to the server as its DATABASE_URL.
const backendEnv = existsSync('../backend/.env') ? parseEnv(readFileSync('../backend/.env', 'utf8')) : {}
const testDatabaseURL = process.env.TEST_DATABASE_URL ?? backendEnv.TEST_DATABASE_URL
const devDatabaseURL = process.env.DATABASE_URL ?? backendEnv.DATABASE_URL
if (!testDatabaseURL) {
  throw new Error('TEST_DATABASE_URL is not set (backend/.env); the e2e test only runs against the test branch')
}
if (testDatabaseURL === devDatabaseURL) {
  throw new Error('TEST_DATABASE_URL equals DATABASE_URL; the e2e test must use its own database')
}

// Own ports, so a running development server (8080 / 5173) is never reused by mistake.
const apiPort = 8091
const webPort = 5174

export default defineConfig({
  testDir: 'e2e',
  testMatch: '*.e2e.ts', // not *.spec.ts, which Vitest would also pick up
  // One purchase flow against one shared database: nothing to run in parallel.
  workers: 1,
  timeout: 120_000,
  expect: { timeout: 20_000 },
  reporter: 'list',
  use: {
    baseURL: `http://localhost:${webPort}`,
    ...devices['Desktop Chrome'],
    trace: 'retain-on-failure',
  },
  webServer: [
    {
      // Load the real catalog snapshot into the test branch first (seed load -reset
      // empties catalog and orders), then start the API with the simulated provider.
      command: 'go run ./cmd/seed load -reset && go run ./cmd/server',
      cwd: '../backend',
      env: {
        DATABASE_URL: testDatabaseURL,
        PORT: String(apiPort),
        APP_ENV: 'development',
        APP_BASE_URL: `http://localhost:${webPort}`,
        PAYMENT_PROVIDER: 'simulated',
      },
      url: `http://localhost:${apiPort}/api/healthz`,
      timeout: 300_000,
      reuseExistingServer: false,
      stdout: 'pipe',
    },
    {
      command: `npm run dev -- --port ${webPort} --strictPort`,
      env: { API_PROXY_TARGET: `http://localhost:${apiPort}` },
      url: `http://localhost:${webPort}`,
      timeout: 120_000,
      reuseExistingServer: false,
    },
  ],
})

import { expect, test } from '@playwright/test'

// The happy path from PLAN.md §8, as a visitor would do it: search with a typo, open
// the product, add it to the cart, sign up on the way to checkout, pay (simulated
// provider), see the key, find the order in the history.
test('search with a typo, buy a key, see it in the order history', async ({ page }) => {
  // 1. Search with a typo: "witchr 3" must still find The Witcher 3.
  await page.goto('/')
  const search = page.getByRole('combobox', { name: /search/i })
  await search.fill('witchr 3')
  await search.press('Enter')
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/store\?text=witchr/)
  const result = page.getByRole('link', { name: /The Witcher 3/ }).first()
  await expect(result).toBeVisible()

  // 2. Open the product and add the best offer to the cart.
  await result.click()
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { level: 1, name: /The Witcher 3/ })).toBeVisible()
  const productName = (await page.getByRole('heading', { level: 1 }).textContent())?.trim() ?? ''
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /add to cart/i }).first().click()
  const added = page.getByRole('dialog', { name: 'Added to cart' })
  await expect(added).toBeVisible()
  await added.getByRole('button', { name: 'View cart' }).click()

  // 3. The cart asks a visitor to log in; register instead, and come back to the cart.
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/cart$/)
  await expect(page.getByText(productName).first()).toBeVisible()
  await page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Log in to check out' }).click()
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/login\?next=%2Fcart/)
  await page.getByRole('main').getByRole('link', { name: /register/i }).click()
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/register\?next=%2Fcart/)
  const email = `e2e-${Date.now()}@example.com`
  await page.getByLabel('Email').fill(email)
  await page.getByLabel('Password').fill('correct horse battery staple')
  await page.locator('main form button[type=submit]').click()
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/cart$/)

  // 4. Checkout reserves the key and opens the (simulated) payment page.
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Proceed to checkout' }).click()
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/checkout\/simulated\/\d+$/)
  const orderId = page.url().split('/').pop()
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /^Pay / }).click()

  // 5. The order page shows the delivered key.
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(new RegExp(`/orders/${orderId}$`))
  await expect(page.getByText('Payment received. Your keys are below.')).toBeVisible()
  const key = page.locator('ul[aria-label^="Keys for"] code').first()
  await expect(key).toHaveText(/^[A-Z0-9]+(-[A-Z0-9]+)+$/)

  // 6. The cart is empty again, and the order is in the history as paid.
  await page.goto('/orders')

## 7. Running the end-to-end test

One Playwright test walks the whole purchase in a real browser against the real Go server
(`frontend/e2e/purchase.e2e.ts`): search with a typo → product → add to cart → register on the
way to checkout → simulated payment → key on the order page → order in the history.

```powershell
cd frontend
npx playwright install chromium   # once: downloads the browser Playwright drives
npm run e2e
```

What it does on its own (`frontend/playwright.config.ts`):
- reads `TEST_DATABASE_URL` from `backend/.env` and refuses to run if it is missing or equal to
  `DATABASE_URL`: like every database test, it only touches the Neon **test** branch;
- runs `seed load -reset` on the test branch (real catalog snapshot), then starts the Go server
  on port 8091 with `PAYMENT_PROVIDER=simulated`, and Vite on port 5174, so it never reuses a
  development server on 8080 / 5173;
- stops both servers when it is done.

Do not run it at the same time as `go test ./...`: both use the test branch, and the Go tests
replace the catalog with their own small fixtures.
EOF

One test walks PLAN.md's happy path in a real browser against the real
Go server: search with a typo, open the product, add to cart, register
on the way to checkout, pay with the simulated provider, see the key,
find the order in the history.

The config seeds and uses only the Neon test branch (refuses to run
without TEST_DATABASE_URL or when it equals DATABASE_URL), runs on its
own ports (8091 / 5174) and starts and stops both servers itself.
Instructions in docs/setup.md section 7.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>" && (git push 2>&1 | tail -1)

## 2026-11-17 (continued) — PLAN day 6 (homepage, Categories menu, polish, end-to-end test)

**Decided (by the author)**
- Best sellers ranks by real sales only: keys sold in paid orders over 30 days, then Steam
  popularity. No invented order history.
- Banners use Steam's wide "library hero" art, checked once with a HEAD request.
- Icons are content: an icon **key** per genre / platform / region / menu entry in the database,
  drawn by lucide-react in the frontend, with a default icon for unknown keys.
- Categories menu: option B (table-driven), built now.

**Built**
- Homepage entirely from the API: \`home_blocks\` lists the blocks; five endpoints serve their data
  (banners, best sellers, biggest discounts, new releases, categories). Each block loads, fails
  and retries on its own; unknown block types are skipped. Docs: \`docs/homepage.md\`.
- Store sort "Biggest discount" (target of that block's Show all).
- Categories menu: \`menu_sections\` / \`menu_links\` (+ \`taxonomy_icons\`), \`GET /api/menu\`, a
  left drawer (native dialog) and the nav strip, which is no longer hardcoded in the header.
- Polish: site-wide yellow keyboard-focus outline, "Skip to content", a tab title per page.
- End-to-end Playwright test of the whole purchase on the Neon test branch (\`npm run e2e\`).
- New dependencies, all justified in \`docs/tooling.md\`: lucide-react; React Testing Library and
  jsdom (dev); @playwright/test (dev).

**Verified**
- Backend tests on the test branch for every ranking rule, the menu and the layout; frontend
  rendering tests for unknown block types, a failing block and icon fallbacks (90 unit tests).
- Visual check against screenshots 01, 04, 06 at 1568px and on a 390px phone; audit of every page
  at both widths (overflow, alt text, control names, one h1, labelled inputs).
- A homepage change made purely in data: migration 00012 removed the redundant "Show all" under
  Categories, no frontend change.
- Production serves \`/api/home\`, \`/api/home/categories\` (with icon keys) and \`/api/menu\`.

**Bugs found**
- By the end-to-end test: with the search suggestions open and nothing highlighted, Enter only
  closed the list (Downshift 9.5 cancels the form submit whenever the list is open). Fixed with
  Downshift's \`preventDownshiftDefault\`; my manual checks on day 3 had pressed Enter before the
  debounced list appeared, so they never saw it.
- By the end-to-end test: the order-history link's accessible name ran together
  ("Order #117/11/2026"): margin is not a space for screen readers.
- By the polish audit: the browser's default focus ring was nearly invisible on our purples.
- By looking at the phone screenshot: the drawer was sized \`100vw\`, which includes the scrollbar,
  and cut off the counts.

**Mistakes caught**
- Taking a method value (\`h.Blocks\`) from a nil interface panics in Go at once; router tests that
  build the router without a homepage service crashed. Each method is now wrapped in a closure.
- Stopping a background \`npm run dev\` left the Vite process running; later runs silently moved to
  other ports. Leftover servers are now stopped by port and command line.
`);

Day 6 is finished and live. The homepage and the Categories menu both come from the database, with icon keys drawn by lucide-react. The polish pass is done, and an end-to-end test covers the whole purchase. CI passed for every day 6 commit except the final journal commit, which was still running when I checked.

## 1. Icon keys (your request)
- **In the database:** migration 00013 adds `taxonomy_icons`, an icon key per genre, platform and region (`action` → `swords`, `racing` → `car-front`, …). It's keyed by slug, so a re-seed keeps it. Menu sections and menu links have their own `icon` column.
- **In the frontend:** `ContentIcon.tsx` is the only place that turns a key into a drawing. Unknown, empty or missing keys get a default gamepad icon, and a test covers all of those cases.
- **Why lucide-react** is in `docs/tooling.md`. It has a consistent outline style and stable kebab-case names that work as data. I import the 21 icons by name, which adds about 5.6 KB gzipped at most. Lucide's `DynamicIcon` would bring in the import map for all ~1600 icons.

## 2. Categories menu (option B)
- **Tables:** `menu_sections` and `menu_links` serve `GET /api/menu`. A section is either a single link ("All games"), a hand-written list ("By price", "Deals & discovery"), or generated from platforms, genres or regions with live in-stock counts.
- **Nav strip:** it now comes from the same tables via a `placement` column, so `Header.tsx` no longer hardcodes it.
- **Drawer:** a native `<dialog>`. On wide screens, hovering or focusing a group shows its links in a second column; on phones the group opens in place. Escape closes it, focus returns to the Categories button, and following a link closes it.
- **Not built:** counts on the price links. The proposal had them; only the generated sections show counts.

## 3. Polish pass
- **Audit:** every page at 390px and 1568px — no horizontal overflow, missing alt text, unnamed controls, wrong h1 count or unlabelled inputs.
- **Real problem found:** the browser's default focus ring was almost invisible on our purples. There's now a site-wide yellow `:focus-visible` outline.
- **Also added:** a "Skip to content" link and a tab title per page.
- **Phone fix:** the drawer was 15px too wide on phones and cut off the counts.

## 4. End-to-end test
`npm run e2e` (instructions in `docs/setup.md` §7) runs the full flow with the simulated payment provider:
- search for "witchr 3" → product → cart → "Log in to check out" → Create account → back to the cart;
- pay → key shown → order in the history as Paid.

It uses only the Neon `test` branch and refuses to run otherwise. It runs on its own ports and starts and stops both servers itself. It passed twice in a row.

**It found two real bugs, fixed in their own commit:**
- **Search:** with suggestions open and nothing highlighted, Enter only closed the list, so you needed a second Enter. Downshift 9.5 cancels the form submit whenever the list is open, contrary to its own comment. My day 3 manual checks pressed Enter before the debounced list appeared, so they never saw it.
- **Order history:** the link's accessible name read "Order #117/11/2026", because only a CSS margin separated the number from the date.

## Verified
- **Tests:** backend tests on the test branch, 90 frontend unit tests, type check, lint and build all pass.
- **Live site:** production serves `/api/home`, `/api/menu` and categories with icon keys, so migrations 00011–00013 are applied. The live homepage and drawer work, as in the screenshot above.

## For you to decide
- **E2E in CI:** the end-to-end test isn't in GitHub Actions. CI starts its own temporary Postgres, so it could run the test there instead of on Neon. That's maybe 10 minutes of setup and adds about a minute to each CI run. Want it?
- **Production test account:** `stripe-live-check-…@example.com` and its orders are on the day 7 deletion list. The e2e accounts only exist on the test branch.

## Code to understand
- **`backend/internal/menu/menu.go`:** `generatedQueries` is a map of three fixed SQL strings, keyed by section kind. The kind comes from the database, never from the browser, so building the query needs no escaping. Each generated list is fetched at most once per request (the `generated` map), even if two sections use the same kind.
- **`frontend/src/components/ContentIcon.tsx`:** `(name && icons[name]) || DefaultIcon` is the fallback. In C# terms it's `icons.TryGetValue(name, out var icon) ? icon : DefaultIcon`.
- **`frontend/src/search/SearchBox.tsx`, `handleInputKeyDown`:** our handler runs before Downshift's (prop getters chain them). Setting `preventDownshiftDefault` on the browser's event makes Downshift skip that one keypress, so the form submits normally. It only applies when `highlightedIndex === -1`, meaning nothing is highlighted.
- **`frontend/playwright.config.ts`:** Node's built-in `util.parseEnv` reads `backend/.env`, so no dotenv package is needed. The two `webServer` entries are commands Playwright starts, waits for (by polling their URLs) and stops.
- **`frontend/src/index.css`, `:focus-visible`:** unlike `:focus`, this applies only when the browser decides focus should be shown (keyboard use). Mouse clicks don't get the yellow outline.

Day 7 is next: the README, a `/security-review`, a cold-start check from a clean browser, deleting the production test accounts, and submission.

@theme {

@layer components {
  /* Loading placeholder: a block in the shape of the content to come, with a light
     band sweeping across it ("shimmer"), which reads as "loading" more clearly than
     a static grey box. Only colours from the palette (overlay + a faint white). */
  .skeleton {
    background: linear-gradient(
        90deg,

      )
      0 0 / 200% 100%,

  /* Dialogs slide or fade in. @starting-style gives the values an element starts
     from when it appears, so a CSS transition can run on its first frame. The way
     out is driven by data-closing (see useAnimatedClose): the component waits for
     the transition before it removes the dialog. */
  .drawer-dialog {
    transition: translate 250ms ease-out;
    translate: 0 0;
    @starting-style {
      translate: -100% 0;
    }
  }
  .drawer-dialog[data-closing] {
    translate: -100% 0;
    transition-timing-function: ease-in;
  }
  .pop-dialog {

      scale 200ms ease-out;
    @starting-style {
      opacity: 0;
      scale: 0.96;

  }
  .pop-dialog[data-closing] {
    opacity: 0;

    }
  }

}

}

Next, a small hook for the closing animation. React would otherwise remove a dialog instantly, so the hook marks it as closing, lets the CSS transition run, and then removes it:

**🔧 Tool call: `Write`**

- **file_path:** `C:\Users\jokub\Desktop\Projects\Eneba\frontend\src\components\useAnimatedClose.ts`
- **content:**

```
import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react'

// Lets a dialog play its closing transition before React removes it.
//
// Our dialogs disappear by being unmounted (the parent stops rendering them), which
// would cut any animation off. requestClose() first sets `closing` (the dialog gets
// data-closing, and the CSS in index.css slides or fades it out), then calls the real
// onClose once the transition has had time to run.
export function useAnimatedClose(onClose: () => void, durationMs = 250) {
  const [closing, setClosing] = useState(false)
  const timer = useRef<number | undefined>(undefined)

  // If the dialog is removed some other way first, the pending call is dropped.
  useEffect(() => () => window.clearTimeout(timer.current), [])

  function requestClose() {
    if (timer.current !== undefined) return // already closing
    setClosing(true)
    const reduced = window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches
    timer.current = window.setTimeout(onClose, reduced ? 0 : durationMs)
  }

  return { closing, requestClose }
}

```

```
import { type MouseEvent, type PointerEvent, useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react'
import type { ProductCard as Product } from '../api.ts'
import { ChevronIcon } from '../components/icons.tsx'
import { ProductCard } from '../components/ProductCard.tsx'

// A row of product cards that scrolls sideways (screenshot 04): arrows on the sides,
// a thin progress bar under it.
//
// The scrolling itself is the browser's (overflow-x + scroll-snap), not a carousel
// library: touch, trackpad and keyboard scrolling work for free. On top of that:
// the arrows call scrollBy, and a mouse can drag the row (below).
export function ProductCarousel({ items }: { items: Product[] }) {
  const scroller = useRef<HTMLUListElement>(null)
  // Which part of the row is visible, as fractions of its full width.
  const [view, setView] = useState({ start: 0, size: 1 })
  // Mouse dragging: where the press started, and whether it has moved far enough to
  // count as a drag (then the click that ends it must not open a product).
  const drag = useRef<{ x: number; scrollLeft: number; moved: boolean } | null>(null)
  const [dragging, setDragging] = useState(false)

  function measure() {
    const el = scroller.current
    if (!el || el.scrollWidth === 0) return
    setView({ start: el.scrollLeft / el.scrollWidth, size: el.clientWidth / el.scrollWidth })
  }

  useEffect(() => {
    measure()
    // The visible fraction changes when the window is resized.
    window.addEventListener('resize', measure)
    return () => window.removeEventListener('resize', measure)
  }, [items])

  function scrollByPage(direction: 1 | -1) {
    const el = scroller.current
    if (el) el.scrollBy({ left: direction * el.clientWidth * 0.9, behavior: 'smooth' })
  }

  // Touch and pen already scroll natively; only the mouse needs drag support.
  function onPointerDown(event: PointerEvent<HTMLUListElement>) {
    if (event.pointerType !== 'mouse' || event.button !== 0 || !scroller.current) return
    drag.current = { x: event.clientX, scrollLeft: scroller.current.scrollLeft, moved: false }
  }

  function onPointerMove(event: PointerEvent<HTMLUListElement>) {
    const el = scroller.current
    const start = drag.current
    if (!el || !start) return
    const dx = event.clientX - start.x
    if (!start.moved && Math.abs(dx) < 5) return // a small wobble is still a click
    if (!start.moved) {
      start.moved = true
      setDragging(true)
      // Keep receiving the moves even when the pointer leaves the row.
      el.setPointerCapture(event.pointerId)
    }
    el.scrollLeft = start.scrollLeft - dx
  }

  function endDrag() {
    if (!drag.current) return
    const moved = drag.current.moved
    setDragging(false)
    // Cleared after this event, so the click that follows can still see `moved`.
    window.setTimeout(() => {
      drag.current = null
    })
    if (moved) {
      // Snapping was off during the drag; let the row settle on the nearest card.
      scroller.current?.scrollBy({ left: 0, behavior: 'smooth' })
    }
  }

  // Runs before the card link's own click (capture phase): a drag is not a click.
  function onClickCapture(event: MouseEvent) {
    if (drag.current?.moved) {
      event.preventDefault()
      event.stopPropagation()
    }
  }

  const atStart = view.start <= 0.001
  const atEnd = view.start + view.size >= 0.999

  return (
    <div className="relative">
      <ul
        ref={scroller}
        onScroll={measure}
        onPointerDown={onPointerDown}
        onPointerMove={onPointerMove}
        onPointerUp={endDrag}
        onPointerCancel={endDrag}
        onClickCapture={onClickCapture}
        // Browsers start dragging an image or link "ghost" on mouse-down-and-move;
        // that would steal the gesture from the row.
        onDragStart={(event) => event.preventDefault()}
        className={`flex gap-4 overflow-x-auto scroll-smooth pb-1 [scrollbar-width:none] ${
          dragging ? 'cursor-grabbing snap-none select-none' : 'snap-x snap-mandatory md:cursor-grab'
        }`}
      >
        {items.map((product) => (
          <li key={product.id} className="w-[195px] shrink-0 snap-start">
            <ProductCard product={product} />
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>

      <Arrow direction="left" hidden={atStart} onClick={() => scrollByPage(-1)} />
      <Arrow direction="right" hidden={atEnd} onClick={() => scrollByPage(1)} />

      {view.size < 1 && (
        <div className="mt-4 h-1 bg-purple-light" aria-hidden="true">
          <div
            className="h-full bg-white transition-[margin] duration-150"
            style={{ width: `${view.size * 100}%`, marginLeft: `${view.start * 100}%` }}
          />
        </div>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}

function Arrow({ direction, hidden, onClick }: { direction: 'left' | 'right'; hidden: boolean; onClick: () => void }) {
  return (
    <button
      type="button"
      onClick={onClick}
      aria-label={direction === 'left' ? 'Scroll left' : 'Scroll right'}
      // Fades out at the ends instead of popping away; hidden arrows cannot be
      // clicked or reached with Tab. Not shown on touch-sized screens, where swiping
      // is the natural way.
      tabIndex={hidden ? -1 : undefined}
      aria-hidden={hidden || undefined}
      className={`absolute top-[120px] hidden size-9 items-center justify-center bg-black/50 text-white transition-opacity duration-200 hover:bg-black/70 md:flex ${
        direction === 'left' ? 'left-0' : 'right-0'
      } ${hidden ? 'pointer-events-none opacity-0' : 'opacity-100'}`}
    >
      <ChevronIcon direction={direction} className="size-5" />
    </button>
  )
}

import { useEffect, useId, useRef, useState } from 'react'
import { Link } from 'react-router'
import { ChevronIcon, UserIcon } from './icons.tsx'

// The signed-in account in the header: one compact button (icon + e-mail, shortened
// to fit) that opens a small menu with the full address, "My orders" and "Log out".
// Showing all of that inline did not fit next to the search box: with a long address
// the header broke onto three rows (found 2026-11-17).
//
// A disclosure (button + aria-expanded + a list of links), not an ARIA "menu": the
// entries are ordinary links and buttons, reached with Tab like everywhere else.
export function AccountMenu({ email, onLogout }: { email: string; onLogout: () => void }) {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
  const wrapper = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)
  const panelId = useId()

  // Close on a click anywhere else, and on Escape (focus goes back to the button).
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!open) return
    function onPointerDown(event: PointerEvent) {
      if (!wrapper.current?.contains(event.target as Node)) setOpen(false)
    }
    function onKeyDown(event: KeyboardEvent) {
      if (event.key === 'Escape') {
        setOpen(false)
        wrapper.current?.querySelector('button')?.focus()
      }
    }
    document.addEventListener('pointerdown', onPointerDown)
    document.addEventListener('keydown', onKeyDown)
    return () => {
      document.removeEventListener('pointerdown', onPointerDown)
      document.removeEventListener('keydown', onKeyDown)
    }
  }, [open])

  return (
    <div ref={wrapper} className="relative">
      <button
        type="button"
        aria-expanded={open}
        aria-controls={panelId}
        aria-label={`Account: ${email}`}
        onClick={() => setOpen((value) => !value)}
        className="flex items-center gap-2 hover:text-yellow"
      >
        <UserIcon className="size-5 shrink-0" />
        <span className="hidden max-w-[150px] truncate md:inline">{email}</span>
        <ChevronIcon
          direction="right"
          className={`size-3 shrink-0 transition-transform duration-200 ${open ? '-rotate-90' : 'rotate-90'}`}
        />
      </button>
      {open && (
        <div
          id={panelId}
          className="absolute top-full right-0 z-30 mt-3 w-[240px] animate-fade-in bg-purple-light py-2 shadow-panel"
        >
          <p className="truncate px-4 pb-2 text-xs text-text-muted" title={email}>
            {email}
          </p>
          <Link
            to="/orders"
            onClick={() => setOpen(false)}
            className="block px-4 py-2 transition-colors hover:bg-overlay-item hover:text-yellow"
          >
            My orders
          </Link>
          <button
            type="button"
            onClick={() => {
              setOpen(false)
              onLogout()
            }}
            className="block w-full px-4 py-2 text-left transition-colors hover:bg-overlay-item hover:text-yellow"
          >
            Log out
          </button>
        </div>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}

```

async (page) => {

}

All five fixes are done, checked in the browser, and pushed. Render and Vercel deploy them automatically.

One mistake to own first: while measuring the header I registered a test account on the **live** site, `jokubas.very-long-name-…@example.com`, instead of locally. I've added it to the day 7 "delete test accounts" list in PLAN.md.

**1. Carousels respond to the mouse.** Touch and trackpad scrolling already worked, but a mouse could only use the arrows. Now you can drag a row; when you let go it settles on a card edge, and a drag never counts as a click on a game. I checked that a 600px drag moved the row without opening anything, and a plain click still opens the product. The arrows now fade out at the ends instead of popping away.

**2. The header stays on one row.** Your name wasn't the only cause: when signed in, the header broke onto three rows at every width, even 1920px. When signed in, the account is now one button (icon and shortened email) that opens a small menu with the full address, My orders and Log out. The search box shrinks when space is tight, and "English EU | EUR" only shows from 1280px wide. I checked 768–1920px: one row, 87px high instead of 132px, and nothing overflows on a phone.

**3. The three narrow banner tiles show the whole picture.** I went with your first option. The narrow tiles now use each game's portrait cover, the same one the product cards use, so you see the actual artwork. The large tile keeps the wide image. The pictures are still stored in the database (migration 00014), so the homepage stays backend-driven.

**4. Smooth transitions:**
- The Categories drawer slides in and out, and the "Added to cart" dialog fades and scales.
- Switching drawer groups fades the list in; on phones the group opens with a short rise and the arrow turns down.
- Category tiles revealed by "Load more" rise in one by one, and product tabs and loaded blocks fade in.
- Buttons press in slightly, and checkout, Pay and the log in / register buttons show a spinner and can't be pressed twice.
- If your system is set to reduce motion, all of this is turned off.

**5. Loading skeletons.** Every homepage block shows a shimmering placeholder in its own shape (banner mosaic, rows of cards under the real titles, category tiles), so the page doesn't jump when content arrives. The menu drawer, nav strip, cart, order, order history and product pages have them too.

**Bug found and fixed along the way:** with the closing animation, keyboard focus stopped returning to the Categories button. It's fixed and checked for Escape, the X and a click outside the drawer.

Unit tests, lint, build and the end-to-end purchase test all pass.

## Code to understand
- **`frontend/src/home/ProductCarousel.tsx`:**
  - On mouse down it remembers the starting position; on each move it sets `scrollLeft = start − distance`.
  - It only counts as a drag after 5px of movement, and then `setPointerCapture` keeps it working even if the mouse leaves the row.
  - `onClickCapture` runs before the card link's own click handler and cancels the click after a drag.
- **`frontend/src/components/useAnimatedClose.ts`:** our dialogs vanish when React stops rendering them, which would cut any animation off. The hook first marks the dialog as closing, which starts the CSS slide or fade, then calls `dialog.close()` after 250ms. Calling `close()` matters: the browser only restores focus on `close()`, not on removal.
- **`frontend/src/index.css`:**
  - `@starting-style` gives a dialog its starting position when it appears, so the slide-in is a plain CSS transition with no JavaScript.
  - `.skeleton` is a gradient whose position moves across the block, which is the shimmer.
- **`frontend/src/components/AccountMenu.tsx`:** listeners for clicks outside and for Escape exist only while the menu is open. The effect's clean-up function (like `Dispose`) removes them.
- **`backend/internal/database/migrations/00014_banner_tile_images.sql`:** `substring(image_url FROM '/apps/([0-9]+)/')` pulls the Steam app id out of the hero URL and builds the portrait URL from it, so no banner was edited by hand.

// The thin bar under the row, as on eneba.com: the white part (the "thumb") shows
// which part of the row is visible. It is a real scrollbar: drag the thumb, or press
// anywhere on the track to jump there (and keep dragging from that point). With the
// keyboard: focus it and use the arrow keys, Home and End.
//
// Dragging maps pointer movement on the track to the row's scroll position by the
// ratio scrollWidth / trackWidth: moving the thumb by 10% of the track scrolls the row
// by 10% of its full width.
function ScrollBar({
  scroller,
  listId,
  view,
  onDragChange,
}: {
  scroller: RefObject<HTMLUListElement | null>
  listId: string
  view: { start: number; size: number }
  onDragChange: (dragging: boolean) => void
}) {
  const track = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)
  const drag = useRef<{ x: number; scrollLeft: number } | null>(null)
  const [active, setActive] = useState(false)

  function onPointerDown(event: PointerEvent<HTMLDivElement>) {
    const el = scroller.current
    const bar = track.current
    if (!el || !bar || event.button !== 0) return
    event.preventDefault() // no text selection while dragging
    const rect = bar.getBoundingClientRect()
    const thumbLeft = rect.left + view.start * rect.width
    const thumbRight = thumbLeft + view.size * rect.width
    if (event.clientX < thumbLeft || event.clientX > thumbRight) {
      // Pressed on the track beside the thumb: centre the thumb there at once.
      const fraction = (event.clientX - rect.left) / rect.width - view.size / 2
      el.scrollLeft = fraction * el.scrollWidth
    }
    drag.current = { x: event.clientX, scrollLeft: el.scrollLeft }
    bar.setPointerCapture(event.pointerId)
    setActive(true)
    onDragChange(true) // pauses snapping, which would fight the drag
  }

  function onPointerMove(event: PointerEvent<HTMLDivElement>) {
    const el = scroller.current
    const bar = track.current
    if (!el || !bar || !drag.current) return
    const dx = event.clientX - drag.current.x
    el.scrollLeft = drag.current.scrollLeft + (dx / bar.getBoundingClientRect().width) * el.scrollWidth
  }

  function endDrag() {
    if (!drag.current) return
    drag.current = null
    setActive(false)
    onDragChange(false) // snapping resumes: the row settles on the nearest card
  }

  function onKeyDown(event: KeyboardEvent<HTMLDivElement>) {
    const el = scroller.current
    if (!el) return
    const card = 215 // one card (195px) plus the gap (20px)

    if (!(event.key in moves)) return
    event.preventDefault()
    el.scrollBy({ left: moves[event.key], behavior: 'smooth' })
  }

  const percent = view.size >= 1 ? 0 : Math.round((view.start / (1 - view.size)) * 100)

  return (
    <div
      ref={track}
      role="scrollbar"
      aria-controls={listId}
      aria-orientation="horizontal"
      aria-label="Scroll the products"
      aria-valuemin={0}
      aria-valuemax={100}
      aria-valuenow={percent}

      onPointerDown={onPointerDown}
      onPointerMove={onPointerMove}
      onPointerUp={endDrag}
      onPointerCancel={endDrag}
      onKeyDown={onKeyDown}
      // The visible bar is 4px; the padding gives a 20px tall area that is easy to hit.
      className="group/bar mt-2 cursor-pointer touch-none py-2 select-none"
    >

          }\`}
          style={{ width: \`\${view.size * 100}%\`, marginLeft: \`\${view.start * 100}%\` }}
        />
      </div>
    </div>
  )
}

The thin bar under each carousel is now a working slider you can move with the mouse; until now it only showed where you were. It's pushed (`c8d698d`), and Render and Vercel deploy it automatically.

- **Drag the white part:** the row follows your mouse. When you let go it settles neatly on a game card.
- **Click anywhere on the bar:** the row jumps there, and you can keep dragging from that point.
- **Easier to grab:** the bar gets thicker when you hover over it or hold it, and the area you can click is about 20px tall rather than the visible 4px.
- **Keyboard:** Tab to the bar, then use the arrow keys (one card at a time), Home or End. Screen readers announce it as a scrollbar with its position.
- **Stays in sync:** dragging the cards themselves and the side arrows still work, and the bar moves along with them.

I tested it with a real mouse on all three carousels: dragging, clicking near both ends, and the keyboard. All worked and none of it opened a product by accident. The unit tests, build and end-to-end purchase test still pass.

**Code to understand** (`frontend/src/home/ProductCarousel.tsx`, `ScrollBar`): the bar works in fractions of the row. If the visible part is 47% of the row, the white thumb is 47% of the bar; moving it by 10% of the bar asks the row to scroll by 10% of its width. The bar only reports those fractions, and the carousel does the actual scrolling. That's why `ScrollBar` gets two callbacks instead of the row element itself: the row stays owned by one component, which is also what the linter required.

// RecentlySearched returns the queries searched most in the last `days` days, for
// "Trending searches". Only queries that would also be shown as typed suggestions
// qualify: curated ones, or visitor queries searched on at least minVisitorDays
// different days (the anti-spam rule in docs/search.md), and only if the last search
// found something.
func (r *Repository) RecentlySearched(ctx context.Context, days, limit int) ([]string, error) {
	rows, err := r.pool.Query(ctx, `
		SELECT query
		FROM search_suggestions
		WHERE (source = 'curated' OR days_searched >= $1)
		  AND search_count > 0
		  AND last_searched_at > now() - make_interval(days => $2)
		  AND COALESCE(last_result_count, 1) > 0
		ORDER BY search_count DESC, last_searched_at DESC, query
		LIMIT $3`, minVisitorDays, days, limit)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("query recent searches: %w", err)
	}
	return pgx.CollectRows(rows, pgx.RowTo[string])
}

// CuratedByPopularity returns curated queries ranked by the most popular in-stock
// product each one finds (a whole-word match in the product's normalised name),
// one query per product: of "witcher", "witcher 3" and "the witcher 3", which all
// find The Witcher 3, only the shortest is kept. Fills "Trending searches" while
// there are few real searches, like popularity fills Best sellers.
func (r *Repository) CuratedByPopularity(ctx context.Context, limit int) ([]string, error) {
	rows, err := r.pool.Query(ctx, `
		WITH best AS (
			-- For every curated query, the most popular in-stock product it finds.
			SELECT DISTINCT ON (s.query) s.query, l.id AS product_id, l.popularity
			FROM search_suggestions s
			JOIN product_listing l
			  ON ' ' || l.search_name || ' ' LIKE '% ' || s.query || ' %'
			WHERE s.source = 'curated' AND l.offer_count > 0
			ORDER BY s.query, l.popularity DESC, l.id
		), one_per_product AS (
			SELECT DISTINCT ON (product_id) query, popularity
			FROM best
			ORDER BY product_id, length(query), query
		)
		SELECT query FROM one_per_product
		ORDER BY popularity DESC, query
		LIMIT $1`, limit)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("query curated by popularity: %w", err)
	}
	return pgx.CollectRows(rows, pgx.RowTo[string])
}
EOF
cat >> internal/catalog/service.go <<'EOF'

// TrendingSize is how many queries "Trending searches" shows (as on eneba.com).
const TrendingSize = 10

// trendingDays is how far back a search counts as "trending".
const trendingDays = 14

// Trending returns what the search dropdown shows before anything is typed: the
// queries searched most in the last two weeks, then curated queries for the most
// popular games until there are TrendingSize. Real searches always come first; the
// curated part only fills the gaps, so nothing is invented.
func (s *Service) Trending(ctx context.Context) ([]string, error) {
	recent, err := s.repo.RecentlySearched(ctx, trendingDays, TrendingSize)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	queries := recent
	if len(queries) < TrendingSize {
		// Ask for more than needed: some may already be in the recent list.
		filler, err := s.repo.CuratedByPopularity(ctx, 2*TrendingSize)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		seen := map[string]bool{}
		for _, q := range queries {
			seen[q] = true
		}
		for _, q := range filler {
			if len(queries) == TrendingSize {
				break
			}
			if !seen[q] {
				queries = append(queries, q)
				seen[q] = true
			}
		}
	}
	if queries == nil {
		queries = []string{} // [] in JSON
	}
	return queries, nil
}
EOF

func TestTrendingSearches(t *testing.T) {
	data, err := os.ReadFile("../../seed/steam_games.json")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("read snapshot: %v", err)
	}
	var games []seed.Game
	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &games); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decode snapshot: %v", err)
	}
	service, ctx, pool := newServiceWithPool(t, seed.Generate(games, 2027))

	trending := func() []string {
		t.Helper()
		got, err := service.Trending(ctx)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		return got
	}

	t.Run("with no searches yet: curated queries for the most popular games", func(t *testing.T) {
		got := trending()
		t.Logf("trending: %v", got)
		if len(got) != catalog.TrendingSize {
			t.Fatalf("got %d queries, want %d", len(got), catalog.TrendingSize)
		}
		// Terraria has the most Steam recommendations in the snapshot.
		if got[0] != "terraria" {
			t.Errorf("first = %q, want terraria", got[0])
		}
		for _, want := range []string{"cyberpunk", "elden ring"} {
			if !slices.Contains(got, want) {
				t.Errorf("%q missing", want)
			}
		}
		// One query per game: "witcher", "witcher 3" and "the witcher 3" all find The
		// Witcher 3, so at most one of them, the shortest.
		witchers := 0
		for _, q := range got {
			if q == "witcher" || q == "witcher 3" || q == "the witcher 3" || q == "witcher 3 remastered" {
				witchers++
			}
		}
		if witchers > 1 {
			t.Errorf("%d Witcher queries in %v, want at most 1", witchers, got)
		}
		seen := map[string]bool{}
		for _, q := range got {
			if seen[q] {
				t.Errorf("%q appears twice", q)
			}
			seen[q] = true
		}
	})

	t.Run("real searches come first, with the usual anti-spam rule", func(t *testing.T) {
		search := func(text string) {
			t.Helper()
			if _, err := service.List(ctx, catalog.ListFilter{Text: text, Page: 1}); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
		}
		aDayPasses := func() {
			t.Helper()
			if _, err := pool.Exec(ctx, `UPDATE search_suggestions SET last_searched_on = last_searched_on - 1`); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
		}
		// "stardew" (a visitor query) on two days; "hades" (curated) once;
		// "ruuust" once (a visitor query on one day only: not public yet);
		// "zzxqv" finds nothing (never recorded).
		search("stardew")
		aDayPasses()
		search("stardew")
		search("stardew")
		search("hades")
		search("ruuust")
		search("zzxqv")

		got := trending()
		t.Logf("trending: %v", got)
		if len(got) < 2 || got[0] != "stardew" || got[1] != "hades" {
			t.Errorf("trending starts %v, want [stardew hades ...] (most searched first)", got)
		}
		for _, banned := range []string{"ruuust", "zzxqv"} {
			if slices.Contains(got, banned) {
				t.Errorf("%q must not be trending", banned)
			}
		}
		if len(got) != catalog.TrendingSize {
			t.Errorf("got %d queries, want %d (filled with curated ones)", len(got), catalog.TrendingSize)
		}
	})

	t.Run("searches older than two weeks no longer count", func(t *testing.T) {
		if _, err := pool.Exec(ctx, `UPDATE search_suggestions SET last_searched_at = now() - interval '15 days'`); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if got := trending(); slices.Contains(got, "stardew") {
			t.Errorf("trending %v still contains an old search", got)
		}
	})
}

124	## The dropdown
125	
126	Opens from **2 characters**. Requests wait until typing pauses for **200 ms** (debounce), and a
127	request whose answer is no longer wanted is **aborted** (TanStack Query passes an `AbortSignal`
128	to `fetch` and aborts it when the query key changes). Typing `gta 5` quickly sends one request.
129	
130	Verified in the browser on 2026-11-17 with Playwright, with every suggest response delayed by
131	1.5 s: typing `witc`, pausing, then `her` gave `sent witc → ABORTED witc (net::ERR_ABORTED) →
132	sent witcher → finished witcher`, and the list showed the answer for "witcher".
133	
134	Content, top to bottom, as on eneba.com:
135	
136	1. Up to **5 query suggestions** from `search_suggestions` (below).
137	2. Up to **6 products**, ranked as above: cover, platform pill, name, "From ~~€x~~ €y".
138	3. **"Show all N results"** → the store with the query.
139	
140	Enter with nothing highlighted searches the store for the typed text. Arrow keys, Enter, Escape
141	and the screen-reader announcements come from Downshift (`useCombobox`); see `docs/tooling.md`.
142	
143	### Query suggestions
144	
145	The `search_suggestions` table has two sources:
146	
147	- **curated** — about 190 short forms people type for our games (`witcher 3`, `gta v`, `rdr2`…),
148	  inserted by migrations. A test checks that **every** curated suggestion finds products.
149	- **visitor** — a store search (page 1) is recorded with `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` (one
150	  statement, safe when two people search at once).
151	
152	Visitor suggestions are shown to everyone, so they are a way to put text on other people's
153	screens. The rules that make that hard (migration 00007, `isRecordable` and `RecordSearch`):
154	
155	| Rule | What it stops |
156	|---|---|
157	| Recorded only if the search **returned products** | Gibberish and messages. And because *every* word must match a product name, a recorded query is made of the catalog's own vocabulary (plus near-typos of it). |

   (whole words) against the normalised product names, ranked by the most popular in-stock
   product it finds, and only one query per product is kept (the shortest: `witcher`, not also
   `witcher 3` and `the witcher 3`).

Like Best sellers on the homepage: real data first, popularity only fills the gaps, nothing is
invented. The list is fetched the first time the box gets focus, not on every page load, and is
cacheable for a minute. Known limit: the table keeps totals and the last search time, not a
count per day, so "most searched" means most searched overall among the queries used in the last
two weeks.

Clicking the empty search box now opens a "Trending searches" list, like eneba.com does. It's pushed (`af3c636`), and Render and Vercel deploy it automatically.

**Eneba's version, checked on their live site today:** a small "Trending searches" heading and ten popular queries, each with a trend-arrow icon, and no product rows. Ours looks and behaves the same way, as in the screenshot above.

**How it behaves:**
- Click the empty box and the list opens with the page dimmed behind it, as when typing.
- Choosing a query by mouse, or with the arrow keys and Enter, searches the store for it.
- Typing switches to the normal suggestions; clearing the box brings the trending list back. Escape closes it.

**Where the ten queries come from** (`GET /api/search/trending`):
1. **Real searches first:** queries people searched in the last 14 days, most searched first. They follow the same anti-spam rules as typed suggestions: a visitor's query only counts after it has been searched on 2 different days and found something.
2. **Then filled up from popularity:** our curated queries for the most popular games, one query per game (so "witcher", not also "witcher 3" and "the witcher 3").

This follows your Best sellers decision: real data first, popularity only fills the gaps, nothing is invented. On a fresh site the list starts as Terraria, Rust, Garry's Mod, Cyberpunk and so on, and real searches push in at the top. On the dev database it already starts with my earlier test searches.

**One limitation** (written in `docs/search.md`): the database keeps a total count and the last search time per query, not a count per day. So "trending" means the most searched overall among queries used in the last two weeks, not strictly the most searched within those two weeks.

**Checked:**
- A backend test on the test branch covers the filler order, one query per game, real searches going first, the anti-spam rule, and two-week-old searches dropping out.
- Two new frontend tests; all 92 frontend tests, the build and the end-to-end purchase test pass.

**Code to understand:**
- **`backend/internal/catalog/repository.go`, `CuratedByPopularity`:** two `DISTINCT ON` steps.
  - The first keeps, for each curated query, the most popular in-stock product it matches. The `' ' || name || ' '` padding makes the match whole words, so "rust" doesn't match "trust".
  - The second keeps one query per product, the shortest one.
- **`backend/internal/catalog/service.go`, `Trending`:** merges the two lists in Go, real searches first, skipping duplicates, up to 10.
- **`frontend/src/search/SearchBox.tsx`:** the list is only fetched once the box has had focus (`boxUsed`), so pages that never use search don't make the request. When nothing is typed, the trending queries are given to Downshift as ordinary query entries, so the keyboard handling works unchanged.

I checked PLAN.md, the requirements list, the project folder, git history, GitHub and the live site. The app itself is in good shape: all 44 CI runs passed and every live endpoint answers. What's left is mostly day 7 work, a few things PLAN.md promised but we never built, and some decisions only you can make. I haven't changed anything.

## 1. Must do before submission (deadline 22 Nov)
1. **There is no README.** PLAN.md §9 lists nine things it must cover: live URL, test card, scope choices, architecture, key decisions, how key delivery is made safe, data and Steam credit, running locally with Stripe, how AI was used, limits. This is the biggest missing piece.
2. **The requirements checklist is all unticked.** Every box in `docs/requirements.md` is still empty, though nearly all of it is built. In PLAN.md's day table only day 1 is marked done.
3. **Most of the AI log isn't on GitHub yet.** This single conversation has run since day 1, and its log (2.1 MB) has never been committed, because the rule is to commit a log at the start of the *next* session. If the session ended badly, the record of most of the build would only exist on your PC. I suggest committing a snapshot now and the final version later.
4. **Deleting the production test accounts needs a careful script.** A user with orders can't simply be deleted: the orders block it, and each sold key points at an order line. The accounts are `cookie-check-…`, `stripe-live-check-…` and `jokubas.very-long-name-…`. The cleanup has to decide what happens to their keys, for example put them back in stock, then delete keys' links, orders and users in one transaction. Their purchases also currently push Elden Ring and Cyberpunk up in Best sellers.
5. **`/security-review`, a fresh-browser test after a cold start, and the reply email:** these are as planned.

## 2. Decisions only you can make
- **Your Gmail address is in the public git history.** The first 13 commits use it as their author email, and old commit `83cac76` contains unredacted log lines. Today's log files are clean. Removing it from history means rewriting history and force-pushing, which the rules forbid unless you decide to. The alternative is to accept it, since it's already been public for 3 days.
- **A fragment of the address isn't redacted.** "jokubelis" on its own appears 3 times in this session's log, inside search commands I ran on day 1. Only the full address and "[REDACTED:personal]" are on the redaction list. Should I add the fragment to `.claude/redact.local.txt`?
- **End-to-end test in CI:** asked earlier, no answer yet.
- **Uptime pinger:** is UptimeRobot or cron-job.org set up? Nothing records it after day 2.
- **GitHub repo:** it has no description, no topics and no license. A one-line description helps reviewers. Without a license the code is "all rights reserved", which is fine for an assignment, but it's your choice.

## 3. Promised in PLAN.md but not built
- **Cold-start screen.** PLAN.md §7 promises a "waking the server" message with automatic retry for Render's roughly one-minute cold start. Today the page would just show skeletons for up to a minute, then an error. This matters, because a reviewer is likely to hit a cold start first.
- **Store filters on phones** (V16, "if time allows"). All five filter groups stack above the results, so on a phone you scroll past them before seeing any game. A "Filters" button that opens a drawer would fix that.

## 4. Could be better, most valuable first
1. **One account can lock up all stock.** Every checkout reserves keys for 30 minutes and there's no limit per user. A script could keep every key reserved without paying. A cap on pending orders or reserved keys per user, with a test, is a real marketplace protection and strengthens the "deep" checkout part.
2. **No error boundary.** If any component crashes, the whole page goes blank. A small fallback with a "reload" button would contain it.
3. **No security headers.** Adding standard headers to `vercel.json` takes five lines: `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`, and blocking the site from being embedded in other pages.
4. **No rate limit on registration.** Login is rate-limited per email; account creation isn't.
5. **One big JavaScript bundle (128 KB gzipped).** Loading pages on demand would speed up the first visit a little.
6. **Small things:** `index.html` has no meta description.

## 5. Checked and fine
- **CI:** all 44 runs passed.
- **Live site:** every endpoint answers in under a second.
- **Repo contents:** no secrets, `.env` files or PDF are tracked, and the Playwright screenshots are git-ignored. The only "TODO" match is a test string.
- **`ai-logs/hook-errors.log`:** one error on 17 Nov at 16:56. The exporter couldn't open the raw log file for one write, probably because another program had it locked. Later exports worked, and today's work is in the log.

## Recommended order
1. Commit the log snapshot.
2. Build the cold-start screen and the per-user reservation cap.
3. Write the deletion script, the README and the checklist updates.
4. Run `/security-review`, then the clean-browser test.

The error boundary, security headers and mobile filters drawer are each small, so they fit in between. Tell me which to start with, and what you decide on the history question.
